docs.title: Model Protocol Lab — documentation
docs.text:
Model Protocol Lab answers one question with measurements: is a local language model failing because of its weights, or because its conversations are formatted incorrectly? It renders chat-format hypotheses — a 29-family catalog, plus bounded BOS, prefix and thinking-mode mutations — as exact token sequences, sends them to a local checkpoint, and compares task answers and response boundaries token-for-token. A strict search/held-out fixture discipline selects a single winning format or abstains.

This documentation is organised in four parts, by what you are trying to do:

  • Tutorials — learning-oriented. A guided path through a first experiment, step by step.
  • How-to guides — task-oriented. Short routes from a concrete job (choosing boundary IDs, authoring fixtures, comparing two runs) to the section that documents it.
  • Reference — information-oriented. The complete usage reference, the security and data-handling record, and the validation evidence.
  • Explanation — understanding-oriented. Why the lab measures what it measures, and the design record behind each probe.

New here? Start with the tutorial path. Running a model today? Go straight to the usage reference — and read it before your first run: boundary token IDs must be established from the actual checkpoint tokenizer.

The project itself lives at strmt7/model-protocol-lab; the validation record is VALIDATION.md and the change history is the CHANGELOG.

docs.title: Candidate aliasing audit — design contract
docs.text: Status: shipped in cycle 181 (wave-7 research rank 2). This document is the frozen contract for model_protocol_lab/aliasing.py and the aliasing payload; the digest definition travels inside every payload as protocol data, so this prose and the payloads can be checked against each other.

docs.title: What it answers
docs.text:
Candidates are names for renderings. On a given tokenizer and fixture set, two differently named formats can render byte-identical prompt token sequences on every search fixture — a BOS mutation that is a no-op for a family whose framing already starts with that token, two families whose framing coincides on short single-turn messages, a field the fixture set's turn shapes never exercise. A leaderboard cannot see the collapse (tied rows look normal); this lab can, because it renders every candidate itself and abstains on ties — and a tie between two names for one token sequence is a different event from a tie between two genuinely different prompts.

Utility, in one sentence: an operator who ran a 24-candidate sweep uses the audit to decide whether to prune the candidate set before the next (expensive) run — and whether an ambiguous abstention was two genuinely different templates tying, or one token sequence wearing two name tags.

docs.title: Two class notions, never conflated
docs.text:
The design's first draft defined one equivalence (identical input_ids) and spent it as three different things. The cross-check (red-team A F1, upheld as amended by red-team B) split it:

  • Render class — identical recorded input_ids on every fixture of the cohort. Supports exactly one claim: these names produced the same prompt token sequences on this fixture set.
  • Measurement class — a render class refined by the candidate's own response boundary (boundary_token_ids). Boundaries are part of the measurement: each candidate is judged under its own terminator, and under --boundary-map two candidates with identical prompts and different boundaries are different experiments that happen to share a prompt.

Effective counts are reported for both notions (n_effective_render, n_effective_measurement) next to n_candidates_recorded and n_primary_cohort. Pruning language and the alias-suspect flag cite measurement classes only. In the default configuration (no --boundary-map) every candidate shares one boundary and the two notions coincide; the distinction is load-bearing exactly in the mode where it matters.

docs.title: Cohorts and evaluable cells (A1')
docs.text:
Classes exist only inside cohorts of candidates with identical completed fixture sets: pairwise identity over differing sets is not transitive, so union "classes" would not be classes. On genuine runs the eligible candidates always share the full search set and at most one ineligible interrupter exists; the cohort discipline is what keeps foreign or interrupted records honest. The primary cohort is chosen by a total deterministic order (most candidates, then most fixtures, then lexicographic) so the producer and the diff validator derive the same cohort from the same records.

A cell counts only if it is evaluable: status == "completed", input_ids a nonempty list/tuple of exact ints (bools excluded) >= 0, the fixture unique within its entry, and the observation's candidate field present and equal to the entry's name. The nonempty rule is load-bearing: the abort path in core.evaluate records input_ids == () for render/encode failures, so the empty tuple is a failure sentinel that collides with itself — two failed candidates would "coincide" on it. A completed cell with empty or malformed IDs is an artifact defect (recorded_ids_invalid, the determinism audit's vocabulary), never a class member. Duplicate fixture IDs and candidate-field mismatches fail the whole candidate closed with named details; duplicate search entries for one name make that name unavailable (duplicate_candidate_entry).

Classes are computed from recorded input_ids only — never from candidate_fingerprint, the format dict, or input_text. The fingerprint hashes asdict(fmt) including the name (its own docstring says so deliberately), so fingerprint classes would be singletons by construction: the audit would report "no aliasing" on every run, forever. Named tests pin the two executed counter-pairs (name-only difference with repeat_bos under an empty BOS; assistant_turn_end difference on single-turn fixtures) as aliased despite different fingerprints and different format dicts.

docs.title: The redundant count (one formula)
docs.text: n_redundant_completed_observations = Σ over the primary cohort's fixtures of (candidates completed on the fixture − distinct (input_ids, boundary_token_ids) tuples on it). It counts each redundant observation once, is additive over fixtures, sees partial aliasing that a global-class formula misses, and is recomputable from the ground records. The render analogue travels under its own name (n_redundant_render_observations); the two are never summed, and pair-matrix entries are never summed into either (pairs overlap by construction). The word "wasted" appears nowhere in the payload: a boundary-distinct evaluation is a distinct measurement, not waste, and even a measurement-redundant evaluation is the replicate the A2' cross-check consumes.

docs.title: The determinism tripwire (A2')
docs.text:
Within one measurement class, the recorded output_ids are identical per fixture, and the outcome fields (exact_match, boundary_found, boundary_text_match, status) are identical — checked as independent corollaries, not consequences (the outcome fields pass through the backend's decode). The premise is checkable and checked: core.request_seed_for(seed, case_id) derives the per-request seed from the run seed and the fixture ID only — the candidate is not an input — and the generation cap is run-global, so identical measurement configurations present identical generate() inputs.

A violation is reported per (class, fixture) as a determinism-suspect cell, kind output (output digests differ), outcome (outcome fields differ), or both: recorded cells a deterministic backend could not have produced from one measurement configuration, attributable to backend nondeterminism (stateful or order-dependent backends included — candidates are evaluated sequentially in one run) or artifact corruption. The audit asserts neither cause; verify --determinism replay is the discriminating follow-up. This mirrors the house precedent in experiments.ws_canonicalization (n_same_ids_verdict_flips: same IDs, different verdict ⇒ determinism anomaly, never counted as the probe's own effect), at the native-run layer.

docs.title: The alias-suspect flag (A3')
docs.text:
alias_suspect_abstention fires iff (i) the recorded decision is ambiguous; (ii) the passing set — primary-cohort, eligible candidates whose every evaluable cell passes — recomputed from the ground records has ≥ 2 members; (iii) the passing set is contained in a single measurement class; and (iv) that class contains no outcome-suspect cell. Withholding reasons are produced in a fixed priority order, and the validator recomputes the expected reason in the same order: candidate_unavailable, decision_not_ambiguous, passing_set_inconsistent, determinism_suspect_in_class, passing_spans_classes, boundaries_differ_within_passing_set. alias_suspect_detail is "" exactly when the flag fires (the scorer-lens winner_detail discipline); the fired case's class members travel in alias_suspect_class_members.

Two negative cases are pinned as tests because users will ask about them. A tie whose passing set spans classes never fires: two different prompts both passing everything is a genuine tie between distinct measurements — the lab working as intended, not an artifact. And a post-boundary-only output divergence inside the containing class does not suppress the flag: every selection-relevant quantity is identical there, so the aliasing explanation of the tie is intact; the cell is still reported as a suspect cell. The flag is advisory — it never modifies the recorded decision or selected_candidate, and it asserts the structural containment only, not that any candidate would have survived held-out (held-out was never run for any of them).

docs.title: The payload and its ground layer
docs.text:
Token IDs in a payload are prompt text by proxy (the house strips recorded ID subsequences from the public view for exactly this reason), so the payload carries, per candidate: the boundary tuple (operator configuration, already public in every search entry), eligibility, planned count, and per-fixture ground records {fixture, status, evaluable, input_sha256, output_sha256, exact_match, boundary_found, boundary_text_match} — digests and small enums only. Digests are None for non-evaluable cells, never a digest of the empty list (the abort sentinel must not re-enter through the digest layer). The digest definition is one canonical form, frozen as protocol data: SHA-256 of the compact JSON encoding of the ID list, version string sha256-json-intlist-v1, computed identically for input and output IDs. At top level the payload also carries decision, selected_candidate, backend_fingerprint, seed, and max_new_tokens, so it is interpretable standalone at the diff's payload-only interface.

What the validator's recompute buys, stated without overselling: _valid_aliasing re-derives cohorts, both class partitions, both effective counts, both redundant counts, the pair matrix, every suspect cell, the passing set, and the flag from the ground records with independent code, and rejects duplicate candidate names, duplicate fixtures, and payloads beyond the run caps (24 candidates, 2400 cells). That is an internal-consistency recompute — it detects aggregates inconsistent with their records; it cannot detect fabricated ground records. That limitation is the standing one for every house ground layer (refusals, scorer-lens), and the design says so rather than claiming verifiability. Digest handling in the validator is version-agnostic (equality only): a coherent foreign digest version validates internally, and a version mismatch across a diff is protocol_drift.

Two size/privacy facts settle the flag-gating: the ground layer is the largest per-cell payload the lab ships — measured 921,192 bytes (≈0.92 MB) at the 2400-cell cap in the indented public JSON — so the audit runs behind run --aliasing, following the refusals/scorer-lens precedent. And an unsalted SHA-256 of a short, structured token sequence is a guess-confirmation oracle: anyone holding the payload, a candidate prompt, and the tokenizer can verify a guess offline. The docs claim exactly that and no more: no raw token IDs or text; per-cell digests permit offline confirmation of a guessed prompt. The same trade was already accepted for prompt_sha256 in the surface-noise probe.

docs.title: Back-porting, stated precisely
docs.text: The profile runs over the in-memory result at run time. Back-porting to stored artifacts works over --include-evidence artifacts only: reporting._public_view strips search[].observations from the default public results.json. An entry with no observations key degrades its candidate to observations_missing; the top-level payload is {"available": false, "detail": "observations_stripped"} only when every search entry lacks the key (the determinism._plan test) — otherwise the top level stays available with per-candidate records (the refusal-profile precedent). A run made without --aliasing carries no aliasing key at all, and reporting/diff render that as "not recorded", never "no aliasing found".

docs.title: Diff semantics
docs.text: diff_aliasing reports measurement-partition drift over the common candidates (pairs_joined / pairs_split), per-candidate boundary drift, count drift over the effective counts, the redundant count, and the suspect-cell count, flag drift, candidates added/removed/excluded, and the evaluable-mismatch change. Three drift gates set comparable: false while still listing drift: fixture_set_drift (classes are fixture-set-relative), backend_drift, and protocol_drift (digest definition). backend_drift means the recorded backend fingerprints differ — tokenizer identity not proven equal, because the fingerprint also binds device, context limit, and dependency versions; it must never be paraphrased as "a different tokenizer". The pair matrix is pairwise data with explicit denominators and is never clustered into "partial classes" in the HTML or the diff.

docs.title: Provenance
docs.text: Wave-7 research rank 2. Red-team A returned DO NOT BUILD AS SPECIFIED (10 findings). Red-team B's cross-check upheld the verdict, downgraded five severities, refuted one sub-claim (the scorer-lens precedent A cited for duplicate fixtures accepts them — the duplicate rule is new, not a transplant), caught an internal contradiction in A's own n_nominal definitions, and repaired four of A's prescribed fixes (the stripped-artifact trigger, the redundant-formula ambiguity, flag suppression keyed on any suspect cell instead of outcome-suspect cells, and the inverted detail-field precedent), plus four findings A missed (the guess-confirmation wording, the missing run-configuration fields, the digest-of-empty rule, duplicate search entries). The build follows gates 1, 4, 10 as A wrote them and gates 2, 3, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9 as B amended them. All A1'–A3' claims are pinned by named tests in tests/test_cycle181_aliasing.py, including a brute-force oracle differential for A1' and a run_experiment construction of the flag case through the real run flow.

docs.title: Round summary (coordinator #39, design round only — nothing built)
docs.text:
• Tree at main f31e72e1ace4 (cycle 212 closed green, 8,439 tests, precise coverage 95.3455%). This round was READ-ONLY except for this doc and the briefs; no suite was run, no push was made, no tag was cut or discussed.
  • Specialists (blind to each other): researcher (~/workspace/agents_out/answersyntax/research.md), red-team A (redteam_a.md), red-team B (redteam_b.md), verifier/claims auditor (verifier.md). All four briefs landed; the verifier resolved every externally checkable claim against primary sources, re-ran every surviving PoC script, and recomputed all decision math with its own simulator. The coordinator re-executed the load-bearing claims itself (§4).
  • Convergence and divergence, in one paragraph: all three blind briefs return NO-BUILD for the candidate as specified in the circulated sketch (three syntax arms, JSON-vs-YAML endpoint contrast, field-order's decision rule transplanted unchanged), and the verifier upholds that unanimously. The researcher additionally specifies an amended instrument (JSON-vs-XML headline endpoints, YAML descriptive only, neutral schema description, re-derived 13-spec paired pool, parsed-value headline scorer) and recommends BUILD for it; the verifier upholds that instrument as-amended, subject to corrections (§5), and flags that the amendments change the endpoint pair, the paired population, and the headline scorer. The coordinator's verdict is NO-BUILD — for the sketch, and as a build order for the amended instrument in this round — for the procedural reason stated in §2: under this program's own adjudicated distinction (payload round vs negation round), the amended instrument is a resubmission, and a resubmission is reviewed as a new design before it is built. §3 records it as the resubmission candidate in full. No fabricated citation or symbol was found in any brief this round; the failures found were one wrong p-value, several unreproducible secondary figures, and sloppy line ranges, all handled in §5.

docs.title: 1. Why NO-BUILD: the fatal defects of the candidate as specified
docs.text: Each defect below is individually blocking and was established by execution (attribution: A = red-team A, B = red-team B, V = verifier, C = coordinator).

docs.title: F1 — Population and scorer are both undefined (rank-2 F1/F4, inherited)
docs.text: The claim names "the shipped flat structured-output spec pool" (9 specs, structured.py:75-223); the budget names field-order's pool (15 specs, 10 paired). The claim, the budget, and the decision rule therefore have three different denominators. Worse, "the answer field's exact-value accuracy" has two readings in the tree — byte-exact (core.py:797: exact_match = status == "completed" and answer == case.expected) and field-order's parsed-value digest comparison — and they give opposite verdicts on identical behaviour (B, executed with stub policies: a JSON-only policy with always-correct values scores endpoint 10/10 vs 0/10 under byte-exact, 10/10 vs 10/10 under parsed-value; a perfect policy with reversed YAML key order scores 0/10 byte-exact). A design whose headline flips with an unmade scorer choice does not have a headline.

docs.title: F2 — The conditioning makes the adherence half of the claim unfalsifiable (new fatal)
docs.text: The sketch's only decision rule conditions the value contrast on specs adherent under both endpoint arms, yet adherence-rate equality is half of the claim sentence — and no rule anywhere in the sketch tests the adherence contrast. Executed (B, deterministic): a candidate with JSON adherence 10/10 and YAML adherence 5/10 — a 50-point adherence gap — leaves a conditioned pool of 5, below the floor of 6, so the verdict is insufficient by construction; Monte Carlo over adherence gaps of 0.95 vs 0.55 falsifies 0.000–0.013 of the time and returns insufficient 0.977–1.000 of the time. The conditioning also biases the value contrast it does test toward the null (C, executed: with a true 0.60 value gap on 40% of a 10-spec pool, mean discordant specs fall from 3.72 unconditioned to 1.74 conditioned — the floor of 6 is unreachable in that world). Outcome-dependent exclusion of exactly the cases the treatment moves is the payload round's F4 lesson, here at the level of the claim itself.

docs.title: F3 — The XML arm can never pass the tree's schema checker (new fatal)
docs.text: XML parsers produce strings for every scalar. The tree's checker is type-exact (structured.check_schema, structured.py:500; _field_value_ok, structured.py:529-565: an integer field requires type(value) is int). Executed (B; C independently): all 10 of field-order's paired specs contain at least one non-string field, so the only document an XML parser can produce for a perfect model answer returns schema_failed on 10/10 paired specs. Scoring XML at all requires a schema-directed coercion layer that does not exist in the tree; the sketch neither names nor freezes one, and its choices (whitespace, "36.0", "yes") would be the headline. That is rank-2 F2 arriving through the scorer: "same value" across syntaxes is exactly what has to be stipulated, and the sketch does not stipulate it.

docs.title: F4 — The YAML endpoint rests on ground the rank-2 round already buried (rank-2 F6)
docs.text: Zero runtime dependencies (pyproject.toml:28, dependencies = []); no stdlib YAML parser exists. PyYAML imports in this VM only as an environment accident — executed (C): version 6.0.3 in the project venv and 6.0.1 in the system interpreter, two different accidents, neither declared. Both parser choices break a claim (B, executed): JSON is a subset of YAML flow style, so a JSON echo is adherent and correct under a real YAML parser and parse_failed under a block-only subset parser — the "YAML adherence rate" is a property of the parser choice, not of the model. And a real parser imports YAML 1.1's coercion folklore into the measurement (executed by A, B, and C: yes/on → True; no in a string field → False; 0123 → 83 (octal); 0x24 → 36 (hex); 500,000 → the string "500,000"; duplicate keys silently last-wins, with no hook to express field-order's duplicate-key pairing condition). The sketch supplies no reckoning with any of this; rank-2 F6 already held that a hand-rolled mirror parser is new untrusted code whose choices become hidden treatments, and that holding was not answered.

docs.title: F5 — The transplanted decision rule is borrowed, and near-inert on its own panel
docs.text: The binding constraint of this program is that floors are derived for the panel, never borrowed (the negation round removed borrowed (6,2) floors that fired on a random labeller 58% of the time). The sketch transplants field-order's (6, sign-test) rule unchanged and prints none of this panel's operating characteristics. Executed (A, B, C, V — independent code, reconciled by V): the rule's false-fire rate is fine (exact 0.9% on a random labeller, 10-spec pool, adherence 1.0 — C), but its power at the canonical gap field-order itself advertises (0.90 vs 0.60) is 3.2% through the full conditioned pipeline (A), 5.1% at adherence 0.95 (B), 7.4–7.7% at adherence 1.0 (B, C, V). On the shipped pool alone (9 specs, 4 paired under field-order's flags) the floor of 6 discordant specs is unreachable by construction (C): the instrument can only ever answer insufficient. An instrument that returns its withheld label 82–97% of the time across the plausible world will be read — whatever its docs say — as an acquittal machine.

docs.title: F6 — The congruence dilemma: the schema description bundles the treatment (rank-2 F3)
docs.text: structured.describe_schema (structured.py:403-443) renders a JSON-shaped description — executed verbatim (V): {"age": integer (>= 0); "name": string} (required: age, name; no other keys allowed). Hold it constant across arms and every non-JSON arm is depiction-incongruent (a JSON-shaped schema inside a YAML/XML demand); re-render it per arm and the instruction's shape, length, and escaping move together with the treatment. The sketch mentions neither horn. The arm-length bundle is likewise real and systematic (C, executed on the shipped 9 specs with an <answer>-root XML renderer: expected documents run YAML 0.65–0.79× and XML 1.57–2.12× the JSON length; the researcher's <response>-root renderer gives XML 1.49–2.35× across the 15 — quote lengths only with the renderer named, §5 R-11). A paired contrast over these arms attributes a flip to "syntax" only if the claim is worded as discordance between named frozen prompt+rendering pairs; the sketch's claim is worded as syntax sameness in the abstract.

docs.title: F7 — The XML surface is unfrozen, and its parser surface is unsafe as shipped defaults
docs.text: Attribute-form and element-form documents encoding identical content score {} under each other's parsers (A and B, executed); namespaced answers yield {urn:x}-style keys and fail schema; no attribute-vs-element ruling, namespace policy, whitespace policy, DTD policy, or size cap is named in the sketch. The stdlib parser the build would reach for, xml.etree.ElementTree, expands internal entities on untrusted model output (C, executed: a depth-4 nested-entity document expands to 10,000 chars; A, executed and V-reproduced: expanded lengths 7,290 / 65,610 / 590,490 chars at increasing depth), while external entities raise ParseError. ET alone is therefore not a safety story for parsing model output; a frozen pre-parse screen is required, and even behind such a screen the ET call needs a bandit disposition at build time (B314 fires regardless — V, §5).

docs.title: Non-fatals, adjudicated
docs.text:
• Multiplicity. Per-candidate decisions at 24 candidates compound: B executed P(≥1 falsified candidate) ≈ 0.197 on pure noise for the sketch's panel (and ≈0.48 if all three pairs are read as decisions). Any successor design must print its panel-wise expectation beside the verdicts; the amended instrument does (0.36 expected false falsifications per 24-candidate panel at its executed random rate).
  • Naming. The sketch performs no naming audit; "syntax adherence" is already owned by the tool-call probe (toolcall.py:1; cli.py:374). The researcher's in-design audit (§3, item 8) resolves this and is carried into the resubmission specification.
  • Overlap. structured owns JSON adherence, fieldorder owns value contrasts within JSON, toolcall owns its call notation. The residue — demanded document syntax as a treatment — is real but thin relative to the slate's largest build; that is a value judgment the fresh review of §3 must make with the power question (§3, item 6a) in front of it, not a fatal in itself.
  • ID-divergence discipline is unstated in the sketch; the amended instrument states it (reported, not gated, with a rendering-anomaly exclusion) and the resubmission inherits that text.

docs.title: 2. Why the amended instrument is a resubmission, not an amendment
docs.text:
The negation round's BUILD verdict rested on a stated test: every defect was corrected inside the adjudication doc, by amendment to the same instrument — same population, same arms, same scorer, same joint-rule shape — whose population and arms were already frozen and executable before the round began. The payload round's NO-BUILD rested on the complementary test: where the amendments replace an undefined instrument with a different one, the result is a resubmission and "must be reviewed as a new design, not built as 'this probe with amendments'".

Measured against that test, the researcher's amended instrument changes: the endpoint pair (JSON–YAML → JSON–XML); the YAML arm's role (headline endpoint → descriptive only, behind a new schema-directed subset decoder); the paired population (10 → 13, under a new pairing derivation); the headline scorer (byte-exact/adherence conjunct → parsed answer-field value accuracy, with adherence demoted to descriptive rates); and the prompt's schema text (the shipped describe_schema → a neutral field list). The sketch's instrument was never frozen and executable in the first place — its YAML arm has no parser, its scorer is ambiguous between opposite-verdict readings (F1), and its population is self-contradictory (F1). This is the payload configuration, not the negation one.

The verdict is therefore NO-BUILD for this round. This is explicitly not a finding that the amended instrument is unsound: the verifier upheld it as-amended (subject to §5's corrections), it answers every fatal in §1 by construction rather than by disclosure alone, and measured against red-team B's nine resubmission conditions it satisfies 1, 2, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8 and the naming half of 9 in full. What it has never faced is a blind red team of its own: its novel machinery — the §3.4 coercion table, the neutral description renderer, the YAML subset grammar, the XML screen-and-decoder rules, the 13-spec pairing derivation — was claim-verified and math-verified in this round, not adversarially attacked. The program does not build its largest instrument on verification alone.

Express narrowing accepted by the coordinator (B's condition 3, decision half): the candidate's claim is narrowed to answer-field value invariance between the JSON and XML endpoints. Adherence is reported as per-arm descriptive rates with denominators and carries no decision rule in the resubmission. Any future design that reintroduces an adherence falsification claim must supply an unconditioned adherence decision rule with its own derived operating characteristics; it may not reattach adherence to the conditioned value rule.

docs.title: 3. Resubmission specification (NOT a build order)
docs.text:
A resubmission is reviewable as a NEW design only if it satisfies all of the following in full. Partial compliance is still NO-BUILD. The researcher's amended instrument (~/workspace/agents_out/answersyntax/research.md §1–§6, with the frozen items of its §11) is the resubmission candidate and is incorporated by reference, subject to items 1–5 below; the fresh review's job is to attack the frozen machinery itself (the coercion table, the neutral renderer, the subset grammar, the decoder rules, the pairing derivation), not to re-litigate the sketch, which is dead.

  1. Corrections applied before review. The XML length ratio is 1.49–2.35× across the 15 specs (§5 R-6), quoted only with its renderer named (R-11); the YAML decoder reading is the brief's poc2 reading — line grammar plus schema-directed coercion, with the plain-safe grammar binding the emitter only (R-8); tree line ranges as corrected in §5 (R-7, R-9, R-10).
  2. Ratifications recorded. (i) The document_kind rename (object → document) for the two new arms is accepted as a disclosed vocabulary adaptation; the JSON arm keeps the shipped set. (ii) The adherence narrowing of §2 is accepted expressly. (iii) The build must carry a bandit disposition for the ElementTree.fromstring call (it is flagged even behind the frozen <! screen): an in-code justification following the tree's # nosec precedent, or an equivalent restructure; the screen, not the parser, is the safety mechanism and must be described as such. (iv) The neutral field list is named identically in the design's prompt template and its worked examples.
  3. The voiding rule carries verbatim in substance: the resubmission's frozen items (arms and roles, prompt template and neutral description, population and pairing, renderers and decoders and coercion table, the three readouts with parsed answer-field accuracy as sole headline, the decision rule and its printed operating characteristics, the §6.3 vocabulary of the brief, counts and caps, digest-only records, the validator mirror) are frozen; deviation from any one voids the design and requires fresh review.
  4. Monday-morning utility (narrowed instrument): a team exposing a prompt-only extraction endpoint uses this, per candidate (checkpoint × chat template), to decide whether to standardise the endpoint's answer document on JSON or XML — and to see YAML subset adherence descriptively before considering it — instead of choosing JSON by habit. Where the verdict is insufficient or not_falsified, the honest deliverable is "this panel cannot distinguish them; choose on other grounds", and the design must say so in those words' substance.
  5. Name: --document-syntax (module documentsyntax.py, ref marker documentsyntax/<id>), per the brief's in-design naming audit — toolcall owns "syntax adherence" (toolcall.py:1, cli.py:374) and --answer-syntax collides with it and with numform's answer forms. The name ships only after the build cycle's USAGE naming audit (the rank-2 §8.46 precedent) regardless.
  6. What the fresh review must settle head-on (silence on any of these is NO-BUILD): a. Panel power. The amended panel (13 paired, adherence-gated) falsifies a true 0.90-vs-0.60 gap only ~14% of the time (researcher E3: 0.136; verifier's independent simulator: 0.1385) and a 0.90-vs-0.50 gap ~30%. The resubmission must either accept this with the operating characteristics printed beside every verdict, enlarge the entailed pool with generated specs (each carrying a recorded reader-entailment derivation, per the FIELDORDER_DESIGN F1 discipline), or add replicated generations per (spec, arm) — and argue the choice against the §3.4 decision, not default to it. b. The YAML descriptive arm's cost. It is a third decoder plus a full validator mirror, bought for a subset-adherence rate that must be labelled "YAML (frozen block subset)" wherever it appears and can never be quoted as YAML adherence generally. Keep it, or cut v1 to the two headline endpoints; either is reviewable. c. Family-wise expectation. Printed beside the per-candidate verdicts: at the amended panel's executed random-labeller rate (0.0151), a full 24-candidate panel expects ≈0.36 false falsifications, P(≥1) ≈ 0.31. No pooling of discordance across candidates, ever.
  7. Counts (as frozen in the brief): 15 specs × 3 arms × 24 candidates = 1,080 generations maximum (720 on headline endpoints); records are digests and decoder commitments only; the diff validator re-implements — never imports — the neutral renderer, all renderers, all decoders, and the coercion table, and recomputes every aggregate.
  8. Sources are limited to §6 of this doc, with their fencing. No "first" is claimed anywhere; the contribution, if the resubmission is ever built, is the combination stated in the brief's §7.

docs.title: 4. Adjudication evidence (coordinator's own execution)
docs.text:
All snippets read-only; no suite was run. Scripts in /tmp/asyn/ during the round.

docs.text:
All five were resolved against their primary sources this round by the researcher and independently by the verifier (abstract level, title and authors confirmed; fencing must travel with each):

docs.title: 7. What a build cycle must NOT do on the basis of this doc
docs.text:
• Do not build the circulated sketch, any YAML headline endpoint, or the transplanted field-order decision rule.
  • Do not build the amended instrument on this doc's authority: it enters only through a fresh design review (blind red-team pair + verifier) of a resubmission satisfying §3 in full, and only on a BUILD verdict from that review.
  • Do not reintroduce an adherence falsification claim without its own unconditioned decision rule and derived operating characteristics (§2).
  • Do not carry field-order's "~15% power" figure, the removed figures of §5, or any arm-length figure without its renderer named, into any doc or help text.
  • Do not ship the flag under --answer-syntax; the resubmission's name is --document-syntax, and even it ships only after the build cycle's USAGE naming audit.

docs.title: Real batch path for the local backend — design
docs.text:
Cycle 192 (wave-8 rank 4). An operator who will serve the checkpoint batched learns whether the lab's solo greedy verdicts survive the lab's own batched execution token-for-token — the audit that since cycle 153 could only answer batch_unsupported on the real backend — before trusting a winner measured one request at a time.

This is a capability cycle, not a new probe. Cycle 153 built the audit (model_protocol_lab/batchinv.py, experiments.batch_stage, run --batch-invariance) around an optional backend contract and pre-registered as its claim 1 that no backend in the tree exposes a batch path. This cycle builds the path — LocalHFBackend.generate_batch — and supersedes claim 1 by construction. The audit, its verdict vocabulary (batch_invariant / batch_variant / unavailable), and its diff section do not change; the stage changes in exactly the ways §"Stage amendments" lists, each forced by a red-team finding.

Design history: v1 froze two premises the red teams disproved. Red-team A returned DO NOT BUILD AS SPECIFIED (nine amendments); red-team B tried to disprove A and confirmed every finding (two were understated), rejected the coordinator's chunking adjudication as specified (unrecorded chunk composition would manufacture invariance for the longest prompts), and corrected the coordinator's validation-precedence candidate in one place. This v2 is the adjudicated contract: A's amendments 1–9 with amendment 1 implemented as B's C1-with-changes, amendment 8 as B's C3-with-changes, and amendment 2 (the bound) resolved as an honest byte-derived refusal with a distinct stage detail — the resolution B's closing asymmetry argues for and this repo's batch_unsupported precedent embodies: a silent weaker measurement is worse than an honest refusal. Briefs: ~/workspace/agents_out/wave8/ (cycle192_redteam_a.md, cycle192_redteam_b.md).

docs.title: What supersedes what, exactly
docs.text:
• batchinv.py's pre-registered claim 1 ("No backend in the current tree exposes a batch path, so on the real local backend the stage records batch_unsupported") becomes false the moment generate_batch lands. The claim text is rewritten in the same change to record the history: true through cycle 191, superseded at cycle 192 by the real path on LocalHFBackend. Claims 2 and 3 stand unchanged.
  • Backends without the method — including the tree's own wrapper backends (TruncatedPromptBackend, TokenHealingBackend), which transform the token stream in their solo generate — still record batch_unsupported. The wrappers deliberately do not forward the inner backend's batch path: their solo contract rewrites inputs the batch path would bypass, so inheriting it would compare two different streams and call the difference "batch variance". (Verified at source: no __getattr__ exists anywhere in the package, so the stage's getattr probe on a wrapper finds nothing.)
  • The backend fingerprint does NOT gain a batch-capability field. The fingerprint already binds code and policy (library versions, adapter and generation-policy strings) — deliberately: it binds everything that can change the solo recorded observations, and batch capability cannot change a single solo token. Changing it would make every pre-192 artifact unreplayable under verify --determinism (fingerprint-gated, solo-only, search-observations-only) for zero measurement gain. The batch_invariance payload itself records availability.

docs.title: The implementation contract
docs.text:
LocalHFBackend.generate_batch(prompts, *, max_new_tokens, seed, cancel) implements the signature batchinv.py already documents:

  • Input: a tuple of prompt id-tuples. Returns a tuple of continuation-only id-tuples, one per prompt, in input order, each of length exactly max_new_tokens.
  • Decoding mirrors the solo generate exactly in every respect that is not batching itself: fp32 full-prefix recompute (use_cache=False), greedy argmax of the last-position logits, no EOS or boundary stopping, the same model call kwargs plus attention_mask (the real mask, where solo passes all-ones) and position_ids (below — solo passes none because an unpadded row's implicit positions are already correct), under the backend lock, in inference mode. The seed is validated and, as in solo greedy, does not influence selection. All tensors — input, mask, position ids, appended columns — are built with device=self._device and long dtype, matching solo. The method uses self._torch exactly like generate / forward_logits and adds no imports: backends.py imports torch only under TYPE_CHECKING and in __init__, which is what keeps the package importable without the hf extra (the cycle-105 audit guards that regime), and the stage's getattr probe must find the attribute without importing anything.
  • Batching mechanics: prompts are left-padded to the batch's longest prompt with pad id 0. The attention mask is 0 on pads and 1 on real and generated positions. Position ids are recomputed from the current mask at every step (mask.cumsum(-1) - 1, clamped at 0), including steps after generated columns are appended, so every row's real tokens sit at the same positions they occupy solo. The rationale is architecture-scoped: for learned-absolute- position models (GPT-2) omitting position ids demonstrably diverges on padded rows; for RoPE models (Llama) a uniform pad shift preserves relative positions and the omission happened to be harmless in testing — the ids are passed uniformly for both, which was exact on both. Each generation step runs ONE forward over the whole padded batch and takes the per-row argmax at the last column (left padding puts every row's frontier there). The chosen token column and a 1-column of mask are appended; repeat for exactly max_new_tokens steps.
  • Unpadding is by recorded lengths only: a row's returned ids are exactly the max_new_tokens tokens its own argmax produced, collected per row during the loop. Nothing is sliced out of the padded tensor and nothing is scanned for a pad id — a pad id is a legitimate token id (the pad value used is 0, which real prompts may contain), so any scan-based unpadding would be a bug by construction. Per-step bookkeeping extracts plain Python ints per row and drops the step's result/logits references before the next step (solo's result = logits = None pattern): a retained logits[:, -1, :] view would keep every step's full (rows, L, vocab) tensor alive for the whole call.
  • Finite check: each step's last-position logits block must have shape [rows, vocab] and be all-finite, mirroring the solo per-step check; any violation fails the whole batch (below), never a per-row salvage — a partial batch result would be unattributable in the audit.
  • Lock and cancel mirror solo generate's discipline: the lock is acquired by polling (acquire(timeout=0.05)) in a loop that re-checks cancel; cancel is checked before acquisition, after acquisition, before each forward, and after each forward before committing the step's tokens. The batch holds the lock for its whole run, as a solo generation holds it for its own; concurrent callers wait with their own polling-cancel, and the CLI run path is sequential anyway. Deliberate raises never sit inside the inference try: cancel and failure detected mid-inference are carried out as flags and raised after it, because the tree's heal_input_ids re-raise guard cannot distinguish the method's own codes from torch RuntimeErrors raised by tensor ops in the same try — inside the try, every exception converts to the failure flag, so nothing raw can leak and the cancelled code is never eaten by the conversion to local_batch_failed.

docs.title: Invariants
docs.text:
• I1 (shape, falsifiable). For valid inputs the result is a tuple of len(prompts) tuples, each exactly max_new_tokens long, each id an int (not bool) with 0 <= id < vocab_size.
  • I2 (no pad leakage — construction invariant). Returned ids come only from per-row argmax bookkeeping; the pad value never enters a returned tuple as padding. This is not output-falsifiable (a genuinely generated pad id is indistinguishable), so it is verified by construction and review; its observable consequence — prompts containing id 0 behave exactly as solo — is pinned by I4's cases.
  • I3 (real batching, anti-theater, falsifiable). Every generation step issues exactly one model forward whose batch dimension equals the number of prompts. The pin is the tree's white-box mechanism (cycle-81 precedent): patch.object(backend._model, "forward", wrapper) records the full shape sequence — max_new_tokens forwards, every call's input_ids.shape == (rows, longest + step). A backend-level wrapper cannot observe forwards and proves nothing. Secretly looping solo calls is the one forbidden implementation.
  • I4 (equivalence is measured, not assumed). Property tests pin, on the tree's tiny GPT-2 checkpoint: batched == solo token-exactly at batch sizes {1, 2, 3, 5} over seeded prompt sets of mixed lengths (including prompts containing token id 0), one 32-row case (the real caller batches up to 100 rows; the pin's composition should not stop at toy sizes), and permutation invariance (the same prompt with different companions and at different positions returns identical ids). Pre-build prototypes by the coordinator and both red teams confirmed these properties on tiny GPT-2 and tiny Llama (0 divergences across randomized, near-tie, near-context, and 100-row sets). On any real checkpoint where they fail, the audit reports batch_variant with first-divergence positions: divergence is a finding, not a defect to tune away. Nothing in this cycle adds batch-invariant kernels or any numeric correction.
  • I5 (fixed vocabulary, falsifiable). Every failure is a ValueError or RuntimeError carrying one fixed code from the sets below. New RuntimeError("local_*") codes are added to cli.py's _KNOWN_LOCAL_FAILURE_CODES in the same change and raised in the literal raise RuntimeError("local_batch_…") form the cycle-132 AST pin scans for (a test pins the sets equal).
  • I6 (cancel means no result, falsifiable). If the cancel event is set before or during the batch, the method raises RuntimeError("local_batch_cancelled"). It never returns partial rows: the audit compares against complete solo runs, so partial rows would manufacture phantom divergences — the exact failure the stage's contract forbids. (The stage passes a fresh event, so this is unreachable inside the audit; it binds direct callers.)

docs.title: Failure vocabulary and precedence
docs.text:
Validation is type()-strict throughout, mirroring solo (type(x) is int for scalars — True is not a valid seed or cap; type(prompts) is tuple, per-prompt tuples checked by the same _ids_valid solo uses; isinstance(cancel, Event)). The precedence order is pinned (B's C3-with- changes — solo's order, with the batch-specific slots named):

  1. prompts container type, then per-prompt ids → ValueError("invalid_input_ids"). Deliberate precedent choice: generate_batch is a raising method, so it uses the raising methods' code (forward_logits, heal_input_ids), not solo generate's returned invalid_or_empty_input.
  2. max_new_tokens not an int or outside 1..4096 → ValueError("invalid_output_cap").
  3. seed not an int or outside [0, 2**64) → ValueError("invalid_seed").
  4. cancel not a threading.Event → ValueError("invalid_cancellation_event").
  5. cancel already set → RuntimeError( "local_batch_cancelled") (mirrors solo, which reports cancellation before the context check).
  6. Any prompt with len(prompt) + max_new_tokens over the backend's context limit → ValueError("context_limit_exceeded").
  7. _ready() — an uninitialized backend raises RuntimeError("local_backend_not_initialized"), as in every sibling method.
  8. Empty prompt tuple → return (). The shortcut sits here, after all validation: an empty call returns () exactly when a valid one-prompt call would have proceeded, and scalar/cancel violations are never masked by emptiness. (batch_stage never calls it empty.)
  9. Size bound (below) → ValueError("batch_size_exceeded").
  10. Lock polling, then the step loop. Runtime failures — the model forward raising, non-finite or mis-shaped logits, any other inference error — raise RuntimeError("local_batch_failed") from None; cancel observed at any check point raises local_batch_cancelled instead.

docs.title: The size bound (byte-derived refusal)
docs.text:
The v1 position-count bound is deleted. It refused ordinary legal runs (a 100-fixture split with paragraph-length prompts at default settings) while permitting multi-GB single tensors, because positions do not proxy bytes — the dominant transient, HF's full-sequence logits, scales with the vocabulary. v2 refuses on an estimated peak, computed from the backend's own quantities:

L       = longest_prompt + max_new_tokens   (final padded length)
peak    = 4 * rows * L * vocab_size          (full-sequence fp32 logits)
        + 2 * (4 * rows * heads * L^2)       (eager attention scores:
                                              matmul output and softmax
                                              output co-live, one layer)
        + 4 * rows * L^2                     (the (rows,1,L,L) fp32
                                              additive mask, held for
                                              the whole forward)

with vocab_size the backend's _vocab_size (the bound generate validates against, not raw config.vocab_size) and heads the loaded config's query-head count (num_attention_heads; n_head on GPT-2 configs). If peak > _BATCH_FORWARD_BYTE_BUDGET (2^33 bytes, 8 GiB), the call raises ValueError("batch_size_exceeded") before any forward runs.

The budget's role is stated plainly: it is a conservative ceiling on one forward's estimated transient peak, set just above the default caller scale (a 100-fixture split of paragraph-length prompts on a GPT-2-vocabulary model estimates ≈ 7.8 GB by this formula), so that an audit call degrades to a labelled refusal instead of an OOM kill — which, being a process kill rather than a Python exception, would defeat the probe's never-fail-the-run contract. It is not a memory guarantee: weights are already resident, allocator behaviour varies, and no byte budget consulted from Python can promise a machine will hold a tensor. The recorded limitation, not hidden: at large-vocab × long-context × full-split scale the audit records batch_size_exceeded (surfaced distinctly — see the stage amendments) and the operator's levers are --max-new-tokens and the fixture count. Chunked execution with recorded composition is the known future remedy if that limitation bites in practice; it is explicitly deferred, not silently absorbed — unrecorded chunking was rejected in this cycle's red-team round because singleton chunks manufacture invariance for exactly the longest prompts while diluting the divergence rate.

docs.title: Stage amendments (experiments.batch_stage)
docs.text:
Forced by F1 (the stage fed the batch path every prompt, including solo-ineligible ones, so one long fixture collapsed the whole audit to batch_failed — the exact per-prompt degradation the stage exists to avoid):

  1. generate_batch is called with only the solo-evaluable prompts, in the stage's sorted order; the arity/contract check and the zip use the evaluable id list in the same edit. (Strengthening fact: the evaluable subset provably cannot trip the backend's caller-contract ValueErrors — solo success implies the context and vocab checks passed, and the stage pre-validates seed and cap — so residual batch failure from the stage path is runtime failure or the size refusal, each with its own honest detail.)
  2. When no prompt is evaluable the call is skipped: the stage returns an available payload with n_evaluable == 0 and verdict "unavailable", every prompt carrying its solo_failed entry. (Today that case surfaces as batch_failed; the change is owned here and pinned by a test.)
  3. A ValueError("batch_size_exceeded") from the batch path maps to {"available": False, "detail": "batch_size_exceeded"} (new batchinv constant BATCH_SIZE_EXCEEDED), never plain batch_failed. The diff validator does not validate unavailable payloads' detail strings and tolerates this addition; no other detail vocabulary changes.
  4. The stage docstring's "runs all prompts together" is amended: the batch path runs the solo-evaluable prompts together.

docs.title: Edges pinned by tests
docs.text:
• batch sizes {1, 2, 3, 5} vs solo, mixed prompt lengths, prompts containing id 0 and the pad value as real content; one 32-row case; permutation invariance
  • forward counting/shapes (I3) via the model-forward patch, full (rows, longest + step) sequence
  • cancel set before the call; cancel set mid-batch (a forward wrapper sets it during the first forward) — both raise local_batch_cancelled, no partial result; cancel set while waiting on a held lock (polling acquire)
  • every ValueError code in the precedence list, including multi-violation cases that pin the order (bool seed/cap; bad ids + bad cap → ids win; pre-set cancel + over-context prompt → cancelled wins, mirroring solo)
  • empty batch returns () on a ready backend; empty batch with a bad cap raises invalid_output_cap; empty batch on an unready backend raises local_backend_not_initialized
  • the size bound just under and just over the line (small config: scaled-down budget via the module constant's seam — the test computes a prompt set whose estimate crosses 2^33 only if the formula is honest; a cheaper equivalent pins the estimate arithmetic against the formula on the tiny config and the raise at a patched budget)
  • non-finite logits (hostile forward wrapper) → local_batch_failed; a raising forward → local_batch_failed; the flag-carrying conversion (§"Lock and cancel": cancellation detected inside the inference try surfaces as local_batch_cancelled, never eaten by the conversion to local_batch_failed)
  • batch_stage end-to-end on the real backend: available payload, verdict batch_invariant; the CLI probe (_run_batch_probe) recording the available payload instead of batch_unsupported; a mixed stage case (one over-context prompt among good ones) degrading per-prompt with the audit still available (the F1 regression test); the all-solo-fail case returning the pinned available/unavailable payload; a size-refusing stub backend mapping to the batch_size_exceeded detail
  • a deliberately batch-variant stub through the real stage wiring (already pinned at cycle 153; re-verified, not re-built)

docs.title: Non-goals
docs.text:
• No KV cache, no continuous batching, no padding-free packing, no batch-invariant kernels, no chunking in this cycle, no new dependency (stdlib + the existing torch/transformers only).
  • No new module, CLI flag, diff section, or report section: the mypy source-file pin (55) and both diff oracles are untouched. The stage payload gains no fields. README/ VALIDATION counts move only by the new test count, measured.
  • No change to solo generate, forward_logits, or the diff code, except: the batchinv.py claim-1 text, the stage amendments above, and the doc/help wording that asserts the local backend is batch-less — batchinv.py claim 1, docs/USAGE.md §8.21's honesty note, and README.md's Capabilities bullet ("the local backend exposes no batch path…"). The CLI flag help and probe docstrings are conditional ("when one exists") and stay true unchanged — checked, not assumed.
  • Determinism scope, stated to prevent a wrong assumption: verify --determinism replays solo search observations only; the batch payload is covered by no determinism certificate, before or after this cycle.

docs.title: Monday-morning utility
docs.text: An operator about to serve a checkpoint batched runs model-protocol-lab run --batch-invariance and learns — from the lab's own real batched execution, not a stub — whether the winner it measured solo survives batching token-for-token, before trusting that winner in production.

docs.title: Round summary (coordinator #46, design round only — nothing built)
docs.text:
Wave-11 slate rank 5, the last wave-11 item: question bundling (tentatively run --bundle). The candidate sketch (~/workspace/agents_out/wave11/slate_candidates.md Candidate 5): generated cases of K=3 independent questions (fact recall + small arithmetic, disjoint answer spaces); a bundled arm (all K in one user turn, frozen convention "reply with one line per question, 1: <answer>", one generation, per-question verdicts parsed from the response) against a split arm (three scripted turn pairs with frozen assistant replies, the scored question rotated through all three positions); falsified by any (position, candidate) discordant pair; worst case 20 cases × (1 + 3) arms × 24 candidates = 1,920 generations (arithmetic verified correct by all lanes).

  • Tree at main a6705d1b9607 (cycle 213 closed green, 8,442 tests, precise coverage 95.3455%). This round was READ-ONLY except for this doc and the briefs; no suite was run, no push was made, no tag was cut or discussed.
  • Specialists (blind to each other): researcher (~/workspace/agents_out/bundle/research.md), red-team A (redteam_a.md), red-team B (redteam_b.md), verifier/claims auditor (verifier.md). All four briefs landed; the verifier resolved every externally checkable claim against primary sources, re-ran every surviving PoC, and recomputed all decision math with independent code; the coordinator re-executed the load-bearing claims itself (§4). Fabrication sweep: clean — a sixth consecutive round. No invented symbol, no fabricated citation, and no unreproduced load-bearing number in any brief; the failures found were two non-load-bearing line drifts in red-team B (≤ a few lines, substance intact), handled in §5.
  • Convergence: unanimous NO-BUILD — researcher, both blind red teams, and the verifier each reached it independently for the sketch as specified, fatal by fatal, by execution. The two red teams, working blind, converged on the same core defects (scorer inversion, unfrozen parser, cap censoring ordered by slot, the noise-firing falsifier) with independently executed numbers that agree. The researcher additionally specifies a complete redesigned instrument (run --multi-question, §3) and recommends it as a resubmission candidate; the verifier reproduced its decision math exactly and ruled it a resubmission, not an amendment, under this program's own test, and the researcher himself classifies it the same way. The coordinator concurs: the verdict is NO-BUILD — for the sketch, and as a build order for the redesigned instrument in this round. §3 records the resubmission specification in summary, including the seven points the fresh review must settle head-on.

docs.title: 1. Why NO-BUILD: the fatal defects of the candidate as specified
docs.text: Each defect below is individually blocking and was established by execution (attribution: R = researcher, A = red-team A, B = red-team B, V = verifier, C = coordinator).

docs.title: F1 — The scorer cannot emit the headline: one byte-exact span per fixture, and the arms' reply contracts are mutually unsatisfiable
docs.text: core.evaluate emits exactly one verdict per fixture: core.py:797 exact_match = status == "completed" and answer == case.expected, where answer is the whole decoded pre-boundary span (core.py:939 answer_ids = output_ids if cut is None else output_ids[:cut]; core.py:966 answer = decoded). There is no per-question verdict anywhere in the tree's scoring path. Executed through the real evaluate with stub backends (R poc1, A poc1, B poc1, V re-ran; C re-ran, §4): a perfectly correct, fully compliant bundled reply (1: Paris\n2: 42\n3: blue) scores False against every per-question expected string and against newline-joined bare answers; it scores True only against the whole bundled string as expected — which collapses the headline to one all-or-nothing verdict in which a 2-of-3-correct bundle and an all-wrong bundle are the same observation, an omission, an answer swap, and all-wrong are indistinguishable, and one trailing "." fails a fully correct bundle. Against the whole-string expected, 8 of 9 semantically identical formatting variants (no labels, 1. separators, a preamble, reordered labelled lines, a trailing period) fail — the verdict is formatting luck. And the inversion is verbatim DIRECTIVE F1: a disobedient model that outputs only the first answer (Paris) passes the Q1 fixture where the compliant bundled model fails. The split arm has the same trap in mirror image: under the shared convention its compliant reply 1: amber fails a bare-answer expected and passes a labelled one, while its bare reply does the reverse — whichever expected string is chosen, one of two compliant behaviours fails. The sketch never chooses, because it cannot: the two arms demand different reply contracts under one scorer.

docs.title: F2 — The line grammar is unfrozen, honest parsers disagree on the same responses, and parse failure has no honest home
docs.text: The sketch's per-question readout rests entirely on a "frozen line grammar" that is never frozen: it states no label syntax, no strip policy, no duplicate/missing-line rule, no rule for answers containing :. Executed (A poc2, B poc3, V re-ran): two honest parsers — positional vs by-label — return different verdict vectors on the same responses (reordered lines: [F,F,T] vs [T,T,T]; a preamble: [F,F,F] vs [T,T,T]). A charitable strict line parser passes only 2 of 10 semantically perfect bundled variants (prose preface or trailing prose, bold labels, blank lines, glued lines, unnumbered lines, 1) labels, 0-based labels all lose slots wholesale); one missing line loses every slot under positional parsing, and first-wins vs last-wins duplicate handling disagrees on self-correcting responses. The sketch specifies no parse-failure outcome code: folding parse failures into "wrong" makes the headline a formatting measure, and excluding them is treatment-selected attrition (the bundled arm produces the parse failures) — answer-syntax F2 through the parser door. The tree's precedent (structured's parse-vs-schema split, structured.py:68 OUTCOMES) exists precisely because this pooling is dishonest, and the sketch adopts none of it.

docs.title: F3 — Digest-only records cannot carry per-slot verdicts (instruction-distance F2 verbatim)
docs.text: Every sibling generated probe's records carry digests only (negation.py:57: "Records carry digests only"; the verdict identity is verdict == (answer_digest == sha256(expected)) and boundary_found, recomputed by the diff validator). Executed (A poc, B, C §4): ten distinct bundled texts — all-correct, Q1-wrong, Q2-wrong, a swap, an omission, a parse failure — collapse to the same record class under a whole-answer digest (the digest differs, but nothing in it says which slot failed, or whether anything parsed). Per-slot verdicts, swap flags, and parse decompositions are underivable from the records the lab keeps, and therefore unrecomputable by the diff validator. The sketch specifies none of the three tree escapes: a numform-style digest-bound answer text (the one sanctioned exception, cycle 190), density-style carried primitives (e.g. an ordered word-hash list), or stage-attested booleans (the forgery surface the digest discipline exists to remove). A probe whose headline cannot be recomputed from its own records is not buildable in this tree.

docs.title: F4 — There is no decision rule: the any-discordant-pair falsifier fires on noise, and the panel's cells are clustered
docs.text: The sketch's falsifier is "any (position, candidate) discordant pair" over 20 × 3 × 24 = 1,440 pairs, with no floor, no direction, no test. Executed (R, A, B, V; C independently, §4): P(any discordance in the panel) = 0.9439 at per-arm jitter ε = 0.001 and 1.0000 at ε ≥ 0.005 (analytic, Monte-Carlo confirmed by three lanes). The one apparent number disagreement of the round — the researcher's 0.763 at "ε = 0.001" — is a parametrisation difference, settled by the verifier and re-derived by the coordinator: 0.763 is P(any) when 0.001 is the per-pair discordance probability (1 − 0.999^1440 = 0.7632 exactly); 0.9439 is the same quantity when 0.001 is the per-arm flip probability. Both are correct under their stated nulls; the fatal is unaffected (the rule fires with probability 1.000 by ε = 0.005 under both). A random labeller reaches ≥6 discordant of 60 per candidate with probability 1.000000, so no borrowed floor rescues it either. Worse, the panel's bundled cells are clustered by construction: the three bundled slot verdicts share one generation, so one boundary miss, truncation, or parse event flips all three together (executed, A: a boundary miss fails all 3 bundled slots vs 1 split slot) — any pair-counting repair that treats the 1,440 pairs as independent is mis-calibrated on this instrument specifically.

docs.title: F5 — Cap censoring is ordered by slot, and the budget is asymmetric by construction
docs.text: The run's default cap is 64 new tokens (cli.py:198). The bundled answer is K lines; the split answer is one. Executed (A, B, R poc3; C §4): a perfect model whose bundled reply needs 70 tokens records completed, truncated mid-slot-3, boundary missed, retained as an ordinary failure — while all three split replies pass. Survival by slot at caps 50/64 is [T,T,F]: the cap alone manufactures the sketch's advertised headline, "position 3 degrades first", on a model with no bundling deficit at all. The asymmetry is constitutive, not a tuning detail: the split arm receives K × 64 tokens of budget across its generations against the bundled arm's 64. Raising the bundled cap breaks comparability with the split arm; keeping it censors the readout's own axis. The sketch has no liveness rule (a truncated cell removing its whole case, attrition printed) of the kind density's _live discipline provides.

docs.title: F6 — Neither arm is what the claim names: the contrast bundles at least six variables, and "position" is two different variables in the two arms
docs.text: Executed renders (A, B; chatml bundled 205 chars / 1 message vs split-Q3 354 chars / 5 messages): the split arm's unscored questions are never answered by the model at all — its history is frozen assistant text the sketch never specifies. Both readings of that text are already owned or confounded: answers as history = fewshot demonstrations; Noted. = multiturn's scripted arm verbatim (multiturn.py:85 SCRIPTED_REPLY). The production alternative the utility names — asking separately, i.e. independent single-turn calls — does not exist in the sketch. What the contrast actually varies, simultaneously: turn count, scripted history presence and content, convention load (one instruction governing K lines vs one line, repeated), prompt length (whose sign reverses by position: the bundled prompt is longer than split-Q1's and shorter than split-Q3's), generation-cap exposure (F5), scoring machinery (parser vs byte-exact, F1/F2), and autoregressive exposure to the model's own earlier answers (the contamination the sketch wants to measure is present only in one arm — it is part of the treatment bundle, not separable from it). No separating control can even be stated: a length-matched control would need a different filler dose per position, and length-padding is itself the shipped distraction treatment. A discordance from this contrast is attributable to "bundling" only as a named bundle of all of the above — and the sketch's claim is written as a single-cause packaging claim. Separately, "position" pools two variables: in the bundled arm a slot is a fixed question identity/type (no within-bundle permutation is specified, so slot ≡ item), while in the split arm position is history depth by renderer construction (scored positions 1/2/3 = 1/3/5 messages). A by-position readout compares list position against turn depth and calls both "position".

docs.title: F7 — The disjointness the swap readout needs fails by chance, and when it fails the failure is invisible
docs.text: The sketch's contamination mitigation is disjoint answer spaces, "planted so a swapped answer is detectable as a swap". Executed (B; C spot-checked the arithmetic, §4): two small arithmetic answers in one case coincide with probability ≈ 0.07, and at least one collision among three with probability ≈ 0.19–0.21 — under the natural operand distributions, coincidence is a routine event, not an edge case. When two expected answers are equal, a swap is byte-identical to a perfect response: contamination becomes invisible in exactly the cells where it occurred. The sketch specifies no generator screen (contrast multiturn's built-in redraw discipline), and adding one post hoc selects the population (cases whose answers happen to collide are systematically easier/harder — the screen is a population choice, not a hygiene step). Without enforced-by-construction distinctness, the swap decomposition the sketch promises cannot be delivered; with it, the population is no longer the sketch's.

docs.title: F8 — The selection headline is manufactured by conjunction, and forbidden on this population besides
docs.text: The utility promises whether "the template they selected survives bundling". Executed arithmetic (A, B; C re-derived, §4): if a case passes bundled only when all 3 slots pass, then at identical per-question accuracy p in both arms the case-level gap is p − p³ = 0.171 at p = 0.9, 0.288 at p = 0.8, 0.357 at p = 0.7 — a large "bundling effect" manufactured by the conjunction alone, with zero treatment effect. If instead no case-level aggregation is defined, there is no selection readout at all: the tree's selection rule consumes per-fixture verdicts, and a bundled fixture has three. And the deeper bar is already settled in-tree: the numform settlement forbids a winner/selection readout on a generated population (experiments.py:11049 pattern; negation v1 adopted the same bar) — the sketch's population is generated, so its headline readout is one the program has already ruled out for exactly this population type.

docs.title: F9 — The population cannot deliver the utility: one K, the wrong K, and "recall" that is not generatable
docs.text: The utility sentence asks for "the bundle size at which per-question verdicts start moving" for a front-end bundling five questions. The instrument has exactly one K, and it is 3. One point is not a size readout: no curve, no threshold, no "at which" (prune-sweep F5's permutation/shape point in miniature). The population is also undefined where it matters: fact-recall questions with known answers are not seed-generatable and validator-regenerable the way this tree's generated probes require — a fact the model is asked to recall must come from a frozen external set (a different instrument, with provenance obligations) or be planted in the prompt, in which case the task is extraction, not recall, and the claim must be re-scoped to say so. The sketch says neither. Finally, with no family × slot rotation, slot and question family are perfectly collinear (F6), so even the descriptive by-position readout the sketch falls back on pools item difficulty into "position".

docs.title: F10 — The name is taken: bundle is the sealed-bundle term of art (blocking rename, independently of F1–F9)
docs.text: Executed naming audit (R §5, A, B, V): pack.py:1 "Sealed result bundles (model-protocol-lab pack / verify --bundle)", format id mpl-bundle/1 (pack.py:49), a live verify --bundle <path> flag (verify.py:645-675, dispatch to pack.run_verify_bundle), and USAGE §13.1 (docs/USAGE.md:3320, "Sealing a result (pack, verify --bundle)"). "Bundle" in this tree already names one thing, in adjacent subcommands, with a file format attached. A run --bundle flag is free only as an argparse string; under the tree's USAGE naming discipline (one word, one meaning, the same terms in USAGE/FAQ/CLI help — repo AGENTS.md) it fails the audit outright. Any future instrument in this space ships under a different name (the resubmission proposes run --multi-question, §3).

docs.title: Non-fatal, adjudicated
docs.text:
• Generation-count arithmetic: the sketch's 1,920 worst case is correct (all lanes).
  • Duplication, precisely: no arm is byte-identical to a shipped probe's arm (checked by render comparison, not asserted). The boundary is exact per neighbour — placement owns question serial position within one turn; multiturn owns the full-vs-sharded-vs-scripted turn-packaging contrast (the sketch's split arm is multiturn's scripted construction); density owns simultaneous-demand load and per-serial-position fall under a byte-exact single-task scorer; needle owns fact position in filler; structured owns multi-part response parsing on user fixtures. The only element no shipped probe owns — K per-question verdicts from one generation — is exactly the element F1–F3 show the tree cannot currently score or record. The candidate is not a duplicate; it is a request for the one readout the record discipline forbids as specified.
  • External citation: Cheng, Kasai & Yu, batch prompting, arXiv:2301.08721 — verified at the primary source by the verifier (the sketch's citation is accurate, and fenced: API models, plain/few-shot formats, per-sample accuracy, no template-family crossing). It supports the phenomenon's existence; it does not support this instrument.

docs.title: 2. Amendment or resubmission
docs.text: Under the program's standing test (negation = amendment: same population, arms, scorer, and rule shape, all already frozen and executable; payload / answer-syntax / directive / instruction-language / instruction-distance / history-frame / prune-sweep = resubmission when those change), the researcher's redesign changes every load-bearing element: population, arms, scorer, decision rule, headline, and name (§3). The sketch was never executable as a measurement — its split arm has no specified replies (F6), its scorer cannot emit its readout (F1), its records cannot carry its readout (F3), and its falsifier is a noise printer (F4). This is the payload configuration, not the negation one. The redesigned instrument is recorded in §3 as a resubmission candidate. It is not a build order; no build cycle may act on it without a fresh blind design review.

docs.title: 3. The resubmission candidate (summary; full specification in the researcher brief §3)
docs.text:
run --multi-question (module multiquestion.py), specified in full in ~/workspace/agents_out/bundle/research.md §3:

  • Population: generated, stage-local panels at K=3 and K=5, 24 cases each; sub-questions are planted-fact extraction (placement/density construction, named extraction, never "recall") and small arithmetic, all with single-normalized-word expected answers; family × slot rotation; generator screens enforce pairwise-distinct expected answers within a case (redraw discipline), so swap detection is a construction property.
  • Arms: bundled (one turn, K numbered questions) vs split_j (one turn, only question j, renumbered to 1, no history anywhere) — the production "asking separately" the utility names. Length difference disclosed as constitutive of packaging, printed per case, never gated; the claim is scoped to the packaging bundle, not a single cause.
  • Scorer: one total, marker-aligned parser over density's carried ordered word-hash list, symmetric across arms; per-slot outcomes pass / wrong_value (with swap flag) / parse_failed (decomposed missing_marker / extra_words); no answer text carried — the digest-compatible design is density's, so the numform exception is not invoked. Composite byte-exact printed as sensitivity only. Liveness: a case enters the headline only if the bundled cell and all split cells completed with boundary found; attrition printed.
  • Decision rule (derived, never borrowed): per candidate per panel, case-aggregated discordance (slots within a case share one generation — clustering handled by construction); D ≥ 6 discordant cases, F > P, and exact sign test p ≤ 0.05 → multiquestion_drop_observed; D < 6 → insufficient; else below_threshold. Researcher's 20k-trial Monte Carlo (verifier reproduced the full table exactly): fire 0.017 random / 0.012 competent-null / ≤ 0.014 clustered at K=3; power 0.979 at a 25% drop (K=3), 0.999 (K=5). Family-wise expectation printed: 48 decisions, ≈ 0.81 false labels expected under the random null, P(≥1) ≈ 0.56.
  • Counts: 240 generations per candidate; legal maximum 5,760; 1,152 ground records; house 12 MiB cap.
  • Vocabulary: frozen house pattern only — decisions {insufficient, below_threshold, multiquestion_drop_observed}, whole-stage fail-closed multiquestion_unavailable; no invented verdict words (verifier checked the set against the negation/density pattern).
  • No selection readout (numform settlement honoured).

The fresh review must settle head-on (silence = NO-BUILD): (a) split renumbering (to-1 vs keep-slot-number — different treatments); (b) the decision-rule operating characteristics re-run under a case-clustered drop model and at real completed-case counts after attrition; (c) parse-failure in the headline (counted as not-pass with decomposition printed, vs conditioning on parse-ok cells — the latter is outcome-dependent conditioning and needs its own rule); (d) K=5 cost (5,760 legal-maximum generations) vs a K=3-only probe with honestly narrowed utility; (e) word-rule leniency (case-folding, punctuation-insensitive) as the headline scorer, with byte-exact demoted to sensitivity — or the reverse, with the rule re-derived; (f) extraction-not-recall scoping (a genuine-recall population is a different instrument and may not be smuggled in as an arm); and (g) the verifier's addition: arithmetic sums landing in {1..5} are not screened from the parser's marker words in §3.1 as written and would break the §3.3 grammar — the screen set must be closed before any build.

docs.title: 4. Coordinator re-execution (independent, this session)
docs.text:
• Scorer (F1): stub backend through the real core.evaluate — a fully compliant bundled reply scores False against per-question expected amber and against 1: amber, True only against the whole three-line string; a split reply 1: amber scores False against expected amber and True against 1: amber, with the bare reply exactly reversed. Both arms cannot be satisfied under one expected-string choice.
  • Records (F3): whole-answer digests of all-correct / Q1-wrong / Q2-wrong bundles are three distinct hashes with no slot information recoverable from any of them.
  • Falsifier (F4): both parametrisations reproduced exactly — 1 − 0.999^1440 = 0.7632 (per-pair reading, researcher's number) and 1 − (1 − 2·0.001·0.999)^1440 = 0.9439 (per-arm reading, red teams' number); at ε = 0.005 per-arm, P(any) = 1.0000.
  • Conjunction (F8): p − p³ re-derived — 0.171 / 0.288 / 0.357 at p = 0.9 / 0.8 / 0.7, matching red-team B exactly.
  • Disjointness (F7): under a triangular two-operand sum distribution the coordinator obtains P(pair coincidence) ≈ 0.075 and P(any of three) ≈ 0.21 — same magnitude as red-team B's 0.068 / 0.191 under its operand range; the substance (coincidence is routine) is confirmed, the small difference is the operand-range choice, not an error.
  • Cap (F5): a three-line bundle of moderate answers exceeds the 64-token default in character proxy (71 chars for three 20-char answers plus labels) where each split line is 23 — the censoring gradient is on the readout's own axis, as the red teams' token-level executions show.

docs.title: 5. Errors found in the briefs (none load-bearing)
docs.text:
• Red-team B: two line drifts (structured.py OUTCOMES at :68, cited ~:56; the exact_match record site at core.py:797, cited ~:815). Substance verified at the correct lines by the verifier.
  • The researcher's F3 number (0.763) and the red teams' (0.944) initially read as a disagreement; both are correct under their stated null parametrisations (§1 F4). No brief is wrong; the design doc prints both with their nulls.
  • No other errors: the verifier's mechanical sweep resolved every remaining symbol, line, count, and external citation in all three briefs (catalog = 29 families executed; grep counts exact).

docs.title: 6. Verdict
docs.text: NO-BUILD — unanimous (researcher, red-team A, red-team B, verifier; coordinator concurs on its own re-execution).
