The sketch's headline readout cannot be emitted by the tree's scorer (F1), cannot be parsed by the grammar it never froze (F2), cannot be carried by the records the lab keeps (F3), cannot be decided by the falsifier it specifies (F4), is manufactured by the generation cap on a perfect model (F5), compares two arms neither of which is the thing the claim names (F6), promises swap detection its population defeats by chance (F7), promises a selection readout that conjunction arithmetic fabricates and the numform settlement forbids (F8), at a bundle size its own utility does not ask about (F9), under a name the tree already owns (F10). The redesigned run --multi-question instrument in §3 is a resubmission candidate for a future fresh blind design review — not a build order, and not queued ahead of any existing item. With this round, the wave-11 slate is fully adjudicated: ranks 1–5 all NO-BUILD, each with a resubmission candidate recorded.

docs.title: Canonical-form ladder — cycle 209 design (ADJUDICATED: buildable on the amendments below; researcher, blind red-teams A and B, and verifier converged, coordinator adjudication in ~/workspace/agents_out/cycle209/build_log.md)
Background: the gap this closes
docs.text:
The lab ships exactly one Unicode transform over prompt text, and it is a compatibility transform: surface-noise's unicode_variant operator (model_protocol_lab/perturbation.py:101-123, registered at :131) replaces a seeded subset of ASCII alphanumerics with their fullwidth forms (U+FF01–U+FF5E), which are NFKC-foldable and visibly different characters. A full-tree census of every unicodedata.normalize call in model_protocol_lab/ (core.py:201, :758; contamination.py:55; confidentiality.py:249; leading.py:153; refusals.py:149,155; scorerlens.py:156,171) confirms every other use is a comparison key, a detection signature, output classification, or post-hoc answer regrading. Stored fixture data stays byte-exact; only the comparisons normalize (Split docstring, core.py:168-175). Nothing shipped re-renders prompt or fixture message text under a different canonical form and re-measures verdicts or re-derives a winner.

Canonical equivalence (UAX #15 §1.1) is "a fundamental equivalency between characters or sequences of characters which represent the same abstract character, and which when correctly displayed should always have the same visual appearance and behavior." UAX #15 §10, point 3: "Higher-level processes that transform or compare strings, or that perform other higher-level functions, must respect canonical equivalence or problems will result." The annex defines the equivalence and warns about it; it measures nothing about models or tokenizers. Sclar et al. (arXiv:2310.11324) measure visible formatting sensitivity (up to 76 accuracy points on LLaMA-2-13B), not canonical form. Rana et al. (arXiv:2511.03237v1, "IndicSuperTokenizer") put NFKC in a pre-tokenization pipeline and compare NFC/NFD/NFKC intrinsically by fertility (§3.2, Table 16; metrics in §3.5) — tokens-per-word, not task verdicts, not winner re-selection. The v1 pin matters: arXiv now lists v2 (2026-03-22) retitled "MUTANT: A Recipe for Multilingual Tokenizer Design"; the IndicSuperTokenizer title and §3.2/Table 16 content are v1 facts, and any doc citing them must say v1 or a future verifier resolving the bare ID will "refute" a true claim.

The differentiator is the combination, never "first": canonically equivalent, visually identical prompt text × the lab's 29 hand-rendered template families × conservative winner re-selection with abstention, on a local checkpoint with exact token sequences. A web pass over the named neighbours (LM Eval Harness, HELM, DSPy, PromptPerfect, OpenAI evals, 2026-10-26) found no prompt-side canonical-form instrument; the closest neighbour found, Promptfoo's normalizeUnicode, normalizes at the assertion side (equals / contains answer comparison, NFC by default), the same side as the lab's scorer-lens rung — not a prompt re-render. That pass is a search result, not proof of nonexistence, and the claim below does not depend on it.

docs.title: Pre-registered claim (falsifiable)
docs.text:
Over generated fact-recall cases whose NFC and NFD renderings are byte-different but canonically equivalent, the selected winner and every per-case verdict are identical under both forms — conditioned on the falsification population defined below. The claim states exactly what would prove it wrong:

  • The falsification population is ID-DIVERGENT paired cases only: cases where both arms completed AND the two arms' full render id sequences differ. Under greedy decoding, a case whose two arms produce identical id sequences cannot flip a verdict except through backend nondeterminism, so pooling id-identical cases into the denominator dilutes discordance toward a fake acquittal.
  • Per case, the report is three-way: ids-identical / divergent-concordant / divergent-discordant, with the per-case id-length delta (NFC token count minus NFD token count) so that trivial byte-fallback divergence is visible as such rather than pooled with merge-level divergence.
  • The claim is falsified per candidate when invariance_falsified is true (see Decision vocabulary). A same-ids verdict flip is recorded as a determinism finding (n_same_ids_verdict_flips), never as canonical-form fragility — the ws-scan precedent (wscanonical.py docstring claim 2), which conditions fragility on id divergence and records same-ids flips separately.
  • The winner half is falsified only by winner_changed (both arms select, winners differ). Selection-vs-abstention is NEVER a winner change: it vacates the winner half to winner_abstention_asymmetric (exactly one side selects) or winner_undefined (neither selects).

Scope limits, printed with the numbers: the probe measures whether the NFC/NFD distinction survives this checkpoint's full text→ids pipeline and, if it does, whether it moves verdicts. A run that lands 100% in the ids-identical bucket has measured the checkpoint's tokenizer normalizer, full stop: the readout is "instrument inapplicable to this tokenizer", never "the model is robust to canonical form". A no-discordance result acquits the candidate only on this generated population, never in general. A discordant result proves the winner picked on NFC text can change when the same text arrives decomposed; it proves nothing about weights.

docs.title: Monday-morning utility
docs.text: An engineer whose prompt text arrives from mixed sources (files, web copy-paste, user uploads) uses the readout to decide whether their harness must NFC-normalize all incoming text before evaluation — or whether the template winner they picked on NFC text silently changes when the same text arrives decomposed.

docs.title: Invariants (binding on the build)
docs.text:
1. Two arms only: nfc, nfd. No NFKC arm in v1 (NFKC is a compatibility transform per UAX #15 Table 1; §1.2 warns the K forms "must not be blindly applied to arbitrary text" because they erase distinctions; a K arm would also sit closest to the already-shipped fullwidth operator). No as-authored control arm: for an NFC-authoring generator it is byte-identical to NFC by construction and would burn a third of the generation budget re-measuring the NFC arm.
  2. THE SCORER PIN. Verdicts are core.evaluate's byte-exact answer == case.expected (core.py:797). A model echoing the prompt's canonical form flips its verdict with zero behavioural defect if the expected value itself carries accents — executed through the real pipeline in adjudication (NFC True, NFD False for an accented value; both True for an ASCII value). Therefore: decomposable characters live in carrier prose, topic, and question ONLY; every expected value is pure ASCII (placement-style word-number codes). The generator enforces this and a test pins it. The alternative (compare this probe's verdicts after NFC) is REJECTED: it would change what "verdict" means relative to every sibling probe and to the diff validator's digest-identity verdict.
  3. Generated cases only. No user-fixture arm in v1: the shipped fixtures are pure ASCII (0 non-ASCII strings in examples/fixtures.json and fixtures.csv), and the arm is structurally unbuildable through the fixture path anyway — Split compares message inputs by NFC key (core.py:193-214), so an NFC fixture and its NFD twin are the same fixture by the lab's own anti-leakage discipline. Generated cases are stage-local (placement precedent) and never enter the user's Split, so no variant can cross the search/held-out boundary.
  4. Message-content transform only, never the whole render. Templates are not touched: the transform applies to generated case text; template renders are byte-identical across arms by construction except for the message content they carry. (For ASCII messages, all 29 catalog families render canonical-invariantly — executed in adjudication.)
  5. Single source of truth for the arms. The generator authors case text in NFC (precomposed literals). The NFD arm is unicodedata.normalize("NFD", content) of that one authored render — never independently authored, which would invite drift the asserts then have to catch.
  6. Alphabet by mapping, not by block. A character is eligible iff NFC(ch) != NFD(ch). Singletons (characters whose NFD is a single different codepoint, e.g. U+2126 OHM SIGN, U+212B ANGSTROM SIGN) are excluded: they are canonical-equivalent but identity-changing in a way that invites misreading. Hangul syllables are deferred to a labelled stress variant: NFD renders run ~3x the code points, confounding form with length. Compatibility-only characters (NFC == NFD, e.g. ligature U+FB00, vulgar fraction U+00BD) are excluded automatically by the divergence assert. The generator reports its effective alphabet size; no block count (such as "Latin-1 letters") is asserted.
  7. Canonical ordering by construction. Authored text is NFC, so its NFD derivation is canonically ordered by definition of the normalization algorithm. Marks are never hand-assembled from base letters plus combining marks, which would make the authored text a third form equal to neither arm.
  8. The ONLY load-bearing pre-generation assert is byte-divergence: NFC(content) != NFD(content) byte-wise, plus authored == NFC(authored). Cases failing either are excluded pre-generation WITH counts (n_excluded_non_divergent), reported, never silently dropped. The equivalence assert NFC(NFD(x)) == NFC(x) is a theorem of canonical equivalence (holds universally, spot-checked in adjudication) and is NOT presented as a validation check anywhere.
  9. Id divergence is measured at encode time on the FULL render id sequence (what the model sees), per (case, candidate) — a per-(case, backend) property, never a property of the text alone. Template text contributes nothing to it beyond the message content it carries.
  10. Content commitment (the field-order pattern, not placement's). Records carry SHA-256 digests of both arms' message contents. The diff validator's independent mirror regenerates both forms from the seed and checks: each digest against the mirror's form, NFC digest != NFD digest, ids_identical implies equal arm token counts, and id_length_delta equals the token-count difference. A validator that checked token counts alone could never establish that the NFD arm's prompts were the NFD form of the case text. Payload-supplied normalized strings or equivalence flags would be tautological and are never trusted.
  11. Fail-closed vocabulary: {"available": False, "detail": "canonical_form_unavailable"}, with stage details cancelled, canonical_form_record_budget_exceeded, canonical_form_screen_failed in the same pattern as placement. Per-cell details reuse the fixed pair arm_context_exceeded / arm_evaluation_failed. Rates carry denominators; a rate is None only when its denominator is 0.
  12. Reporting discipline: counts and rates only; no payload, question, or answer text is rendered. Every payload-derived string goes through _escape_text (the cycle-206/207 lesson, not bare escape()).

docs.title: Decision vocabulary (total functions)
docs.text:
Floors transplanted from placement (placement.py:172-173): MIN_PAIRED_EVALUABLE = 6, MIN_DISCORDANT = 2. They gate the label only, never a reported count or rate.

Per-candidate classification over the id-divergent paired population (n_paired = both cells completed AND ids diverged; n_nfc_only / n_nfd_only = discordant directions):

  • insufficient — n_paired < 6.
  • no_discordance_observed — discordant == 0.
  • discordant_balanced — n_nfc_only == n_nfd_only >= 2.
  • discordant_asymmetric — max(n_nfc_only, n_nfd_only) >= 2.
  • below_threshold — otherwise (discordant == 1 at sufficient population: observed, but below the floor — NOT falsified).

invariance_falsified is true exactly when the classification is discordant_balanced or discordant_asymmetric. The direction is stated here deliberately: falsified means the invariance claim fell, not that an effect was confirmed absent.

Per-arm selection mirrors placement's _selection_over: over the shared fixture set (recorded for every candidate), a candidate "passes" an arm iff it passes every completed case on that arm; exactly one passer selects, several passers give ambiguous, none give no_candidate; withheld (unavailable) when completed sets differ across candidates or are empty. The winner headline compares the two arms' selections:

  • winner_changed — both arms select, winners differ.
  • winner_stable — both arms select, same winner.
  • winner_abstention_asymmetric — exactly one side selects.
  • winner_undefined — neither side selects.

docs.title: Record shape (per candidate)
docs.text:
{
  "fixture": "canonicalform-00",
  "topic": "<accented topic, NFC authored>",
  "expected_digest": sha256(ASCII value),
  "nfc_tokens": int, "nfd_tokens": int,
  "ids_identical": bool,
  "id_length_delta": int,            # nfc_tokens - nfd_tokens
  "nfc_content_digest": sha256, "nfd_content_digest": sha256,
  "cells": {"nfc": cell | None, "nfd": cell | None},
  "cell_details": {"nfc": "", "nfd": ""},
}

Cell shape (placement): verdict, boundary_found, boundary_text_match, input_tokens, answer_digest, where a cell's verdict is re-derived by the validator as answer_digest == expected_digest conjoined with the boundary flag, and a completed cell's input_tokens must equal the record's arm token count. Aggregates additionally carry the per-case id_length_delta_by_case list (in case order) and max_abs_id_delta, so a reader can separate "diverged by 1 id" from "diverged into byte ids" at a glance.

Generation budget: 24 cases × 2 arms × up to 24 candidates = 1,152 generations worst case (placement's cap). Records bytes bounded by the house 12 MiB, as placement.

docs.title: Risks, pre-registered readings
docs.text:
• R1 (tokenizer erasure): SentencePiece normalizes with an NFKC variant before tokenization by default (default rule nmt_nfkc), so on SentencePiece-family checkpoints both arms may be token-identical on every case. That outcome is a tokenizer finding ("instrument inapplicable to this tokenizer"), never model robustness. HF tokenizers pipelines declare their normalizer explicitly per checkpoint; the probe discovers it by measuring ids, never asserts it in docs.
  • R2 (byte-fallback divergence): for byte-level tokenizers, NFD text may fall back to per-byte tokens where NFC had a merged token. The per-case delta list is the mitigation that exists.
  • R3 (scripted backends): the suite's fake backends encode at word/character level; on them id divergence is guaranteed and meaningless as tokenizer evidence. Payload language scopes bucket-1/2/3 to the run's backend fingerprint, and no test result is ever described as a tokenizer finding.

docs.title: Rejected alternatives (with reasons)
docs.text:
• NFKC third arm: compatibility, not canonical; closest to shipped territory (fullwidth operator); least new information. Deferred as a separately labelled compatibility arm, never pooled with the canonical headline.
  • As-authored control arm: degenerate (== NFC for NFC-authored literals); a genuinely distinct mixed-form control would make the control's distance to each arm case-specific and break discordance accounting.
  • NFC-compare in the verdict layer: changes what "verdict" means relative to every sibling probe and to the validator's digest identity; the ASCII-value pin achieves the same defusal by construction, without redefining verdicts.
  • Fixture arm: vacuous on shipped data and structurally unbuildable through the fixture path (Split NFC keys).
  • Single-discordance falsification: uncalibrated — one scorer artifact (or one noisy case) would close the question. The floors (6 paired, 2 discordant) plus the below_threshold state are the transplant that fixes it.

docs.title: Sources
docs.text:
• UAX #15, Unicode Normalization Forms (unicode.org/reports/tr15/, rev. 58): §1.1 canonical equivalence definition; Table 1 (NFD = Canonical Decomposition, NFC = decomposition + composition, K forms = compatibility); §1.2 K-form warning; §5 composition exclusions; §10 point 3 ("must respect canonical equivalence or problems will result").
  • Sclar, Choi, Tsvetkov, Suhr, arXiv:2310.11324 (FormatSpread; "up to 76 accuracy points", LLaMA-2-13B; visible formatting features, not canonical form).
  • Rana et al., arXiv:2511.03237v1, "IndicSuperTokenizer: An Optimized Tokenizer for Indic Multilingual LLMs" (§3.2 NFKC in pre-tokenization + Table 16 fertility by NFC/NFD/NFKC; §3.5 intrinsic metrics). Cite as v1, never unversioned.
  • SentencePiece, "Text Normalization in SentencePiece" (github.com/google/sentencepiece, doc/normalization.md): normalization before tokenization by default, default rule nmt_nfkc, partial-NFKC caveat.
  • Hugging Face tokenizers Normalizers API (huggingface.co/docs/tokenizers/api/normalizers): NFC, NFD, NFKC, NFKD, Precompiled normalizer components exist as pipeline components; per-checkpoint configuration is a per-checkpoint fact.
  • Promptfoo deterministic assertions (promptfoo.dev/docs/configuration/expected-outputs/deterministic/): normalizeUnicode (NFC default, NFKC option) applies to equals/contains answer comparison — answer-side, not a prompt re-render. The neighbour that normalizes, on the other side of the measurement from this probe.
  • Tree: model_protocol_lab/placement.py (generator, floors, classification, selection mirror), experiments.py:9220,9271 (cell/stage), diffreports.py:10386,10530 (recompute/diff), reporting.py:6885 (section), cli.py:612,1893,3883 (flag, runner, dispatch), core.py:797 (byte-exact verdict), core.py:193-214 (Split NFC keys), wscanonical.py (id-divergence discipline), catalog.py (29 families).

docs.title: Choice-scoring audit design (run --choice-audit, cycle 195)
docs.text: Status: frozen contract, red-team cross-checked before code (research wave-8 rank #6). The swarm record is in docs/RESEARCH_LOG.md (cycle 195): researcher brief, red-team A (16 findings, verdict BUILD WITH AMENDMENTS), red-team B (every executed claim of A's re-run bit-identically; 6 findings confirmed, 10 partially confirmed, 9 sub-claims refuted, 5 B-NEW findings). This document is the contract the build implements; where the original wave-8 brief and this document disagree, this document governs.

docs.title: 1. Utility
docs.text: Monday morning: a practitioner deciding whether to trust the lab's greedy-generation winner — or an lm-eval-style log-likelihood ranking they got elsewhere — learns, per template family, how often teacher-forced choice scoring and free generation pick different answers on the same fixtures, and whether the two methods' top candidates agree. The audit is a second opinion: it never selects, never feeds the selection rule, and its payload contains no decision about the run. (Vocabulary rule in §10.)

docs.title: 2. What is measured
docs.text:
Post-hoc over a completed run, teacher-forced only. The audit adds no generations beyond the native search it audits; its cost is forward passes (§9). For each search fixture, a four-choice set is constructed from the run's own search fixtures (§3). Each choice is teacher-forced under each candidate over that candidate's recorded search prompt for the fixture, using the existing scoring.py engine. Three rankings of the same cells are reported (§4). Headlines per candidate: choice accuracy under the total ranking, the generation × choice discordance table (§7), and difficulty strata (§7). Method level: whether the choice method's top candidate agrees with the run's primary winner, computed only over the common evaluable population (§6).

Two scope sentences that ship in the docs and CLI help with the feature:

  • The generation side is the lab's greedy generation. Nothing here speaks to sampled decoding.
  • The choices are scored in separate forward passes over the same recorded prompt; they are never presented to the model as a list. There is no position or primacy confound and no permutation arm.

docs.title: 3. Choice-set construction (frozen order of operations)
docs.text:
Construction is a pure function of the search split. The order is frozen (red-team B, B-NEW-5): construct → screen → dedup → score → non-finite demotion → evaluability → argmax and tie classification, per ranking. No step may be reordered by an implementer; the producer and the diff validator walk the same order.

  1. Exclusions. A fixture whose expected answer normalises to empty at rung 1 of the scorer-lens ladder is excluded from every choice population, as a target and as a donor, with the exclusion counted (scorer-lens / leading precedent; rung 1 begins with a trim, so strip-empty is the same set — one exclusion, one reason, blank_expected). A blank true choice would score ok_empty with total 0.0 — the maximum attainable — and win its set by construction; that is a fixture defect, not a measurement.
  2. Donor rule smallest-eligible-id-first-three-v1 (probe-local name; modelled on leading's donor rule, extended from one donor to three — leading's machinery itself yields exactly one plant per fixture and is not reused). For target fixture T, the donor pool is every non-excluded search fixture whose group differs from T's group (donors may share a group among themselves). A pool fixture is eligible when its expected is non-equivalent to every expected in T's group under the screen in step 3. Donors are taken in ascending fixture-id order.
  3. Screen scorerlens-r4-plus-containment-v1 — literally leading's equivalent_claim: rung-4 equivalence under scorerlens.rung_match, or folded containment either way (NFC + casefold + strip). What the screen does not prove: paraphrases outside the ladder's grammar still pass — "1/2" against "0.5" is the named example (the frozen numeric grammar is ASCII-decimal; fraction notation is outside it). The screen also has a stated cost: containment removes the best legitimate distractors (donor "Paris, Texas" against true "Paris" is a genuinely different, maximally plausible choice). The screen is adopted anyway — ambiguity in the correctness definition is worse than an easier set, and the resulting upward bias is disclosed by the strata in §7.
  4. Dedup. Donors are deduplicated by byte identity, then by rung-4 equivalence class, in pool order: a donor whose class is already represented in the set is skipped. The realised set is the true choice plus the first three distinct-class eligible donors.
  5. Shortfall. If fewer than three distinct-class eligible donors exist, the fixture is not constructible: it enters no choice population for any candidate, and the shortfall is counted in the per-fixture eligibility record. There is no numeric-perturbation fallback (leading's digit surgery is rejected on the record: a fabricated string is not a plausible choice the way it is a plausible claim, and the fallback would relieve shortfall selectively for numeric fixtures — a difficulty-correlated denominator distortion).

The construction is recorded per fixture in the payload (fixtures block: target id and group, exclusion reason if any, the chosen donors' fixture ids and groups, a SHA-256 digest of every choice text, the realised distinct-choice count, constructible or not) and bound by donor_map_sha256 over the whole block (leading's precedent: editing fixture B's expected changes fixture A's choice set, so the map is part of the treatment and is digested as such). Choice order is frozen — true choice first, then donors in ascending fixture-id order — and is presentational only, since each choice is scored in its own forward pass.

docs.title: 4. Rankings (three, one headline)
docs.text:
Per fixture and candidate, each choice carries the engine's reported values: float32-rounded total log-likelihood, float32-rounded mean per scored token, scored token count, and target byte length (TargetScore already reports all four).

  • Total (headline): argmax over reported totals. This is lm-eval's acc semantics exactly (EleutherAI, https://blog.eleuther.ai/multiple-choice-normalization/).
  • Per-byte: score defined as reported total ÷ target byte length, computed from the reported values so producer and validator agree bit-for-bit. This is lm-eval's acc_norm semantics (byte-length-normalised).
  • Per-token mean: argmax over reported means. This is the token-length-normalised quantity the harness deliberately does not report (it is not tokenization-agnostic). It is reported because the engine already produces it and the comparison here is intra-checkpoint (one tokenizer), but it must never be labelled acc_norm in any surface — payload, report, docs, or CLI help.

The reported mean is taken from the engine's reported means directly. It is not derivable from the reported total (the engine rounds the mean from the unrounded total), and no code — producer, validator, or test oracle — may exact-check mean == total / count or total == sum(per_token); either check manufactures phantom drift on honest payloads. Per-token values are not stored at all.

The audit measures total-vs-normalised disagreement; it applies no PMI or calibration correction (Holtzman et al., arXiv: 2104.08315, surface-form competition, is the cited reason such corrections exist). A discordant cell is evidence about the scoring rule, not a repaired score.

docs.title: 5. Cells, evaluability, ties
docs.text:
• Cell. One (candidate, fixture, choice) teacher-forced score. The prompt span is alignment-checked once per (candidate, fixture) (check_alignment over the prompt with an empty target): a prompt-side failure (decode_failed, encode_failed, prompt_roundtrip_mismatch from that pre-check) voids all four cells with that reason, is counted once per fixture in n_prompt_failures, and reserves the per-cell reasons for target-side causes (target roundtrip, boundary merge, provider and context codes — including context_limit_exceeded, a first-class counted reason).
  • Non-finite demotion. A cell whose reported total or mean is non-finite (reachable with status ok: float32 saturation of an extreme finite logit sum — the cycle-76 pin) is stored as unavailable with the fixed reason non_finite_score, in producer and validator vocabularies alike. A verbatim -inf would crash the allow_nan=False report write; the shipped logprob diagnostic's per-fixture path carries this latent exposure today and the audit does not inherit it.
  • Evaluability. A fixture has a choice verdict under a candidate iff it is constructible and every constructed cell has status exactly ok with finite reported values. (ok_empty is a distinct engine status, not ok: strip-empty choices never reach scoring because construction excludes them, so an ok_empty cell appearing anyway is a protocol violation, counted under its own reason, never folded into alignment unavailability.) Anything else is choice_unavailable for that candidate, with per-reason cell counts beside it. Partial choice sets are never argmaxed: unavailability correlates with the choice's surface form and with the candidate's rendering, so a surviving-subset argmax is an easier, different task per fixture.
  • Ties. Per fixture and ranking, the verdict is correct (true choice uniquely at the reported maximum), tied (true choice at the maximum with at least one other choice), or incorrect (otherwise). Ties are counted, never broken, and never counted as correct. All argmax comparisons — producer and validator — operate on the reported (float32-rounded) values, so a tie is a property of the published numbers, not of hidden precision.

docs.title: 6. Populations, denominators, the method-level headline
docs.text:
• Per-candidate accuracies are reported beside their own denominators (evaluable fixtures for that candidate). A candidate with zero evaluable fixtures reports accuracy None with a fixed detail — never 0.0, never a crash (scorer-lens precedent).
  • The method-level comparison is computed only over the common evaluable population: fixtures with a choice verdict under every candidate. n_common is an always-reported readout, next to the floor outcome — never a silent absence.
  • The floor is the probe-local constant MIN_COMMON_EVALUABLE = 6. Below it, the agreement claim is withheld with the fixed detail choiceaudit_common_population_below_floor; the counts still print. The floor gates the claim, never the reporting. Note the compounded arithmetic (B-NEW-3): all-cells evaluability intersected across up to 24 candidates makes a withheld headline a routine, expected outcome on boundary-hostile tokenizers — a known property of the instrument, stated here so it is never mistaken for a defect.
  • Native comparator. The run's primary outcome is mapped exactly as leading maps it: compatible_on_fixture_set and held_out_failed map to (selected, selected_candidate); any other decision passes through with its winner (usually None). The audit is gated on a complete search before any scoring: decision in {failed, cancelled}, a missing search list, or a search list shorter than the candidate list yields the whole payload {"available": False, "detail": "native_search_incomplete"} (leading's wrapper gate, same detail string).
  • Agreement is multi-state, never a bare boolean, with frozen priority: withheld (below floor) → native_abstain (mapped primary decision is not a selection) → choice_tied (choice accuracies tie at the top over the common population) → agree / disagree.

docs.title: 7. Discordance and strata
docs.text:
• Generation verdict per (candidate, fixture), from the recorded observation's stored facts: pass iff the observation is present with status completed and exact_match and boundary_found; fail iff completed and not both; missing otherwise (no observation, or not completed), counted as n_generation_missing. (In genuine runs exact_match is construction-gated on completion at core.py's single observation site; the status check is kept anyway so a foreign payload cannot convert a missing measurement into a generation fail.) Records store the facts (status, exact_match, boundary_found); the verdict is derived identically by producer and validator.
  • The 2×2 per candidate, headline (total) ranking, over fixtures with a generation verdict and a choice verdict of correct or incorrect: all four cells printed (gen-pass/choice-correct, gen-pass/choice-incorrect, gen-fail/choice-correct, gen-fail/choice-incorrect). Tied choice verdicts are counted beside the table, never forced into it. The generation-fail row is split by boundary_found into labelled sub-counts. The word "boundary" names two different facts in this payload — generation boundary_found (the response terminator was found) and the scoring reason boundary_merge_mismatch (a token straddles the prompt/answer seam) — and the report glosses the seam reason once as tokenisation alignment so the two are never read as one. Boundary-caused discordance is a named component of discordance, reported, not discounted: termination behaviour is part of what free generation does and teacher forcing does not.
  • Strata per candidate (total ranking, zero extra forwards): accuracy split by numeric vs non-numeric true answer (the ladder's numeric grammar decides), accuracy on the token-length-matched subset (every donor within ±1 scored tokens of the true answer's scored token count), and the per-ranking verdict-agreement counts (total vs per-byte, total vs per-token mean). Donors are unmatched — answers to unrelated fixtures, screened for equivalence only, not for plausibility, type, or length — so choice accuracy is an upper bound on item-matched choice accuracy, and the design says so wherever the number is introduced.

docs.title: 8. Ground records and the diff validator
docs.text:
The payload is self-contained (the default report view strips observations, so nothing may be joined back at diff time): protocol object (version, donor rule, screen name, K, ranking names, donor_map_sha256, backend fingerprint), the fixtures construction block (§3), and per-candidate entries carrying status/detail, the aggregates of §6–§7, and one record per search fixture: fixture id, the generation facts, the prompt reason if any, and the four cells (status, reason, reported total, reported mean, scored token count, target byte length — no per-token values).

The diff validator (diff_choiceaudit) recomputes every derived value from these ground records with its own mirrored implementation (diffreports loads standalone; it imports nothing from the producer): the donor-map digest over the stored block, donor distinctness and cross-group membership from the stored ids/groups, per-ranking verdicts and tie classification from the reported values, accuracies, the 2×2 and its boundary split, the strata, the common population, and the method-level agreement including its withholding. It asserts every stored float is float32-representable (mirrored struct check) — recompute from reported values is only meaningful if the stored values are the reported values. It never derives a mean from a total.

What the validator does not verify, stated plainly: the equivalence screen and donor provenance against the fixture texts (records carry digests, not texts — the same binding standard as the shipped scorer-lens and leading validators, which verify binding and arithmetic over producer-asserted ground records). Protocol, donor-map, or backend drift between two payloads marks the comparison not comparable, with the drift still listed.

docs.title: 9. Cost, caps, cancellation
docs.text:
• Cost: 4 forward passes per candidate per fixture (9,600 at the legal maximum of 24 candidates × 100 search fixtures), stated in the CLI help in the tree's cost-sentence form. A scoring forward is one pass; this is one to two orders of magnitude cheaper than a generation probe's budget at the same caps, and cheaper than the native search the run already paid for.
  • Caps, checked before any scoring (the house pattern): records = candidates × search fixtures ≤ MAX_RECORDS = 2400 (fits the legal maximum exactly — no legal scale is made unavailable) and a 12 MiB records byte cap; breach fails closed with choiceaudit_cell_budget_exceeded.
  • Cancellation is checked at each fixture boundary (per-cell checks are permitted, not required); a cancelled audit is {"available": False, "detail": "cancelled"} with no partial aggregates.
  • Backends without forward_logits (everything except LocalHFBackend today) yield the whole audit unavailable with the engine's logits_not_supported detail — honest degradation, and the dispatch tests are built for it.

docs.title: 10. Vocabulary and boundaries
docs.text:
Second-opinion vocabulary, frozen: ranking keys live under the choice_audit payload; the native comparator is always named primary_*; the HTML section is titled "Choice-scoring audit (second opinion)". The tree's discipline is namespacing, not word bans (scorer-lens emits winner_by_rung inside its own payload; leading emits per-condition decision/winner beside primary_*) — the audit follows it. Two boundary sentences, identical in this doc, USAGE, and CLI help:

  • Against --logprob-diagnostic: the diagnostic teacher-forces only each fixture's expected answer and bands its mean logprob beside the native verdicts; it constructs no choice set, ranks nothing, and cannot express that another scoring method would have picked a different answer or template.
  • Against --scorer-lens: the lens re-grades the recorded generations under normalisation rungs and re-derives a winner from the same answers; the audit scores answers the model never generated and compares the two methods' winners.

docs.title: 11. Uniqueness (research pass, cycle 195)
docs.text: Log-likelihood choice scoring is established prior art — it is lm-eval's native multiple-choice mode (acc over summed log-probability; acc_norm over byte-length-normalised log-probability; EleutherAI, https://blog.eleuther.ai/multiple-choice-normalization/), and HELM showed that the choice between likelihood scoring (separate) and generating the answer (joint) can swing accuracy by tens of points across models under a standardised prompt (Liang et al., arXiv:2211.09110). What no surveyed tool does is run both scoring ontologies over the same hand-rendered chat-template candidates on a single local checkpoint — greedy generation judged by exact match plus response boundary under the lab's conservative unique-winner/abstention rule on one side, and teacher-forced choice scoring over donor-screened choice sets built from the run's own fixtures on the other — and audit their disagreement per fixture (the full generation × choice 2×2) and at the method level (whether the two methods' top candidates agree, ties reported as ties). The combination — donor-screened choice sets × template family × generation-winner discordance audit — is the claim. Nearest neighbours, each missing at least two limbs: HELM's adaptation comparison (across models, dataset- native choice sets, no abstention winner), Molfese et al. (arXiv:2503.14996 — its "Logprobs" is the answer letter token's probability, not full-string scoring), and the MCQ vs free-generation comparison of arXiv:2403.17752 (a study, not a tool; no template candidates, no winner audited).

docs.title: 12. Falsification
docs.text: Zero discordance on completed, fully-evaluable cells under the total-loglikelihood ranking — over the reported completed-cell denominator, for greedy generation, this checkpoint, and this fixture set — falsifies "the scoring method matters for this checkpoint/fixture set": a publishable null that cross-validates the native winner. An audit whose 2×2 population is empty claims no falsification; it reports its denominators.

docs.title: Verbalized-confidence × template (run --confidence) — design
docs.text: Cycle 199 (wave-8 rank #8, the last wave-8 item). This document is the shipped contract. It folds the wave-8 research brief (docs/RESEARCH_LOG.md, wave-8 round), the cycle-199 researcher pass (primary sources re-verified), red-team A's ten findings (F1–F10) and nine amendments (A1–A9), red-team B's disproofs of A's positive amendments (its own amendments B1–B7), and a verifier pass that re-executed both red teams' probes and confirmed every load-bearing claim (V1–V12). Where the brief and the shipped contract differ, this document wins, and the differences are the adjudicated amendments, recorded below.

docs.title: What this is, honestly framed
docs.text:
--confidence appends one frozen suffix to each search fixture's last user message, asking the model to end its reply with a line of the form Confidence: <integer 0–100>, and re-evaluates every candidate template on the search split. The elicited text is parsed under a frozen grammar; the stated number is then set against the exact-match verdict the lab already trusts, per candidate: how often the model complies, what it states when it is right vs wrong, and what the suffix itself costs (verdict flips against the recorded native run). A generated pair runs alongside: planted-fact cases whose answer the prompt states (knowable) vs the same cases with the payload binding a different key (donor-key control), testing whether the stated number drops when the answer is not knowable from the prompt.

Monday-morning utility: a practitioner serving a checkpoint behind a template learns whether the confidence number the model states under that template tracks whether it was right — and whether it drops when the answer is not in the prompt — before exposing that number to anyone downstream.

A stated confidence is model output text, not a probability, and nothing in this probe turns it into one. The readouts describe agreement between the stated number and the measured verdict under each template. No readout is a calibration error; the words "calibrated", "overconfident", and "ECE" appear nowhere as findings (the verifier confirmed no shipped section uses them). What would change the picture: a stated number that separates correct from incorrect compliant answers and drops on the donor-key control is evidence the number carries answer-dependent signal under this instrument; a number that does neither is evidence it is theatre under this instrument. Both are claims about this checkpoint, this fixture set, this suffix, and this seed — nothing more is claimed.

docs.title: Prior art and the scoped uniqueness claim
docs.text:
Verbalized confidence is a studied elicitation method; the lab's contribution is not the method but the combination: (1) per-template candidate crossing — prompt format as the independent variable, the stated number compared across the lab's candidate templates on identical fixtures; (2) the confidence line separated from the scored span under a frozen grammar, so elicited generations are scored by the lab's ordinary exact-match verdict on the span (published studies score generated text with a judge model, or score log-probabilities instead); (3) verdict flips against the recorded native run — the elicitation cost of asking, which no surveyed study reports; (4) a donor-key knowability control — a paired generated control in which nothing false is stated and the asked fact is simply absent; and (5) the result shipped as a fail-closed diff-validated section of the lab's deterministic report, recomputed from digest-bound ground records. No surveyed tool or study ships this combination (researcher pass, cycle 199: lm-evaluation-harness, HELM, Inspect AI, OpenAI Evals, promptfoo, DSPy — Inspect's primitives could assemble something similar, but primitives are not a shipped measurement).

The neighbours, named so a reviewer does not have to discover them, with the researcher's corrections applied:

  • Kadavath et al., "Language Models (Mostly) Know What They Know" (arXiv:2207.05221): logit-based self-evaluation (P(True)/P(IK)), not verbalized confidence; cited only for the logit line of work, never as a verbalized precedent.
  • Lin et al., "Teaching Models to Express Their Uncertainty in Words" (arXiv:2205.14334): the origin of "verbalized probability", and a fine-tuning result (GPT-3 trained on CalibratedMath). Zero-shot untrained calibration is not shown there and is not claimed here.
  • Tian et al., "Just Ask for Calibration" (arXiv:2305.14975): the method ancestor (answer-then-confidence elicitation), with two differences that forbid numeric comparison: their scale is a float 0.0–1.0, and their correctness is GPT-judged, not exact-match. Their closing open question — how sensitive the method is to the prompt — is part of what a per-template crossing speaks to.
  • Xiong et al., "Can LLMs Express Their Uncertainty?" (arXiv:2306.13063): the lab's exact surface form (integer 0–100, "Answer and Confidence (0-100)") and the documented shape to expect: stated values cluster at multiples of 5 in the 80–100 range with a peak at 95, and vanilla elicitation is heavily overconfident by their (judge-scored) measure. Top-bin-dominated, sparse low bins are the pre-registered expected shape here, not a surprise.
  • Seo et al., "ADVICE: Answer-Dependent Verbalized Confidence Estimation" (arXiv:2510.10913): a primary fine-tuning study (an earlier brief miscited it as a survey; the researcher corrected the genre and the verifier confirmed it against the paper). Its §7 answer-masking experiment — replace answer tokens with padding and watch stated confidence — is the nearest published neighbour of this probe's knowability control, and is cited by name for that reason: the donor-key control differs by manipulating the prompt's evidence instead of the model's own answer tokens, and by needing no fine-tuned model. ADVICE's five-format taxonomy includes ScorePercent; the lab's surface form is literature-standard, claimed as such, not as an invention.
  • Damani et al., "Beyond Binary Rewards" (arXiv:2507.16806): RLCR, the RL-with-calibration-rewards training method (verbalized-confidence ECE 0.37 → 0.03 on HotpotQA after training). An earlier brief attributed that number to a different paper (arXiv:2604.26152, a single-author observability survey); the researcher refuted the attribution and the verifier confirmed Damani et al. as the primary source against the full text. Training a model to calibrate is the opposite direction from measuring an untrained checkpoint, and no number from it is comparable to anything this probe prints.
  • Yang, Tsai & Yamada, "On Verbalized Confidence Scores for LLMs" (arXiv:2412.14737): the strongest published prompt-method-sensitivity result for verbalized confidence — reliability "heavily depends on how we ask for it", with method rankings inverting between small and large models. Named here because it is the published reason a per-template crossing is a measurement and not a formality.

Cross-study numeric comparison to published calibration numbers is invalid and the docs must not invite it: the correctness ground truths differ (exact match here, judge models or human labels elsewhere).

docs.title: The instrument
docs.text:
Suffix and surgery. The suffix is a frozen constant (confidence.SUFFIX): "Answer the question, then state your confidence that your answer is correct. Put the confidence on its own final line as a whole number from 0 to 100, in exactly this form: Confidence: ". It is appended to the last user message only, as content + " " + SUFFIX (dateline's joiner and surgery pattern; id, group, and expected are unchanged, so the per-fixture seed is the same as the native run's). The placeholder line in the suffix is deliberately not a grammar line: a model echoing the instruction verbatim is malformed_line, never compliant. Before any generation, the suffix is screened against every candidate's special-token inventory (fixtures.audit_special_token_literals, the repetition precedent): a collision fails the stage closed with confidence_screen_failed, because a framing that turns the suffix text into a special token would forge the elicitation.

The grammar and the parser. A compliant final line matches ^Confidence: (0|[1-9][0-9]?|100)$ exactly — ASCII digits, no sign, no leading zeros, no surrounding whitespace. The regex is load-bearing, not pedantry (executed in the red-team passes): int() accepts +85, 8_5, 85, and non-ASCII digits, and an unflagged \d matches fullwidth digits, so any strip-and-int parser manufactures compliance the grammar does not grant. The parser is a total function over all strings, pure str (it never encodes, so a lone surrogate cannot raise), with five outcome codes and a final-line-first precedence, adjudicated in cycle 199 over red-team A's count-first alternative:

  • lines come from split(" ") with exactly one trailing empty element dropped (splitlines() is never used — it also splits on U+2028/U+0085 and would manufacture a final line);
  • a grammar-matching final line: ok if it is the only grammar line in the answer, multiple_lines if any earlier line also matches;
  • else a final line starting with Confidence: (exact) or confidence: (case-insensitive): malformed_line — even when an earlier line matched (the model's last act decides);
  • else any grammar line elsewhere: confidence_not_final;
  • else missing_line.

The span is the answer with the compliant line removed for ok cells, and the whole answer for every other code. A cell's verdict is one definition everywhere: span_digest == expected_digest and boundary_found. Compliance and correctness are separate axes and the joint table keeps them apart: a correct answer that never stated a number is correct and non-compliant; the verdicts recorded on suffixed generations by the raw evaluator are meaningless (the suffix text is part of the answer), which is why every verdict here is re-derived from the span.

Screens. A fixture is screened out of every elicitation population — its record carries the class and no cell, for every candidate identically — when: its expected answer is blank under strip() (expected_blank; a whitespace-only expected is "correctly" answered by whitespace, the vacuous pole); its expected answer already contains a grammar line anywhere (expected_confidence_shaped; red-team B's executed counterexample showed a final-line-only screen lets an honest generation gain a second grammar line through no act of the model's); its last user message is vacuous (vacuous_last_user; the suffix would be the whole turn, measuring suffix echo, not elicitation — red-team B forced the exclusion over red-team A's keep-or-exclude ambiguity); or it has no user turn (no_user_turn). Screens are computed by the stage and recorded in the protocol; the validator checks protocol/record consistency (see Residue).

The generated pair. 24 planted-fact cases, derived from the run seed: each binds a synthetic key (key-<8 hex>) to a 6-hex value, pairwise distinct by construction. The knowable arm's payload states the asked key's true binding; the control arm's payload states the next case's key and value. The control is red-team B's donor-key construction, and what it replaced matters: red-team A's original repair replaced the stated value with a false one, and B executed a definitionally payload-faithful backend against it — the faithful model reads the only stated value, answers it at Confidence 95, and the falsification boolean convicts correct behaviour of theatre (95 ≥ 95 fires backwards). Donor-key states nothing false about the asked key; the asked binding is simply absent. Pre-registered expectation: a model whose stated number tracks knowability states a lower number on the control arm; a model confidently answering the donor value there is copying the only value it can see — genuine answer-independence, the ADVICE mechanism, measured from the prompt side. Stated values are unguessable (16⁻⁶) and unmemorizable (seeded hex), so the knowable arm measures reading and the control its absence. The generated cases are instrument cases, labelled as such in the report; they are not operator fixtures.

docs.title: The readouts
docs.text:
Per candidate, over the operator population (unscreened search fixtures): completed and compliant counts with the compliance rate; the compliant × correct joint table; mean stated confidence over compliant cells, split by verdict, and their separation gap — descriptive only, printed beside the compliance rate and the joint table, and withheld with a named reason (no_compliant_cells, no_correct_compliant, no_incorrect_compliant) when a class is empty, because the three situations the bare None would conflate are themselves findings. The frozen four-bin table ([0,24] [25,49] [50,74] [75,100], edges in the protocol fingerprint) counts compliant cells per bin with per-bin accuracy (withheld at n = 0). Elicitation cost: verdict flips against the recorded native run, split by direction (pass_to_fail / fail_to_pass), over fixtures with a native verdict and a completed elicited cell.

Per candidate, over the generated population, each arm gets the same block. Between the arms, the knowability readout: over cases where both arms are compliant, the paired means and falsified = control_mean >= knowable_mean. The boolean is withheld (insufficient_paired_compliant) below 6 paired compliant cases (placement's MIN_PAIRED_EVALUABLE floor precedent: floors gate readouts, never counts). Two scope statements ship with it, in the report text and here: the boolean conditions on joint compliance — it asks only "among cases where the model stated a number both times, did the number drop?" — and a control arm whose compliance collapses is not folded into the boolean; it is reported as its own per-arm compliance count beside it. The word "elicited" never names a population mean in this design (red-team B showed the brief's elicited_mean was ambiguous between operator and generated arms); the boolean compares the two generated arms only.

docs.title: Payload and diff validation
docs.text:
Ground records are digest-bound: one record per (candidate, fixture) and one per (candidate, generated case). A cell carries answer_digest, span_digest, boundary_found, code, confidence, final_line, final_line_length, input_tokens, and the derived verdict. Red-team A's original record shape carried the confidence as a bare attested integer, and red-team B executed the forgery: editing only the integers moves the gap +5 → ±100 and flips the falsification boolean while passing every consistency check A proposed, because the residue was the probe's headline axis. The shipped binding (B2) closes it:

  • an ok cell carries its final line verbatim. The line is one of exactly 101 strings and a bijection with the scalar already in the record, so carrying it discloses zero additional information — and the validator re-runs the grammar over it and derives the scalar, rejecting any record whose scalar disagrees. Stage/validator parser divergence and internally inconsistent records die with it.
  • a malformed_line cell carries the first 32 characters of the final line plus the full line length — exactly what re-verifying the class takes (the classification prefix is 11 characters; a grammar line is at most 15).
  • every other code's final line is ordinary answer text and is never carried.
  • digest relations are code-dependent and unconditional: span_digest == answer_digest for every non-ok code, != for every ok cell — with no exception: red-team A's draft excepted the answer that is exactly one grammar line, and B and the verifier both executed the disproof (sha256("") ≠ sha256("Confidence: 50")).
  • scalar typing is strict: type(confidence) is int — a JSON true must not validate as confidence 1 (the tree's F2 discipline).

The generated case set is regenerated from the protocol seed by the diff validator's own mirror and must match the protocol exactly (ids, key digests, expected digests, both payload digests), so the control arm's construction is bound, not attested. Caps are enforced before any recompute (2,400 operator records, 576 generated records, 12 MiB combined — the combined-bytes measure is the stage's own construction, repeated verbatim by the validator). Every derived value is recomputed from the records by the validator's independent mirror and compared type-strictly; the diff section reports per-candidate compliance/gap/flip drift, knowable and control mean drift, and falsification drift, with protocol or backend drift marking the comparison not comparable.

Residue, named. What remains stage-attested: that the carried line was the generation's final line and the only grammar line (finality and multiplicity have no textual artefact that may be carried — the final lines of missing_line/confidence_not_final/multiple_lines cells are ordinary answer text); the span split itself; the screen classes (the fixture texts are not in the payload, so screens are checked for protocol/record consistency, not recomputed); and the digest↔text relation every digest-bound probe in the tree shares. The diff validator's standard is the answer-collision standard: everything with a checkable artefact is derived, and what cannot be is named here rather than silently trusted.

docs.title: Cost
docs.text: One full extra search evaluation (2,400 generations at the legal maximum: 24 candidates × 100 fixtures) plus the generated paired control (2 arms × 24 cases × 24 candidates = 1,152) — 3,552 extra generations in total, each on a suffix-lengthened prompt. (Red-team A's draft priced the generated arms as 576 records; generations and records carry different constants — placement.py's own comment — and B's recount, confirmed by the verifier, is the figure above.) No second checkpoint load, no teacher forcing. Defence in depth: the records caps above are also the budget the stage enforces before evaluating (confidence_cell_budget_exceeded).

docs.title: Guards and failure vocabulary
docs.text: The CLI wrapper adopts the choice-audit wrapper gate verbatim (the verifier confirmed the shipped wrappers' conditions): a failed, cancelled, or truncated native search gates the probe to zero forwards with native_search_incomplete. Stage unavailability details: confidence_screen_failed, confidence_cell_budget_exceeded, confidence_records_budget_exceeded, native_search_incomplete, cancelled. Per candidate, a failed evaluation degrades that candidate's cells alone (absent cells, never fabricated ones); a candidate with no completed cell anywhere is listed in unavailable_candidates, a set the validator re-derives exactly. Scope: the search split only — held-out fixtures are never treated; the probe never touches the decision, the selected candidate, or the exit code; and confidence cells are outside verify --determinism scope — the determinism certificate covers the recorded native search observations, and the report section states so in the same three places the multiturn/needle/placement/dateline sections state it (design doc, USAGE, section text).

docs.title: Tests
docs.text: tests/test_cycle199_confidence.py: the parser battery (24 named shapes, including every int()/regex trap and both contested precedence cases); a mutation gate over the parser — eight mutants (sign, leading zeros, non-ASCII digits, any-line, multiple-threshold, splitlines, loose-regex-plus-int, count-first precedence), each killed by a named battery case, with the unmutated control passing the whole battery; screens and surgery; case-generation distinctness/determinism/donor pairing; stage behaviour over scripted backends (faithful, theatrical, per-candidate failure, budget, cancel, suffix screen); a one-break-at-a-time validator tamper battery (19 breaks, including the scalar edit the carried line exists to catch); diff-section behaviour; the HTML section including a hostile candidate name through the C0/surrogate-stripping escape; the CLI wrapper gate; and one tiny-checkpoint end-to-end run. The diff-section blast radius is covered in test_cycle67_diffreports_audit.py (independent oracle trio, a fuzz builder that runs the real stage over scripted backends with hostile mutations and a coherent foreign fingerprint, the _identical_expected key set, and the flip-identical gate anchor extended in both its original and mutant texts — the same pass also repaired two sections the oracle's identical conjunction had silently omitted, placement and precision) and in test_cycle27_diffreports_verify.py (availability oracle recomputing through the producer's aggregation). CLI pins: test_cycle179_cli_dispatch.py (flag + helper-dispatch entries) and test_cycle44_validation_audit.py (source-file count 58 → 59).

docs.title: Date-line sensitivity design (cycle 188)
docs.text: Status: frozen before code. This document is the contract the implementation, the diff validator, and the test oracles are built against. It resolves red-team A's F1–F15 and red-team B's corrections (M1–M6) from the cycle-188 briefs in ~/workspace/agents_out/wave8/cycle188/; where A and B disagreed, B's cross-checked disposition governs and is cited inline.

docs.title: Utility
docs.text:
If your serving stack prepends a "Today is …" line, run --dateline tells you — per template family, on your own checkpoint — how often changing only that date flips a task verdict, and whether the template you picked still wins afterwards, so a calendar rollover cannot silently change your eval results after you ship.

The phenomenon is published: Sanz-Guerrero, Bui, Mager, and von der Wense, Dating the Model: Hidden Dates in System Prompts Affect LLM Evaluation (arXiv:2609.36931, 2026) — across 9 recent LLMs and 6 datasets (MCQA, math reasoning, code generation, machine translation), changing only the injected current date moves scores by up to 6% on MCQA, 14% on math reasoning, 7% on code generation, and 2.84 BLEU on machine translation; rankings shift; the effect exceeds batch-size and numerical-precision variance; few-shot does not reduce it and chain-of-thought amplifies it. That work varies the date inside each vendor's own system-prompt rendering on served models. No surveyed harness ships the combination frozen here: a frozen date-line treatment × hand-rendered template families × one local checkpoint × exact-match greedy scoring with an abstention rule × a length-matched no-date control (uniqueness survey: RESEARCH_LOG cycle 188; the claim is the combination, never "first", and generic plumbing in lm-eval/promptfoo/Inspect could approximate it by hand — what is claimed is a shipped, frozen, recompute-validated probe).

Boundary, one sentence: doctor --template-probe asks whether the checkpoint's own template code changes its rendering in response to message content (render-only, no generation, no scoring), whereas run --dateline asks whether an operator-supplied date string in the message content changes the model's scored verdicts under each hand-rendered template family (generation, exact-match). Note the sharper limit from TEMPLATE_PROBE_DESIGN T4′/T2′: a day-granularity date injection is constant across a template-probe pair and is therefore not a template-probe finding at all; the two probes are complementary, not mirror images.

docs.title: Construction
docs.text:
The lab has no system role (core.Message is user/assistant only), so the date line is delivered the way hierarchy delivers privilege blocks: folded into a user turn inside a frozen bracketed block. Placement is the probe family's uniform choice (repetition, distraction, leading all operate on the last user message): the block is prepended to the last user message's content. The construct is therefore named honestly everywhere (this doc, USAGE, CLI help, section prose): a date line immediately before the final user message — for single-turn fixtures that is the head of the conversation; for multi-turn fixtures it is not, and the search set's multi-turn share is reported beside the headlines (G9†).

  • Block template (frozen literal): [Context] Today's date is {DATE}. [/Context]
  • Joiner (frozen literal): " " between the block and the original content — block + " " + content. (Leading appends with " "; a prepended block takes the hierarchy-style blank line. The choice is frozen here, not left to the builder.)
  • The arm fixture keeps the native fixture's id, so core.request_seed_for pairs request seeds across arms.

docs.title: The frozen arm set (G1†, G7)
docs.text:
Eight date values, each rendered in three frozen formats. Weekday names are part of the protocol data: every arm's weekday was computed from its own calendar date at freeze time and is pinned by test; no weekday is ever derived at runtime (a builder templating the anchor's weekday into every arm would silently convert five arms into extra lie arms — the validator's weekday rule below exists to catch exactly that).

value key date weekday anchor 2026-10-21 Wednesday minus_day 2026-10-20 Tuesday plus_day 2026-10-22 Thursday minus_year 2025-10-21 Tuesday plus_year 2027-10-21 Thursday leap 2028-02-29 Tuesday boundary_eve 2026-12-31 Thursday boundary_day 2027-01-01 Friday

Formats (frozen renderers over frozen English month/weekday tables; no strftime, no locale anywhere in the module, the stage, the reporting section, or the validator):

  • iso: 2026-10-21
  • long: 21 October 2026
  • weekday_iso: Wednesday, 2026-10-21 — weekday name + ISO, the primary paper's own hidden-prompt shape ("Today is Wednesday, 2025-12-03"). B's correction is adopted: the weekday-long hybrid (Wednesday, 21 October 2026) appears in no cited source and would re-confound weekday with the long-form rendering in every pair; weekday-ISO keeps the date tokens identical to the ISO arms, so the ISO↔weekday-ISO pair per value isolates the weekday channel.

Arm keys: {value}_{format} for the 24 date arms (e.g. anchor_iso, leap_long), plus the controls and the lie below — 28 treated arms in total.

Arm → effect mapping (the design text asserted the set "spans the effects the primary source reports" with no mapping; here it is): anchor is the reference date every contrast is anchored to; minus_day/plus_day are the smallest calendar step (the paper's week-of-dates variation); minus_year/plus_year span the year-scale variation — under the weekday-bearing format they necessarily shift the weekday too (365 ≡ 1 mod 7, no Feb 29 in either span), so that contrast is named year+weekday shift, never "±1 year" alone; leap is the rare-valid-date arm, frozen to 2028-02-29 (the nearer leap day, +496 days, and the next one a stack frozen at the anchor actually rolls into; its distance from the anchor exceeds every other arm's, so leapness is confounded with distance and the doc says so wherever the arm is reported); boundary_eve/boundary_day are consecutive days straddling the anchor's next year rollover — the cleanest year-number contrast in the set, at near-constant distance.

The anchor is named anchor date (frozen 2026-10-21) in the protocol, the payload, and the docs. It is "current" only on the freeze date; under the reproducibility rule below every later run's anchor is a stale date by design, and the naming must not invite a "the probe used yesterday's date" misreading.

docs.title: Weekday-lie arm (G1†, F8)
docs.text: One lie arm: arm key lie. Date value: the anchor. Format: weekday-ISO only (the lie is defined inside the weekday-bearing format; it is never compared against ISO/long arms as a format contrast). Direction: +1 — literal string Thursday, 2026-10-21 (the calendar weekday of 2026-10-21 is Wednesday; +1 is the smaller length step, 9→8 characters, minimising the length confound that honest-vs-lie unavoidably carries). The lie is a single date × single format cell family; the design says so wherever its counts appear. Its role is inside the date-loss truth table (below): it separates "any date text perturbs" from "the date's content matters".

docs.title: Reproducibility (G10)
docs.text: All dates are protocol constants. Nothing in dateline.py, the experiments.py stage, the reporting section, or the validator may read the wall clock or the locale: no date.today(), datetime.now(), strftime, or strptime with %A/%B. A scoped pin test greps exactly those surfaces (doctor.py's legitimate run_date_utc is out of scope). A run must be byte-reproducible on any day. Dateline cells are recorded search-side treatments, not recorded search observations: they are outside verify --determinism's scope, and the docs say so rather than implying coverage. Held-out fixtures are never date-treated, never screened, and never enter any readout; every readout is a search-side readout.

docs.title: The no-date control (G4†)
docs.text:
The control is a sized neutral text, not a sentence — B's adjudication of A F4: a single grammatical sentence has one length per candidate render and cannot match arms that provably differ in length from each other (the design's own block shape spans 48–64 characters across arms before any tokenizer effect), and even a per-format control is matched to at most one date value in that format, because date values differ in length within a format too. The honest construction is the precedents' one (repetition's pad, distraction's spans): whole neutral units plus at most one truncated suffix, sized per (candidate, fixture) against rendered token ids, with unmatchable cells flagged and the evaluable share reported.

Frozen choices, priced in the budget below:

  • One control per format: arm keys nodate_iso, nodate_long, nodate_weekday_iso — 3 control arms.
  • Each control cell is sized to match that format's anchor arm for the same (candidate, fixture): the control fixture's rendered token count must equal the anchor fixture's. The date-vs-control contrast is therefore exact at the anchor. For non-anchor date values the control contrast is length-unmatched by construction and is labelled as such wherever reported, with the per-cell input_tokens deltas available in the payload — the doc does not let the word "matched" drift onto those contrasts. (The fully-matched alternative — one control per date value — costs 24 control arms and 117,600 worst-case generations for a contrast the headline does not use; rejected and priced here so the rejection is auditable.)
  • Neutral unit (frozen literal, new for this probe, temporally inert): The reference panel is mounted on the north wall of the room. Repetition's filler is not reused: it contains the temporal phrase "that morning", which would put temporal priming in the no-date control of a date probe.
  • The control block keeps the envelope and replaces the sentence: [Context] {NEUTRAL} [/Context], same joiner, same position.
  • Sizing rule (frozen name): whole-units-plus-one-truncated-suffix-v1 over the neutral unit, search budget 512 encodes per cell (repetition precedent), verified on rendered ids. Cells that cannot be matched carry control_evaluable: False; date-vs-control contrasts are computed only over matched pairs, and each control arm's evaluable share is a payload field, never silently absorbed into a denominator. Matching failure is candidate-correlated (tokenizers chunk date digits differently), so denominator loss is not random across the candidates being compared — the shares are reported per candidate for exactly that reason.
  • Stage-start screens (fail-closed, leading/distraction precedent): the block template, the neutral unit, and every arm string are audited against the catalog's special-token literals (audit_special_token_literals), and the neutral text is screened against every fixture's expected answer and every candidate's decoded boundary text (screen_filler discipline). A failure fails the stage closed (dateline_screen_failed), before any generation.

docs.title: Eligibility screen (G5†)
docs.text:
A fixture whose expected answer is itself date-derived measures copying, not sensitivity: the date line hands the model the exact string to copy. Screened fixtures are excluded from every treated population and form their own record class; the screened share per candidate is a payload field.

The design's original screen — scorerlens.rung_match of the expected against the arm strings — is unsound as specified (A F5, executed; B §1 reproduced the battery verbatim): rung-4 is an equality predicate with no containment component, so expecteds 21, 2026, and October match nothing, and an expected written as a date in a third format (October 21, 2026) matches nothing either. The opposite pole — substring/containment — is equally unsound (executed: equivalent_claim('1', '2026-10-21') is True, and a containment screen voids nearly every single-digit numeric fixture, precisely the population the source paper's math result concerns). The frozen screen is component-wise equivalence, amended per B §1:

  • Rule name (frozen): dateline-components-r4-v1.
  • The expected is decomposed too (B's granularity correction: A's cure compared the whole expected against each component and so missed every multi-token date-derived expected — March 3, October 21, 21 October). Both sides are tokenised on non-alphanumeric boundaries and compared as component sets.
  • A fixture is screened out if any of these holds:
  • rung-4 equality of the whole expected against any full arm string;
  • rung-4 equality of any expected component against any date-bearing component of any arm string — years, month numbers, month names, day numbers, weekday names, and the frozen abbreviation aliases (Jan, Feb, Mar, Apr, Jun, Jul, Aug, Sep, Sept, Oct, Nov, Dec; Mon, Tue, Tues, Wed, Thu, Thur, Thurs, Fri, Sat, Sun). Carrier words (Today's, date, is, Context) are not components: B executed rung_match('is', 'is', 4) = True, and screening on envelope words would void common-word expecteds for a property of the envelope, not the date;
  • a closed-format date-parse leg: the whole expected is tried against a frozen list of explicit formats (ISO YYYY-MM-DD; D Month YYYY; Month D, YYYY; D/M/YYYY; M/D/YYYY; D.M.YYYY; YYYY/M/D) using the protocol's own frozen English month table — no strptime %B/%A, no locale, no new dependency (the stdlib has no general date parser; B §1.2(c)). Slash dates are ambiguous by construction (3/4/2026 is 2026-03-04 or 2026-04-03): an expected is excluded if either reading lands on an arm date — over-exclusion, disclosed. A year-less month/day (March 3, 21 October) whose month/day equals an arm date's month/day is likewise excluded.
  • Rung-4's collapse of leading-zero and decimal variants (021, 21.0 rung-match the day component 21) is a deliberate over-exclusion, disclosed here: the screen is a copy/priming screen over values, not a byte screen, and leading's donor eligibility already treats rung-4-equal answers as the same answer. The screened share is reported so the cost stays visible.
  • Scope is fixture-level (one flag, clean denominators; the arm-level alternative makes every pair's population different). Blank expecteds are not screened — they are their own record class (expected_blank, leading precedent).
  • A fixture whose messages state a date turns the arm into a hierarchy-style conflict rather than a sensitivity measurement: fixtures whose message text contains a date-parse-leg hit are flagged (message_date_bearing) and excluded from the treated populations as their own class, reported beside the screened share.
  • Pin battery (from A's execution and B's counterexamples, all become tests): 21 screened, 2026 screened, October screened, Wednesday screened, October 21, 2026 screened, February 29 and October 21 screened (year-less month/day leg), Oct screened (alias), March 3 not screened (no arm date falls on it — the screen is arm-relative, not a general date detector), 3/4/2026 not screened unless a reading hits an arm date, 021 screened (disclosed collapse), is not screened, 26 not screened (no arm component carries that value — substring's false positives die), while 2 is screened: it rung-matches the leap arm's zero-padded ISO month component 02 under the same disclosed value collapse. (Corrected during the build: the battery as first drafted claimed 2 unscreened, which the executed screen disproved — the component set is taken from the arm strings as rendered, padding included.)

docs.title: Records (G8, M4)
docs.text:
The record schema is leading's, adopted wholesale: one ground record per (candidate, fixture) holding the native cell plus one cell per treated arm; per-fixture classes vacuous, expected_blank, echo_fixture, screened, message_date_bearing; per-cell input_tokens, boundary_found, boundary_text_match, answer digest, construction classification (id_exact vs text_level with seam token ids — a candidate whose prefix merges into [Context] must be distinguishable from a clean render), and per-cell degradation (arm_context_exceeded, control_evaluable: False, never a silent drop).

M4's rule (from the numform F3 backlog): ground records carry answer digests only. The verdict is recomputed by the validator as answer_digest == expected_digest ∧ boundary_found — there is no stored derived answer field to forge. Any derived answer field (parsed date, normalised value, …) is forbidden in dateline records unless digest-bound; numform's own unbound field was closed the same way in cycle 190 (digest-bound answer text, re-parsed by its validator) — dateline never needed the fix, because it never stored the unbound field in the first place.

Byte-cap arithmetic (the driver is cells per record, since the 2,400 ground-record cap already folds in the candidate multiplication): leading carries ~3.9 KB/record at 5 cells (native + 4 treated); dateline carries 29 cells (native + 28 treated) of the same minimal shape. The implementation must measure the real per-record bytes on the shipped schema before fixing MAX_RECORDS_BYTES, show the arithmetic in the module, and set the cap so the legal-maximum payload (2,400 records) fits under the 32 MiB whole-file loader limit with headroom — if the measured schema cannot fit, the schema is trimmed, never the record cap lowered silently. (A's "~9.0 MiB at 19 cells" was an estimate, not a measurement — B §5; the build replaces it with the measured number.)

docs.title: Readouts (G3, G6†, G9†)
docs.text:
Scoring is the native exact-match + boundary conjunction, unchanged.

Headline: per-pair discordant contrasts, partitioned by pair type. The design's original headline — "fraction of fixtures whose verdict differs between any two date arms" — is a union over C(24,2) = 276 pairs under the amended format set, of which 84 are pure-date (same format, different value: 28 per format × 3), 24 are pure-format (same value, different format: 3 per value × 8), and 168 change date and format together. A union over that population saturates under generic fragility — under independent per-arm failure probability q, P(any-pair flip) = 1 − (1−q)^k − q^k reaches 0.56 at q = 0.05, k = 16 — so a checkpoint with 5% per-arm wobble would headline as "56% date-flip". (The independence assumption makes that table a worst case, not an expectation — real failures correlate across arms and lower the union — and it is quoted only with that caveat.) The shipped readouts are therefore:

  • Pure-date pair table (the headline family): per candidate, per format, per value pair (28 × 3): discordant counts in leading's shape (pass-A-only / pass-B-only / both / neither) with the frozen floors below and a total classification function.
  • Pure-format pair table (the format control): per candidate, per value, per format pair (3 × 8): same shape. This is numform's axis, reported so a date claim can be checked against the format effect on the same fixtures — never merged into a date number.
  • Cross-both pairs are not computed and feed no statistic. Any retained union statistic is pure-date-only, uses the all-arms-completed denominator (fixtures completed in every date arm of the union — a different, smaller set than any per-pair denominator, defined here because the design left it undefined), and prints beside the date-loss baseline below, never alone.

Floors and classification: MIN_PAIRED_EVALUABLE = 6, MIN_DISCORDANT = 2 (leading's frozen constants), and a total classification over (n_paired, a_only, b_only) in leading's vocabulary. Below the floors the readout is "insufficient" with denominators shown — the shipped example search set has 2 fixtures, so on the example every classification is insufficient by construction, and the CLI help says so with the real budget (the --leading help precedent).

Date-loss subset (G6†; the design's "pure-date caving", renamed). Nothing is planted here for the model to adopt, so leading's word "caving" — which in leading's payload splits by byte-exact adoption of the plant — is not reused.
