The subset is date-attributable loss, defined per date value with formats collapsed: a fixture counts toward value v's loss set when it passes the no-date control and fails v, over the denominator of fixtures evaluable in the control and in v in at least one format (per-value denominators, defined per value, not globally). The truth table per value carries the lie cell, which is what separates the readings: loss with the lie also failed is consistent with "any date text perturbs"; loss with the lie passed is content-specific. The asymmetric counterpart — fails the control, passes every date arm — is reported beside the loss counts; a subset printed without its counterpart and without the per-pair table is not a shipped readout shape.

Native's role (G6†, F7 as downgraded by B). Native enters no flip, loss, or paired population. Its only roles are the per-record baseline and the per-arm selection-flip comparison (the leading/distraction pattern). One sentence, frozen here because the design listed native first among "arms" and a builder could reasonably have included it.

Selection and the common population (G9†). Per-arm selection is re-applied per arm and withheld when completed fixture sets differ across candidates for that condition (withholding is per condition across candidates; arms do not withhold each other — A's "withheld almost always" prognosis is not adopted as a premise). The primary cross-candidate vehicle is leading's common-population readout: fixtures in every candidate's population, with the pure-date pair table recomputed over that population. Per-arm selection is the secondary readout.

Falsification (G11†, M1). The design's clause — "date arms never flip a verdict that the no-date control doesn't also flip" — is incoherent as written: a flip is a pairwise property and a single control arm cannot "also flip". Restated in the shipped vocabulary: for a candidate, the date-content claim is falsified on this fixture set when every pure-date pair's discordant count is zero and every date value's loss count is zero — the section then reports exactly that (available, zero discordants, denominators shown). That restated condition, not the original sentence, is what the section prints.

docs.title: Diff validator (G8, F11)
docs.text:
diff-reports gains a dateline section held to the cycle-187 standard. The validator carries its own literal copy of the arm table — every date string in every format, the block template, the joiner, the neutral unit, the sizing-rule name, the lie literal — as _DATELINE_* constants in diffreports.py, never imported from dateline.py (independence is the point; the _LEADING_TEMPLATES / _numform_recompute precedent). It rebuilds the protocol fingerprint from those frozen scalars plus the payload's fixture-set digest and backend fingerprint, recomputes every aggregate above from the ground records, verifies control matching from per-cell input_tokens, and enforces the record caps. Two validator-specific rules:

  • Weekday recomputation: the validator parses each arm string back to (year, month, day) with its own frozen English month table and recomputes the weekday via datetime.date.weekday() mapped through its own frozen English weekday table (no strftime, no locale — the validator carries a small date parser, deliberately). Every non-lie weekday-bearing arm's weekday name must equal the recomputed one; the lie arm must equal the frozen lie literal and differ from its recomputed weekday. A validator that derived weekdays instead of checking them would silently correct the lie into an honest arm.
  • Stated limit: the eligibility screen is a property of expected text, and payloads carry digests only. The validator checks the screened/message-date-bearing flags' cross-candidate constancy (leading's reference-field pattern) but cannot re-derive them. This sentence also appears, in substance, in the validator's docstring, as leading's does.
  • Primary-pair binding (cycle 196, oversight edge-case F3): primary_decision / primary_winner are bound to the run-level decision vocabulary (compatible_on_fixture_set, held_out_failed, ambiguous, no_candidate, cancelled, failed), with the winner required to be one of the payload's own candidate names exactly when the decision is winner-bearing, and None otherwise. Before the binding, the pair was only type-checked, so a label contradicting its own section's arm outcomes could validate. What the binding does not do is recompute the parent run's decision: the section does not carry the parent run's fixture outcomes, so within the vocabulary the decision remains stage-attested. The same binding applies to the repetition, distraction, and leading validators, which carry the same pair under the same mapping.

Both test oracles (cycle-27 and cycle-67) mirror the validator in the same push, per the standing oracle blast-radius rule; after adding the section, the full identical conjunction is audited for silently omitted sections (the cycle-186 lesson).

docs.title: Budget (G2†)
docs.text:
Priced for the amended protocol, not the as-written design (whose §(d) claimed "~6–8 treated arms" for its own 18):

component arms generations at the legal maximum (24 candidates × 100 fixtures) date arms (8 values × 3 formats) 24 57,600 no-date controls (1 per format) 3 7,200 weekday-lie 1 2,400 treated total 28 67,200

Native is reused at zero cost. 67,200 is 2.8× the largest budget shipped before (distraction, 24,000) — the price of the full value × format crossing plus per-format controls, stated here and in the CLI help with this decomposition, before any run. The de-crossed alternative (weekday-ISO on the anchor ±1-day pair only) was rejected: it would leave the lie's format present for only two values and break the pair partition's uniformity — but it is named here so the rejection is a decision, not an oversight.

docs.title: Pin blast radius (G12†)
docs.text: Same push: test_cycle44 source-file pin 52 → 53 (dateline.py); cycle-179 dispatch tables gain the --dateline row and the _run_dateline_probe helper; cycle-31/64/84 flag audits as they apply; reporting's three touchpoints (compute, TOC tuple, body concatenation) with the TOC entry immediately after numform, before the post-hoc block; the reporting section returns empty on a missing dateline key so sample-report regeneration stays byte-identical (the sample runs none of the post-cycle-179 probes — B M6); README/USAGE/VALIDATION/CHANGELOG updated with the measured test count and coverage after the gate, never before.

docs.title: Instruction-density design (cycle 204, v2 — adjudicated)
docs.text: Wave-9 rank 3. Question: when one prompt carries many simultaneous instructions, at which density does adherence start dropping, and how does satisfaction vary by serial position — measured per template family on a local checkpoint, with every constraint decidable from a digest commitment and every verdict re-derived by the diff validator. v1 was rejected by the cycle-204 adversarial round (two FATAL findings: no satisfiability guarantee; an uncalibrated falsification statistic); this v2 incorporates the adjudication in agents_out/cycle204/coordinator_adjudication.md.

docs.title: Utility
docs.text: A practitioner stacking simultaneous instructions into one prompt learns, per template family on their own checkpoint, how adherence falls as simultaneous-instruction density rises from solo to sixteen, and how satisfaction at full density varies across early, middle, and late serial positions — before shipping a template under which the later instructions silently stop being followed. Position claims are scoped to what the denominators support (see Readouts): per-position rates at full density carry n = 20 per cell, so the headline position readout is band-pooled.

docs.title: What this probe is not
docs.text:
• Not IFScale (Jaroslawicz, Whiting, Shah & Maamari, arXiv:2507.11538 — verified against the abstract in this cycle): 500 keyword-inclusion instructions on a long business report, 20 frontier API models, best 68% at max density, bias towards earlier instructions. That is the phenomenon at API scale on long free-form output; it does not vary the chat template, does not run under exact-token discipline, and its output imports a verbosity confound this design removes with short answers. The uniqueness here is the combination: simultaneous-instruction density × serial position × template family, on a local checkpoint, with digest-decidable constraints and a recomputing diff validator. The claim is the combination, never first.
  • Not hierarchy (two conflicting privileged instructions), not distraction (irrelevant text carrying no demands), not multiturn (instructions spread over turns), not structured (one schema, adherence only). None varies the count of simultaneous compatible instructions as the independent variable.
  • Not a judge-based instrument: no LLM scores anything.

docs.title: The digest-decidability constraint (slate adjudication)
docs.text: The diff validator derives satisfaction from stored digest data alone — never from stored satisfaction booleans. The vocabulary is capped to what a word-level commitment can decide, and the cap is printed here: case, sentence, and paragraph structure constraints (all-lowercase, no-commas, N sentences, bullet form) are NOT decidable from the commitment and are excluded from v1 by name. One deliberate measurement choice, stated where a reader can see it: word identity is exact after normalization — include_word("seven") scores an answer of "7" as failure; there is no digit↔word mapping.

docs.title: Construction
docs.text:
CASE_COUNT = 20 cases, generated from the run seed by a frozen generator (density.py); the diff validator carries an independent mirror of the generator, the rendering, and the checking rule.

Each case has:

  • A base task from a frozen pool of short-answer task templates over synthetic content. The base instruction asks for a short answer and carries NO numeric length demand (length demands live only in word_count_at_most, where they are counted). Each case carries expected_word_digest: the SHA-256 of the task value's normalized word (multi-word values: the ordered hash list's digest), so task performance is measurable from the commitment (task-value presence) without a whole-answer digest — a compliant answer at high density necessarily differs from the canonical task answer as a string.
  • A frozen ordered list of 16 constraints, positions 1..16. The K-density prompt for K in {2, 4, 8, 16} is the base task plus the first K constraints; K = 1 is the solo arm of constraint 1 (see Arms). A constraint's serial position is identical at every density that includes it.

docs.title: Constraint vocabulary (frozen) and kind allocation
docs.text:
Kinds (each a pure function of the word commitment):

  1. include_word(W) — the answer's word multiset contains W.
  2. start_word(W) — the answer's first normalized word is W.
  3. end_word(W) — the answer's last normalized word is W.
  4. word_count_at_most(N) — the answer's word count <= N.

Kind allocation per case is FIXED: 4 include, 4 start, 4 end, 4 count, in a kind order that rotates across cases by case index (case c starts the repeating kind cycle at offset c mod 4), so each position carries each kind exactly 5 times across the 20 cases. Count parameters come from the frozen set {8, 12, 16, 24}.

docs.title: Satisfiability invariant (generator-enforced, mirrored)
docs.text: Per case: all start_word constraints share ONE target; all end_word constraints share ONE target; the distinct word targets across groups — 4 include targets, the start target, the end target, the expected task word — are pairwise distinct AFTER normalization (D <= 7 distinct words); and min(N over the case's count constraints) >= D, which the frozen N set guarantees (8 > 7). A satisfying answer always exists (start target, include targets, task word, end target in <= 7 words). The invariant is proven by test over the pools and seed sweeps, including a pinned perfect-model test: a constructed perfect follower scores discordance f = 0 and joint satisfaction 20/20. Stated limit: at k16 the start and end demands repeat (same target four times), so for positional kinds the density treatment is partly a repetition treatment; per-kind readouts keep this visible.

docs.title: Word commitment and normalization (frozen rule)
docs.text:
For each generated answer the stage records ONE commitment object: word_hashes, the ordered list of SHA-256 hashes of the answer's normalized words (multiplicity preserved), and word_list_digest, SHA-256 of the list's canonical encoding (compact JSON, frozen in the RULE_TEXT). A word is a maximal run of alphanumeric characters, case-folded; every other character is a separator. Derived from the list, everywhere (stage aggregation and validator alike): the word multiset (count the list), word_count (the list's length), the first word (list head) and last word (list tail), or None when the list is empty. The first word is the first NORMALIZED word: leading tokens that normalize to nothing are skipped by construction.

Satisfaction of every constraint is DERIVED from the commitment; no satisfaction boolean is stored (the rotation F4 pattern — the primitive determines the verdicts for all four kinds). Records also carry answer_digest (SHA-256 of the exact boundary-cut answer text, the standing pattern).

Stated limits. (1) Fidelity residue: the commitment's internal consistency is validator-checked (digest over the list), but its fidelity to the generated answer is stage-attested — no digest of free text admits membership recompute against the text itself, and the verbatim-text alternative (the numform cycle-190 exception) was ruled out for this probe by the slate adjudication. (2) Exposure: the ordered hash list discloses the answer's word SEQUENCE to a dictionary pass over the (public) frozen pools — a strictly greater degree of disclosure than a whole-answer digest, of the same class; accepted because the determination property (F4) requires the ordered primitive, and the answers are short synthetic-task outputs.

docs.title: Rendering (frozen)
docs.text: Each kind's instruction template, the constraint-list joiner and numbering, the base task templates, and the neutral statements are frozen text in density.py, carried by digest in the protocol (the needle SIZING_RULE_TEXT pattern). The payload carries, per (case, arm), the user-turn content digest; the validator's mirror re-renders the content and requires digest equality — the treatment is derived, not attested. Records carry input_tokens under the rotation arm_tokens discipline.

docs.title: Draw rules (frozen; the mirror reproduces them exactly)
docs.text: Slot order per case: task template, task parameters, the sham arm's neutral statements, then per position 1..16 the constraint kind (fixed by the allocation rotation) and its parameter. Collision rule, with "occurs" defined as normalized-word equality: word targets must be distinct across groups (above) and must not occur in the case's base task text; constraint 1's target additionally must not occur in the case's neutral statements (the only constraint that shares an arm with them). Redraw scope: the offending parameter only, at its own slot counter; redrawn parameters are re-checked against the same frozen texts. Termination: pools are sized so the redraw always has a fresh candidate (pool sizes frozen in density.py and stated in the protocol; the generator test sweeps seeds to prove termination). Pool screen (pinned property, proven by test): all pool words are pairwise distinct after normalization, and no pool word equals a number word after normalization.

docs.title: Screening (rotation-shaped)
docs.text:
Stage level: before generation, all frozen texts (task templates, kind renderings, neutral pool, word pools) are audited with audit_special_token_literals against every candidate, and boundary-text containment is checked; failure fails the stage closed with density_screen_failed. Per case: a case whose rendered texts contain a candidate's decoded boundary text is screened as a unit, with its own counter. Records carry a per-record detail in {"", arm_evaluation_failed, arm_context_exceeded}; records with a detail, and boundary-screened cases' records, are present in the record list (completeness below) with word_hashes = [] and word_count = 0.

Live population: records with detail "" whose case is not boundary-screened for that candidate. There is NO word-cap screen: generation is bounded by the frozen max_new_tokens (64), so every live record's commitment is complete and every kind's verdict is decidable for it in both directions. Zero-word live records (empty answer: first emitted token is the boundary, or the answer normalizes to no words) carry their own counter and are excluded from word_count_at_most checked denominators (their count verdicts are vacuous); they still fail word-target kinds, decidably.

Screen accounting per candidate, counters disjoint by the stated order (boundary screen first, then detail, then zero-word within live): n_generated, n_boundary_screened, n_detail_screened, n_zero_word, n_live — all printed.

docs.title: Arms
docs.text:
Per case and candidate, 21 generations:

  • 16 solo arms solo_1..solo_16: base task + only constraint j — the per-constraint paired baselines. solo_1 IS the K=1 density arm (the v1 design generated it twice under two names; merged).
  • 4 density arms k2, k4, k8, k16: base task + the first K constraints.
  • 1 sham arm sham: base task + constraint 1 + neutral statements selected by the frozen rule below, separating "many instructions" from "much text".

Sham construction: block length is the user-turn word count of the appended block. Neutrals are appended in frozen slot order, wrapping to the start of the drawn list, until the sham block's word count first reaches or exceeds the case's k16 block word count; both block lengths are recorded per record through the content commitment, and the selection is a deterministic function the mirror recomputes. (Build-time amendment, measured: without wrapping the sham stayed shorter than k16 in 3,992 of 4,000 generated cases — the length match the control exists for almost never held. Wrapping adds no pool words: the neutrals are pinned pool-free, so repetition cannot smuggle a target in.) The sham readout is computed over cases live in all three arms (solo_1, sham, k16), denominators printed.

docs.title: Records
docs.text: Exactly 21 × CASE_COUNT records per candidate, in canonical (case, arm) order; the validator rejects any other count, order, or arm set, and rejects duplicate candidate names (the run-level guard's clause, stated as rotation's validator states it). Each record carries: candidate, case index, arm id, detail, answer_digest, word_hashes, word_list_digest, word_count, input_tokens, the content digest of its arm, and the backend fingerprint via the shared _backend_fingerprint guard (cycle-202 F2). The protocol object carries: the frozen rule texts by digest (generation, rendering, normalization+checking), pool sizes, densities, CASE_COUNT, the paired floor and discordant-case floor, alpha, the word cap implied by max_new_tokens, and the record/payload caps. Caps: MAX_DENSITY_RECORDS = 10,080 (21 × 20 × 24); MAX_DENSITY_PAYLOAD_BYTES = 52 MiB (sizing: a record's ordered list is at most 64 entries × 68 B ≈ 4.4 KB plus ≈ 0.4 KB of fields ≈ 4.8 KB; 10,080 × 4.8 KB ≈ 48.4 MiB — the derivation, printed per the house pattern). Stage detail vocabulary: {cancelled, density_record_budget_exceeded, density_screen_failed}.

docs.title: Readouts
docs.text:
Per candidate, over live records; every rate is None iff its denominator is 0; every readout prints its denominators.

  • Satisfaction by density: for each K in {1, 2, 4, 8, 16}, the pooled satisfaction over that arm's constraints (K = 1 reads solo_1), printed BESIDE the same constraints' pooled solo rate (the composition control). The raw curve is labelled not composition-controlled.
  • Task-value presence by arm (the F6 readout): share of live records whose commitment contains the expected task word, per arm, beside the constraint readouts.
  • Position at full density: per-position satisfaction within k16 (16 rates, n = 20 denominators, descriptive), and the band-pooled headline: positions 1–5, 6–11, 12–16 pooled rates with denominators.
  • Per-kind satisfaction at solo and at k16, with denominators (the repetition-limit readout for positional kinds).
  • Joint satisfaction at k16: share of live k16 records with all 16 constraints satisfied, with denominator (the IFScale headline analogue — meaningful only because the satisfiability invariant guarantees it is attainable).
  • Sham readout: position-1 satisfaction in solo_1, sham, and k16 over the intersected live population, with the two block lengths printed.
  • Discordance: per (case, position) paired solo vs k16 satisfaction over eligible pairs (both records live; for count-kind pairs, neither record zero-word): f = solo-pass/k16-fail count, p = solo-fail/k16-pass count, printed pooled and per position (the per-position table is a density-and-position mixture — solo_j sits at effective position 1 — and is labelled as such).

docs.title: Falsification (pre-registered, scoped)
docs.text: Claim, scoped to the contrast the test supports: for a candidate, per-constraint satisfaction at full density (k16) equals its solo satisfaction — independence of the endpoint density contrast; intermediate densities are descriptive (the satisfaction curve), and a non-monotone intermediate dip does not falsify and is not claimed to. Decision, a total function per candidate over the eligible pairs: aggregate discordance per case, d_c = f_c − p_c. If the candidate has no live records, its block is unavailable. If the number of cases with d_c != 0 is below 6, the verdict is insufficient — the boolean is withheld, never defaulted to acquittal, and the counts are printed. Otherwise: falsified iff Σf > Σp AND the exact two-sided sign test over the discordant cases gives p <= 0.05; the p-value, f, p, and the discordant-case count are printed beside the boolean. The level is per-candidate; across 24 candidates at alpha = 0.05, roughly one false falsification is expected by chance (1 − 0.95^24 ≈ 0.71 for at least one), and the section text says so.

docs.title: Diff validator
docs.text: diff_density in diffreports.py with a full independent mirror: regenerate the cases, re-render every arm's content and require the payload's content digests to match, verify each record's commitment (list digest), derive every satisfaction verdict, task-presence verdict, headline, and the falsification decision (including the sign test), and require equality with the payload. Availability and insufficient states are mirrored per candidate. The diff-section blast radius is the standing three-element one (test_cycle67 oracle + flip_identical anchor + _identical_expected; test_cycle27 oracle + stub), verified by executed grep at build time.

docs.title: Budget
docs.text: Generations: 21 arms × 20 cases = 420 per candidate; 10,080 at the 24-candidate legal max. Solo arms are 16 of 21 arms; they earn their cost because the decision (fixed) and the composition control both consume them — the cycle-204 F17 sequencing condition. Construction is one render per arm. Records and payload caps as above.

docs.title: Pin blast radius (rewritten from executed greps)
docs.text: cli.py flag --density + dispatch + help; experiments.py stage mirroring rotation_stage; reporting.py three touchpoints (compute, TOC tuple, body concatenation); diffreports.py section + validator; new test file tests/test_cycle204_density.py plus the scoped test files the gate names; test_cycle27 and test_cycle67 oracle extensions (grep-counted at build time, rotation's footprint: 25 / 80 placement-era hits are the model); test_cycle179 dispatch e2e pattern; test_cycle44 mypy source-file pin 60 → 61; test_cycle178 VALIDATION header pin cycles 10–204 AND the live counts it pins (VALIDATION test-count lines and the CI-scope ruff file count); VALIDATION.md first-Evidence prose probe list gains the density entry; README test count, capability bullet, and BOTH section enumerations (the diff-reports sentence and the sample-report paragraph — grep both); USAGE §8.51; CHANGELOG entry in the same push; RESEARCH_LOG cycle-204 entry (exists — design phase already appended; the build appends its closure half); sample-report impact verified at build time (regenerate byte-identically twice if the section joins it).

docs.title: Open points — dispositions
docs.text:
1. Solo-arm cost: PAID (16 solos kept; k1 merged into solo_1). The entry-density alternative covers positions 1–8 only and changes the estimand per position; rejected with the reason recorded.
  2. Sham position confound: position 1 is matched across solo_1/sham/k16 (held by both red teams); the length and population confounds are fixed by the frozen selection rule and the intersected population.
  3. Fidelity residue: stands as a stated limit (above); the commitment's internal structure is now fully determining (F5 fix), so the residue covers origin only.
  4. Vacuous count satisfaction: zero-word records are counted and excluded from count-kind denominators (F13 fix); the residue is printed, not hidden.
  5. Pooled-only boolean: replaced by the case-aggregated sign decision with an insufficient state (F2/F10 fixes); the claim is scoped to the endpoint contrast (B-F5).
  6. Replication control (B's alternative for the duplicated arm): considered and deferred — the case-level decision does not consume a noise-floor readout; if a future cycle needs one, the duplicate arm is the place to add it, with this paragraph as the pointer.

docs.title: Determinism self-audit — design contract
docs.text: model-protocol-lab verify --determinism --model <checkpoint> <report-dir> re-executes a recorded run's search observations against a locally loaded checkpoint and reports whether the recorded output tokens reproduce exactly. This document is the contract: what the audit claims, what it refuses to claim, and the invariants the implementation is held to. The audit lives in model_protocol_lab/determinism.py; verify.py wires it into the verify command.

docs.title: Why this exists
docs.text:
Every lab result rests on one assumption: greedy generation on the recorded checkpoint is deterministic, so the recorded output_ids are the tokens that checkpoint produces for the recorded input_ids. Plain verify re-derives the decision from the stored artifact (decision replay); nothing re-checked the generation itself. The determinism audit is the generation-replay counterpart: it turns the assumption into evidence, one way or the other.

Monday-morning utility: a reviewer challenges a published result — "prove the backend actually generated those tokens deterministically" — and this command answers with a certificate or a per-cell divergence table instead of an assertion.

docs.title: What the audit proves, and what it does not
docs.text:
• It proves a statement about the re-execution: in this audit run, with the checkpoint identified by the recorded backend fingerprint, every re-executed recorded search cell did or did not reproduce its recorded output_ids token-for-token.
  • It does not prove the original run was deterministic. The environment may have changed since the original run; the audit observes only its own re-execution.
  • A divergence is a backend-determinism finding — evidence about the backend, its numeric path, or its environment. It is not an instrument failure, not an artifact-integrity failure (plain verify covers artifact self-consistency), and not proof that the original run's decision was wrong: it shows the recorded tokens do not reproduce here, now, on this backend.
  • The audit detects divergence; it does not diagnose the mechanism. The known mechanism in batched serving stacks is lack of batch invariance — reduction order in normalisation, matmul, and attention kernels varies with batch composition, so temperature-0 outputs vary run to run (He, "Defeating Nondeterminism in LLM Inference", Thinking Machines Lab, 2025, DOI 10.64434/tml.20250910: 1,000 greedy completions of one prompt produced 80 distinct outputs; batch-invariant kernels produced 1,000 identical ones). The lab's backend is sequential, batch size 1, full-prefix recompute, fp32 — that mechanism is largely absent in-process, so divergence under this backend points more at checkpoint, library-version, device, or context drift. The fingerprint gate (below) rules most of those out before any cell runs; what remains is a genuine numeric-path finding.
  • Search observations only. Held-out observations are not re-executed: the search set is the selection evidence, and the bound keeps the audit's cost at or below the largest search phase the lab can record.
  • Greedy only, like everything in the lab.

docs.title: The certificate
docs.text: When every claimed cell reproduces, the audit emits a determinism certificate. The word is a local label, not a term of art: the certificate is unsigned and self-issued, exactly like the pack seal. It states who ran it (the operator, on their own machine), what it covers, and what it does not. It binds to the exact cells compared via cells_digest — SHA-256 over the canonical JSON of (candidate, fixture, input_ids, output_ids) for every attempted cell, in recorded order — plus the backend fingerprint, the run seed, and the token budget, so a certificate cannot be transplanted onto another artifact or another cell set. It also states what is not certified: the recorded prompts are replayed as stored; their authenticity against the fixture files and format definitions is a property of the original run, not of this audit.

docs.title: Invariants
docs.text:
• I1 — one seed derivation. The audit re-derives each cell's per-request seed through core.request_seed_for, the same function core.evaluate uses (extracted verbatim from the original inline derivation). Fixture IDs are used byte-exactly as recorded (surrogatepass encoding, no normalisation anywhere in the audit path): an NFC and an NFD spelling of the same visible ID are different IDs with different seeds, and the audit must not "help" by normalising. (surfacenoise.py carries a pre-existing private copy of the same formula for its own protocol; a drift-guard test pins the two derivations equal on edge-case IDs.)
  • I2 — fingerprint gate before any generation. If the replay backend's fingerprint differs from the recorded backend_fingerprint, the audit is unavailable and zero generate calls happen. The fingerprint binds checkpoint assets, library versions, device, and context limit, so a mismatch means "a different experiment", never "nondeterminism".
  • I3 — recorded cells are validated before they are blamed. A legitimately recorded completed cell satisfies hard invariants of the recording pipeline: non-empty input_ids, output_ids of exactly max_new_tokens (a completed generation reached the cap), integer non-boolean IDs, and — when the replay backend exposes a vocabulary bound — IDs inside the vocabulary. A cell violating any of these cannot have been recorded by this pipeline against this backend; it is an artifact defect and is reported as a skip, never as divergence and never as a backend error.
  • I4 — fail closed, in fixed vocabulary. The audit never raises on a malformed or hostile artifact. Every defect lands in a documented detail code (below). Backend error text is never exported: replay errors are classified through the same allowlist core uses for recorded observations (core._BACKEND_ERROR_CODES); anything else collapses to backend_reported_error. A replay context_limit_exceeded is a per-cell skip (replay_context_limit_exceeded): with the fingerprint binding the context limit, a completed recorded cell cannot legitimately hit it, so it marks an artifact inconsistency, not a backend failure.
  • I5 — full denominators. n_cells counts every recorded search observation. Skipped and errored cells are counted and listed, never dropped. A certificate requires every claimed (completed) cell to have been attempted and reproduced: any blocking skip (stripped entry, invalid/length-inconsistent/out-of-vocabulary recorded IDs, replay context limit, cell budget) or backend error caps the verdict at inconclusive. Cells the original run itself did not complete (observation_not_completed) are scope, not gaps: the certificate states their count.
  • I6 — a partial run earns no certificate. If the artifact records an aborted search (decision cancelled/failed, or any search entry not aggregate-eligible), the recorded cells are still replayed and reported, but the verdict is capped at inconclusive with detail search_incomplete: the audit does not certify a selection process that never finished.
  • I7 — bounded cost. At most MAX_AUDIT_CELLS = 2400 cells are attempted — 24 candidates × 100 search fixtures, the largest search phase run_experiment accepts — so a foreign artifact (the loader admits up to 32 MiB) cannot turn the audit into an unbounded generation job. Every claimed cell is re-executed individually; duplicate prompts are not memoised, because a backend whose output depends on call count is precisely the nondeterminism this audit exists to catch.
  • I8 — plain verify is untouched. Without --determinism, output is byte-identical to before. The audit section and its check exist only in the opt-in mode, and backend construction is skipped entirely when the artifact precheck fails, so a malformed artifact never triggers a checkpoint load.

docs.title: Verdict and check mapping
docs.text:
The audit verdict is one of deterministic, diverged, inconclusive, or unavailable (available: false with a detail code: artifact_malformed, unsupported_schema_version, observations_stripped, no_replayable_cells, backend_fingerprint_mismatch). Inside verify, the determinism_replay check maps: deterministic → passed; diverged → failed (the recorded outputs positively contradict the re-execution — verify's standing doctrine for failed); any inconclusive or unavailable outcome → unavailable, with counts in the detail. Consequence, stated plainly: verify --determinism can exit 0 while its determinism check is unavailable (for example when the backend errors during re-execution). Exit 0 means no check failed; the JSON determinism section is the audit's actual result and must be read.

Per-cell outcomes: reproduced, diverged (with first_divergence, shared_prefix, and both lengths), error (fixed detail codes: generate_failed, invalid_generation, backend_reported_cancelled, an allowlisted backend code, or backend_reported_error), and skipped (recorded_ids_invalid, recorded_length_inconsistent, recorded_ids_out_of_vocab, observation_not_completed, observations_stripped, replay_context_limit_exceeded, audit_cell_budget_exceeded). Cells carry entry index, candidate, and fixture for identity, and never the token IDs themselves — those live in the artifact; cells_digest binds them.

docs.title: Falsifiable claims (pre-registered, cycle 173)
docs.text:
• F1. A deterministic scripted backend whose output is a pure function of (input_ids, seed) reproduces every recorded completed search cell token-exactly: verdict deterministic, certificate issued, digest matching an independent recomputation.
  • F2. A call-count-dependent backend diverges on at least one cell, and the reported first_divergence equals an independent oracle's computation.
  • F3. The seeds the audit uses equal the seeds core.evaluate used for the same artifact — shown end-to-end with a seed-recording backend double, with expectations computed by an independent inline hashlib oracle, not by the shared helper.
  • F4. A fingerprint mismatch produces zero generate calls.
  • F5. Hostile artifacts (string IDs, negative IDs, boolean seed, non-list observations, missing keys, lone surrogates in fixture IDs) produce fixed-vocabulary output — never an exception, never a traceback.
  • F6. Flipping one recorded output token makes exactly that cell diverge, at exactly that token index; truncating one recorded output makes that cell a recorded_length_inconsistent skip, not a divergence.
  • F7. An artifact whose search aborted earns no certificate even when every recorded completed cell reproduces.

docs.title: Provenance
docs.text: Design reviewed before implementation by a four-specialist round (researcher, red-team A, red-team B with the explicit job of disproving A, verifier); the uniqueness pass is logged in docs/RESEARCH_LOG.md (cycle 173). Findings that changed this design: recorded-length and vocabulary validation before any blame (A1/A3), the replay-cost bound (A4/B2), the failed/unavailable doctrine mapping (A6), the aborted-run certificate block (A8/B), and the rejection of replay memoisation (B1).

docs.title: Round summary (coordinator #41, design round only — nothing built)
docs.text:
• Tree at main f31e72e1ace4 (cycle 212 closed green, 8,439 tests, precise coverage 95.3455%). This round was READ-ONLY except for this doc and the briefs; no suite was run, no push was made, no tag was cut or discussed.
  • Specialists (blind to each other): researcher (~/workspace/agents_out/directive/research.md), red-team A (redteam_a.md), red-team B (redteam_b.md), verifier/claims auditor (verifier.md). All four briefs landed; the verifier resolved every externally checkable claim against primary sources, re-ran every surviving PoC, and recomputed all decision math with independent code; the coordinator re-executed the load-bearing claims itself (§4). Fabrication sweep: clean — no invented symbol, no fabricated citation, and no unreproduced load-bearing number in any brief (the rank-5 clean result repeats); the failures found were line drift (all ≤9 lines, substance intact), one vacuous statistic, and one wrong author attribution, all handled in §5.
  • Convergence and divergence, in one paragraph: all three blind briefs return NO-BUILD for the candidate as specified in the circulated sketch (three directive arms appended to the last user message, verdicts through core.evaluate unchanged, selection re-applied per arm, falsified by any pass-set difference or selection flip), and the verifier upholds that unanimously, fatal by fatal, by execution — four independent stub backends through the real core.evaluate agree on the central defect. The researcher additionally specifies a redesigned instrument (categorical panel of named strings, a frozen final-line contract in every prose arm, a span-verdict headline with byte-exact demoted to an elicitation-cost readout, a panel-derived decision rule, screens, the name --response-directive) and recommends it as a resubmission candidate; the verifier reproduced its decision math exactly and ruled it a resubmission, not an amendment, under this program's own test. The coordinator concurs: the verdict is NO-BUILD — for the sketch, and as a build order for the redesigned instrument in this round. §3 records the resubmission specification in full, including the three points no brief fully closed (budget discipline at the recorded cap, the directive-bearing-fixture screen, the absent neutral-suffix control).

docs.title: 1. Why NO-BUILD: the fatal defects of the candidate as specified
docs.text: Each defect below is individually blocking and was established by execution (attribution: R = researcher, A = red-team A, B = red-team B, V = verifier, C = coordinator).

docs.title: F1 — The byte-exact scorer × prose arms: compliance is punished, disobedience rewarded (the load-bearing fatal)
docs.text: core.evaluate has no answer extraction: the scored answer is the whole decoded pre-boundary span (core.py:939 answer_ids = output_ids if cut is None else output_ids[:cut]; core.py:966 answer = decoded), and the verdict is core.py:797: exact_match = status == "completed" and answer == case.expected. A brief/steps-compliant response is by the arm's own demand a strict superstring of the expected answer, so P(pass | full compliance, brief/steps) = 0 by construction. Executed through the real evaluate with stub backends (R poc1, A scorer_stub, B scorer_stub, V scorer_poc — four independent implementations; C re-ran A's, §4): a perfectly compliant model passes brief 0/4 and steps 0/4 — including the most charitable variant, the correct final answer alone on its own final line — while a model that ignores the directives entirely passes 4/4 in every arm. The manufactured share of the arms' discordance equals the candidate's compliance rate, which the instrument never measures. The sketch's conceded mitigation (a boundary-failure taxonomy printed beside flips) does not cover the mode: the compliant failures have boundary_found=True and land in non_label under the tree's decomposition — indistinguishable from genuinely wrong answers. No shipped machinery rescues it: confidence survives its suffix only because the suffix demands a severable grammar line and its verdict is re-derived on the span (confidence.py:400-410 cell_verdict; CONFIDENCE_DESIGN records that raw evaluator verdicts on suffixed generations are "meaningless"), and an explanation is not severable — executed: parse_verbalized_confidence on a brief answer returns the whole text as the span (missing_line), and scorerlens.rung_match recovers a compliant brief/steps answer at no rung 0–4 (the ladder has no label-strip operation, scorerlens.py:53,133). Negation survived this trap by construction: a byte-identical answer-only reply contract in every arm (negation.py:125-137). The sketch's arms have different reply contracts, two of them unsatisfiable under its own scorer. This is rank-4's F3 shape (a perfect XML answer scoring schema_failed 10/10) arriving through the verdict path.

docs.title: F2 — There is no decision rule: the any-difference falsifier fires on noise with probability 1
docs.text: The sketch's falsification is "any candidate whose pass set differs between arms, or a selection flip in any arm" over 7,200 cells. Executed (A, B, V; C independently, §4): under a null of per-cell verdict jitter ε, P(any pass-set difference in the panel) = 1.000 at every ε from 0.001 to 0.05 (analytic E[discordant pairs] = 71.6 at ε=0.005, matching Monte Carlo exactly), and conditioned on a native winner existing — the only case where a selection flip is observable — P(winner loses all-pass status in ≥1 of 3 arms) = 0.951 at ε=0.01 (analytic 1−(1−p)^300, Monte-Carlo confirmed). A rule that fires with certainty under any nonzero jitter is a discordance printer wearing a falsification label (the payload / answer-syntax F2 pattern), and its two headline tests are degenerate in opposite directions: pass-set difference fires always, while at typical pass rates there is usually no native winner to flip at all. Every surviving probe in this tree pairs discordance with a derived floor and printed operating characteristics (negation (8,5), leading (6,2)); the sketch has none, and none can be borrowed — its population is the user's fixtures, whose pass distribution is data-dependent (the borrowed-floor trap of answer-syntax F5 / instruction-language F4; the researcher's poc3 confirms the borrowed (6,2) row fires 0.94–1.00 on this panel's nulls too).

docs.title: F3 — There is no ladder: the arms are incomparable bundles, and native is not a rung
docs.text: By construction from the arm texts (R §2, A F3, B F3, V P5 — unanimous): on demanded pre-answer prose, native = direct (0) < brief (one sentence) < steps (unbounded); on output restrictiveness, steps (none) < brief (one sentence) < direct ("only"); on suffix length, direct (34 chars) < steps (47) < brief (unfrozen, see F4). Brief and steps swap rung order depending on the property measured; direct is a sign flip on prose (forbidding it), not a smaller dose of it; native is a control condition, not rung 0 — under native a model may emit more prose than brief's cap allows. No single named dimension orders the arms, so "ladder" and any rung/trend language attribute a bundle (contract strictness, prose budget, prose function, length) to a dose — payload F3 in miniature. The tree's one real ladder, scorerlens, is a pipeline in which each rung consumes the previous rung's output and monotonicity is a theorem; nothing here is cumulative.

docs.title: F4 — The brief arm is not even a frozen string
docs.text: The sketch quotes direct (34 chars) and steps (47 chars) verbatim and gives brief only as a paraphrase ("a one-sentence explanation, then the final answer"). The three briefs each had to invent a different brief string (64, 60, and 55 chars) — the demonstration itself. An arm that exists only as a paraphrase cannot be audited against the tree's frozen-instrument discipline (special-token screen, length accounting, material digest): the instrument as specified is not buildable without inventing load-bearing text.

docs.title: F5 — Token-cap censoring is ordered by arm, and counting it does not fix it
docs.text: The run's default cap is 64 tokens (cli.py:198), and the recorded native run was generated at that cap. The arms place the answer at treatment-dependent positions — token 0 for native/direct, after all demanded prose for brief/steps — so the effective answer budget under one shared cap is ordered steps < brief < direct = native. Executed (A, V re-run; codepoint stub): a compliant steps output needing 78 tokens before its boundary records answer_len=64, boundary_found=False, status still completed — censored, not measured, and retained in the "common completed" population as an ordinary failure. Raising the cap for the treated arms breaks comparability with the recorded native run, which cannot be re-generated at a new cap; keeping it manufactures steps failures in proportion to explanation length. The verbosity convention the sketch echoes (a capped length is a lower bound, reported as a share) is a descriptive label over recorded runs; here the unobserved quantity is the verdict itself.

docs.title: F6 — Conditioning is outcome-dependent, the native arm is asymmetric, and the population scope is unstated
docs.text: (a) core.evaluate aborts the whole report at the first failed/cancelled cell: executed (A, V re-run), one arm-only backend error (context_limit_exceeded — exactly the error a longer treated input invites) at fixture 1 of 4 yields a failed report with 2/4 observations, aggregate_eligible=False. The "common completed set" after such an error is a prefix selected by the treatment (answer-syntax F2 verbatim), while truncated cells (F5) do the opposite damage and stay in as failures — the population split is decided by backend error mechanics, not by the design. (b) The native arm is the recorded run: held-out fixtures are evaluated in run_experiment only for the selected candidate, so a directive-arm "selection flip" can never be followed through to a held-out verdict for the new winner within the stated budget — the flip readout is a search-only hypothetical and the sketch never labels it so. (c) The sketch says "100 fixtures" without stating search-only scope; every sibling stage is search-only, and silence on population scope in a selection probe is a defect, not a detail — treated held-out fixtures with re-applied selection would be held-out contamination of exactly the kind the Split discipline exists to prevent. (d) The sketch also never states the same-run / configuration-digest obligation for the reused native baseline (the cycle-207 _require_native_match / _configuration_digest machinery, experiments.py:3884 / :3940, exists because a baseline from another configuration was silently compared before) — a spec gap, recorded as such, not an executed defect.

docs.title: F7 — The tree's only concrete population already carries the treatment's contradiction
docs.text: Executed (B fixture_conflicts; C re-ran it and read the file directly, §4): all 4 shipped example fixtures (examples/fixtures.json, 2 search + 2 held-out) carry an answer-only directive in the last user message — "Reply with exactly BLUE and nothing else.", "Now reply with exactly GREEN and nothing else.", "Return only the numeral 7.", "Replace that answer with the single word SOUTH." On such fixtures direct is a near-duplicate paraphrase of the incumbent instruction (treatment ≈ no-op), and brief/steps contradict it: the model must disobey one instruction to obey the other, so discordance measures instruction-conflict resolution — hierarchy's construct — unscreened, uncounted, and varying by fixture. Confidence's screens (confidence.py:225-247) cover blank / confidence-shaped expected answers and vacuous turns, not directive-bearing turns. The shipped example set is small (2 search fixtures), but it is the lab's own fixture style, and any realistic answer-only fixture set is affected in proportion to how well its fixtures are written. No screen is specified.

docs.title: F8 — No neutral-suffix control: discordance cannot be attributed to directive content
docs.text: Appending anything to the last user message changes the token sequence and can flip a greedy path. The sketch's only contrast is native vs directive-suffix, so its discordance pools (a) directive semantics, (b) suffix presence/length (+34/+47/+60 chars), and (c) recency effects. The tree already treats the control as mandatory: repetition.py ships a pad arm matched per (candidate, fixture) on rendered token length precisely so the repetition effect is separable from the length effect (repetition.py:66-71: ARMS ("x1", "x2", "pad"), CONTRASTS length_effect / repetition_effect). Without a length-matched neutral arm, even a scorer-fixed headline could not say the directive did it.

docs.title: F9 — Single-phrasing collinearity kills the class-level claim (instruction-language F1 pattern)
docs.text: One frozen string per directive makes treatment and rendering perfectly collinear: every discordance is an effect of these strings, with this joiner (which the sketch does not even specify). The claim that survives scoping — "appending these exact strings changed these candidates' pass sets on these fixtures in this run" — does not clear the Monday-morning bar the sketch sets itself (a prompt engineer choosing a directive for their prompt learns nothing about step-by-step directives as a class, and nothing about whether steps improves the answer, the decision-relevant quantity F1 makes unmeasurable). String scoping is the negation/instruction-language settlement and the resubmission adopts it (§3); the sketch's claim is written at class level, and at class level it is false advertising.

docs.title: Non-fatal, adjudicated (the sketch's defence, and what passed)
docs.text:
• Duplication. The brainstorm's defence — "confidence never re-applies selection per arm" — is literally true of confidence (V §1 S7: confidence_stage copies primary_decision / primary_winner from the native result) and refuted as a novelty claim about the tree: prefill re-applies selection per condition (experiments.py:2585 prefill_adherence; prefill's pre-registered claim 1 is a winner-under-condition contrast), canonical-form re-applies it per arm over a restricted shared population (canonicalform.py:599 arm_selection, :641 winner_headline), and confidence already ships the elicitation-cost flips readout (pass_to_fail / fail_to_pass vs the recorded native run). Surgery, native reuse, flips, and per-arm selection are all shipped measurements; the only unshipped element is the treatment strings — and F1 makes the treatment unmeasurable for two of its three arms. Sustained against the defence; not independently fatal to a future instrument whose novelty is argued on treatment alone (researcher §9 concedes exactly this, and §3 item 6(e) puts the judgment to the fresh review).
  • Selection re-application on user fixtures is legitimate (R §4, upheld by V as dispute D4): the numform settlement (experiments.py:11049-11051) bars winners over synthetic sets; this population is the user's own search fixtures — the same contest — with prefill/canonical-form as shipped precedents, under the conditions of §3 item 2 (restricted-set recompute, search-only labelling, primary decision untouched).
  • Passed checks (not findings): the suffix lands inside the last user turn for every catalog family (executed renders, chatml/llama3 checked explicitly; Format.render, core.py:76); the special-token audit over all 29 catalog candidates returns 0 findings for all three suffix strings; per-fixture seeds are id-derived (core.py:371 request_seed_for), so id-preserving surgery keeps arm seeds identical to native — an obligation the design must pin (the prefill id-prefixing pattern would silently break it), not a defect found; the 7,200-generation arithmetic is consistent with the tree's caps (24 candidates × 100 search fixtures, determinism.py:32-38, experiments.py:4014).
  • Naming. directive has zero hits in the package, docs/USAGE.md, README.md, and docs/FAQ.md (R, V, and C greps concur); the only hits anywhere are prose "owner directive" in docs/RESEARCH_LOG.md:3814, :5596, :5755. --directive is therefore free as a string but over-broad as a name (it names any instruction — hierarchy's whole territory), the payload §8.46 failure shape; the resubmission proposes --response-directive (§3 item 5).

docs.title: 2. Why the redesigned instrument is a resubmission, not an amendment
docs.text:
The negation round's BUILD verdict rested on a stated test: every defect was corrected by amendment to the same instrument — same population, same arms, same scorer, same joint-rule shape — whose population and arms were already frozen and executable before the round began. The payload and answer-syntax rounds rest on the complementary test: where the amendments replace an undefined or unexecutable instrument with a different one, the result is a resubmission and must be reviewed as a new design before it is built.

Measured against that test, the researcher's redesigned instrument changes: the arms (new texts carrying a frozen final-line contract; the panel is categorical and the "ladder" framing is dropped); the headline scorer (span verdict — final line equals expected, conjoined with boundary — with byte-exact demoted to a beside-the-headline elicitation-cost readout); the population discipline (fixture screens, the restricted common-completed-set selection recompute, search-only labelling); the decision rule (none in the sketch → a derived joint rule, §3 item 3); and the name (--directive → --response-directive). The sketch's instrument was never executable as a measurement in the first place: its brief arm has no string (F4), its scorer inverts its headline (F1), and its falsifier is a tautology (F2). This is the payload configuration, not the negation one.

The verdict is therefore NO-BUILD for this round. This is explicitly not a finding that the redesigned instrument is unsound: the verifier reproduced every one of its operating characteristics by independent exact enumeration (and the coordinator re-ran the enumeration, §4), it answers F1, F2, F3, and F9 by construction rather than by disclosure, and its author states its central risk himself (§3 item 6(e)). What it has never faced is a blind red team of its own: its novel machinery — the span parser over prose arms, the frozen decomposition classes, the per-run-N operating-characteristics printing, the not-yet-designed directive screen of F7, the not-yet-settled budget discipline of F5 — was claim-verified and math-verified in this round, not adversarially attacked. The program does not build an instrument on verification alone.

Two alternative residues were also recorded by the red teams and are noted here so the fresh review can weigh them against the main candidate, not silently lose them: (a) red-team B's directive-phrasing probe — every arm demands the same answer-only reply contract under different frozen phrasings, plus a length-matched neutral control, scoreable under core.evaluate unchanged (a different, smaller instrument measuring phrasing sensitivity, not production-style effects); (b) red-team A's residue — a confidence-style descriptive flip readout for the direct arm alone, the only arm whose compliant behaviour the byte-exact scorer can pass, as an extension of an existing instrument family rather than a new probe.

docs.title: 3. Resubmission specification (NOT a build order)
docs.text:
A resubmission is reviewable as a NEW design only if it satisfies all of the following in full. Partial compliance is still NO-BUILD. The researcher's redesigned instrument (~/workspace/agents_out/directive/research.md §5–§11) is the resubmission candidate and is incorporated by reference, subject to items 1–5 below; the fresh review's job is to attack the frozen machinery itself (the arm texts, the span parser, the decomposition, the screens, the rule at realistic N), not to re-litigate the sketch, which is dead.

  1. Corrections applied before review. Tree line ranges as corrected in §5 (JOINER confidence.py:78; parser def confidence.py:177, body to :205; SUFFIX confidence.py:85-89; answer span core.py:939 / :966); the author of arXiv:2511.04108 is Qiu & Srivastava and the paper is dropped as load-bearing in any case (§5); the RESEARCH_LOG naming claim is three prose hits (:3814, :5596, :5755), not two; the rule table's "0.0000" per-decision rate at N=100 is ≈2.4e-5 and must never be quoted as zero.
  2. Frozen items that carry verbatim in substance: the population (the run's search fixtures only, post-hoc stage, native arm = the recorded run never re-executed, held-out never treated; the selection-flip readout labelled search-only wherever it appears); the arms (terse / brief / steps with the researcher's §5 frozen texts and the "\n\n" joiner, every prose arm mandating the final answer on its own final line; special-token screen over every suffix for every family before generation); the headline scorer (span verdict) with the byte-exact verdict printed beside it as elicitation cost, never conflated; the frozen decomposition (span_pass / answer_line_not_final / answer_embedded / answer_absent, boundary-only discordance decomposed out first, preanswer_present counts printed); the decision rule of item 3; the selection readout (canonical-form winner_headline transplanted per two-arm contrast, selections recomputed on the restricted common completed set, withheld when sets differ or are empty, selection-vs-abstention never a winner change, the primary run's decision/winner/exit code never touched); the fail-closed vocabulary of research §8 (stage details {cancelled, directive_record_budget_exceeded, directive_screen_failed}, per-cell {"", arm_context_exceeded, arm_evaluation_failed}, whole-stage directive_unavailable, section labels directive_drop_observed / below_threshold / insufficient); token-ID divergence reported, not gated (negation disposition; same-ids = rendering anomaly, same-ids flip = determinism finding); digest-only records with the span split named as stage-attested residue (no carried final line — it is the answer); the validator mirror obligation (suffixes, joiner, screens, span parser, decomposition, rule, restricted-set selection — re-implemented, never imported).
  3. Decision rule (as derived in research §7, verified twice independently): per candidate, per arm-vs-native contrast, over the common completed set — D = native passes, J = of D, arm span-verdict fails, R = reverse discordants printed beside J; fire directive_drop_observed iff D ≥ 10 and J ≥ 5 and J ≥ D/4 and McNemar exact one-sided p(J vs J+R) < 0.05; D < 10 → insufficient; otherwise below_threshold. Operating characteristics (exact enumeration; researcher, verifier, and coordinator agree cell-for-cell): random labeller fires 0.0377 (N=100) / 0.0304 (N=30); no-effect competent rows 0.0000–0.0071; power at a true 25% drop is 0.5027 (N=100) / 0.3441 (N=30) — a coin flip; at a 50% drop, 1.0000 / 0.9490. Because the panel size is the user's own fixture count, the section must print the operating characteristics at the run's own N (no single frozen paragraph), and the family-wise expectation with them (at N=30, ≈0.51 expected false labels per 72 decisions, P(≥1) ≈ 0.40; at N=100, P(≥1) = 0.002). below_threshold is weak evidence and must say so; small user sets (the shipped example has 2 search fixtures) read insufficient — correctly.
  4. Monday-morning utility (resubmission, string-scoped): a prompt engineer who has picked a template family and is about to ship a response-style directive in the user turn uses this, per candidate, to decide whether that exact directive string can ride along without changing the lab's winner on their own fixtures — before the choice silently flips a selection they already made. Where the verdict is insufficient or below_threshold, the honest deliverable is "this panel cannot distinguish them; choose on other grounds", and the design must say so in those words' substance.
  5. Name: --response-directive (module responsedirective.py), per research §10's in-design audit — --directive is free as a string but names any instruction and overclaims the scope; "ladder" is dropped entirely. The name ships only after the build cycle's USAGE naming audit (the rank-2 §8.46 precedent) regardless.
  6. What the fresh review must settle head-on (silence on any of these is NO-BUILD): a. Budget discipline at the recorded cap (F5). At the recorded --max-new-tokens the steps arm's span verdict still grades a censored population (truncated cells are completed, answer never emitted). The resubmission's per-arm n_limit counting and decomposition label the censoring; the fresh review must decide whether labelling suffices, whether truncated cells leave the headline population under a pre-registered rule (and what that does to the conditioning, F6), or whether the instrument needs a different budget regime — argued against the native comparability constraint, not defaulted. b. The directive-bearing-fixture screen (F7). A frozen, decidable screen for fixtures whose messages already carry an answer-style directive (in any turn, not only the last — the shipped example carries it in the last turn, but nothing in the fixture format confines it there), with screened fixtures counted and classed pre-generation, never silently dropped. The researcher's §4 screen list (multiline / blank / vacuous / no-user) does not include this class; without it the span verdict on such fixtures measures conflict resolution, not directive sensitivity. c. The neutral-suffix control (F8). Include a length-matched neutral arm (the repetition.py pad precedent), or argue — against F8, not around it — why the span-verdict design attributes discordance to directive content without one. Suffix-presence is a real channel: any appended text can flip a greedy path. d. Panel power at realistic N (F2/item 3). The rule is coin-flip powered at a 25% drop even at N=100, and most real user sets are far smaller. The fresh review must either accept this with the at-N operating characteristics printed beside every verdict, or change the panel/rule — and argue the choice, not default to it. e. The confidence-overlap judgment. Machinery reuse from confidence is total (surgery, span verdict, flips, wrapper gate); the treatment difference is the whole claim to novelty (research §9, conceded by its author). The fresh review decides whether that difference justifies a new probe, an extension of confidence, or nothing — with red-team B's phrasing variant and red-team A's direct-arm residue (§2) in front of it as the competing smaller instruments. f. Neighbour re-survey. The uniqueness pass's neighbour set (LM Eval Harness, HELM, PromptPerfect, OpenAI evals, DSPy) was NOT re-surveyed this round (research §11, UNEXECUTED; the cycle-199 survey covers the confidence combination). The fresh review re-runs it before any build; the claim stays combination-scoped to surveyed sources until then.
  7. Counts (as frozen in the brief): 3 treated arms × ≤100 search fixtures × ≤24 candidates = 7,200 generations maximum (native reused, 0); ground records = 24 × 100 = 2,400 multi-cell records; caps frozen in the module with derivations (confidence's 2,400-record precedent). The 7,200 figure must never be quoted without its search-only and recorded-cap qualifications (§5).
  8. Sources are limited to §6 of this doc, with their fencing. No "first" is claimed anywhere; the contribution, if the resubmission is ever built, is the combination stated in research §11 (per-template crossing of frozen response-directive strings on the user's own fixtures, span-verdict discordance plus byte-exact elicitation cost, conservative selection re-applied per arm on a common completed set), scoped to surveyed sources.

docs.title: 4. Adjudication evidence (coordinator's own execution)
docs.text:
All snippets read-only; no suite was run.

  • Scorer line and answer span. core.py:797 read directly: exact_match=status == "completed" and answer == case.expected; core.py:939 answer_ids = output_ids if cut is None else output_ids[:cut]; core.py:966 answer = decoded. No stripping, parsing, or extraction anywhere on that path.
  • Scorer inversion (F1). Re-ran red-team A's /tmp/redteama/scorer_stub.py (stub backend through the real core.evaluate): compliant native 4/4, direct 4/4, brief 0/4 (answer 'The question asks for a known fact. 42'), steps 0/4 — including the final-answer-on-its-own-line variant, 0/4; ignoring model 4/4 in all four arms; parse_verbalized_confidence on the brief answer returns missing_line with the whole answer as span; scorerlens.rung_match recovers neither the brief answer nor a bare label-prefix answer at any rung.
  • Population (F7). Re-ran red-team B's /tmp/redteamb/fixture_conflicts.py and read examples/fixtures.json directly: 2 search + 2 held-out fixtures, all four last user messages carrying an answer-only directive (texts in §1 F7); catalog = 29 formats; special-token audit 0 findings for all three suffix strings; suffix lands inside the user turn in chatml and llama3 renders.

Coordinator Monte Carlo (300 trials, jitter null): P(any pass-set difference in the 24×100×3 panel) = 1.000 at ε = 0.001, 0.005, and 0.01; analytic E[discordant pairs] = 14.4 / 71.6 / 142.6. Selection, conditioned on a native winner (analytic): P(winner loses all-pass) = 0.394 / 0.634 / 0.867 for one arm at p = 0.005 / 0.01 / 0.02, and 0.778 / 0.951 / 0.998 over three arms.
  • Resubmission rule (item 3). Re-ran the researcher's /tmp/researcher/poc3b_mc.py (exact enumeration): every cell of the research §7 table reproduced — random 0.0377 / 0.0304, drop-25% power 0.5027 / 0.3441, drop-50% 1.0000 / 0.9490, family-wise N=100 P(≥1) = 0.002, N=30 expected 0.51, P(≥1) = 0.402. This is the third independent reproduction (researcher, verifier, coordinator).
  • Tree settlements verified by reading (clean reads this round): cli.py:198 (--max-new-tokens default 64); cli.py:827 ("--confidence",); confidence.py:400-410 (cell_verdict: span-digest equality plus boundary_found); canonicalform.py:599 (arm_selection); density.py:131-138 (STAGE_DETAILS / RECORD_DETAILS pattern); repetition.py:66-71 (pad arm and length/repetition contrasts).

The coordinator did not re-run those in full; they are credited to the verifier, not claimed as coordinator executions.

docs.title: 6. Sources the resubmission may safely cite
docs.text:
All resolved against their primary sources this round by the researcher and independently by the verifier (abstract/HTML level; fencing must travel with each):

  • Wei et al., arXiv:2201.11903 — chain-of-thought via few-shot exemplars improves arithmetic/commonsense/symbolic reasoning at scale. Fencing: the treatment is demonstrations, not an appended zero-shot directive; the sketch's steps suffix is Kojima-shaped, not Wei-shaped. Citable only for "intermediate reasoning steps can change answers", never for suffix directives or templates.
  • Sprague et al., arXiv:2409.12183 — meta-analysis of 100+ papers plus own evaluations (20 datasets, 14 models): CoT's benefit is concentrated in math/logic/symbolic tasks; on MMLU direct answering is almost identical to CoT absent an equals sign. Fencing: benchmark accuracy; no chat-template crossing, no selection rule, no byte-exact boundary scorer. Its load-bearing use here is predictive: the steps arm's answer effect on the lab's mostly short-answer fixtures is expected small — which is why the contract/truncation channels (F1, F5) dominate the sketch and must be designed out, not disclosed away.
  • Qiu & Srivastava, arXiv:2511.04108 — batching multiple queries into one prompt suppresses overthinking in large reasoning models. NOT directive evidence; the researcher drops it as load-bearing and a resubmission should too.
  • Kojima et al., arXiv:2205.11916 — NOT SAFE: unresolved at primary source this round (seen only in secondary bibliographies; the researcher labelled it UNRESOLVED and non-load-bearing, and the verifier concurs). Resolve primary-first before any use.
  • In-tree precedents a resubmission doc may cite: docs/CONFIDENCE_DESIGN.md (span-verdict precedent; raw verdicts on suffixed generations are meaningless); negation.py OPERATING_CHARACTERISTICS / decompose_cell (joint-rule and decomposition precedents); canonicalform.py arm_selection / winner_headline (restricted-set selection precedent); repetition.py pad arm (length-matched control precedent); confidence.py screen_fixture (screen precedent — whose classes do not cover directive-bearing fixtures, §3 item 6(b)).

No "first" is claimed anywhere in this doc. The contribution of any future resubmission is the combination stated in §3 item 8, never priority.

docs.title: 7. What a build cycle must NOT do on the basis of this doc
docs.text:
• Do not build the circulated sketch, any "ladder" framing or rung/trend readout, the any-difference falsifier, or brief/ steps arms scored through core.evaluate unchanged.
  • Do not build the redesigned instrument on this doc's authority: it enters only through a fresh design review (blind red-team pair + verifier) of a resubmission satisfying §3 in full, and only on a BUILD verdict from that review.
  • Do not ship a flag under --directive; the resubmission's name is --response-directive, and even it ships only after the build cycle's USAGE naming audit.
  • Do not re-apply selection over held-out fixtures, quote the 7,200-generation figure without its search-only and recorded-cap qualifications, or carry any figure listed in §5 into a doc or help text.
  • Do not present the span verdict and the byte-exact elicitation-cost readout as one number, or let the decomposition rescue a discordant cell into a pass.

docs.title: Distractor dilution probe — design
docs.text:
model-protocol-lab run --distract answers a deployment question the selection loop cannot see: once a template is chosen, how much irrelevant context can be poured around the real prompt before the chosen candidate starts failing — and does irrelevant text that merely looks like it contains a different answer actively capture the model, or does failure under load come from dilution alone? Retrieval pipelines, long system preambles, and multi-document prompts all add exactly this kind of load, so the answer decides how much context budget a deployment can spend before the protocol itself becomes the risk.

The probe is post-hoc and observational: it reuses the recorded search observations as the native (dose 0) arm, generates treated cells on the same backend, and never touches candidate selection. The primary decision is reported per condition only as a flip marker against the recorded outcome.

docs.title: Conditions and protocol
docs.text:
Ten conditions, frozen in code (distraction.CONDITIONS):

  • neutral filler at 64, 256, and 1024 tokens, placed before and after the fixture's last user message (6 cells per fixture);
  • near-miss filler at 64 and 256 tokens, before and after (4 cells per fixture).

Near-miss cells exist only where a planted answer is defined (see below); at 1024 the near-miss arm does not exist, so capture curves terminate at 256. That is a scope decision, not an omission: the near-miss claim is about capture at moderate load, and the generation budget (below) is spent on the neutral dose curve first.

Filler is whole corpus sentences joined by a single newline, nested by construction — the dose-d span's sentence sequence is a prefix of the dose-1024 sequence — with the final sentence truncated to hit the exact token target where whole sentences cannot. The sizing rule (whole-sentences-plus-one-truncated-suffix-v1) searches candidate spans by rendered token delta against the native render and takes the first exact hit within a frozen encode budget (512 encodes per cell); a cell that cannot be sized exactly is recorded arm_unmatchable, never approximated. The rendered dose is an identity the diff validator re-derives for every compared cell: cell.input_tokens - native.input_tokens must equal the nominal level.

Both corpora are frozen constants whose SHA-256 digests ride in the protocol block: a 71-sentence neutral corpus (no digits, no special-token literals) and four near-miss sentence templates with a single {planted} slot, cycled to fill the span. Every span is screened before generation: special-token literals for any candidate, or the candidate's own boundary token texts appearing in the span, reject the cell as arm_screened — filler must never smuggle protocol structure into the prompt.

docs.title: The planted answer (digit-string surgery v2)
docs.text:
A fixture's expected answer yields a planted string only when it is a plain ASCII number: optional ASCII sign, an integer part either plain or comma-grouped in threes (or a bare fraction like .5), an optional fraction, an optional exponent. The plant is the same string with the last mantissa digit incremented, carry propagating through digits only, regrouping commas on overflow ("9,999" → "10,000", "007" → "008", "-0" → "-1", "42.0" → "42.1", "1,000.5" → "1,000.6"). Everything else — surrounding whitespace, underscores, non-ASCII digits, inf/NaN, dates, number words — yields no plant. The rule is total and deterministic, independent of any ambient decimal context; the exact battery lives in the cycle-184 tests. Where no plant exists, or the plant equals another fixture's expected answer, or the candidate's native answer already is the plant, the near-miss arm is undefined for that (candidate, fixture) and its cells record near_miss_undefined.

Scope, stated plainly: near-miss capture is defined only for fixtures whose expected answer is a number in the ASCII shape above. On answer sets without such fixtures the near-miss arm is empty by construction and the probe reduces to the neutral dose curves.

docs.title: Claims and denominators
docs.text:
• D1′ (dose curve). Per candidate, per filler kind and placement, the paired pass rate at each level: records where the native arm passes or fails, the cell was generated, and both sides exist. Rates are reported per dose, never pooled across placements or kinds.
  • D2′ (first flip). Over native-passing records with a complete curve, the distribution of the first failing level, plus two counters the flip histogram alone would hide: returns (passing levels above the first flip — recovery under more load is evidence the flip was noise, not a threshold) and gains (native-failing records that pass at some dose).
  • D3′ (capture, an upper bound). Over native-passing records whose near-miss cell was generated, the share whose answer is exactly the planted string. Byte-exact scoring can only undercount capture (a captured answer with stray formatting scores as a plain failure), so the rate is labelled an upper bound on clean capture in the report. The headline number is the excess over neutral: records captured under near-miss whose same-dose neutral answer is not the plant. Dilution alone cannot manufacture the planted string in the neutral arm, so the excess separates active capture from generic load failure.
  • D4′ (per-condition selection). The conservative selection rule re-run per condition over the candidates that completed that condition on the same fixture set. Where completed sets differ, selection is withheld for that condition (selection_withheld_mismatched_sets) rather than compared across different evidence. Flips are marked against the recorded primary decision under the same vocabulary mapping the diff validator uses.
  • D5′ (construction honesty). Every cell records how its treated prompt relates to the native render: id_exact when the token ids decompose exactly into native prefix + inserted span + native suffix (the intended surgery), text_level when only the text decomposes (a tokenizer seam merged across the junction). Seam token ids (first/last inserted id) are recorded for text-level cells. A dose claim is only as strong as its construction, and the report keeps the two apart.

Vacuous fixtures (empty expected answer, or expected contained in the prompt) and echo fixtures are counted and excluded from every rate. Records whose native arm is unavailable make the whole candidate unavailable: the probe never mixes a partial native arm with generated cells.

docs.title: Cost
docs.text: Worst case is frozen in the protocol: 10 conditions × 2,400 ground records = 24,000 generations, where ground records are candidate × fixture pairs with a completed native arm. The CLI help states the count and the local backend's forwards formula (M·L + M(M−1)/2 for M forwards of growing length L with the KV cache off) so the price is visible before the run, not after. Per-cell sizing probes are capped separately (512 encodes) and never generate.

docs.title: What the probe does not do
docs.text:
• No grouping readout in v1: the think/non-think style grouping used by the repetition probe's disclosure is not repeated here; construction class and capture carry the honesty load.
  • No capture claim at 1024 (see Conditions).
  • No cross-backend claims: the protocol fingerprint binds the backend fingerprint, both corpus digests, the rule versions, the budgets, and the fixture set; a diff across differing protocols reports drift and refuses comparability.
  • The diff validator recomputes every derived value from the records (curves, first-flip state machine, capture, per-condition selection, fingerprint) and rejects payloads whose shape pre-checks fail (record caps, byte bound, digest shapes) before recomputing. Like every recompute validator in this project, it proves internal consistency of the payload against the frozen protocol — it cannot prove the generations really happened; that is what the sealed bundle and the determinism audit are for.

docs.title: Frequently asked questions
docs.text: Troubleshooting and interpretation questions, answered from the documented behavior. Each answer points at the authoritative section in docs/USAGE.md.

docs.title: How do I find the right --boundary-ids?
docs.text: From the checkpoint's actual tokenizer, never from another model. Run doctor --model DIR --boundary-ids ...: it reports the tokenizer's declared added_tokens with their IDs, which is where boundary markers usually live, and verifies each ID against the vocabulary (see USAGE §2, §4). Then confirm the tokenization is stable: decode the IDs and re-encode the text — if the IDs change, the boundary text has multiple tokenizations and the exact token-ID match can miss (USAGE §4).

docs.title: run fails with local_context_limit_exceeds_declared_window — what now?
