docs.text: Your --max-context exceeds the checkpoint's declared window. Stock GPT-2 checkpoints declare n_positions=1024, below the CLI default of 2048: pass --max-context 1024 (or less). After a clean doctor, the suggested next command already fills in the right value (USAGE §2, §3).

docs.title: run fails with context_limit_exceeded — what now?
docs.text: Prompt tokens plus --max-new-tokens exceeded the checkpoint's declared context window: the backend refused generation rather than silently truncating. Retry with a smaller --max-new-tokens. The doctor suggestion already sizes it so the longest fixture prompt fits the window; if you raised it afterwards, that is the cause. The report's decision banner names the failure in a "Failure diagnosis" line, and each candidate summary in results.json carries the sanitized failure_code.

docs.title: boundary_found=false but boundary_text_match=true — is my run broken?
docs.text: Not broken — this is the tokenization-mismatch diagnostic doing its job. The model emitted the boundary text with a different tokenization than your configured IDs (one string can be many token sequences). The pass criterion is unchanged (token-ID match only); treat the observation as a prompt to pick boundary IDs whose tokenization is stable in this checkpoint's tokenizer, and verify with doctor --boundary-ids (USAGE §4).

docs.title: Why does inspect warn about empty expected answers?
docs.text: An empty expected answer passes vacuously: any output that emits only the boundary token satisfies it. The warning names the fixtures so the measurement gap is visible; consider giving them real expected answers or removing them (USAGE §1).

docs.title: What do ambiguous and no_candidate mean? Can I use held-out to break ties?
docs.text: ambiguous means several candidates passed every search fixture; no_candidate means none did. The lab abstains in both cases by design, and the held-out set is never used to break ties — it only validates the single search winner. This is the conservative selection rule (USAGE §5); there is no flag to change it.

docs.title: The stop matrix disagrees with real vLLM / HF — which is right?
docs.text: The matrix cells are emulations with documented approximations, not reproductions. The HF cell mirrors StopStringCriteria's matching rule including its byte-space tables for byte-level tokenizers, but token texts for unmappable tokens fall back to isolated decodes, and the truncation is post-hoc (exact only for greedy decoding). The vLLM cell approximates incremental DecodeStream detokenization with per-prefix batch decodes, strips the stop string from the returned text by default (include_stop_str_in_output=False, the upstream default -- HF always keeps it), and models min_tokens gating (default 0). Disagreements are expected at these edges; the matrix answers "which semantics could flip this verdict", not "what vLLM would print" (USAGE §8.2).

docs.title: The lab generates straight through EOS — how do I match that in HF / vLLM?
docs.text:
The lab's decoding discipline is "exactly N tokens, no implicit EOS stop": generation runs to the token cap even when EOS appears. Both competitors stop on EOS by default -- HF's generate() auto-adds EosTokenCriteria, and vLLM defaults to ignore_eos=False -- so neither matches the lab out of the box. To make each backend behave like the lab:

  • HF: pass eos_token_id=None to generate() (disables the auto-added EosTokenCriteria; no other stop source is on unless you pass stop strings).
  • vLLM: pass ignore_eos=True, stop=[], stop_token_ids=[] and min_tokens=0 (every stop source explicitly disabled).

Sources: transformers main stopping_criteria.py (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/huggingface/transformers/main/src/transformers/generation/stopping_criteria.py), vLLM main v1/engine/detokenizer.py (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vllm-project/vllm/main/vllm/v1/engine/detokenizer.py), vLLM PR #22014 (min_tokens gating). See docs/RESEARCH_LOG.md "R2" for the full divergence write-up.

docs.title: What happens if I interrupt a run with Ctrl+C?
docs.text: Cancellation is cooperative: the run stops after the current backend operation, keeps a partial report (exit 130), and the output directory stays claimed so a retry needs a fresh path. Model loading itself may not be promptly interruptible (USAGE §5, §6).

docs.title: Can I share the report? What's in it?
docs.text: results.json excludes raw observations unless you pass --include-evidence; the HTML view never embeds raw prompts or generations. With --include-evidence, token IDs can reveal private prompts — inspect the report before sharing. Summary metadata, candidate names, format markers and fingerprints are always present (USAGE §6, README "Privacy").

docs.title: Can I compare candidates that need different boundary IDs?
docs.text: Yes: run --boundary-map NAME=ID,ID (repeatable) overrides --boundary-ids per candidate, so each format hypothesis is measured with its own end-of-turn marker. The selection rule is unchanged -- one candidate must pass every search fixture under its own boundary. See USAGE §4.

docs.title: The sensitivity sweep is slow / reports failed depths — normal?
docs.text: Yes. The sweep re-runs the whole search at every depth in 1..--max-drop-bytes, so it multiplies compute by that number; it is opt-in for exactly this reason. A depth that would split a UTF-8 codepoint records a failed decision for that depth instead of silently skipping it (USAGE §8.5).

docs.title: doctor says ok but run fails — what did I miss?
docs.text: doctor validates assets, config, tokenizer structure and fixtures without loading weights. It does not check RAM/VRAM, CUDA availability beyond the flag, or that the checkpoint's weights match its tokenizer's expectations beyond the manifest checks. When the decision is failed, the report's decision banner carries a "Failure diagnosis" line naming the sanitized failure code (e.g. context_limit_exceeded) with what to do about it -- read that before anything else. local_backend_initialization_failed means the checkpoint failed the adapter's strict loading checks (USAGE §3).

docs.title: How do I read the token-budget frontier?
docs.text: It recomputes the search decision at every smaller token budget from the recorded outputs (exact under greedy decoding, no extra model calls). "Stable across 1–N" means the verdict never depended on the cap you chose; flip ranges like "budgets 1–9: no_candidate" mean the winner only emerges once it gets enough tokens — the verdict is budget-contingent and a larger --max-new-tokens (or a cheaper winner) deserves a thought (USAGE §8.6).

docs.title: There are dozens of run --… probes — where do I start?
docs.text: Run the base experiment first; every probe is opt-in and answers one question the base run leaves open (which stop semantics, which template field, which serving stack). USAGE §8 gives each probe its own subsection, and each opens with the decision it informs. The probes split by cost: the portfolio, verbosity, refusal, cache-profile, stop-cause, scorer-lens and candidate-aliasing readouts are computed from the recorded answers after the run and cost no extra model calls, while the re-evaluation stages (perturbation, hierarchy, ablation and the rest) re-run the search split under their treatment.

docs.title: Can I prove a result file wasn't altered after the run?
docs.text: You can seal it: model-protocol-lab pack writes a bundle whose manifest hashes every file in the report directory, and model-protocol-lab verify --bundle re-hashes everything offline, then replays the decision from the sealed results as a second, independent layer. The seal is unsigned — it proves the bits are unchanged since packing only if you keep the bundle digest somewhere else (verify --expect-digest); it is not an attestation and says nothing about who packed it (USAGE §13.1).

docs.title: Can I check whether my checkpoint actually reproduces its own runs?
docs.text: model-protocol-lab verify --determinism --model DIR re-executes the recorded search observations token-for-token and compares. If every cell reproduces, it issues an unsigned determinism certificate bound to those cells; if a cell diverges, the divergence is reported as a finding about the backend's determinism — the audit proves the re-execution, never the original run (USAGE §13.2).

docs.title: My fixture file is hand-written — how do I know the loader reads it as intended?
docs.text: inspect validates the file against the strict schema and runs the search/held-out contamination check (USAGE §1). For the loaders themselves, model-protocol-lab fixtures fuzz runs a fixed, published 133-case mutator table against the documented accept/reject contract — same seed, same report, byte-for-byte — so a loader behavior change shows up as a contract diff instead of a surprise mid-run (USAGE §9).

docs.title: The model repeats things it was told to keep internal / refuses benign prompts — can the lab measure that?
docs.text: Two probes, both per template. The labeled-block confidentiality probe (USAGE §8.34) folds a privilege-marked block with a secret marker into the user turn and measures whether frozen elicitation prompts can pull the marker out, verbatim or in fragments. The suspected-refusal profile (USAGE §8.36) scans the recorded answers with a frozen refusal-opener detector and reports a per-template suspected-refusal rate on benign fixtures — suspected, because opener matching is a weak baseline, and the rate travels with exact counts so you can judge it yourself.

docs.title: Where is the evidence that any of this was actually verified?
docs.text: VALIDATION.md: exact commands, counts, dates and environment for every verification round — including what is still not established.

docs.title: Schema field-order probe — design (cycle 205, wave-9 rank 4)
docs.text: Status: v2, adjudicated after the adversarial round and shipped in cycle 205 (agents_out/cycle205/{redteam_a,redteam_b,verifier, coordinator_adjudication}.md: A filed 2 FATAL / 9 MAJOR / 4 MINOR, the verifier reproduced every load-bearing number, B confirmed both FATALs with corrections and added NB1–NB6). v1's defects that shaped this rewrite: answer labels the contexts do not entail (F1), a self-contradictory non-finite sentinel with an undefined canonical form (F2), overstated arm distinctness (F3), unfrozen new specs (F4), and a decision rule whose printed operating characteristics understated its weakness (F5/F6).

docs.title: Utility
docs.text: A practitioner defining a JSON schema for extraction learns, per template family, whether putting the main answer field first vs last in the schema changes the values the model produces for it — before a cosmetic schema reorder in a code review silently changes extraction accuracy in production.

docs.title: Question and claim
docs.text:
For a fixed candidate (chat template) and a fixed set of flat JSON extraction/classification/routing specs, is the value produced for a spec's designated answer field invariant under the field's position in the presented schema?

Pre-registered claim: per-field value accuracy is invariant under schema field order. Proved wrong, per candidate, if the designated field's paired accuracy differs between the answer-first and answer-last arms on specs adherent in both arms, under the decision rule below. Intermediate arms (canonical, reversed) are descriptive context, never decision inputs.

Motivation, stated precisely: Tam et al. (arXiv:2408.02442) establish that format restrictions degrade reasoning; their abstract makes no key-order claim. Their §4.1 does report direct key-order evidence of a different kind: 100% of GPT-3.5 JSON-mode Last-Letter responses placed the "answer" key before the "reason" key, "resulting in zero-shot direct answering", and the authors conclude that "the order of keys in structured outputs … emerge as important factors". That is emitted key order under constrained JSON mode, on a reasoning task — not the order in which a prompt presents a schema's fields. The presentation-order hypothesis — a field the schema presents earlier is also emitted earlier, with less of the object's content in context — is the lab's own reasoning, built on Tam et al.'s two verified results. JSONSchemaBench (arXiv:2501.10868, cited by structured.py) varies constrained-decoding frameworks and models, not prompt-only field order crossed with chat templates. The combination — prompt-only field order × template family × per-field exact scoring — is the contribution; no "first" is claimed.

docs.title: Spec set
docs.text:
The shipped structured spec set (9 specs) is reused unchanged, and six further specs in the same flat dialect are added in fieldorder.py (the structured set itself is not modified). Reason for the addition, stated plainly: the shipped schemas have at most 2 fields, and three have exactly 1, so on the shipped set alone the arms collapse to at most two distinct orders per spec and the reversed arm is rarely a distinct treatment. The new specs carry 3–4 fields.

Canonical order is the order the shipped instrument presents: alphabetical by field name (structured.describe_schema sorts properties and the required list). Each spec designates one answer field and a frozen paired flag. Pairing rule (derived, from frozen data): a spec enters a candidate's paired population iff paired is yes, its first/last orders differ, both endpoint records are adherent, and neither endpoint record has duplicate keys.

Reader-entailment rule (F1): a spec may be paired: yes only if a reader given the question, context, and schema — but not the answer table — can derive the answer field's value uniquely. Two shipped specs fail it and are paired: no (kept as adherence/descriptive specs; the shipped set cannot be edited): route-alert (channel = pager — nothing maps 97% disk usage to pager over sms/email) and route-order (warehouse = south — nothing entails it; Porto is in northern Portugal). Non-answer fields of shipped specs may carry frozen judgement values (route-ticket's priority = 3); they feed descriptive per-field readouts only and are named here so the noise is not discovered later.

The six new specs, frozen in full (schema dialect exactly as in structured.py; every answer passes check_schema against its own schema, verified at module load in tests):

  • extract-product (extraction, paired yes). Q: "Extract the product's brand, model, price and stock status." Context: "The catalogue lists it as: brand Acme, model Rotor X2. It costs 349 dollars and is currently in stock." Schema: brand (string), model (string), price (integer ≥ 0), in_stock (boolean). Answer: {brand "Acme", model "Rotor X2", price 349, in_stock true}. Answer field: model. (The catalogue split is stated verbatim in the context, so the answer field is determined, not convention-dependent.)
  • extract-event (extraction, paired yes). Q: "Extract the event venue, day and attendance." Context: "The workshop meets at Harbor Hall on Friday with 40 attendees." Schema: venue (string), day (string, enum monday…sunday, all lowercase), attendance (integer ≥ 0). Answer: {venue "Harbor Hall", day "friday", attendance 40}. Answer field: venue.
  • route-complaint (routing, paired yes). Q: "Route the complaint and record whether a defect was confirmed and whether data was lost." Context: "Complaint: 'The update deleted my saved files.' Front-line support confirmed the update itself is defective." Schema: team (string, enum [sales, support, technical]), defect_confirmed (boolean), data_lost (boolean). Answer: {team "technical", defect_confirmed true, data_lost true}. Answer field: team. (Every field is entailed: files deleted, defect confirmed by support, and a confirmed product defect routes past front-line support to technical.)
  • classify-document (classification, paired yes). Q: "Classify the document's type, language and confidentiality." Context: "Document: a German-language internal memo marked confidential." Schema: doc_type (string, enum [memo, report, invoice]), language (string, enum [english, german, french]), confidential (boolean). Answer: {doc_type "memo", language "german", confidential true}. Answer field: doc_type.
  • extract-vehicle (extraction, paired yes). Q: "Extract the vehicle make, year, fuel and seat count." Context: "The 2019 Volvo wagon runs on diesel and seats five." Schema: make (string), year (integer 1900–2100), fuel (string, enum [petrol, diesel, electric]), seats (integer ≥ 1). Answer: {make "Volvo", year 2019, fuel "diesel", seats 5}. Answer field: make.
  • route-delivery (routing, paired yes). Q: "Route the delivery and flag its requirements." Context: "Delivery: vaccines to a clinic in the south, sent by express courier for tomorrow morning; a signature is required and the box must stay refrigerated." Schema: region (string, enum [north, south, east, west]), speed (string, enum [standard, express]), signature_required (boolean), refrigerated (boolean). Answer: {region "south", speed "express", signature_required true, refrigerated true}. Answer field: region.

Designation table (canonical = alphabetical order; position of the answer field within it):

spec canonical order answer field (position) paired extract-person age, name name (2/2) yes extract-city city, population city (1/2) yes extract-book title, year title (1/2) yes classify-sentiment label label (1/1) no (one field) classify-urgency level level (1/1) no (one field) classify-language language language (1/1) no (one field) route-ticket department, priority department (1/2) yes route-alert ack_required, channel channel (2/2) no (unentailed) route-order express, warehouse warehouse (2/2) no (unentailed) extract-product brand, in_stock, model, price model (3/4) yes extract-event attendance, day, venue venue (3/3) yes route-complaint data_lost, defect_confirmed, team team (3/3) yes classify-document confidential, doc_type, language doc_type (2/3) yes extract-vehicle fuel, make, seats, year make (2/4) yes route-delivery refrigerated, region, signature_required, speed region (2/4) yes

Paired pool: 10 specs (extraction 6, routing 3, classification 1). Across them the answer field sits first in 3 canonical orders, last in 3, and in a middle position in 4, so the endpoint contrast is not confounded with "the answer field is always the alphabetically-first field".

docs.title: Arms
docs.text:
Per spec, four renderings of the same prompt, differing only in the field enumeration order inside the schema description (the property list and the required list both follow the arm order):

  • canonical: alphabetical (the shipped presentation).
  • answer_first: the answer field moved to the front; the remaining fields keep canonical relative order.
  • answer_last: the answer field moved to the end; the remaining fields keep canonical relative order.
  • reversed: canonical order reversed (generic-reordering control).

Distinctness, stated exactly (F3): the four orders are all distinct only when the answer field sits in a middle position (4 specs). When it sits at a canonical endpoint with ≥ 3 fields, there are 3 distinct orders (canonical coincides with that endpoint arm; 2 specs). With 2 fields there are 2 distinct orders (6 specs); with 1 field, 1 (3 specs). Canonical therefore coincides with an endpoint arm on 6 of the 10 paired specs, and its readouts there are replicates of that endpoint arm under greedy decoding — labelled as such wherever canonical numbers are printed next to endpoint numbers. Per candidate the stage runs 60 arm-generations covering 37 distinct prompts; the duplicate generations are kept (uniform code path and record shape), and the cost is printed as 60, not 37. The decision is unaffected: answer-first ≠ answer-last on all 10 paired specs.

The prompt template is structured.render_prompt's, with the schema description rendered in the arm's order by an order-parametrised describe function whose canonical output is byte-identical to structured.describe_schema (pinned by a test). Shipped specs keep the (ref: structured/<id>) marker; new specs use (ref: fieldorder/<id>). The schema presentation and the implied output key order move together — that is the production change being tested; no separate output-order instruction exists in the shipped prompt, and none is added.

docs.title: Records and recompute (residue stated, §Records)
docs.text:
Generation mirrors the density/rotation stages: one record per (candidate, spec, arm), exactly 15 × 4 = 60 per candidate in canonical (spec, arm) order with unique (spec, arm) keys — the validator rejects any other record set for a candidate (NB1). Records come from core.evaluate at MAX_NEW_TOKENS = 64, fixed by the protocol rather than threaded from the CLI: the record caps below are derived from it (NB4). Budget cap: 24 candidates → MAX_FIELD_ORDER_RECORDS = 1,440. Screening mirrors density: the stage-level special-token audit runs over the frozen text inventory (questions, contexts, templates, description components), and a per-spec boundary-containment screen runs over the rendered prompts (NB5). Stage details {cancelled, field_order_record_budget_exceeded, field_order_screen_failed}; per-record detail ∈ {"", arm_evaluation_failed, arm_context_exceeded}.

Record shape (frozen):

{candidate, spec_id, arm, detail, case_screened, boundary_found,
 duplicate_keys, answer_digest, document_kind, document_digest,
 field_values, input_tokens, content_digest}

Digest preimages (NB2): content_digest = SHA-256 of the arm's rendered user content (the prompt string), recomputed by the validator from its literal spec table. answer_digest = SHA-256 of the decoded answer text, or None when there was no generation.

  • document_kind: "object" | "non_object" | "unparseable" | "" ("" exactly when there was no generation). unparseable means JSON parse failure only.
  • duplicate_keys: a stage-observed bool — the raw answer contained a repeated object key. Scoring consequences (derived, below): a duplicate-key document is never adherent and never enters pairing, because its extraction is parser-dependent (Python's json.loads keeps the last occurrence; a production parser may keep the first). Per-field readouts score the last-wins parse, with duplicate counts printed beside them.
  • field_values: for "object" documents, a dict mapping every produced key to the canonical JSON string of its parsed value (canonical form pinned below), or to None when the produced value has no canonical form — a non-finite number (NaN/±Infinity, which json.loads accepts as a Python extension) or a value beyond the int↔str digit limit. A produced JSON null is the string "null", never None — the sentinel is unambiguous. {} for every other kind, and for degraded records (detail set or screened: kind "", digest None, field_values {}).
  • document_digest: the digest of the document's canonical form, stored only where the validator recomputes it: non-None ⟺ kind is "object" and no field_values entry is None; then it must equal the digest of the reconstructed document. Otherwise None.

Canonical JSON, pinned (F2c): structured._canonical_json exactly — json.dumps(value, sort_keys=True, separators=(", ", ": "), ensure_ascii=True, allow_nan=False). Worked example: the document {"name": "Ada Lovelace", "age": 36} canonicalises to the string {"age": 36, "name": "Ada Lovelace"} (note the spaced separators — this probe's canonical form is the structured convention, not density's compact one).

Everything scored is derived from the record fields, by the producer's aggregator and the diff validator's mirror alike:

  • A field's produced value is correct iff its key is present in field_values with a string whose digest equals the expected value's canonical digest (expected values come from the frozen spec table). A None (non-finite) value is incorrect for every field, since no expected value is a non-finite number. Correctness is exact canonical equality; every numeric field in the spec set is integer (F11), and number-typed fields are out of scope for answer-field designation.
  • The schema verdict is recomputed by re-running the flat schema check over the reconstructed document (each field_values string parsed back; the validator requires every stored string to be exactly the canonical form of its parse, and requires document_digest consistency as above — so the stored values are bound, not attested). A None value fails its key's field check before reconstruction, so a null-typed field can never be passed by the sentinel (no current spec has a null field; the rule is frozen anyway). "non_object" and "unparseable" documents are schema-failed by kind.
  • Validator totality (F10): any exception while parsing or canonicalising a stored string — ValueError (including the int↔str digit limit), RecursionError, TypeError — makes the section invalid, never a crash. Both mirrors use a safe canonicaliser with that catch (classify_response's RecursionError handling is the in-tree precedent).
  • Adherence per record: parse_ok iff kind ∈ {object, non_object}; adherent iff parse_ok, the recomputed schema verdict is ok, and not duplicate_keys — structured's parse/schema decomposition, kept, so a value effect cannot hide inside an adherence effect.

Caps (F8, derived from enforced premises): per record, the summed length of field_values strings is at most 4,096 chars, validator-enforced. Derivation: MAX_NEW_TOKENS = 64 and at most 32 decoded chars per generated token for the tokenizers this lab targets bound an answer at 2,048 chars; the cap is 2× that. Producer rule: a live record whose values exceed the cap is stored with detail arm_evaluation_failed and empty field_values (counted under n_detail_screened). Payload cap MAX_FIELD_ORDER_PAYLOAD_BYTES = 8 MiB: 1,440 records × (4,096 + ≈ 1.4 KB of other fields and JSON overhead) ≈ 7.9 MB.

Stated residue (F9): the link between answer_digest and (document_kind, field_values) is stage-attested — the validator recomputes every verdict from the record fields, but it cannot prove the fields came from the answer the digest names (the same origin-only residue density discloses). duplicate_keys and boundary_found are stage-observed facts of the same status; every consequence drawn from them is recomputed.

docs.title: Aggregation and decision
docs.text:
The aggregate candidate block always carries detail ("" or "field_order_unavailable") plus every readout key below, so a zero-live candidate prints None rates and an insufficient decision with n_paired = 0 rather than vanishing (NB6). Live = not screened, no detail, boundary found.

  • Adherence by arm: n, parse/schema/adherent rates over live records (structured's decomposition; rates None iff n = 0).
  • Per-field accuracy by arm: for every field of every spec, correct / live-in-arm (missing counts incorrect; denominators printed). Plus whole-document accuracy by arm — all spec fields correct and no extra keys in field_values — over live records (F15).
  • Answer-field accuracy by arm over all live records, and over the paired population below.
  • Pairing and attrition: per candidate, the paired population per the rule above; attrition printed per arm (specs lost to non-adherence, to duplicate keys, to the paired flag / order rule). Beside the paired counts, the ungated discordant counts — all paired: yes specs whose endpoint orders differ, scoring non-adherent records' answer fields by their field_values — are printed as a sensitivity, because adherence gating is outcome-dependent selection: a generation failure that makes the answer field wrong in one arm often makes that record non-adherent and removes the spec from pairing, deflating measured discordance (F6; the deflation is bounded in this instrument — most incorrect values here are adherent-shaped, e.g. a wrong enum member — but the direction is disclosed, not hidden).
  • Decision: per paired spec, answer-field correct in first / correct in last; discordant counts n_first_only, n_last_only; exact two-sided sign test over discordant specs. falsified iff discordant ≥ MIN_DISCORDANT_SPECS = 6 and p ≤ 0.05 (direction recorded); insufficient iff discordant < 6 — the boolean is withheld, never defaulted to acquittal; else not_falsified. Printed sensitivities: the same decision recomputed on the extraction-only paired specs (6), and the paired counts split by field count (2-field vs ≥ 3-field — on 2-field specs the answer field's promotion is the companion's demotion, F13).
  • Operating characteristics, printed wherever the verdict is (F5/F12): critical splits — at 6–8 discordant specs only a unanimous split falsifies; at 9, 8–1 (p = 0.0391); at 10, 9–1 (p = 0.0215). Power: a true 0.90-vs-0.60 endpoint accuracy gap yields falsified only ≈ 15% of the time (simulated, independent specs); most such runs print insufficient or not_falsified. The sign test's α is exact under independent discordance directions across specs; specs are a fixed panel, not a sample, and within-shape direction correlation degrades the calibration (at the extreme of one direction coin per shape, conditioned on full discordance, the false-falsification rate reaches ≈ 50%; unconditional rates stayed ≤ ≈ 4.4% across the round's parameter sweep). Per-candidate α = 0.05 gives ≈ 1.2 expected false falsifications across 24 candidates at the nominal rate (probability of at least one ≈ 0.71); the realised per-candidate rate is below nominal by discreteness.

Protocol object: {seed, backend fingerprint, spec/arm inventory, and digests of three frozen rule texts — GENERATION (spec set, designations, paired flags, arm derivation), RENDERING (prompt construction), CHECKING (canonicalisation, sentinel, duplicate rule, correctness, schema recompute, pairing, decision)} — mirror-recomputed by the validator from its own literal copies, as in cycles 203/204.

docs.title: Surfaces
docs.text:
• Pure module fieldorder.py (spec table, arm derivation, rendering, checking, aggregation, protocol).
  • experiments.fieldorder_stage / fieldorder_analysis mirroring density_stage; CLI --field-order with the utility sentence and the 1,440-generation cost in help.
  • Reporting section "Schema field order"; diff section field_order whose validator recomputes everything above from the records (full literal-table mirror in diffreports).
  • USAGE §8.52; RESEARCH_LOG cycle-205 entry; CHANGELOG; VALIDATION counts by measurement.
  • Pin blast radius (NB3), all in the same push: test_cycle44 mypy source-file pin 61 → 62 (fieldorder.py is the 62nd) and its VALIDATION.md line; test_cycle178 header pin "cycles 10–204" → "cycles 10–205"; test_cycle27 + test_cycle67 oracle elements for the new diff section (oracle trio, identical key set, summary literal, flip-gate anchor original + mutant); README capability bullet + sample-report and diff-section enumerations; VALIDATION probe list.

docs.title: Known limits (printed in the report)
docs.text:
• Flat schemas of 1–4 fields; endpoint placement only — nothing is measured about middle positions as a treatment.
  • Canonical coincides with an endpoint arm on 6 of 10 paired specs; single-field specs cannot enter the pairing; the reversed arm coincides with an endpoint on 2-field specs.
  • Two shipped specs are excluded from pairing because their frozen answer labels are not entailed by their contexts (route-alert, route-order); one shipped non-answer field is a frozen judgement value (route-ticket priority).
  • Adherence gating selects specs the candidate already handles, and selects against discordance; the paired claim is conditional on adherence in both endpoint arms, with the ungated counts printed as sensitivity.
  • Duplicate-key documents are scored by their last occurrence in per-field readouts and excluded from adherence/pairing.
  • 10 paired specs and a sign test: only very large endpoint effects can falsify, and they usually will not (≈ 15% power at a 30-point gap). The verdict's printed characteristics say so.

docs.title: Fixture fuzzer — design
docs.text:
Status: built in cycle 172 (model_protocol_lab/fixturefuzz.py); this document is the published contract table the corpus implements. Instrument name (honest): fixture fuzzer — a contract fuzzer for the lab's own fixture loaders. It is not coverage-guided fuzzing and does not explore: the mutator table is fixed, published below, and every case carries its expected outcome from the loaders' documented contract.

Monday-morning utility: a maintainer who just changed the fixture loaders (or is about to accept contributed fixture files) runs model-protocol-lab fixtures fuzz to prove the loaders still reject hostile or malformed fixture files gracefully — with the loaders' own ValueError vocabulary — instead of crashing mid-run or silently accepting a file the rest of the pipeline cannot handle.

Positioning (web-checked 2026-10-20, see docs/RESEARCH_LOG.md cycle 172): fuzzing models is occupied (PromptFuzz/ps-fuzz and garak fire jailbreak/injection attacks at endpoints), and fuzzing code is occupied (Atheris/libFuzzer are coverage-guided engines a developer wires to a target). No LLM evaluation harness checked ships a first-class command that fuzz-tests its own fixture loaders against a published accept/reject contract, across both of its input formats (strict JSON at runtime, CSV at authoring time). That combination is the contribution; nothing stronger is claimed.

docs.title: 1. The contract under test
docs.text:
The loaders (datasets.parse_dataset / load_dataset, fixtures.parse_fixture_csv / read_authoring_file, discipline via core.Split) document a fail-closed contract: any malformed input is refused with ValueError; valid input is accepted exactly as written (stored fixture data stays byte-exact; only comparisons normalize). Outcomes:

  • accept — the loader returns normally.
  • reject — the loader raises ValueError (any message).
  • accept_warn — CSV only: the loader returns normally and the fixture is named in the returned empty-expected list (the documented vacuous-pass warning channel).

A case whose observed outcome differs is a finding, classified:

  • crash — a non-ValueError exception escaped the loader;
  • unexpected_accept / unexpected_reject — the outcome flipped;
  • warning_mismatch — the warning channel disagreed.

docs.title: 2. Corpus
docs.text:
Two base corpora, both minimal and known-valid (each carries a control case proving the harness itself is green before any mutation is trusted): a JSON dataset (2 search + 2 held-out fixtures, distinct ids/groups/message sets) and the equivalent authoring CSV. Mutators apply exactly one contract violation (or one documented non-violation) each; combination mutations are out of scope because their expected outcome is not independently derivable. Seed-parameterized mutators (overlong lengths, confusable choice) vary values, never the expected outcome class. Case classes, per target:

  • JSON: marker literal in content/expected (accept — content has no blocklist at load time; the special-token audit is a separate, warning-only layer), homoglyph twin id/group/messages (accept — documented out-of-scope in core.Split: no normalization form unifies confusables), NFD/NFC twin id, group, and message set plus the U+2126/U+03A9 canonical-singleton twin (reject — NFC uniqueness/leakage), the U+FB01 ligature near-twin and within-partition identical messages and trailing-space/case-differing cross-partition groups (accept — Split compares NFC-normalized, unstripped, case-sensitive keys across partitions only), overlong and at-limit fields (char-counted, including a 16,384-astral-char field), empty and whitespace-only expected (accept, no warning channel), duplicate ids (same/cross partition), cross-partition group, identical cross-partition messages, missing/extra top-level keys, duplicate JSON keys (top-level, nested, and escape-equivalent), a legitimately escape-spelled key (accept), NaN/Infinity constants, 1e999 overflow and 5,000-digit integers, deep nesting (5,000 — outcome-asserted only; the guard that fires is depth- and interpreter-dependent), truncated, trailing-garbage, BOM-prefixed, empty, and whitespace-only text, top-level non-object, wrong field types (number/null/float in string fields), missing / extra fixture and message fields, messages not a list, empty / over-long / misalternating / assistant-final message lists, blank id/group with the exact code point named (space rejects; U+00A0 rejects — strip() removes it; U+200B-only accepts — it does not), empty partition, 101-fixture partition, 100-fixture partitions (accept boundary), byte-oversize document, exactly-2,000,000-byte document (accept boundary), control characters raw in the source string (reject — strict JSON) vs escape form (accept), zero-width content (accept), key order permuted (accept), lone surrogates per field (§3).
  • CSV: bad header (case-changed), BOM-prefixed header (reject — deliberately visible per the module docstring), fully quoted header (accept), trailing empty header column (reject), message columns out of order / too many / none, bad partition, blank id/group with another cell present, an all-empty row (accept — silently skipped by the reader; pinned so the leniency is contractual, not accidental), overlong message cell / expected / id / group (reject — id/group are §3-class fixes, see below), id at the limit (accept), first-message empty, gap-then-content, assistant-final conversation, short row ending after a user message (accept — trailing columns are simply absent), duplicate ids, cross-partition group and identical messages, NFD twin id, too many rows, partition overflow, missing partition, field over the csv parser limit, bare-CR line endings (reject), extra cells in a row, quoted newline in a cell (accept — documented), CRLF line endings (accept), quoting leniencies (unterminated quote at EOF, quoted field with trailing junk, quote mid-field — all accept: the csv reader is non-strict and the stored value is pinned), marker literal in a cell (accept), empty expected (accept_warn), whitespace-only expected (accept, no warning — the warning channel fires on the exact empty string only), literal null/123 field text (accept — CSV fields are strings), empty and whitespace-only documents (reject by different paths), lone-surrogate cell (reject — §3). Raw NUL in a CSV cell is excluded: it accepts on CPython 3.12, but the behaviour is not verified on 3.11/3.13, and a version-dependent case would falsify F3 — the table does not pin what it cannot guarantee.
  • Files (written to a fresh temp directory by the runner): valid control, invalid UTF-8 bytes, CESU-8 surrogate bytes (reject as not-valid-UTF-8 — the file-level surrogate case), BOM bytes (reject at parse), byte-oversize file, directory as path, missing file, FIFO as path (reject, no hang — the readers' O_NONBLOCK + fstat defence), symlink to a regular file (accept — the readers follow links by design) — for both load_dataset and the read_authoring_file + parse path.

Two construction rules the swarm forced (red-team A2/B8): a case's payload construction is part of its identity — raw-text cases are built as raw text, structured cases via json.dumps (which escapes control characters) — because the same semantic value has different contract outcomes in the two constructions; and a reject case may carry a message pin: where the loaders' vocabulary is genuinely fixed (their own literal messages: the nonfinite-constant message, the size-limit messages, the csv parser-limit message, and the §3 surrogate messages), the case asserts the exception is exactly ValueError and the message contains the pinned text. Everywhere else (JSON syntax errors, nesting) only the ValueError class is asserted — those messages are the interpreter's and vary by version (red-team B3).

The corpus digest is SHA-256 over the canonical case list (names, targets, payloads); it is reported with every run so two runs can be compared without diffing output.

docs.title: 3. Pre-registered findings (found by probing and the swarm, pre-build)
docs.text:
Three genuine loader defects, all of one family — the loaders accept or report something their own contract disowns — each fixed fail-closed in cycle 172 and pinned by fuzzer cases plus direct regression tests:

  1. Lone surrogates (JSON). Cycle 86 settled the serializer: a lone surrogate "can never be written to a UTF-8 fixture file", and split_to_json_text refuses it deliberately. The loader was never extended the same rule — parse_dataset accepts JSON escape-form surrogates ("\ud800" in the source text) into every fixture field, producing Splits the repo's own serializer refuses and that strict-encode helpers downstream meet with bare UnicodeEncodeErrors. (Rendering and evaluation tolerate surrogates in degraded form — red-team B verified — so the claim is unwritable and un-round-trippable, not "unusable everywhere"; the loader extension is a new decision registered here, with its falsifier below.) Both parsers also rejected raw-surrogate source text only accidentally: the byte-cap len(text.encode("utf-8")) raises a bare UnicodeEncodeError (a ValueError subclass, so callers survive, but the message is a codec leak, not the loaders' vocabulary). Fix: datasets._text rejects any field containing a lone surrogate (covers the escape form in every stored field — id, group, expected, content; a decoded check, so valid surrogate pairs decoding to astral characters stay accepted); both parsers convert the byte-cap encode failure into a deliberate ValueError naming the surrogate. CSV needs no decoded-value check: it has no escape form, and files cannot carry raw surrogates past the readers' strict UTF-8 decode. Falsifier: if any in-repo consumer is shown to legitimately require surrogate fixture text through the loader, the cases flip to accept and the fix is reverted — none is known (the one surrogate-tolerant consumer, core seed derivation, constructs fixtures directly), and the burden of proof sits with acceptance, because acceptance is what produces unserializable Splits. Note the swarm's vacuity catch (red-team B1): outcome-only assertions cannot pin this fix for raw-surrogate text (it already raised a ValueError subclass), so the raw-surrogate cases carry message pins.
  2. CSV id/group length (red-team A1). parse_fixture_csv length-checked message cells and expected but never id or group: a 17,000-char id was accepted, and the resulting Split then failed split_to_json_text's round-trip — the authoring path accepting exactly what its own by-construction guarantee refuses, and a JSON↔CSV coherence break with no documented reason. Fix: the same MAX_TEXT check, same message, extended to id and group.
  3. csv.Error mislabel (red-team A4). The CSV reader's error handler reported every parse error as "field exceeds the parser limit" — e.g. bare-CR line endings, which contain no large field at all. Fix: the size message is kept for the genuine field-limit error (existing pins depend on it); other parse errors report as parse errors.

docs.title: 4. Determinism
docs.text: Generation is a pure function of the seed: parameter values are derived from SHA-256 over (seed, case name, parameter) — the repo's own seed-derivation precedent — never from random.Random methods beyond random(), whose cross-version reproducibility CPython does not guarantee (red-team B4). Same seed → same case list → same digest. The digest is SHA-256 over case names, targets, and payload bytes (file-case payloads are their bytes; no temp path ever enters a case identity, the digest, or the report — red-team B6). Reports contain no timestamps and no exception message text: a conforming case records a fixed detail token, and a finding records the outcome classification plus, for a crash, the exception class name — because interpreter messages (nesting guards, integer-digit limits, JSON syntax positions) vary by version and configuration even when the outcome does not (red-team B3). Exception details are sanitized (control/bidi/surrogate- stripped, length-bounded) before they enter any human-facing summary — hostile fixture text must not reach a terminal through the fuzzer's own output. The runner executes cases on the calling thread only: the JSON parser's recursion failure mode is stack-sensitive off the main thread (red-team B5). Running the corpus is time-bounded by construction: both loaders check the 2 MB byte cap before parsing, the largest case is a ~2 MB document, and the Split discipline checks are set-based over at most 100 fixtures per partition.

docs.title: 5. Claims and falsifiers
docs.text:
• F1 Every reject case raises ValueError and nothing else; a single non-ValueError escape falsifies the loaders' fail-closed claim, and the fuzzer exists to catch exactly that.
  • F2 Every accept case returns a Split (or split + warnings) whose stored data equals the loader's decoded field values exactly (red-team A17 rescoped this from "byte-exact against the input": JSON escapes resolve, CSV quoting is removed, CRLF is stripped, short rows are padded — stored data is post-decode by construction; NFC normalization is comparison-only and never rewrites it). A stored value that differs from the decoded source field falsifies F2.
  • F3 Same seed → identical digest and identical report, on any supported Python (3.11–3.13). A case whose outcome depends on the interpreter version falsifies F3 and must be redesigned, not pinned per-version.
  • F4 (honest limit) A green fuzz run proves the published table holds — nothing more. It does not prove the loaders accept exactly the valid files, nor that unmutated classes are safe.

docs.title: 6. Non-goals
docs.text: No diff-reports section and no HTML report block: fuzz output is a maintenance artifact, not experiment output (the pack/verify precedent). No fixture-quality judgment (a boring but valid fixture passes; that is correct). No coverage-guided search (see Positioning). No new dependencies; stdlib only.

docs.title: Cross-format history probe — design round (ADJUDICATED: NO-BUILD)
Round summary (coordinator #44, design round only — nothing built)
docs.text:
Wave-11 slate rank 3: cross-format history (tentatively run --history-frame). The candidate sketch (~/workspace/agents_out/wave11/slate_candidates.md Candidate 3): hold every message's text byte-identical, render the history turns in a foreign chat-template family A while the final turn stays in the candidate's own family B, and test whether per-candidate verdicts and the selection are invariant to that reframing.

The round ran the full blind team (briefs in ~/workspace/agents_out/historyframe/: research.md, redteam_a.md, redteam_b.md, verifier.md). The verdict is unanimous NO-BUILD for the sketch as specified — researcher, both blind red teams, and the verifier's blind interim audit each reached it independently, fatal by fatal, by execution. The fabrication sweep is clean — a fourth consecutive round: every cited tree symbol resolves, and both external arXiv identifiers resolve to the cited titles, authors, and substance. The errors found are counting/criterion slips, corrected in §5; none is load-bearing for the verdict.

The researcher additionally specified a complete repaired instrument (research §6: bos-native field splice over synthhistory's frozen prepended history, carrier-Format evaluation, two frozen donor families, a derived McNemar-gated classification). The verifier upholds, and the coordinator concurs, that this instrument is a resubmission, not an amendment, under this program's standing test (§2): it changes the population mechanism, replaces the headline BOS semantics, changes the headline population, and adds the decision rule the sketch lacks. It is recorded in §3 as the resubmission candidate. No build cycle may act on it without a fresh blind design review.

docs.title: 1. Why NO-BUILD: the fatal defects of the candidate as specified
F1 — The population is undefined: "history" has three incompatible readings, and the shipped fixtures are half-vacuous
docs.text: The sketch never says where the history turns come from, and the tree offers three mutually exclusive sources — the fixture's own messages, synthhistory's scripted turns, self-generated replies — each a different instrument with a different construct and budget (RT-A F1, RT-B F4, R §2 F1, V F-POPULATION). Executed on the shipped example set (examples/fixtures.json, verified by all four lanes): search = search-copy-blue (1 message, no history) and search-latest-green (3 messages); held-out likewise 1 of 2. For a single-turn fixture the foreign condition is byte-identical to control by construction — guaranteed-concordant filler in every denominator. The loader admits 1-message fixtures (datasets.py:53-72; MAX_MESSAGES = 21 at datasets.py:14), so no dataset guarantees the sketch's "100 fixtures" of history. Under the fixture-own reading, history length (dose) and content are per-fixture and uncontrolled — in the shipped set the history assistant turns are task answers ("RED", "NORTH") and the final turns refer to them, so discordance would pool framing with history-content leverage (RT-A F12, RT-B F4). Under the self-generated reading the budget is false: each foreign cell needs one generation per history exchange before the scored generation — up to 28,800 generations at history_6 depth against the sketch's 7,200 (RT-A F1, arithmetic verified).

docs.title: F2 — The hybrid renderer does not exist, its seam semantics are unspecified, and the sketch's seam paragraph is wrong in both particulars
docs.text:
Format.render (core.py:76-115) renders a whole message tuple in one framing and requires a final user turn. Executed by all four lanes: render(history_alone) raises ValueError for 29/29 catalog families — a history prefix, which ends with an assistant turn, is not a renderable object. The sketch's literal recipe (render the segments, concatenate) fails its own pre-registered control check: concatenating a history render (which needs a dummy closing user turn to satisfy render at all) with a final-turn render duplicates BOS, strands family A's open suffix mid-prompt, and inserts a dummy turn (RT-A F2: 182 vs 132 chars chatml, 362 vs 246 llama3, control condition included). The sketch's seam note — A's render "may carry its own BOS and closing suffix mid-prompt", to be kept "verbatim (recommended)" — is executed-wrong twice (RT-B F1, verifier V-2.2): in a prefix-truncated A render there is no A closing suffix at the seam (the open suffix is appended only after the final turn), and A's BOS lands at position 0, replacing B's, not mid-prompt. The decisions that determine the prompt's bytes are all unmade in the sketch, and each is load-bearing:

  • BOS ownership. Coordinator execution: the donor-BOS and final-BOS splice readings produce different prompts on 658/812 ordered family pairs. Only the choice is frozen in §3's resubmission; the sketch freezes none.
  • repeat_bos cadence. No catalog base sets it, but shipped candidates do (llama3/toggle-bos via catalog.candidates(mutate=True)). A per-segment cadence restart produces 1 BOS where the control has 4 (RT-A F2).
  • None-vs-empty fallbacks. core.py:57-73 honours empty-string overrides as distinct from None; a hybrid written with the natural or fallback fails control identity for mistral_large alone (open_suffix "" vs assistant_prefix " "), so a casual control test on chatml passes while the renderer is wrong (RT-A F2).
  • Open suffix is not history framing. open_suffix != assistant_prefix for 15/29 families (verifier-confirmed list), 9 of them opening a think block; the suffix is the generation prompt for the next reply, and any recipe that keeps a history render's tail injects it, sometimes unclosed, at the seam.

The control-identity check the sketch pre-registers is a test, not a specification: three independent executions this round (coordinator: 118 candidate Formats × 2 conversations; verifier; researcher: 944/944 renders) prove a faithful field-splice semantics can reproduce B.render(full) byte-identically when A == B — by a recipe the sketch does not contain.

docs.title: F3 — There is no decision rule: the any-difference falsifier fires on noise with probability ≈ 1, and the selection readout is a one-flip tripwire
docs.text: The sketch's falsifier is verbatim the one this program has killed twice (DIRECTIVE_DESIGN F2; INSTRUCTIONDISTANCE_DESIGN F3): "any fixture whose verdict differs … or a selection flip in any foreign-frame condition." No floor, no discordant-pair rule, no fail-closed vocabulary. Executed (RT-A F3, RT-B F3, V F-NOISE): at per-cell jitter ε = 0.001, P(any discordance in the panel) = 0.909–0.992; at ε ≥ 0.005, ≈ 1.000. batchinv.py exists precisely because identical token sequences need not reproduce across batch composition, so ε = 0 cannot be assumed. The selection half is worse: _select_winner (experiments.py:3847-3863) requires the winner to pass every search fixture, so one flipped cell manufactures a "selection flip"; conditioned on a native winner existing, P(it loses all-pass status in ≥ 1 of 2 foreign conditions) = 0.633 / 0.866 / 0.982 at ε = 0.005 / 0.01 / 0.02 (RT-B F3, verifier re-evaluated). Nor can a builder patch in a familiar floor: any (6,·)-shaped discordant floor fires ≈ 1.000 at this panel's N = 100, because the null discordance mean is 50 (random) or ≈ 18 (competent) — the sibling floors were derived for panels of 16 generated cases, and this panel's N is the user's fixture count (RT-B F3). As specified, the instrument can essentially only report "not invariant" — a verdict decided by the rule, not measured from the model.

docs.title: F4 — Attribution: the treatment is a bundle of at least five simultaneous changes, and the claim names one cause
docs.text:
Control vs foreign differ at once in (RT-A F4, RT-B F2, R §2 F4):

  • Marker identity — the named treatment.
  • BOS identity/presence (F2): the prompt's first tokens change with A. The tree treats BOS as a verdict-moving axis in its own right (core.local_repairs, core.py:118-143, ships toggle-bos/no-bos candidates to measure it).
  • History token length. Same six synthetic turns framed: 341 chars (mistral) to 989 chars (kimi3) (verifier-confirmed); per-exchange prompt-length deltas are nonzero for 766/812 ordered pairs, range [−213, +213] chars under a bos-inclusive splice (segment-only splice: 770/812, ±216 — both executions correct under their splice definitions, and the divergence between two honest executions is itself F2's point). Length and final-turn position are shipped axes (needle, distraction, placement).
  • Think scaffolding. Nine families carry think material inside their assistant history prefix itself (glm45, glm53, laguna, ling, nanbeige42, kimi3, k2horizon, hy4, minimax3 — verifier-executed count; §5 corrects RT-A's five). Foreign history in these families injects a foreign reasoning-channel scaffold the control lacks — an output-priming component, not a delimiter relabelling.
  • Closure conventions. deepseek history has no user-turn terminator (user_turn_end=""); some families' turns run together. "Foreign framing" here includes a segmentation change.

The sketch's claim sentence attributes any discordance to framing-as-such. What the contrast can honestly estimate is discordance between two named, frozen prompt strings per (candidate, fixture) — the payload settlement. The sketch's Monday-morning framing ("whether history must be re-rendered on migration or can be carried over as-is") additionally fails on the artifact: the hybrid (A's BOS at the head of a B session, B's final turn) is neither a carried-over transcript nor a re-render — no migration produces it (RT-B F2).

docs.title: F5 — The pair rule is broken: unnamed pairs, a disjointness criterion that excludes the realistic migrations, and a family/candidate unit mismatch
docs.text:
The ordered pair space is 29 × 28 = 812; the sketch freezes 2 (0.25%), names neither, and gives no selection rule beyond "disjoint marker sets" (RT-B F5). Executed by all lanes:

  • Aliased pairs collapse to control. Under the history-segment criterion (bos excluded), 36 ordered pairs have a foreign history segment byte-identical to control: classes {chatml, qwen3, qwen38, kolibri, lfm25, nemotron35}, {gemma, gemma3}, {deepseek, deepseek41}, {muse_glimmer, muse_spark} — 21 distinct history segments across 29 families. Including BOS, 24 ordered pairs are byte-identical outright. Any such cell is a guaranteed null pooled as invariance — the canonical-form ids-identical trap.
  • Disjointness selects against the utility. The aliased ChatML-shaped families are precisely the plausible real migrations (8 families' user_prefix contains <|im_start|>; verifier-confirmed). A disjoint-marker rule excludes every one and selects maximally distant pairs, where F4's bundle is largest. Marker disjointness is in any case the wrong criterion: the operative check is rendered-segment equality (331–355 of 406 unordered pairs are textually disjoint under either lane's extraction, including pairs whose segments are identical).
  • Global vs per-candidate pairs dilemma. Fixed global pairs collapse for candidates B ∈ {A1, A2} (their "foreign" condition is the control); per-B pairs make the per-condition selection compare candidates who faced different treatments — the restricted-common-set defect. The sketch's selection headline is coherent under neither reading (RT-B F5).
  • Unit mismatch. Selection in this tree is over candidates, not families: a run's candidates are one family's base plus local-repair/thinking variants (catalog.candidates, catalog.py:914ff; 118 candidate Formats across the catalog, 89 beyond the 29 bases — §5 corrects RT-B's 107). "Final-turn family B" and "foreign family A" are undefined for variant candidates whose framing differs from base exactly in the fields the splice moves (RT-A F10, RT-B F5).

docs.title: F6 — The boundary mechanism: a correct answer terminating like its history fails as a wrong answer, and the sketch has no decomposition
docs.text: Stage verdicts conjoin exact_match and boundary_found with the boundary resolved per candidate — i.e. per final-turn family B (experiments.py _resolve_boundaries). The hybrid's history demonstrates A's terminator after every assistant turn. Executed through the real core.evaluate (RT-B F6; reproduced exactly by the verifier and by the coordinator with independent stubs): a stub answering GREEN and terminating with B's <|im_end|> → exact_match=True, boundary_found=True; the same stub answering GREEN and terminating with A's <|eot_id|> → exact_match=False, boundary_found=False, answer recorded as 'GREEN<|eot_id|>' — with no boundary cut, the terminator text joins the scored span, so the failure is double-counted as a wrong answer. The sketch never states which boundary governs a hybrid cell and provides no exact-only vs boundary-only decomposition (the payload/negation settlements made that decomposition mandatory). Under the any-difference falsifier, termination-style discordance is indistinguishable from answer discordance, and the migration advice differs completely between the two. Ordered attrition rides along: foreign framings run longer, so arm_context_exceeded censoring is ordered by arm (the DIRECTIVE F6(a) defect), with no per-condition attrition reporting specified.

docs.title: F7 — The token-encoding mitigation is incoherent: "token-real in both frames" selects the headline population by checkpoint, and its fallback contradicts the headline
docs.text: The sketch concedes the deliforge axis leaks in and proposes the headline population be "cells where the history's markers are token-real in both frames, or the confound is disclosed per cell, never pooled silently." Executed/adjudicated (RT-A F7, RT-B F7, R §2 F6, V F-TOKENREAL): token-reality is a property of (checkpoint tokenizer × literal), not of a frame — under HF's default split_special_tokens=False a literal becomes a real control token iff the checkpoint's tokenizer reserves it (control_tokens.py:1-14; backend encode is a plain tokenizer.encode(text, add_special_tokens=False, ...) call, backends.py:1192-1200, :1284). On a given checkpoint, typically only its native family's markers are reserved, so the headline population varies per checkpoint, is selected on exactly the axis being measured, and can be empty — with no eligibility pre-check and no fail-closed vocabulary for that outcome (contrast deliforge's find_encoding_pair, deliforge.py:238-281, which fails closed). "In both frames" is undefined for families whose markers are ordinary text. And the OR-fallback contradicts the pooled selection headline: a per-condition selection is a pooled object. Separately, the single-encode seam re-tokenizes the novel A-terminator/B-prefix adjacency; the tree's own precedent refuses exactly this where a seam matters (prefill joins at the token-id level, prefill.py:19-24), and the sketch records no seam-canonicality per cell.

docs.title: F8 — The build surface is misstated and the utility overclaims: "scoring untouched / size M" is false, and scripted history is not a migrated transcript
docs.text: core.evaluate renders through the candidate alone (prompt = candidate.render(case.messages), core.py:846), and no Format renders the hybrid (F2), so the probe needs a new evaluation surface — a plan-keyed backend wrapper (the DeliforgeBackend precedent, deliforge.py:492-547), an evaluate variant, or the researcher's carrier-Format route (§3) — plus a payload schema from which the diff validator can recompute each cell, plus configuration-digest binding of pair, recipe, and history source (the cycle-207 obligation, _require_native_match, experiments.py:3940; RT-B F9). None of this is in the sketch's size-M estimate (RT-A F5). On the claim side: whichever population reading is chosen, the sketch's utility sentence describes generated history — a live transcript written by a model under A — while the cheap readings measure frozen scripted strings. Multiturn already settled that scripted and self-generated history are different treatments and must not be conflated (multiturn.py:16-46, including its special-token screening discipline, which foreign-framed genuine history violates by design). Compounding it, for the think-scaffolding families the catalog's own comments record that real templates treat assistant history differently from the lab's flattened Format hypothesis (reasoning preserved, dropped, or required, by family and branch): a field splice measures the lab's Format hypotheses' strings, a scoping the sketch never makes (RT-B F8).

docs.title: Non-fatals, adjudicated (what passed)
docs.text:
• Duplication is not a standalone fatal. The residue — genuine history turns, framed in A, preceding a final turn in B, benign content, verdict readout — is narrowly real (verifier §A7 map, upheld): synthhistory owns history presence over prepended turns rendered own-frame; multiturn owns sharded delivery and scripted-vs-self history, always own-frame; faketurn/deliforge own foreign delimiters inside content and the encoding axis; hierarchy owns single-turn privilege position; batch-invariance owns no part of this design but is the standing proof behind F3. The burden the sketch fails is not novelty — it is that the residue is unmeasurable as specified (F1–F8), and that a repaired version must justify itself as a new instrument rather than an arm on synthhistory_stage (RT-A F9).
  • Splice control identity is achievable (F2): three independent executions reproduce B.render(full) under a faithful field splice. Credited to the sketch's instinct, not its text.
  • The single-encode premise is tree-true: backends encode rendered text with add_special_tokens=False (backends.py:1200, :1284), so a concatenated string is a legal prompt input.
  • Budget arithmetic is consistent with the tree's caps (≤24 candidates, ≤100 search fixtures): 3 × 100 × 24 = 7,200 is an honest worst case for the sketch's three conditions; its defect is F1's, not arithmetic.
  • The name is free as a string: --history-frame / history_frame / historyframe return zero hits in the package, docs/USAGE.md, and README.md (all lanes). Whether it overclaims is a resubmission naming-audit question (F8), not a fatal.

docs.title: 2. Why the repaired instrument is a resubmission, not an amendment
docs.text: The standing test (payload, answer-syntax, directive, instruction-language, instruction-distance rounds; contrast negation): BUILD-as-amended is available when the sketch's population, arms, and scorer were already frozen and executable before the round, and the corrections fix the decision rule and claim language of that same instrument. Here nothing load-bearing was frozen: the population source is unspecified (F1), the renderer and its seam semantics do not exist (F2), there is no decision rule (F3), the pairs are unnamed and the pair criterion is wrong (F5), the headline population is incoherent (F7), and the scorer cannot score the treatment (F8). The researcher's §6 repairs all of it — by choosing a population mechanism (synthhistory's prepended frozen history on the run's search fixtures), replacing the headline BOS semantics (bos-native headline plus a descriptive verbatim arm, against the sketch's recommended verbatim headline), changing the headline population (render/ids-divergent gated, against token-real gated), and adding a derived decision rule. That is the payload configuration: a new instrument, reviewable only as a resubmission through a fresh blind design review. Any deviation by a future build from this settlement voids it.

docs.title: 3. Resubmission specification (NOT a build order)
docs.text:
The resubmission candidate is the researcher's §6 (~/workspace/agents_out/historyframe/research.md), incorporated by reference. Its frozen items, in summary:

  1. Treatment (one dimension). The framing strings of the prepended history segment only — per-turn role prefixes, per-role terminators, the segment's internal repeat_bos behaviour — from a Format's fields. Message contents are byte-identical across arms by construction; the final segment, the prompt-initial bos, and the open suffix are always the candidate's own. Token length, seam shape, and marker encoding are consequences, reported per case; the claim subject is the named frozen framing pair.
  2. Population. The run's search fixtures only (≤100), post-hoc stage; held-out never treated; primary decision/winner/exit code never touched. Every search fixture is prepended with synthhistory.build_history_fixtures(cases, condition="history_6") (synthhistory.py:105-131): the frozen benign task-free SYNTHETIC_TURNS, reused, never re-authored. The fixture's own messages are the tail, always framed by the candidate's own family. The claim is scoped to this frozen transcript and says nothing about task-bearing or self-generated histories.
  3. Renderer (frozen formal semantics). A segment function over Format fields with is not None fallback semantics copied from core.py:76-115, global-index repeat_bos cadence following the segment's family, B's bos at the head, A's open suffix never appearing, no separator inserted at the seam. Under A == B it reproduces Format.render exactly (research PoC1: 944/944 renders; arithmetic verifier-confirmed: 118 candidate Formats × 4 message sets × 2 BOS readings).
  4. Evaluation path. One core.evaluate call per (candidate, arm, fixture) through a carrier Format(B.name, "", "", "", "") holding the hybrid text as a single user message (verified this round: the carrier renders its single message verbatim), with B's resolved boundary ids and the fixture's original id in every arm (request-seed identity, core.py:371), following the _canonical_form_cell pattern (experiments.py:9473). The own arm is byte- and verdict-identical to the synthhistory history_6 condition through the new path.
  5. Arms. own (headline baseline) / foreign_chatml / foreign_llama3 (headline contrasts; the pair is string-disjoint against each other and the obvious neighbours, executed) / verbatim_chatml (descriptive only: differs from its headline twin only in the leading bos string, so its discordance against foreign_chatml is the BOS-substitution share). Selection readout: per-arm conservative selection recomputed on the common completed set, withheld on mismatched or empty sets, winner headlines in canonical-form's vocabulary (winner_changed / winner_stable / winner_abstention_asymmetric / winner_undefined); flips against the primary run printed separately and labelled as pooling history presence with frame, never the headline.
  6. Eligibility and divergence accounting. Per (candidate, contrast): render-identical fixtures excluded and counted as n_render_identical (a contrast render-identical on every fixture is inapplicable for that candidate — no classification is emitted, and the inapplicable share is printed, never read as robustness); ids-identical cases likewise excluded and counted, a same-ids verdict flip recorded as a determinism finding; per-contrast id_length_delta list and max_abs_id_delta printed. The encoding stratum is a run-level label per foreign family (per-literal token_real iff backend.encode(literal) yields exactly one id; stratum all_single / all_fragmented / mixed, table printed when mixed), printed beside every classification and compared in diff-reports; it never gates the headline. No checkpoint fact is asserted: all token-real evidence this round is stub-level machinery definition.
  7. Decision rule (derived, with printed characteristics). Per candidate per headline contrast over paired completed render-divergent ids-divergent cases (n paired, a = own-only passes, b = foreign-only passes, d = a + b): n < 10 → insufficient; d = 0 → no_discordance_observed; d < 6 → below_threshold; a == b → discordant_balanced (descriptive only); else two-sided exact McNemar p < 0.05 (confidentiality.py:293 mcnemar_exact_p) → discordant_asymmetric, else below_threshold. The falsification boolean is discordant_asymmetric alone. The d ≥ 6 floor is forced by α = 0.05 (5–0 gives two-sided p = 0.0625; 6–0 gives 0.03125). Operating characteristics (research PoC5, verifier spot-reproduced within Monte Carlo error): asymmetric fire ≤ 3.6% on the random-labeller null, ≤ 3.1% on competent nulls, ≈ 0 under ε = 0.01 jitter, at every N tabulated (16–100); power at a 25-point drop is 0.99 at N = 100 but a coin flip (0.50–0.53) at N ≤ 30 — the exact random-labeller fire rate at the run's own n and the family-wise expectation (≈ 1.44 false labels per 48-decision panel under the random null) are printed beside the classifications, and below_threshold is labelled weak evidence in the section.
  8. Decomposition. Every discordant pair decomposed as boundary_only (answer digests equal), exact_only (digests differ, both boundaries found), or mixed; all three counts printed per contrast. Per-arm attrition (n_context_exceeded, n_evaluation_failed, n_render_identical, n_ids_identical) printed beside every paired rate.
  9. Vocabulary (frozen). Classifications exactly canonical-form's: insufficient, no_discordance_observed, discordant_balanced, discordant_asymmetric, below_threshold. Stage details exactly {cancelled, historyframe_record_budget_exceeded, historyframe_screen_failed} (the last bound to the pre-generation screens: S1 per-candidate control identity — any mismatch fails the whole stage before any generation; S2 frozen-text audit via audit_special_token_literals, fixtures.py:471; S3 budget caps). Per-cell details exactly {"", arm_context_exceeded, arm_evaluation_failed}. Whole-stage failure: {"available": False, "detail": "historyframe_unavailable"}; the stage never fails the run.
  10. Counts. 4 generating arms × ≤100 search fixtures × ≤24 candidates = 9,600 generations legal maximum (headline arms only: 7,200); 2,400 multi-cell ground records; 12 MiB records cap (house pattern). A run's actual candidate count is one family's variants (typically ≤ 8): the legal maximum is a cap, not an expectation.
  11. Records and validator. Digest-only records (hybrid-text digest and token count per arm, divergence flags, id_length_delta, canonical-form-shaped cells). The diff validator re-implements the segment renderer, hybrid, eligibility accounting, classification, and restricted-set selection — never imports them — and recomputes every aggregate. Report text passes through _escape_text (reporting.py:28) only.
  12. Claim (the only falsification-class sentence). "On this candidate, on this run's search fixtures preceded by the frozen synthetic history, rendering that history's turns in the frozen chatml [resp. llama3] framing instead of the candidate's own framing produced verdict discordance at or above this panel's derived floor, asymmetric by an exact McNemar test — a history-frame discordance for these named framings and this frozen history, on this checkpoint." No sentence in any report may generalise it to histories, migrations, or templates in general.
  13. Utility (resubmission, scoped). A team migrating a live product between chat-template families — or importing a transcript one client rendered into a session another serves — uses this, per candidate, to decide whether a carried-over history must be re-rendered into the new family's framing before the final turn is trusted, on their own search fixtures, before a silent history-frame flip changes the template winner they already picked. (The sketch's migration sentence is removed for any scripted-history instrument, §5 item 6; this scoped version is the fresh review's to accept or reject under item 14.)
  14. Name. --history-frame is the resubmission's proposal, free as a string (§1 non-fatals); it ships only if a build cycle's USAGE naming audit passes, with help text stating the prepend in its first sentence so no user reads it as reframing their fixtures' native histories.

docs.title: Fresh-review agenda (silence on any item = NO-BUILD)
docs.text:
The fresh review must settle, head-on (research §7, verifier §A4–A5, coordinator additions):

  1. Scripted-only history: accept the §3.12 string-scoped claim as worth the build surface, or require a self-generated variant with its own population discipline and screening — it may not be smuggled in as an arm.
  2. One dose (k = 6 turns) vs a frozen dose ladder with its own decision rule.
  3. Native-history reframing (fixtures' own multi-turn histories): v1 scope accepted as the first instrument, or a deferral of the real one.
  4. Verbatim arm: keep at 2,400 generations' legal-maximum cost, or cut to three arms and print the BOS bundle as a named limitation. Degeneracy (verifier §A4.2): for candidates whose own bos is empty, verbatim_chatml ≡ foreign_chatml byte-identically — the arm must be counted inapplicable there, never pooled.
  5. Small-panel power: at N ≤ 30 the rule is coin-flip powered at a 25-point drop (research PoC5); the shipped example set (2 search fixtures) classifies insufficient, correctly. Accept with at-N characteristics printed, or pair with a generated panel (re-opening the selection-over-generated-sets question) — argued, not defaulted.
  6. Boundary-only counting: §3.8 counts verdict discordance with the decomposition printed beside it; requiring exact-only-counting is permitted only with re-derived operating characteristics.
  7. The rule's high-jitter behaviour (coordinator execution, §4): the McNemar discordant-count rule's null behaviour at ε = 0.05 with high pass rates (D = 80 of 100) was not in research PoC5's grid; the coordinator's rate-based (Fisher) variant held ≤ 1.2% across the ε ≤ 0.05 grid in the same simulation harness. The fresh review must print the chosen rule's characteristics on the ε ∈ {0.01, 0.02, 0.05} × D ∈ {20, 50, 80} grid before freezing it.
  8. Diagonal contrast (RT-A F4): not required for §3.12's named-string claim (verifier §A4.3); required if any future wording claims mixing-specific harm.
  9. Configuration-digest binding (RT-B F9): discharged in §3.11 via per-arm hybrid-text digests plus the validator mirror — the fresh review confirms explicitly.
  10. Instrument vs arm (RT-A F9): the fresh review must explicitly accept the resubmission as a new instrument rather than a synthhistory condition, with the §1 duplication map as the record.
  11. Neighbour-tool re-survey (LM Eval Harness, HELM, PromptPerfect, OpenAI evals, DSPy) is UNEXECUTED this round; the uniqueness combination (§6) stays scoped to surveyed sources until a fresh review re-runs it.

docs.title: 4. Adjudication evidence (coordinator's own execution)
docs.text:
• Render refusal / control identity. Format.render on SYNTHETIC_TURNS raises ValueError (final-user contract). A generalised per-message-format loop reproducing core.py:76-115 semantics is byte-identical to the native render under A == B for all 118 candidate Formats (candidates(family, mutate=True) summed over 29 families) × 2 conversations — and diverges from it under every naive segment-restart or or-fallback variant tried by the lanes.
  • BOS ownership. Donor-BOS vs final-BOS splices differ on 658/812 ordered pairs; char deltas (foreign − control) span [−645, +645] over the 6-turn history.
  • Aliased pairs. Segment criterion (bos excluded): 36 ordered pairs byte-identical, classes {chatml, qwen3, qwen38, kolibri, lfm25, nemotron35}, {gemma, gemma3}, {deepseek, deepseek41}, {muse_glimmer, muse_spark} → 21 distinct history segments. Segment+bos criterion: 24 ordered pairs. (The two counts carry different criteria; §5 item 10.)
  • Boundary mechanism. Independent stub through the real core.evaluate (byte backend, chatml boundary): GREEN + <|im_end|> → pass; GREEN + <|eot_id|> → exact_match=False, boundary_found=False, answer 'GREEN<|eot_id|>'. Reproduces RT-B F6 exactly.
  • Population prevalence. examples/fixtures.json: search and held-out each 1 of 2 single-turn.
  • Carrier route. Format(B.name, "", "", "", "") renders a single user message byte-verbatim (executed on text containing foreign markers and seams) — the resubmission's evaluation path is mechanically real.
  • Pair disjointness. Non-empty framing literals of chatml vs llama3/gemma/mistral pairwise disjoint (executed, ∅ intersections).
  • Decision-rule simulations. Coordinator Monte Carlo (40,000/30,000 trials per cell, seed 20261027): the sketch's any-difference falsifier and any (6,·) floor fire ≈ 1.000 at N = 100 under the nulls (agreeing with RT-B F3); a rate-based Fisher variant of the discordance rule holds ≤ 1.2% null fire across ε ∈ {0.01, 0.02, 0.05} at D ∈ {20, 50, 80}, with power 0.78–0.95 at a 20-point drop for D ∈ {30, 50} — recorded for fresh-review item 7, not substituted into §3.7 (the researcher's McNemar rule is the candidate; its grid is the gap).
  • Counts. candidates(mutate=True) totals 118 Formats (29 bases + 89 variants); local_repairs outputs total 107 including bases. The verifier's interim "136 formats" enumeration (29 + 107) double-counts the bases; the control identity it supported was verified on the correct sets by three independent executions, so the fact stands and the number does not enter this doc.

docs.title: 5. Removals applied (verifier §A6 — none of these enter any build doc)
docs.text:
From the sketch:

  1. The any-difference / any-selection-flip falsifier, in any form.
  2. "Kept verbatim (recommended)" seam semantics and the "BOS and closing suffix mid-prompt" description (wrong in both particulars).
  3. "Disjoint marker sets" as a pair-selection rule (render identity is the operative criterion).
  4. "Headline population = token-real in both frames, or disclosed per cell" (incoherent; contradicts the pooled selection headline).
