The population definition itself is settled (one generated population per panel; extraction and arithmetic are rotating strata of it; the claim is scoped to the mixed panel; genuine recall is a different instrument and is not smuggled in — R §2(c), V §5(c)). The headline's behaviour over the strata is not: F3's cancellation inside d_c means the pooled decision can be annulled by opposite family effects, and no frozen rule governs family sign-disagreement. A print does not settle a decision.

(d) K=5 cap discipline — NOT SETTLED. The F5 sub-point is settled by construction (correct replies ≤ 49 bytes; whole-case liveness removes slot-ordered censoring; both red teams concede the sketch's manufacture does not survive). The liveness discipline itself is F2: post-treatment population selection with executed magnitudes, an inconsistent truncated-vs-parse-failed discipline, and (as written) no at-N characteristics. The budget asymmetry (bundled 1×64 vs split K×64 across generations) is constitutive and disclosed; it is not the defect — the selection is.

(e) Family×slot rotation completeness — SETTLED as completed. K=3 was frozen and exact in the candidate; K=5 was "analogously" (open as written). The frozen completion (F,A,F,A,F / A,F,A,F,A by case parity) is verified by counting on three lanes: every slot 12F/12A at both K, panel totals 36/36 (K=3) and 60/60 (K=5), imbalance zero. Parity- collinearity (§1 non-fatals) is the recorded residue.

(f) No-selection-readout discipline — SETTLED, clean. Red-team A's attack failed by grep + full read; B and V concur; C concurs. No winner, selection, flip-against-primary, cross-K trend, or survival readout exists anywhere in the candidate or the restatement; every readout is per-candidate, per-panel. The numform settlement (experiments.py:11049; repeated at :10018 for negation) is honoured.

(g) Naming audit for --multi-question — SETTLED, clean. Executed greps (R, B, V, C): multi-question / multiquestion / multi_question occur nowhere in code, USAGE, FAQ, CLI help, or module names — the only tree occurrences are in docs/BUNDLE_DESIGN.md itself. No --question-* flag exists. The sole near-neighbour is --multiturn (cli.py:565, module multiturn.py, USAGE §8.44): a different construct (one task sharded across turns vs K independent questions in one turn), a disclosure obligation for any future build's USAGE text, not a collision. The rejected name's collision is confirmed independently: pack.py:1, format id mpl-bundle/1 (pack.py:49), verify --bundle (verify.py:670-673, flag at :750), USAGE §13.1 (docs/USAGE.md:3320).

docs.title: 3. The amended instrument, recorded as a NEW candidate (not a build order)
docs.text:
The fresh researcher's restated instrument (~/workspace/agents_out/multiquestion/research.md §1) — bundle §3 plus the operand floor a,b ∈ [3,99] (sums ∈ [6,198], screens S1–S5 fail-closed), the frozen K=5 rotation, the total residual-class grammar, mandatory per-family printing, and the corrected OC grid with clustered and at-N rows — is the base text of the next candidate, together with the frozen requirements this round adds:

  1. Commitment binding: each cell record carries density.commitment_digest of its word-hash list; the raw answer_digest is dropped or bound; render-id digests and lengths are carried so id_length_delta is recomputable (negation §3.4 pattern).
  2. Cap discipline stated: pin the probe's generation cap or inherit the run's, in the protocol text, with the ≤49-byte correct-reply bound beside it; liveness mirrors density _live fully (detail == "" ∧ boundary_found per cell).
  3. Rotation: a pattern set richer than the two alternating strings, with marginal balance preserved and verified by counting — or the parity-collinearity disclosed in the section text as a named limitation.
  4. Grammar text: the scan convention frozen (greedy sequential first-occurrence), class names that describe their events, the -7-class leniencies disclosed.

And the three open decisions the next candidate must settle in its own text before its fresh review — they are the substance of F1–F3, and a review that finds them still open returns NO-BUILD on sight:

  • Rule purity vs claim re-scope (F1). Pick one and freeze it: either the firing condition counts wrong_value discordance only, with parse-failure discordance as its own non-firing readout (any decision label for it needs its own derived rule), or the headline is re-scoped in words to usable-answer loss under the frozen reply convention, with parser-in-the-loop operating characteristics (per-line slip and formatting-collapse nulls) printed as the headline OC — not verdict-level nulls alone.
  • Liveness (F2). A headline population that is not conditioned on the treated arm's completion alone, or a frozen argument — with executed magnitudes — for why the conditioning cannot manufacture a null for the candidates it most affects; the truncated/parse-failed discipline made consistent under one stated principle; at-N operating characteristics printed at the candidate's live N.
  • Family aggregation (F3). Per-family D/F/P printed beside the pooled decision with a frozen claim rule for sign-disagreement between families, or per-family decisions with a re-derived rule and family-wise accounting over the doubled decision count.

This candidate is not queued ahead of any existing item and is not a build order. It enters only through a fresh blind design review of its own.

docs.title: 4. Coordinator re-execution (independent, this session)
docs.text:
All snippets read-only; no suite was run.

  • Parser + hole. Implemented the §3.3 grammar from the tree's real density.word_hashes / digest_text: baseline correct replies parse ok at K=3, K=5, and split; correct bundled replies with sums 3 (slot 1), 2 (slot 2), 1 (slot 3), 4 (K=5 slot 4) all break to extra_words with no slot verdicts, while the same answers pass split — except sum=1, which breaks the split grammar too (answer = m_1). The arm-asymmetry and its sign are as the lanes report. Sum=6 is safe in both arms. The 25-case behaviour battery (swaps, omissions, duplicates, out-of-order, preamble, empty, markers-only, two-word answer, self-correction, glued lines, trailing prose) matches the lanes cell-for-cell under the residual-class closure — which the coordinator's implementation had to supply, confirming F4's totality gap from the implementer's side.
  • Rotation. Counted from §3.1's patterns: exactly 12F/12A per slot at K=3 and K=5 under the alternating completion; panel totals 36/36 and 60/60.
  • Cap. A generous K=5 composite (10-char answers) is 69 chars / 10 words; the researcher's frozen-format worst case (49 bytes) is the tighter, correct bound. Compliant replies cannot approach the 64-token cap.
  • Operating characteristics. Independent Monte Carlo (20,000 trials/cell, own code, the §3.4 rule exactly): random fire 0.0157 (K=3) / 0.0140 (K=5); competent-null 0.0110 / 0.0121; independent drop-0.25 power 0.9772 / 0.9991 — the printed table's independent rows confirmed.
  • Slip null (F1). Independent implementation: K=5 fire 0.024 / 0.061 / 0.189 at per-line slip s = 0.02 / 0.05 / 0.10 (zero knowledge difference); K=3: 0.016 / 0.028 / 0.071. Whole-case-collapse variant: 0.054–0.181 at collapse rates 0.10–0.20. A's G3/G2 magnitudes confirmed in kind.
  • Naming. Grep over package + docs: multi-question / multiquestion occur only in docs/BUNDLE_DESIGN.md; the only multi* flag in cli.py is --multiturn (:565).

docs.title: 5. Errors and imprecisions found in the briefs (none load-bearing)
docs.text:
• Researcher: the §2(d) worst-case witness repeats umbrella three times, which its own without-replacement draw + S1 distinctness forbids in a real case (V §6.1); the 49-byte bound's conclusion survives (every fact word ≤ 8 chars). The 185/4,860 figure's prose omits its K=3 / single-arithmetic- slot scope; the rate is correct for that simulation. The on-disk MC code's clustered worlds used definitional fudges (V §6.1); the printed §3.2 definitions are clean, analytic- matched, and bracketed by the verifier's independent rows.
  • Verifier: its competent-null K=5 rate differs from the rank-5 table by 0.0034 (~4σ at the stated trial counts) — recorded by the verifier itself; both values are ≪ 0.05 and no conclusion turns on it. Its fabrication sweep ran while the fresh briefs were still drafts; the pending sections are named unswept in its brief. The coordinator read the final briefs in full and reproduced the load-bearing late numbers itself (§4), so no load-bearing claim in the final briefs rests on the sweep alone.
  • Red-team B's 69% vs the verifier's 79% perfect-model panel-fire rate: a generator-detail difference (slot family counts / distinctness handling); the verifier rules B's claim if anything understated. The coordinator's own executions confirm the mechanism and the magnitude class.
  • Clustered-drop power is reported by two models (marginal- matched: 0.4165/0.3401; collapse-rate-0.25: 0.5803/0.5860). Both are printed with their models named wherever this doc cites them; the falsity of the candidate's caveat is unanimous and model-independent.
  • No other errors: the verifier's mechanical sweep resolved every remaining symbol, line, count, and citation in the candidate spec and the landed brief material (catalog = 29 families executed; the 5,760 / 1,152 / 12 MiB counts re-derived exactly).

docs.title: 6. Verdict
docs.text: NO-BUILD — permanent closure of this candidate. The candidate as written is unanimously NO-BUILD: its screen does not close the marker set its own grammar creates (F4: a perfect model is labelled a bundling drop in ~7 of 10 K=5 panels under the natural operand reading), its parser classes are not total in the frozen text, its generator is described rather than frozen, and its operating-characteristics evidence carries a false clustered-drop caveat (F5). The researcher's restated instrument cures F4 and F5 — with closures this review verified and adopts into the record (§3) — but it does not touch F1 (a falsification label that formatting-only worlds fire at 0.19–0.64, calibrated against nulls that omit the instrument's own parser), F2 (a headline population selected by the treated arm's completion, under a conditioning principle the candidate itself forbids elsewhere), or F3 (opposite family effects cancelling inside the decision's own aggregate). Each cure changes the rule, the headline, or the liveness discipline — load-bearing elements a fresh review records for a new candidate; it does not mint them as a build order. The amended instrument in §3 is that new candidate. It is not a build order, and no build cycle may act on it without a fresh blind design review that finds its three open decisions already settled in its text.

docs.title: Multi-turn drift design (cycle 189)
docs.text:
Wave-8 rank #2. The incorporation policy below (P1–P3) is adopted from the wave-8 research brief (~/workspace/agents_out/wave8/ research.md §2 #2) before any code, because cycle 179's closure recorded the policy — not the fixture schema — as the blocker: synthetic fixtures are built in memory on the hierarchy/numform precedent, and core.Fixture's single expected is enough once the policy says which turn is scored.

This is v2 of the design. v1 was attacked by red-team A (~/workspace/agents_out/wave8/cycle189/redteam_a.md, verdict DO NOT BUILD AS SPECIFIED: four design-fatal items) and cross-checked by red-team B (redteam_b.md in the same directory), which confirmed all four fatal items, downgraded two findings, refuted two of A's own amendments, and added one finding A missed. The coordinator adjudication adopted B's surviving must-fix list wholesale; §Adjudication records what changed and why. No code was written against v1.

docs.title: Utility
docs.text: A practitioner shipping a multi-turn assistant learns, per template family, whether the winner chosen on single-exchange fixtures still wins when the model's own earlier replies become the history — and whether verdicts at depth 2 and depth 3 differ — instead of discovering in production that the template only won on conversations that never actually happened. (Each depth is its own generated task set, so a cross-depth comparison is confounded by task length; the probe reports per-depth verdicts, not a depth-onset curve.) Opt-in: model-protocol-lab run --multiturn.

docs.title: The incorporation policy (P1–P3, frozen)
docs.text:
• P1 (what a turn is). A conversation is a frozen sequence of user shards. The model's reply at each intermediate turn is generated greedily under the candidate's own rendering, cut at the candidate's boundary exactly as in native evaluation, and the cut text (never the raw over-generation) is inserted verbatim as the assistant turn of the next prompt. In core.evaluate the cut text is Observation.answer (output up to the first boundary); the multiturn stage builds each next turn's Fixture from it unchanged. Scope of the claim (v2, per A9): the history is the cut text re-rendered under the candidate's own Format — the lab's construction, not a claim about what any vendor template or real deployment would send. For formats whose generation open suffix differs from the history assistant prefix (62 of 118 mutate candidates, 15 of 29 base families — e.g. the thinking variants, where text generated inside an opened think block is re-homed outside it by the history render), the recorded conversation is the lab's uniform construction, disclosed here and in the section's honesty text.
  • P2 (what is scored). Only the final turn's answer, against the fixture's single expected, under the unchanged exact-match + boundary conjunction. Intermediate replies are never scored; they are context, exactly as in a real conversation. This dissolves the "per-turn expectations" problem by refusing to invent them. Per-turn Fixtures the stage builds carry the fixture's final expected; evaluate computes exact_match against it on every turn and the stage ignores intermediate Observation.exact_match (v2, per A8 — a builder must not invent per-turn expectations).
  • P3 (selection). The probe is informational and never touches the native selection. Per-depth selection readouts (for the full and sharded arms; the scripted arm is a control and gets none) re-apply the conservative rule to final-turn verdicts and are withheld (null) when any candidate's completed set at that depth differs from the defined fixture set or completed sets differ across candidates (the dateline wording, v2 per A13).

docs.title: Construction (synthetic, generated, numform discipline)
docs.text:
Fixtures are generated inside the stage from the run seed; no user fixtures are read and no file schema is involved. Values derive from SHA-256, never random.Random, so the same seed regenerates the identical fixture set across runs and PYTHONHASHSEED values.

Derivation (frozen, v2 per A8). _derive(seed, family, depth, index, slot, counter) returns int.from_bytes(sha256(material)[:8], "big") where material = "multiturn-v1|{seed}|{family}|{depth}|{index}|{slot}|{counter}" (the numform _derive construction, with depth deliberately in the material: depths are independent task sets and no nesting or lineage is claimed between them).

Two task families, each a deterministic function of all shards. The question rides the final shard (appended to it), so depth is the number of entries/shelves — there is no replace-reading and no own-turn reading (v2 per A8/S4).

  • ledger — shard i (non-final) is the text Ledger entry: {v}.; the final shard is Ledger entry: {v}. What is the ledger total? Addend for slot i: u = _derive(seed, "ledger", depth, index, i, counter); magnitude 1 + u % 999; value +magnitude when (u >> 32) % 2 == 0, else -magnitude (nonzero, ±1..±999). Entries render as str(int) — entry style and expected style coincide by construction (v2 per B's A8 correction: a +42 entry style against a str(int) expected would manufacture the surface-form confound numform exists to isolate). The expected answer is str(sum). Entry-equality screen (A14 as rescoped by B): if str(sum) equals any stated entry string in the same fixture, the whole fixture is redrawn with counter + 1 until it does not. (Substring screening is not used: it is the wrong predicate — a shelf label is a substring of its own shard text in 100% of fixtures.)
  • shelf — shard i (non-final) is Shelf {label} holds {n} units.; the final shard is Shelf {label} holds {n} units. Which shelf holds the most units? Answer with the shelf label. Labels are A, B, C in shard order. Value for slot i: 1 + _derive(seed, "shelf", depth, index, i, counter) % 99 (range 1..99). Values are pairwise distinct per fixture: if a drawn value equals an earlier slot's value in the same fixture, that slot is redrawn with counter + 1 until distinct, so the argmax is unique. The expected answer is the argmax label. Shelf needs no leakage screen (B).

Depths are 2 and 3 (the shard count). Fixtures per family per depth: 12, so 48 fixtures total. Fixture ids are mt-{family}-{depth}-{index:02d}. Every Fixture the stage builds (per-turn included) carries group "multiturn". The full arm joins shards with the frozen joiner "\n\n" (the dateline JOINER precedent). The scripted reply is the frozen text Noted.. Shard templates, the question strings, the joiner, and the scripted reply are frozen protocol text, screened before any generation (the numform template screen: audit_special_token_literals against the candidate formats, no boundary-text containment).

Ground records store shard texts and generated integers in the clear — synthetic data, and the diff validator must be able to recompute from them (numform precedent).

docs.title: Arms
docs.text:
• full — all shards concatenated into one user turn with the frozen joiner (single-turn control; Laban's Full condition). One generation.
  • sharded at depth d — the same shards delivered one per user turn, with the model's own boundary-cut replies as the assistant turns between them (P1). d generations; only the last is scored (P2).
  • scripted at depth d — the same sharding, but every intermediate assistant turn is the one frozen scripted reply (Noted.), identical for every candidate, fixture, and turn. One generation (the final turn). The sharded-vs-scripted contrast measures a bundle — authorship, content, and history length move together, because a self-generated reply carries computed state and premature answers (rule 6) at whatever length the model produced, and content/length are the mechanism of self-history, not confounders separable from it (v2 per A4 as reduced by B: no length-matched arm — sizing the control to each candidate's own replies would candidate-depend the control and change the estimand). The design, CLI help, and readouts therefore never say the contrast "isolates" authorship; they report the discordant pair (§Readouts) so churn and silence are distinguishable.

docs.title: Stage mechanics (pre-registered edge rules)
docs.text:
The stage is a sequential loop — the first stage in the lab where generation k's output builds generation k+1's prompt. Rules, fixed before code:

  1. Unbounded intermediate. If an intermediate generation finds no boundary, the full generated text (decoded, budget-capped — exactly Observation.answer when boundary_found is false) becomes the history turn, and the cell is flagged intermediate_unbounded. Truncating or dropping the turn would manufacture a different conversation per candidate.
  2. Empty intermediate. If an intermediate cut text is the empty string, it is inserted as an empty assistant turn (legal in every catalog format — verified) and the cell is flagged intermediate_empty (v2 per A9/S1). An empty turn is a no-reply turn, a distinct phenomenon from an unbounded one, and its rendering is family-shaped (e.g. Mistral's empty assistant turn contributes only its turn end), so it is named rather than left derivable-only.
  3. History screen (v2 per A5). Before an intermediate reply is incorporated as history, its text is screened with audit_special_token_literals against the candidate format's own special-token inventory (the audit the shipped stages apply to frozen text). Generated text can contain special-token literals that re-encode to real special-token ids — a forged turn boundary inside history is token-real, not inert text. On a screen hit the sharded cell ends with detail arm_screened (the dateline detail precedent), the cell leaves the paired set, and screened cells are counted per candidate (§Readouts). The final-turn answer is never incorporated, so it is not screened; the scripted history is frozen text, screened once with the protocol text.
  4. Context growth. Before each turn, if the rendered prompt's token count plus max_new_tokens exceeds max_context, that arm's cell for that fixture ends with detail arm_context_exceeded and leaves the completed set at that depth. A completed-set event, reported — never a crash, never a silent truncation of the conversation.
  5. Cancellation, with precedence (v2 per S3). The run's cancel event is threaded into every evaluate call and is checked immediately after every evaluate return, before the evaluation-failure mapping (rule 6) — a cancel observed during a turn must not be mislabelled an evaluation failure. A cancelled stage returns the fail-closed payload (available: False, detail: "cancelled"), never partial candidates.
  6. Evaluation failure. A turn whose evaluate report is not aggregate-eligible ends the cell with detail arm_evaluation_failed.
  7. Request seeds (v2 pins per A12). Each (fixture, arm, turn) evaluates under a distinct case id — {fixture_id}-full, {fixture_id}-scripted, and {fixture_id}-sharded-t{k} for k = 1..depth (turn depth is the final turn) — so core.request_seed_for gives every generation its own deterministic request seed. Final-turn seeds are deliberately unpaired across arms (contrast numform's paired discipline); the real backend does not use the seed for selection, and tests must not assume pairing.
  8. Premature answers are signal. An intermediate reply may contain the final answer early (Laban's anchoring mechanism). Nothing detects, penalises, or repairs this; P2 scores only the final turn.

Attrition is arm-asymmetric by construction (a sharded cell must survive d sequential evaluations; the others one), and the exiting cells are treatment-correlated (long or unbounded intermediates), so every paired denominator is reported beside per-arm completion counts with a detail breakdown (v2 per A11).

docs.title: Records
docs.text:
One record per (candidate, fixture), carrying everything the diff validator recomputes from:

  • fixture_id, family, depth, shards (texts), values (the generated integers), expected.
  • Per arm (full, sharded, scripted): a cell or a detail string from the house vocabulary (arm_context_exceeded, arm_evaluation_failed, arm_screened). A cell is verdict, boundary_found, boundary_text_match (v2 per A6 — the only diagnostic separating "model failed" from "boundary text emitted under a different tokenisation"), input_tokens (final turn), answer_digest (SHA-256 of the final answer text), and for sharded also intermediate_unbounded, intermediate_empty, and turns: one entry per turn (length == depth), each input_tokens, answer_digest, boundary_found. The last turns entry is the final turn and must agree with the cell on digest, boundary, and input_tokens (validator-checked identity, v2 per A6); intermediate_unbounded ≡ any intermediate turn with boundary_found false, and intermediate_empty ≡ any intermediate turn whose digest is SHA-256 of "" (validator-checked identities, v2 per A6). The scripted arm records no turns (its intermediates are frozen text; there is nothing to attest).
  • ground_sha256 over the canonical generated fixture rows binds the payload to the generator (numform generator_sha256 precedent).

The protocol object carries: version, families, depths, fixtures per family per depth, the shard templates, question strings, joiner, and scripted reply (fingerprinted via a template digest, numform precedent), the floors, GENERATION_BUDGET, MAX_GROUND_RECORDS, MAX_RECORDS_BYTES, the seed, and the backend fingerprint. Protocol drift in any of these makes two payloads not comparable.

docs.title: Readouts
docs.text:
Per candidate, computed by multiturn.aggregate_candidate and recomputed by the diff validator. Rates always travel with denominators; counts are shipped, never rates alone.

Per depth d ∈ {2, 3}:

  • Paired denominator = fixtures of depth d completed in all three arms; per-arm final-turn pass rates over that denominator. Per-arm completion counts with detail breakdowns (including n_screened) are reported beside it.
  • Delivery 2×2 (full vs sharded) over the paired set: drift (pass full ∧ fail sharded), gains (fail full ∧ pass sharded), both-pass, both-fail; McNemar exact p as a diagnostic only. The full vs scripted 2×2 likewise (drift_scripted, gains_scripted, both-pass, both-fail).
  • Self-history pair over the paired full-passers: sh_only (pass scripted ∧ fail sharded), sc_only (fail scripted ∧ pass sharded), both-treated-pass, both-treated-fail. The pair is the headline; net_excess = sh_only - sc_only is reported beside it, never alone, with a McNemar exact p as a diagnostic (v2 per A3 — net-only reporting is the cycle-185 acquittal construction: churn (5, 5) and silence (0, 0) have the same net).
  • Per-family counts beside pooled (v2 per B-NEW-1): drift, gains, drift_scripted, sh_only, sc_only per family per depth. The families have different answer spaces and baseline difficulties; pooling is stated here explicitly, per-family counts ship beside every pooled count, and the classification is pooled (its inputs are visible per family).
  • Selection readouts (P3, §policy) for full and sharded at each depth, or null under the withholding rule.

Classification per candidate — a total function of the per-depth counts with floors MIN_PAIRED_EVALUABLE = 6 and MIN_DISCORDANT = 2 (house constants). A depth is evaluable when its paired denominator ≥ 6. In order (v2 per A2 — the sibling classifiers' below-threshold outcome restored, and the strong label gated on at-floor paired evidence at a single depth):

  1. insufficient_evidence — no depth is evaluable.
  2. self_history_drift — at some evaluable depth, sh_only ≥ 2 and sh_only > sc_only.
  3. framing_only — not (2), and at some evaluable depth max(drift, gains, drift_scripted, gains_scripted) ≥ 2: delivery/framing discordance at floor with no self-history signal at floor.
  4. below_threshold — not (2) or (3), and any discordant count (drift, gains, drift_scripted, gains_scripted, sh_only, sc_only) > 0 at any evaluable depth.
  5. no_drift — no discordance in either direction at any evaluable depth.

There is no cross-depth recovery counter (v1's was a category error — A1: the depths are different generated tasks, so passing at depth 3 after failing at depth 2 is not recovery from anything, and its numerator was not a subset of its stated denominator). Cross-depth reporting is the two per-depth blocks, full stop.

docs.title: Falsifiable claims (pre-registered)
docs.text:
• F1 (per candidate). If at every evaluable depth the self-history pair is (0, 0) while scripted-arm discordance exists, self-authorship adds nothing beyond the framing bundle for this candidate, and the claim "self-generated history is the active ingredient" fails for this candidate and fixture set. The classification concludes per candidate (framing_only or below_threshold), never pooled across candidates (v2 quantifier fix per B).
  • F2. If a candidate shows drift = gains = drift_scripted = gains_scripted = 0 at every depth, the claim "multi-turn delivery is a verdict-relevant surface under this template" is false for this candidate and set; the section says exactly that, with denominators (v2 per A10 — two-directional: drift 0 with gains 5 is a verdict-relevant surface and must not satisfy the null).
  • F3 (instrument). Every derived number in the section is recomputable from the ground records. The binding that makes this true is stated, not implied: for every arm cell, verdict ≡ (answer_digest == sha256(expected)) ∧ boundary_found, with expected from the mirror-regenerated fixture (v2 per A6). One honest exception, disclosed rather than papered over: the correspondence between the recorded intermediate digests and the history that was actually rendered is stage-attested (the DISTRACTION_DESIGN honesty pattern) — the records bind each turn's digest and the validator checks every identity among recorded fields, but no record can prove the stage incorporated the text it recorded. A payload whose aggregates disagree with a recomputation is rejected by diff-reports.

docs.title: Diff validator
docs.text: diff_multiturn recomputes everything (the wave-7 F6 standard): it regenerates the fixture set from the protocol seed through an independent stdlib mirror of the generator (the cycle-187 numform fix — generator_sha256 alone would be tautological), checks every record's shards/values/ expected against the regenerated set, re-derives every cell verdict from its digest identity, checks the turns identities (§Records), recomputes pass rates, the 2×2s, the self-history pair, per-family counts, selection readouts, and the classification from the cells, and rejects on any disagreement. Protocol drift (version, seed-derived fixture set, scripted reply, templates) makes two payloads not comparable.

docs.title: Determinism scope
docs.text: The chain is greedy, so a conversation is a deterministic function of (checkpoint, candidate, fixture). Multiturn cells are outside the determinism self-audit's scope: verify --determinism replays recorded search observations only, and this probe's payload says so rather than implying coverage.

docs.title: Budget
docs.text: Per candidate: depth-2 fixtures (24) cost 1 + 2 + 1 = 4 generations each, depth-3 fixtures (24) cost 1 + 3 + 1 = 5, so 216 generations per candidate; at the tree's 24-candidate cap (run_experiment: "Supply between 1 and 24 candidates"), GENERATION_BUDGET = 5184 (v2 per A7 — v1's 25-candidate / 5,400 figure was wrong). MAX_GROUND_RECORDS = 1152 (24 candidates × 48 records — generations and records are different quantities here and get separate constants, v2 per S2) and MAX_RECORDS_BYTES = 12 * 1024 * 1024 (measured need ≈ 1.2 MB at the legal maximum); caps fail closed before generation, as in numform. The CLI help states the worst case with the forwards formula before the run: generations = candidates × (24×4 + 24×5), and prompt cost grows every turn because each sharded turn re-renders the whole history, so token cost is superlinear in depth even though the generation count is linear.

docs.title: Honesty
docs.text: The generated tasks are a probe instrument, not a benchmark: they measure whether verdicts survive sharded delivery on tasks whose entire information content fits in three short shards. Nothing here estimates performance on real user conversations, which are underspecified in ways a frozen shard sequence is not (Laban's simulations use a user simulator for exactly that reason). Two further disclosures travel with the section: the P1 history construction is the lab's re-rendering, with the open-suffix asymmetry for thinking formats (§policy); and the sharded-vs-scripted contrast is a bundle (authorship + content + length) over a minimal neutral history, reported as a discordant pair, not an isolated authorship effect. The probe's claim is the lab's claim throughout: holding weights fixed, the template decides whether the winner survives the conversation shape.

docs.title: Adjudication (v1 → v2)
docs.text: Red-team A: DO NOT BUILD AS SPECIFIED (A1–A14). Red-team B: confirmed A1, A2, A3, A5, A7, A8, A9 (strengthened), A10, A11, A12, A13; A4 partially (downgraded HIGH → MEDIUM, its length-matched-arm amendment refuted — adopted: wording-only fix, bundle named, "isolates" struck); A6 confirmed- downgraded (HIGH → MEDIUM — the verdict is re-derivable from v1's specified fields; adopted: the identity stated, lineage disclosed stage-attested, boundary_text_match added); A14 partially (phenomenon confirmed; its substring screen refuted — it rejects the shelf family by construction; adopted as rescoped: ledger-only entry-equality screen). Supplementary items S1 (empty-turn render artefacts), S2 (separate budget/record constants), S3 (cancel precedence pin), S4 (third budget reading — closed by the question-placement decision) all adopted. B-NEW-1 (family pooling unstated) adopted: per-family counts beside pooled. Fatal four fixed as specified by A and confirmed by B: recovery deleted (A1), classification rebuilt with below_threshold and single-depth gating (A2), history screen pre-registered (A5), generator fully specified (A8: question placement, derive material with depth, both value mappings, str(int) entries per B's correction, joiner, group, caps, protocol object, house vocabulary).

docs.title: Pin blast radius (coordinator checklist)
docs.text: New pure module multiturn.py (54th source file → test_cycle44 mypy pin in the same push); one stage in experiments.py; one CLI flag --multiturn (cycle-179 dispatch e2e, cycle-31/64/84 audits, cycle-131 Namespace contract); reporting.py's three touchpoints; one diff section (test_cycle67's three elements + test_cycle27's stub); USAGE §8.44 (next free — verify at build); README/VALIDATION/ CHANGELOG currency; sample report regenerates byte-identical (the section renders nothing when its key is absent).

docs.title: Needle-depth probe — design
docs.text:
Cycle 191 (wave-8 rank 3). A practitioner pasting retrieved chunks around a question learns, per template family, at which depth of the surrounding bulk their checkpoint stops finding a planted fact — a per-template recall-vs-depth curve at exact rendered-token depths — instead of a single "long context good/bad" number measured through a vendor's own template.

The probe plants one fact sentence carrying a unique synthetic value inside neutral filler, at five depths of the filler span and two filler doses, and asks for the value. The independent variable is the chat template: same checkpoint, same generated cases, same filler — only the hand-rendered format changes. The stage lives in experiments.needle_stage, the frozen protocol and arithmetic in model_protocol_lab/needle.py, the HTML section in reporting.py, and the full-recompute diff validator in diffreports.py.

Design history: v1 of this document specified contiguous needle-run acceptance over an unstated textual assembly. Red-team A returned DO NOT BUILD AS SPECIFIED (run-existence is fatal on the literal reading; the validator omitted the verdict↔digest binding); red-team B upheld the verdict, downgraded A's impossibility claim with a counter-assembly, refuted the coordinator's first repair sketch (a marker-derived head anchor with a systematic −1 bias), and supplied the surviving measurement (the prefix-anchored difference D). This v2 is the adjudicated contract: delta-based dose, D- anchored offsets, digest-bound verdicts, one headline population. The briefs are in ~/workspace/agents_out/wave8/ (cycle191_redteam_a.md, cycle191_redteam_b.md).

docs.title: Where this sits against prior work
docs.text:
The depth phenomenon is published and is not claimed here: Liu et al. (Lost in the Middle, arXiv:2307.03172) measured a U-shaped recall curve over document position in API-served models, with mid-context accuracy sometimes dropping below the closed-book bound; NoLiMa (arXiv:2502.05167) extends needle-in-a-haystack with minimal-lexical-overlap needles, unique-token counting, and — in its question-type analysis — needles inserted at 25/50/75% within the relevant text; RULER (arXiv:2404.06654) places needles at controlled depths in synthetic local-model tasks; BABILong (arXiv:2406.10149) distributes multiple facts through book text; Chroma's Context Rot report (July 2025, https://research.trychroma.com/context-rot) varies total length with a fixed needle and shows distractor similarity and needle–question similarity move scores materially. Depth as an axis, token-exact placement, literal needles, and distributed facts all exist. What no surveyed harness reports is the combination this probe ships: a recall-vs-depth curve as a function of hand-rendered chat-template family on one local checkpoint, with the depth offset verified on each candidate's own rendered token sequence, a needle-absent false-recall floor and a duplicate-needle control as arms of the same probe, and the lab's conservative selection rule (unique winner or abstain) re-applied per depth cell. The uniqueness pass behind this paragraph, with per-harness coverage, is logged in docs/RESEARCH_LOG.md (cycle 191 entry).

The boundary against the shipped distractor-dilution probe (cycle 184) is one sentence: distract varies how much filler surrounds the fixture's own question and whether a planted wrong answer captures the model; needle varies where an answer-bearing fact sits inside a fixed amount of filler. Distract's conditions are dose × placement of filler around existing fixtures; needle's are dose × depth of the fact itself, over generated cases whose only question is the plant.

docs.title: Cases
docs.text:
Cases are generated inside the stage from the run seed (the multiturn pattern: self-contained, no dependence on the user's fixtures or the recorded search). Twenty cases, ids needle-00 … needle-19. The derivation is frozen exactly, because the diff validator's mirror must reproduce it bit for bit: one draw is int.from_bytes(sha256(f"{seed}|needle|{index}|{slot}|{counter}" .encode("ascii")).digest()[:8], "big") with counter starting at 0. Slot 0 gives the code word WORDS[draw % 64]; slot 1 gives the number 1000 + draw % 9000. The value is "{word}-{number}". If a case's value equals an earlier case's value, counter increments and both slots redraw. Topic i is TOPICS[i] from the frozen list of twenty in needle.py ("astronomy society", "beekeeping circle", …). The fact sentence is one frozen template rendered with the corpus's own trailing-space convention: The {topic} code is {value}. The question is What is the {topic} code?; the expected answer is the value, scored by the standard pipeline (boundary-cut answer, exact match — core.evaluate's literal equality). Question and needle share the topic phrase and the word "code" by construction — needle–question lexical match is deliberate (Chroma's finding is that it moves scores; an unmatched question would measure vocabulary guessing, not position). The protocol carries case_material_sha256, the SHA-256 of the canonical JSON of (fact template, topics, words), so the frozen lists are bound by digest, and ground_sha256 over the canonical generated rows (multiturn's pattern), so the seed's case set is bound as a whole.

Generation-time screens (a failure is a protocol bug, raised before any generation, never a per-cell outcome): topics and words are screened against the filler corpus (case-folded substring) — the frozen lists pass and a test pins that; the twenty values are pairwise distinct by the redraw rule; no value occurs in the corpus. The corpus contains no digits at all, so the numeric half of every value is unplanted by construction everywhere except the needle.

docs.title: Arms and assembly
docs.text:
Fifteen cells per case per candidate. The assembly is frozen exactly (v1's silence here was build-blocking): a case is a single user message whose content is segment concatenation with no joiner anywhere — filler and needle sentences carry the corpus trailing space, and the question follows the bulk directly as the final sentence.

  • dose_0 — content = needle sentence + question. The control arm: it proves the case is answerable when nothing surrounds the fact. (The wave-8 brief called the recorded native run the dose-0 control; the recorded search runs the user's fixtures with their own questions and contains no observation of these generated cases, so the stage-generated arm plays the control role — the multiturn honesty settlement, stated here rather than discovered later.)
  • dose_{1024,4096}_depth_{0,25,50,75,100} — content = prefix filler + needle + suffix filler + question.
  • absent_{1024,4096} — content = filler + question, no needle. Any pass is fabrication or guessing; the pass rate is the false-recall floor, reported per dose beside that dose's curve.
  • duplicate_{1024,4096} — content = prefix filler + needle + middle filler + needle + suffix filler + question, the two needles at 25% and 75%. Separates position from exposure count, with the independence baseline of the Claims section keeping the readout honest.

Dose scoping: the brief's doses {1024, 4096} ship as written. The 4096 dose needs --max-context above 4096 plus the generation budget and prompt overhead; under the default 2048 cap every 4096 cell is arm_context_exceeded — reported per cell, never truncated into existence. The full control set (floor and duplicate) is live at 1024 under defaults, so the default run still carries the falsification framing; the brief's {1024, 2048} fallback was not taken because a 2048 filler dose also exceeds the default cap once the needle, question, and generation budget are added, so it buys no default-liveness and halves the dose axis. The CLI help states the arithmetic before the run.

docs.title: Measurement
docs.text:
All quantities are measured on rendered token ids under three cached renders per (candidate, case): Q (question-only content), Z (the dose-0 content), and the arm render itself. needle_len := len(Z) − len(Q) is the needle's rendered length in the dose-0 context for that candidate and case; a case with needle_len <= 0 for a candidate is degenerate and all its cells for that candidate are arm_unmatchable.

  • Dose is a rendered delta (distraction's semantics, stated plainly): a treated cell is accepted only when len(arm) − len(Z) == dose on the final render — the arm prompt is exactly dose rendered tokens longer than the same case's dose-0 prompt. The absent cell is accepted only when len(arm) − len(Q) == dose — the same equation with the needle term removed, not a separate statistic. The duplicate cell: len(arm) − len(Z) == dose + needle_len. Seam merges at the needle's edges are absorbed into the delta and compensated by the sizing search; the design does not claim the filler text totals the dose standalone.
  • Offset is the prefix-anchored difference D. D(arm, comp) := LCP(arm_ids, comp_ids) − LCP(Z_ids, Q_ids), where comp is the render of the arm's text up to just before the measured needle, with the question appended (needle 1: prefix + question; needle 2 in duplicate: prefix + needle + middle + question). The dose-0 arm is the anchor: its needle sits at offset 0 by construction, and the head-merge term — the generic BPE case, a template head ending in a space or newline merging with the following token — is present in both LCPs and cancels. Acceptance requires D == depth% × dose / 100 exactly (both doses make every target an integer). A construction whose seams move D off target is rejected and the search continues; it is never relabelled. No marker-derived constant appears anywhere in the measurement path (red-team B executed the marker anchor failing outright under the repo's word tokenizer and biasing −1 under merging heads; D matched token-span ground truth in every executed case).
  • Joint final verification is the load-bearing invariant. Both equalities (delta, and D for each needle) are evaluated on the accepted construction's own final ids before the cell is generated. The two-phase search below is an optimisation whose phase-1 measurements the suffix could in principle move (rank-ordered BPE reach-back); the joint check on the final render is what makes acceptance sound — every reach-back case changes the final render's LCP or length and is rejected there, never wrongly accepted.

docs.title: Sizing
docs.text:
Rule needle-phased-exact-v1; its full text is this section, and the protocol carries sizing_rule_sha256 over the frozen rule text constant in needle.py (the multiturn template_digest pattern — a bare version number binds nothing). The filler stream is NEUTRAL_CORPUS cycled in order, six cycles (426 sentences), sentences consumed in stream order: a span is span_text over the stream (distract's whole-sentences-plus-one-truncated-suffix construction), and the next span continues at the sentence after the previous span's last whole sentence (a truncated sentence counts as consumed). One corpus pass is ≈1,278 tokens under a typical tokenizer, so a 4096 bulk wraps the stream about 3.2 times — each sentence appears three or four times in a 4096 bulk, a stated property of the arm.

Phases per treated cell: (1) prefix search — candidates from span_candidates (distract's closeness order; the estimate orders, never decides) targeting the depth offset; a probe is the candidate's arm-context render (prefix + needle + question) plus its comparator render (prefix + question); the first prefix whose D equals the target wins. Depth 0 takes the empty prefix with no search. (2) suffix search — candidates continuing the stream, targeting the remaining delta; a probe is the full arm render; the first suffix satisfying the delta equality (with D re-verified on the same ids) wins. Depth 100 takes the empty suffix. Duplicate adds a middle phase between (1) and (2): candidates continuing the stream targeting needle 2's offset, probed as (prefix + needle + middle + needle + question) plus its comparator; then the suffix phase targets the duplicate delta equality, re-verifying both offsets on the final ids.

Encode budget SIZING_ENCODE_BUDGET = 512 per cell, counting every probe encode in the phases (a phase-1 probe is 2 encodes; a suffix/middle probe is 1, plus its comparator in the middle phase). The cached Q/Z renders and an accepted prefix's comparator are infrastructure, computed once per (candidate, case[, prefix]) and not counted; the joint final verification reuses the accepted construction's renders and adds no encodes. The chars-per-token estimate is measured once per stage from the corpus under the run's backend (distract precedent); it affects search order only, so budget-edge arm_unmatchable outcomes are backend-determined — stated, not hidden. Executed feasibility (coordinator and red-team B, independently): the full word/char grid at both doses and all depths accepts well inside budget (worst observed 257 encodes); merging-tokenizer residue is reject-mode (unmatchable), not wrong-accept, once D is the anchor.

One liveness limit is structural, found by executing the built stage against a merge-dense digraph tokenizer: every span is a prefix of its stream segment, so the rendered delta is a single step function of span length, and where a span's last character toggles a seam merge (a trailing space that merges with the following text, lost as the span grows past it) the step is +2 — the walk steps over the target and no span at any length hits it for that cell. Those cells are arm_unmatchable (about 30% of cells under the adversarial digraph tokenizer in the cycle-191 tests, 0% under word and byte tokenizers); the step-skip can only ever remove cells, never corrupt one — every accepted cell still satisfies both equalities on its final render, and the readouts run over recorded cells with printed denominators.

Per-cell screening runs on the filler texts only (the needle is the plant): filler containing the case value or the candidate's decoded boundary text makes the cell arm_screened. Stage-level, the frozen texts (fact template with slots emptied, topics, words, corpus) are audited for special-token literals against every candidate format before any generation; a hit fails the whole stage closed (needle_screen_failed) because it would forge turn structure in every cell — the multiturn settlement. The screening rule is likewise carried as screening_rule_sha256 over its frozen text in needle.py: per-span, case-folded, the value screen and the boundary-text screen of this paragraph.

Cell detail vocabulary is frozen: "", arm_unmatchable, arm_screened, arm_context_exceeded, arm_evaluation_failed; a cell is present exactly when its detail is "". Stage details: needle_record_budget_exceeded, needle_screen_failed, cancelled; the payload-level fail-closed form is {"available": false, "detail": "needle_unavailable"}.

docs.title: Claims and denominators
docs.text:
Every rate travels with its denominator; readouts are withheld, never zeroed. One headline population per dose keeps every comparative readout like-for-like: the cases where every candidate in the run passed dose_0 with all five depth cells at that dose recorded. (Per-candidate populations were rejected on red-team execution: a flat per-candidate curve could coexist with a +0.50 deficit over a differently-conditioned subset, and per-candidate deficits over different residues are not the comparison this probe exists to make.)

  • Curves: per dose, per depth, n_pass / n_population / rate over the headline population — one denominator per dose, shared by all depths and all candidates. A flat curve over this population makes the deficit exactly zero, by construction.
  • mid_depth_deficit per dose: (rate(0%) + rate(100%))/2 − rate(50%) over the headline population — Lost in the Middle's functional form (edge mean minus middle), credited, not renamed. Withheld (None) when the headline population is below MIN_HEADLINE_POPULATION = 6.
  • first_failure per dose: over the headline population, counts of the first failing depth in 0→100 order, plus n_no_failure; withheld with the deficit.
  • Dose-0 control per candidate: recorded/pass counts and rate over the 20 cases (the candidate's own control level; not part of the headline population arithmetic).
  • false_recall per dose per candidate: evaluable count, false-pass count, rate from that dose's absent cell (own recorded cells — a within-candidate floor, denominators printed).
  • duplicate per dose per candidate, over its own population (dose_0 pass ∧ duplicate recorded ∧ the 25% and 75% cells at that dose recorded): pass count/rate; the independence baseline 1 − (1 − r25)(1 − r75) from the same population's single-needle rates, and excess_over_independence — printed as a descriptive contrast under a stated modelling assumption, not a test; plus mid-fail rescue counts (depth-50 fail ∧ duplicate pass) and the rescue rate over mid-fails (None when there are none).
  • Selection per cell key (all fifteen): the conservative rule over candidates on that cell's completed case set, withheld — decision unavailable, detail selection_withheld_mismatched_sets — when a completed set is empty or the sets differ across candidates. flip compares the cell's outcome to the dose_0 selection recomputed on the same completed set (a paired-restricted baseline; comparing against the full-set dose-0 outcome would mix set differences into the flip), and is None when either side is withheld. The dose_0 condition entry reports the selection over its own completed set with flip: false when not withheld.

There is no summary classification and no latency claim of any kind (the cycle-179 closure: depth curves are verdict curves). The falsification reading is stated, not encoded: a candidate whose curve is flat across depths at both doses — no depth effect beyond its own false-recall floor — falsifies "this template exhibits position-dependent recall" for that candidate, and the section prints the curve either way. Two scope limits are part of the readout, not footnotes: the filler is topically dissimilar prose (Chroma showed similar distractors hurt more, so these curves are a lower bound on position effects under realistic retrieval bulk), and each cell is one greedy generation — the curve is a 5-point sample of position, with per-depth resolution set by the headline population's denominator.

docs.title: Records and validation
docs.text:
Payloads carry ids, counts, and digests only — never needle values or answer text. Each record stores the case id, topic, the expected answer's SHA-256 digest, and question_tokens (the length of the case's Q render for that candidate); each cell stores verdict, boundary fields, input tokens, answer digest, and the measured needle offsets ([t] treated, [t1, t2] duplicate, [0] for dose_0, [] for absent). There are no construction/seam fields: under delta acceptance the seam classification of earlier probes needs a new definition, and the offsets and deltas carry the evidence — silence was the one wrong option (red-team B), so the fields are dropped, not attested.

The verdict is bound, at the multiturn standard: verdict == (answer_digest == sha256(expected)) and boundary_found, with the expected digest taken from the record and the case set mirror-regenerated by the validator (the cycle-187 numform F2 settlement — a payload-derived case hash would be tautological). The diff validator recomputes everything else: the case set from the protocol seed by its own mirror of the derivation table (fixture ids, topics, and expected digests, in order); the protocol fingerprint; cross-candidate fixture order; the cell identities — treated input_tokens − dose_0.input_tokens == dose, duplicate == dose + needle_len with needle_len derived as dose_0.input_tokens − question_tokens, absent input_tokens − question_tokens == dose; needle offsets equal to the frozen targets; and all aggregates and per-cell selection (including the paired-restricted flip baselines) with independent arithmetic.

Honesty (attested links, disclosed). Three fields are stage-attested, at the same standard multiturn discloses: the needle offsets (the validator checks them against the frozen targets; it has no renders and cannot re-derive them — a stage that wrote the targets without measuring would pass, which is why the stage's measurement is itself test-pinned against scripted tokenizers); the absolute level of input_tokens (every identity is a difference, and unlike distraction — whose native counts anchor in the recorded primary run — needle's dose-0 is stage-generated, so no external anchor exists); and question_tokens in the corner where both absent cells of a record are unrecorded (one unobserved degree of freedom shared with the derived needle_len; it feeds no aggregate). The digest-only verdict binding proves internal consistency, not that a generation occurred — the multiturn standard, one step below numform-190's answer-text binding, and stated as such. Needle cells are generations on generated fixtures, not recorded search observations, so they are outside verify --determinism scope (the multiturn settlement).

docs.title: Cost
docs.text: Fifteen generations per candidate per case; 7,200 at the caps (24 candidates × 20 cases × 15), which is also the ground-record arithmetic: MAX_GROUND_RECORDS = 480, GENERATION_BUDGET = 7,200. Prompts reach ~4,100 bulk tokens at the top dose under full-prefix recompute with no KV cache; forwards per generation scale as M·L + M(M−1)/2 in generated length M and prompt length L. The CLI help states the counts, the forwards formula, and the --max-context requirement for the 4096 dose before the run. The run's cancel event is threaded dispatch → wrapper → stage → evaluate, checked between cases and between cells.

docs.title: Negation probe — design round (ADJUDICATED: BUILD, with binding amendments)
Round summary (coordinator #36, design round only — nothing built)
docs.text:
• Tree at main 960b70dcde87 (cycle 211 closed green, 8,402 tests, per the round brief). This round was READ-ONLY except for this doc and the briefs; no suite was run, no push was made, no tag was cut or discussed.
  • Specialists (blind to each other, then audited): researcher (~/workspace/agents_out/negation/research.md), red-team A (redteam_a.md), red-team B (redteam_b.md), verifier/claims auditor (verifier.md). All four briefs landed.
  • Convergence and divergence, in one paragraph: both red teams independently returned NO-BUILD for the loose sketch, and the verifier sustained NO-BUILD for the researcher's narrowed instrument as the researcher specified it — its §1 "iff" is false, its §3.4 operating characteristics story is backwards, its winner readout must be dropped rather than demoted, and its floors, echo decomposition, and scope justification were unfrozen. The coordinator concurs with every one of those judgments about the brief as specified. The verdict below is nevertheless BUILD, for a precise reason stated in §1: every defect the verifier names is corrected inside this doc, by amendment to the same instrument — same population, same arms, same scorer, same joint-rule shape — with the one genuinely quantitative correction (the decision threshold) derived by the coordinator's own execution in §7 and frozen here. The build cycle implements THIS doc, not the research brief. Any deviation from a frozen item in this doc (arms, rule, threshold, vocabulary, echo set, claim language) is not an implementation detail: it voids this verdict and requires fresh review. This is the distinction from the payload round's F6 rule: there the amendments replaced an undefined instrument with a different one (undefined payload → frozen tables, causal → descriptive); here they correct the decision rule and the claim language of an instrument whose population and arms were already frozen and executable.

docs.title: Verdict: BUILD (as amended in this doc)
docs.text:
• Verdict: BUILD — the narrowed instrument specified in §2–§6, under the binding amendments in §1.1.
  • What the verdict is NOT: it is not a build order for the research brief, not for the loose "negation sensitivity" sketch, not for any winner headline, and not for the borrowed 6/2 floors. All four are NO-BUILD and are removed in §8.

docs.title: 1.1 Binding amendments (each incorporated below, none left open)
docs.text:
1. Claim narrowed and made one-directional. No "iff", no "negation-invariance is falsified", no "negation sensitivity" as a headline, no causal "negation changes verdicts" sentence. The section's only falsification-class label is negation_drop_observed, defined exactly in §2.4 as a sufficient pattern detector, with its named rival patterns printed beside it.
  2. Decision threshold re-derived from this panel's own operating characteristics (§7.3), not borrowed. The rule is D ≥ 8 and J ≥ 5 (definitions in §2.4). The borrowed placement/canonical-form floors (6/2) are REMOVED: the coordinator reproduced the verifier's finding that (6,2) fires on a random labeller 58% of the time. At (8,5) the random-labeller fire rate is ~4%, the no-effect competent-candidate fire rate is 0.7%, power at a 0.5 drop rate is 84%, and power at a 0.25 drop rate is only ~21% — the panel is powered for large drop rates and weak for small ones, and the section must print exactly that (§5).
  3. Winner readout DROPPED in v1, not demoted. No per-arm selection, no winner headline, no winner-vs-abstention readout. Per-arm pass rates and the joint pattern are the only readouts. Grounds: the numform settlement (experiments stage docstring, §7.1) forbids selection over the synthetic set, canonical-form's winner_headline is a total function of two arms with no three-arm extension, and NUMFORM_DESIGN itself records that over 16 values an all-pass selection readout "carries almost no information per unit of validator surface". Any future selection claim must first overturn that settlement with argument; it may not be added at build time.
  4. Frozen negation_echo decomposition (§4.2). The echo diagnostic is enumerated, validator-mirrored, and printed beside — never inside — the byte-exact headline. Without it the negated-arm rates are uninterpretable (a perfect comprehender answering "not second" scores 0/16 on the negated arm); with it, that pattern is labelled as echo, not as negation-drop.
  5. Antonym bundle disclosed in the claim itself (§2.2). The negated arm differs from direct in two lexical moves (negation token + larger→smaller antonym swap). The claim is therefore "antonym-negated definite-description discordance", and the section states the bundle wherever the headline appears. The flipped arm is a necessary competence gate, not a control: flipped-pass is necessary, not sufficient, for attributing a negated failure to negation processing, and wording × position interaction remains an unexcluded rival, printed as such.
  6. Scope justification (§6). Semantic instruction variation is deliberately excluded scope for surface-noise (see §6); this probe re-enters that scope for one frozen, derivable-ground-truth criterion variation, for the reasons in §6 — not for paraphrase generally.
  7. Open points decided, not deferred (§2.5, §3, §4): the 2×2 factorial completion is v2; the descriptive alt-negated arm is kept as a non-decision sensitivity only; the record shape is canonical multi-cell (one record per candidate × case, one cell per arm); the stage screen detail is negation_screen_failed, bound to the pre-generation audit screen defined in §4.3.

docs.title: 1. Why the loose sketch was NO-BUILD (fatals, each executed)
F1 — No single arm pair diagnoses negation
docs.text: Red-team B's executed truth table over the seed-0 generated compare set: a larger-default candidate (always answers the larger label) passes direct and negated 16/16 with zero direct–negated discordance, and is indistinguishable from a smaller-blind-lexical candidate on every per-arm pass count and every pair discordance. An always-first candidate yields maximal direct–flipped discordance (16/16) with zero negation content (red-team A E5). The direct–negated pair therefore cannot be the headline, and the direct–flipped pair cannot be a control: it measures antonym/criterion following, position bias, and base-task weakness jointly. Only the per-case triple pattern (pass direct, wrong-label on negated, pass flipped on the same case) diagnoses the negation-drop pattern — and only as a sufficient detector, never as an "iff" (see §2.4: larger-default is an undiagnosed rival pattern, not an acquittal; it is visible in the flipped pass rate printed beside the decision, never hidden).

docs.title: F2 — Byte-exact scorer × negated answer form (reporting fatal)
docs.text: The verdict is byte-exact (core.py:797: exact_match = status == "completed" and answer == case.expected), conjoined with boundary presence in stage cells. A semantically correct negated answer ("not second" for expected "first") therefore fails at every scorer-lens rung — the ladder has no label-strip operation (scorerlens.py: "label_prefix": "no label-strip operation exists") — and numform's own decomposition buckets it as non_label, the same class as gibberish (coordinator execution, §7.2). Wrong-label-only counting in the joint rule neutralises this for the boolean (echoes cannot fire it), but without a frozen negation_echo subclass the negated-arm rates stay uninterpretable and the perfect comprehender still scores 0/16 on the arm. That is why amendment 4 is binding and why the section must never print a negated-arm pass rate without its echo share beside it.

docs.title: F3 — The negated arm bundles treatments; length has no control
docs.text: Direct (79 chars) vs flipped (80) vs "not smaller" (84) vs "not the smaller one" (92) vs "not less than the other" (96) — red-team B's executed character deltas. The negated arm is longer by construction, and no length-matched negated control exists that is not itself a treatment (verbosity territory). Length is therefore a reported rival, not a controlled one: per-case id_length_delta is printed, the descriptive alt-negated arm (longer still) provides a length-gradient check, and a systematic wrong-label pattern (not mere failure) is the only pattern the section may attribute — with the length rival printed beside it, never argued away. Token-count delta is UNEXECUTED in this round (the tree has no frozen local tokenizer; only backend.encode exists) and must not be claimed in the build doc; character delta and render-id length delta are the reported quantities.

docs.title: F4 — Winner re-derivation over this panel is forbidden by settlement
docs.text: See amendment 3. The three-arm winner rule in the research brief is not a total function over three arms, and the settlement it would violate is explicit in the tree (experiments numform stage docstring: "No selection, no winner, no flip against the primary run: the synthetic set is a different contest from the user's fixtures, and a winner over 16 generated values per task would invite exactly the headline the design forbids"). Dropped, not demoted.

docs.title: F5 — Borrowed floors fire on noise (new fatal for the narrowed design)
docs.text: Coordinator reproduction (§7.3): the researcher's 6/2 rule fires on a random labeller (independent 0.5 labels per arm) 58% of the time, and the researcher's §3.4 operating-characteristics story is backwards (it claims the rule "fires only on a fairly lopsided pattern"). A falsification rule that fires on noise more often than not is not a conservative label; it is a broken instrument. The derived (8,5) rule in §2.4 replaces it in full. Borrowed floors are forbidden for every rule in this panel.

docs.title: Non-fatals, adjudicated
docs.text:
• Conditional equivalence survives. "Not the smaller" ≡ "larger" given a ≠ b, by the pair-closed complement rule (§2.3). The article form beats the bare form (the verifier's §6.1: the bare form's own ¬(x<y) ⟺ x≥y concedes the equality ambiguity). Ties are not a population defect: the generator enforces a ≠ b (numform.py:550) and the validator re-derives it; an equal pair fails the stage closed (§4.3), never gets tie-broken. Refuted attacks (red-team B R1–R5): no-equivalent-phrasing, operand-order scoping change, context-capacity threat (max delta +17 chars), single-digit breakage, ties-as-population-defect — all refuted by execution and not carried forward.
  • Scope (red-team A M3) stands as a requirement, not a fatal. Addressed by §6.
  • Form-crossing (red-team A M1) is settled, not open. Plain form only in v1; form-crossing is a v2 panel with its own claim. Budget arithmetic follows from the frozen record shape (§3.3).
  • Degenerate populations (red-team A M4) are pinned, not open. Distinct-only, direct-pass conditioning, per-stratum/per-band reporting (§3).

docs.title: 2.1 Home and frozen base
docs.text:
The home is the numform compare task, plain form only. Its frozen template is model_protocol_lab/numform.py:121-127 (compare entry):

"Which of these two numbers is larger? Reply with only the word first or second.\n{a}\n{b}"

Compare is the one numform task whose expected answer is a form-invariant label (numform.py:596-603, expected_answer: compare returns expected_label, never a rendered number). The generator constructs compare pairs with a != b enforced (numform.py:550), records which side is larger (larger_first, lines 572–576), and decomposes a compare cell into exact_pass / wrong_label (the other label) / non_label (numform.py:840-863, cell_decomposition). That decomposition is load-bearing: wrong_label on the negated arm is the negation-drop signature, non_label is a different failure, and negation_echo (§4.2) is a frozen subclass of non_label — never pooled into wrong_label, never rescuing a flip into a pass.

docs.title: 2.2 Frozen instruction strings (v1 arms)
docs.text:
Operands are rendered in plain form only and substituted for {a} (first line) and {b} (second line), exactly as numform does. The reply contract — "Reply with only the word first or second." — is byte-identical in every arm, so the answer vocabulary never varies. Operand order is identical across the arms of one case — only the instruction sentence changes.

Arm Frozen instruction (operands appended, one per line) Expected answer direct Which of these two numbers is larger? Reply with only the word first or second. label of the larger operand negated (headline) Which of these two numbers is not the smaller? Reply with only the word first or second. label of the larger operand — the same label as direct flipped Which of these two numbers is smaller? Reply with only the word first or second. label of the smaller operand — the opposite label to direct negated_alt (descriptive only, §2.5) Which of these two numbers is not smaller than the other? Reply with only the word first or second. label of the larger operand — never a decision input

Worked examples (from the shipped generator at seed 0, verified by the coordinator, §7.2): operands [100, 47], larger_first=True, expected_label="first" — direct → first, negated → first, flipped → second. Operands [199, 999], larger_first=False, expected_label="second" — direct → second, negated → second, flipped → first. The label flips with presentation order, so a position-biased candidate cannot pass all three headline arms by position alone, and the generator's larger_first alternation (slot parity, numform.py:572) keeps the direct expected-label balance exact by construction (8/8 at seed 0).

Antonym-bundle disclosure (binding). The negated arm differs from direct in two lexical moves: insertion of the negation token ("not the") and the antonym swap (larger→smaller). Negating the direct predicate alone ("not larger") is the flipped arm. The claim in §2.4 is therefore about the antonym-negated definite description as a whole, and every headline rendering of it states the bundle. No sentence in the report may attribute a discordance to "negation" simpliciter.

docs.title: 2.3 Expected-answer derivation rule (and the distinctness condition)
docs.text:
Let the pair be (x, y), x ≠ y, presented as (first, second). Define L = the label of max(x, y), S = the label of min(x, y); L ≠ S.

  • direct: "larger" denotes max(x, y) → L.
  • negated: "the smaller" is a definite description denoting min(x, y) — it has a unique referent only because x ≠ y. "Not the smaller", read as complement within the presented pair, denotes the pair member that is not min(x, y), i.e. max(x, y) → L. The derivation is the pair-closed complement rule, not a general English equivalence. It is conditional, and the section states the condition wherever the derivation appears.
  • flipped: "smaller" denotes min(x, y) → S = the opposite label.
  • negated_alt: same derivation as negated, for its own phrasing; its scope profile (comparative + "the other" anaphora) differs slightly, which is one reason it is descriptive only.

Distinctness condition (load-bearing, validator-enforced). If x = y, "the smaller" has no unique referent and "not the smaller" is undefined — not "either", not "both", not a third label. The generator asserts a != b (already present, numform.py:550); the diff validator independently re-derives a != b for every case and rejects the record set if any pair is equal; an equal pair is never scored, never silently dropped, and never "resolved" by a tie rule. Equal values are not a v1 population at all — a tie arm would need its own instruction ("neither" is not in the frozen answer vocabulary) and is excluded. Margin classes emitted by the generator are exactly different_length, same_length_early, same_length_last_digit (numform.py:320-342); same_length_middle is a real class the classifier reports but the generator never emits, so a record carrying it fails validation, as does equal.

docs.title: 2.4 Falsifiable claim (pre-registered, one-directional)
docs.text:
For one candidate, over the cases it completes in all three headline arms, let D be the cases it passes on the direct arm, and let J be the cases in D where, on the same case, the negated cell's decomposition is wrong_label (the smaller label — not any failure, not an echo, not a boundary miss) and the flipped cell passes. Then, per candidate:

  • D < 8 → insufficient — withheld, never defaulted to acquittal and never to a robustness claim.
  • D ≥ 8 and J ≥ 5 → negation_drop_observed — the negation-drop pattern is observed on this candidate, on this frozen phrasing, at this panel size. This is a sufficient-pattern detector, not a biconditional: it does not establish "negation-invariance" when it does not fire, and it does not diagnose every negation-related defect when it does.
  • D ≥ 8 and J < 5 → below_threshold — an observed null at this panel size, not proof of invariance. The section prints the operating characteristics in §5 beside every below_threshold.

Named rival patterns (printed beside every decision, never hidden):

  • Larger-default / instruction-ignoring: passes direct and negated, fails flipped broadly. Visible as a low flipped pass rate; it is undiagnosed by J (J = 0 for it by construction) and must be labelled "negation-drop undiagnosed, not absent" whenever the flipped pass rate on D is below 0.5. It is not acquitted as invariant.
  • Echo-comprehension: passes direct and flipped, answers negated with a negated label form (§4.2). Visible as a high negation_echo share; it is not negation-drop and must not be reported as such.
  • Wording × position interaction: a wrong-label pattern that is concentrated in one presentation order (larger-first vs larger-second) is labelled as order-concentrated, not as general negation-drop. The section prints J split by presentation order.

What the claim is not. No causal claim about weights, training, or "negation understanding" as a latent ability follows from any outcome. The instrument measures verdict discordance under greedy decoding on one frozen phrasing, not a mechanism. Generalisation to open-world negation is an extrapolation the report must not make: in an open-world task the complement of the negated description is not a singleton, and the expected answer is underdetermined.

docs.title: 2.5 Variants: kept, descriptive, excluded (all decided)
docs.text: Variant Status in v1 Reason Negated-alt phrasing "not smaller than the other" Descriptive arm only, never a decision input, never pooled Bounds phrasing awkwardness: a joint pattern reproducing on two negated phrasings is harder to dismiss as one phrasing's artefact; a pattern appearing on only one phrasing is labelled phrasing-dependent. Its wrong-label count on D and its alt-joint count are printed descriptively. It is frozen byte-for-byte in §2.2 or it does not ship. Negated-flipped "not the larger" (expected = smaller) EXCLUDED from v1; named as the v2 2×2 factorial completion Fourth cell of criterion {larger, smaller} × polarity {affirmative, negated}. Its expected answer coincides with the flipped arm's, inviting pooling error, and combining two negated contrasts needs its own pre-registered rule. A v2 factorial requires a rewritten claim and fresh review, not a column added at build time. Negated answer option ("reply with the word that is not first") EXCLUDED Changes the answer vocabulary and the scorer's target set at once; failure could be vocabulary confusion, not negation processing. Imperative negation ("Do not pick the smaller…") EXCLUDED from v1 Different speech act (prohibition vs interrogative definite description) and a different scope; a genuine second probe, closer to hierarchy territory, not a variant of this one. Scope variants "not larger" vs "not the larger" (bare vs article) EXCLUDED as arms; REQUIRED as a design note Without the article, "not larger" in open English means ≥, which coincides with the article reading on distinct pairs and diverges on equal pairs — precisely why §2.3's distinctness assert is load-bearing. The article is not decoration; it is the scope pin. Double negation, affixal/implicit negation ("un-", "less", "never", "the other one") EXCLUDED from v1 Compositional and lexical negation are different mechanisms with their own ambiguity profiles. "The other one" is not a negation at all (anaphora) and must not enter a negation headline. Negated operand statement ("The first number is not the smaller…") EXCLUDED That is a claim arm (leading territory), not a criterion arm.

docs.title: 3.1 Generated cases only, stage-local, never the user Split
docs.text: Cases are generated by the shipped numform compare generator (same seed, same value set) and live only in the stage; they never enter the user's search/held-out Split. This is the canonical-form invariant, and it is forced here for a stronger reason than in canonical-form: variant fixtures (direct vs negated vs flipped renderings of one pair) are three fixtures about one pair, and any future Split-adjacent analysis that groups by pair would inherit a triple-counting trap. Stage-local generation avoids the question entirely, exactly as canonical-form does (canonicalform.py:17-22 in its module docstring: generated cases only, stage-local, never the Split). Note the Split mechanics for the record: Split compares message inputs by NFC key and rejects identical message inputs across the split (core.py:169, class Split; uniqueness at line 204, identical-message rejection at line 214) — variant fixtures are not identical messages, so they would not collide, but the triple-counting trap above is the reason to stay stage-local regardless.

docs.title: 3.2 Value ranges, strata, form, and presentation
docs.text:
• Values: reuse numform's bands verbatim — numform.py:99: BANDS = ((1, 3), (4, 6), (7, 9), (10, 12)) digit lengths, 4 values per band per task, giving 16 compare cases per candidate. Margin strata cycle by slot — different_length, same_length_early, same_length_last_digit — and the headline is reported per stratum descriptively, never pooled across strata into a single "negation rate" that hides a stratum effect (e.g. a last-digit-only effect would be a digit-discrimination story, not a negation story). Seed-0 shape (verifier-confirmed): strata 8/4/4, bands 3/4/5/4, 8/16 length-decidable (different_length — the larger is necessarily the longer string, so length alone decides those cases).
  • Form: plain only. Crossing negation with form would be a 3 × 4 (4 × 4 with the descriptive arm) panel whose headline could not attribute a flip to either axis — the payload F3 bundle again. Plain is the form where the operands are bare digit strings and the only moving part is the instruction, which is the point. Form-crossing is a v2 panel with its own claim.
  • Presentation order: the shipped larger_first alternation (numform.py:572-573) is kept byte-for-byte, so direct expected labels are balanced first/second by construction and no new order bias is introduced.
  • Answer contract and decoding: byte-identical reply contract in every arm (§2.2); greedy decoding, same --max-new-tokens, same boundary ids, same seed, same template family per candidate. Templates are not touched: negation lives inside the user message content only.
  • Closed-book screen: none, and canonical-form is the precedent. Placement's screen (placement.py:370-381, screened(): a record is screened when its closed-book cell completed and passed) does not transfer, for a structural reason: in placement the payload is a prose fact passage that can be removed while leaving a well-formed question; in compare, the operands are the task content, and removing them leaves a question with no ground truth. The screen's function — excluding cases the treatment cannot move — is already served by conditioning on D: a case the candidate fails directly is a case negation-drop cannot be shown to move, and it is excluded from the headline population by construction. Canonical-form explicitly takes the same position (canonicalform.py:556-557: "There is no closed-book screen in this probe").

docs.title: 3.3 Counts (frozen, with derivations)
docs.text:
