• Headline generations: 16 cases × 3 arms × 24 candidates (run_experiment's cap, per the placement comment on its 24-candidate panel) = 1,152.
  • With the descriptive alt arm: 16 × 4 × 24 = 1,536 generations.
  • Ground records: 24 candidates × 16 cases = 384 records, in the canonical multi-cell shape (one record per candidate × case, one cell per arm — the canonical-form record shape, not numform's one-record-per-generation shape; this choice is what makes the arithmetic above the record arithmetic, and the diff validator regenerates arms from the same shape).
  • The build cycle states the byte/record cap derivation in CLI help from this shape (the sibling pattern: a frozen cap constant with its derivation, enforced by the stage and re-derived by the validator), and prints these numbers with derivations, not as bare constants.

docs.title: 3.4 Token-ID divergence: reported, not gated
docs.text:
Canonical-form's headline population is ID-divergent paired cases only (canonicalform.py:399, _pair_block_divergent), because NFC/NFD renderings can collapse to identical id sequences, in which case the instrument is inapplicable rather than the model robust. For negation the situation is inverted: the arms differ in instruction text by construction, so their full render id sequences will diverge on any ordinary tokenizer, and divergence-gating would be vacuous — it would gate on a condition that is true by construction and hide the one informative event, a same-ids case, which indicates a tokenizer/rendering pathology. (The research brief's universal "will diverge on any sane tokenizer" is REMOVED: it is an unexecuted universal. The design reports divergence and treats same-ids as an anomaly, which covers both outcomes without asserting either.)

Required machinery (canonical-form shape, different gating):

  • Per case, per arm, record the full render id sequence digest and length, following the canonical-form stage pattern (experiments.py:9639-9647: ids_identical and id_length_delta computed from the arms' render ids at construction).
  • Report, per candidate: n_ids_identical across arm pairs (expected 0), the per-case id_length_delta list in case order for direct-vs-negated (expected positive: the negated instruction is longer), and max_abs_id_delta.
  • Headline population = cases completed in all three headline arms, not id-divergent. A same-ids case, if one ever occurs, is excluded from the headline population and counted separately as a rendering anomaly, never as a pass or a fail, and a same-ids verdict flip is recorded as a determinism finding, never as negation fragility (payload-round rule).
  • Token-count delta is NOT reported as a measured quantity (see F3): the tree has no frozen local tokenizer. Character delta and render-id length delta are the reported quantities.

docs.title: 4.1 Headline scorer
docs.text: core.evaluate's byte-exact verdict (core.py:797: exact_match = status == "completed" and answer == case.expected), conjoined with boundary presence in the stage cell (the canonical-form cell pattern: cell verdict = exact_match and boundary_found). No stripping, no parsing, no normalisation is added to the headline path. The scorer-lens ladder (scorerlens.py:137, RUNGS = (0, 1, 2, 3, 4)) may be reported as a sensitivity beside the headline — in particular, a negated-arm failure that recovers at R1/R3 (whitespace/fence) is a scorer artefact, not a negation discordance — but it never rescues a flip into a pass, and the ladder has no label-strip operation, so "Answer: first" does not recover against "first" at any rung.

docs.title: 4.2 Decomposition and the frozen negation_echo subclass
docs.text:
Every completed cell is decomposed by numform's cell_decomposition (numform.py:840-863) into exact_pass / wrong_label / non_label, where for compare wrong_label means the answer digest equals the digest of the other label and non_label means anything else. On top of that, the build defines and the validator mirrors exactly one frozen subclass:

  • negation_echo: a completed cell whose raw answer is, exactly (byte-for-byte, no stripping, no casefolding), one of the negated forms of the other label for that arm — that is, for an arm whose expected label is E with other label O, the answer is "not " + O or "not the " + O. Concretely: expected first → echo answers "not second", "not the second"; expected second → echo answers "not first", "not the first". Any other negated form ("not the second one", "not second.", "NOT second") is non_label (other), not echo — the set is frozen, and enlarging it at build time voids this verdict.

Reporting rules: per arm, the section prints the exact_pass / wrong_label / negation_echo / non_label (other) split. The negation_echo share is printed beside every negated-arm rate, never pooled into wrong_label and never into a pass. The joint rule (§2.4) counts only wrong_label, so echoes cannot fire it; a candidate whose negated failures are predominantly echo is reported as echo-dominant, not as negation-drop, and the section must say so in words, not merely in a table column.

  • Boundary decomposition (mandatory): every discordance is decomposed into exact-only vs boundary-only. A boundary-only discordance (answer text equals expected, boundary missed) is a boundary effect, never a negation effect, and cannot count toward J. The cell already carries boundary_found, so this decomposition costs no new machinery — but it must be printed, not merely available.
  • Expected values are the two ASCII labels first / second (canonical-form SCORER PIN transplant: decomposable characters live in carrier prose only; here there is no carrier prose at all, so the pin is satisfied trivially and the scorer cannot be a form/encoding confound).
  • Per-arm attrition (n_context_exceeded, n_evaluation_failed) is printed beside every paired rate; ungated discordance is printed as a sensitivity wherever any gating applies.

docs.title: 4.3 Fail-closed vocabulary (frozen before building)
docs.text:
Following the sibling pattern (e.g. density's stage details ("cancelled", "density_record_budget_exceeded", "density_screen_failed") at density.py:131-136, and per-record details ("", "arm_evaluation_failed", "arm_context_exceeded")):

  • Stage details exactly: {cancelled, negation_record_budget_exceeded, negation_screen_failed}. negation_screen_failed is bound to one real screen: the pre-generation audit screen over the frozen instruction strings and the generated set — special-token-literal audit over every frozen instruction string for every family (the fixtures.py:471 audit_special_token_literals pattern), distinctness re-derivation (a != b for every case), and margin-class validity (only the three emitted classes). Failure of that screen makes the stage unavailable with that detail. (Red-team A's negation_template_screen_failed was considered and not adopted: the screen covers the whole generated set, not the template alone.)
  • Per-cell details exactly: {"", arm_context_exceeded, arm_evaluation_failed}.
  • Whole-stage failure: any generator failure, renderer failure, serializer exception, or non-UTF-8 payload degrades the whole stage to {"available": False, "detail": "negation_unavailable"} — never to a per-cell verdict. A validator rejection of the record set (including an equal pair) is likewise whole-stage negation_unavailable, not a per-cell drop.
  • Model parse failure is scored wrong, never a detail. No new verdict words. In particular: no arm_parse_failed, no per-arm "not applicable", no negation_too_large.
  • Section decision labels (negation_drop_observed, below_threshold, insufficient) are section labels only, not cell or stage details, and are defined solely by §2.4.

docs.title: 4.4 Pre-generation audit (counts, never silent drops)
docs.text: Cases failing the §4.3 audit screen are excluded pre-generation with counts (n_audit_excluded, by reason), never silently dropped. For the shipped generator the expected audit-excluded count is 0 (distinctness is enforced by construction); a nonzero count is itself a finding about the generator and must be printed, not normalised away. Screened cases are never scored.

docs.title: 5. Report shape and operating characteristics (printed, not footnoted)
docs.text:
Per candidate, the section prints, in this order:

  1. Per-arm pass rates (direct / negated / flipped / negated_alt descriptive) with per-arm attrition beside each.
  2. The decomposition split per arm (§4.2), with the negation_echo share separated on the negated arms.
  3. D, J, and the decision (§2.4), with J split by presentation order (larger-first / larger-second) and by stratum.
  4. The rival-pattern readouts: flipped pass rate on D (with the gate-weak qualifier when below 0.5), echo-dominant flag, and order-concentration flag.
  5. id_length_delta list (direct-vs-negated, case order) and max_abs_id_delta; n_ids_identical (expected 0; any nonzero count is a determinism finding, §3.4).
  6. Boundary-only vs exact-only discordance decomposition.
  7. The operating-characteristics paragraph, verbatim in substance:

"At D = N, this panel (16 cases) falsifies only negation-drop patterns at least as lopsided as J ≥ 5 at D ≥ 8. It does not establish invariance. Measured operating characteristics of the (8,5) rule: a random labeller (independent 0.5 labels per arm) fires ~4% of the time; a competent candidate with no negation effect (direct/flipped pass 0.9, negated wrong-label rate 0.1) fires 0.7%; power is 84% at a 0.5 drop rate (direct/flipped pass 0.9) and 99%+ at 0.75, but only ~21% at a 0.25 drop rate. Small effects are therefore usually missed; a below_threshold on this panel is weak evidence."

Records carry digests only (per-arm content digests, token counts, ids_identical, id_length_delta, cells, details — canonical-form record shape). Reports render counts/rates only, no payload/question/answer text, every payload-derived string through _escape_text (reporting.py:28), never bare escape().

No winner headline, no pooled discordance. Discordance is never pooled across candidates/templates: per-candidate contrasts only. The per-case joint classification is the primary readout; per-arm rates are descriptive context beside it.

docs.title: 6. Scope justification (red-team A M3, required section)
docs.text:
Surface-noise deliberately excludes semantic instruction variation: its not_measured list includes "semantic paraphrase of instructions" (surfacenoise.py, listed twice in the module's scope declarations), and its perturbation axis is surface-only. This probe re-enters that scope for exactly one variation, on three grounds that paraphrase generally does not meet:

  1. Derivable ground truth. The negated arm's expected answer is derivable by construction from the pair (pair-closed complement, §2.3), without labelling, judging, or a gold set. General paraphrase has no such derivation: a paraphrase's expected answer is "the same as the original" by stipulation, which is exactly the payload round's F2 defect (a false "same content" claim).
  2. One frozen treatment, not a family. The variation is one frozen string (§2.2), not "paraphrase" as an open class. Its scope is the definite-description mechanism, stated in the claim (§2.4), not "instruction meaning" in general.
  3. A sibling precedent for meaning-bearing instruction variation with controls. Leading varies a stated claim and hierarchy varies instruction privilege, both meaning-bearing, both with joint per-case disciplines — the lab's scope exclusion is specific to surface-noise's axis, not a lab-wide ban on semantic treatments. What surface-noise excludes is uncontrolled semantic variation; this probe's variation is controlled by construction (§2.3, §3, §4).

If the build cycle widens the variation beyond the frozen string (any second negated phrasing as a decision input, any paraphrase arm, any imperative arm), it exits this justification and voids this verdict.

docs.title: 7. Adjudication evidence (coordinator's own execution)
docs.text:
All snippets read-only; no suite was run.

  • Seed-0 compare population. build_fixtures(0) gives 16 plain compare cases; the first two match the research brief's worked examples exactly (nf-compare-00: "…larger?… 100 47", expected first; nf-compare-01: " 199 999", expected second). larger_first alternation and the a != b assert are as cited (numform.py:550, 572-576).
  • Echo decomposition. Constructed records through numform.cell_decomposition (numform.py:840-863): answer "not second" against expected "first" → non_label; answer "second" → wrong_label. The echo fatal is therefore real for rates (a perfect echo-comprehender scores 0/16 on the negated arm) and neutralised for the boolean (echoes cannot satisfy the joint rule's wrong_label condition) — exactly the verifier's §6.3 split, reproduced here.
  • Larger-default. By construction (not simulation): a larger-default candidate passes direct (expected = larger) and negated (expected = larger) on every case and fails flipped (expected = smaller) on every case, so J = 0 for it. It is an undiagnosed rival pattern, visible only in the flipped pass rate — hence the gate-weak qualifier in §2.4/§5. The always-first simulation (red-team A E5) and the truth table (red-team B §F1, reproduced row-for-row by the verifier) are accepted on the verifier's reproduction.
  • Operating characteristics (§5 table). Coordinator Monte Carlo, independent labels per arm, 40,000 trials per cell, 16 cases: (6,2) random-labeller fire rate 0.581 (reproducing the verifier's 57.6% within seed noise); (8,5) random 0.036–0.039 across seeds; no-effect competent (0.9, 0.9, 0.1) 0.0073; partial drop (0.9, 0.9, 0.5) 0.84; moderate drop (0.9, 0.9, 0.75) 0.99+; small effect (0.9, 0.9, 0.25) 0.21. The (8,5) rule is the smallest (Dmin, K) pair in the explored grid with random fire below 5% and partial-drop power above 80%; (10,5) fires 0.023 with power 0.85 and is an acceptable stricter variant, but (8,5) is frozen here so the build does not re-derive it. Method note: "random labeller" is a noise-floor null, not a model of a real checkpoint; the no-effect competent row is the realistic false-fire row. Both are printed in §5.
  • Tree settlements verified by reading (line numbers as observed in this round): core.py:797 exact-match line; numform.py:550 distinctness assert; numform.py:572-576 larger-first construction; numform.py:840-863 decomposition; experiments numform stage docstring ("No selection, no winner, no flip against the primary run"); canonicalform.py winner_headline as a total function of two arms; density.py:131-136 stage/per-record detail pattern; surfacenoise.py not_measured including "semantic paraphrase of instructions"; scorerlens.py "label_prefix": "no label-strip operation exists"; NUMFORM_DESIGN's per-form selection exclusion ("over 16 values per task an all-pass selection readout carries almost no information per unit of validator surface").
  • Verifier reproductions accepted: red-team B's Monte Carlo (17,215/2,763/22) bit-for-bit, its truth table row-for-row, red-team A's scorer tables exactly (verifier §4). The coordinator did not re-run those reproductions; they are credited to the verifier, not claimed as coordinator executions.

docs.title: 8. Removals applied (verifier §7.2 — none of these enter any build doc)
docs.text:
• Research §1 "iff" biconditional and the phrase "negation-invariance is falsified" → replaced by one-directional "negation-drop discordance observed" (§2.4).
  • Research §3.4 operating-characteristics story in full → replaced by §5/§7.3 (backwards: the 6/2 rule fires on noise).
  • Borrowed 6/2 floors for every rule in the panel → replaced by the derived (8,5) rule.
  • The winner readout in any form (secondary or headline) → dropped (§1.1 amendment 3).
  • Research R7 word counts 11/9/9 → correct counts are question-only 9/7/7, full 17/15/15 (verifier §7.2); no word counts are load-bearing in this doc, and the §3.6 "3-word instruction delta" implication is removed (character deltas are reported instead, §1 F3).
  • The "Negation Neglect survey" citation and Zhou §4 compositional pointer → REMOVED (unresolved).
  • Rezaei & Blanco as a load-bearing source → REMOVED (real paper, never cited in the body).
  • Kassner & Schütze Table 2 digits (ρ > 85%, 20.1%, 54.2%, 31.3%, p < 0.01) → UNVERIFIED pending primary re-resolution; not declared false, not used. Kassner is not load-bearing in this doc.
  • Vrabcová §§2–3 synthesis as evidence → REMOVED (abstract only is used, §9).
  • Research's "will diverge on any sane tokenizer" universal → REMOVED (replaced by report-and-anomaly, §3.4).
  • Any "negation sensitivity" / "negation-blind" / "negation understanding" causal wording for a pair-only or pooled readout → replaced by the §2.4 language.
  • The payload "F1–F5" count → the payload round has F1–F6.
  • Red-team A M1's "exactly at the cap" gloss → REMOVED (budget arithmetic follows from the frozen record shape, §3.3).
  • Red-team B's bare-phrasing freeze as the default → the article form is adopted (§2.2).
  • Red-team A negation_template_screen_failed → considered, not adopted (§4.3).
  • Wave-10 Elkins & Chun figures (77%/100% under negation) → NOT carried into this doc (not re-verified in this round).
  • Incorrect line ranges corrected, not carried forward (verifier §2.2; substance survives in each case).

docs.title: 9. Sources the build may safely cite
docs.text:
Only verifier-§3.1-confirmed figures, plus the combination framing scoped to fetched sources. No "first" is claimed anywhere in this doc. The contribution is the combination stated in §2–§5, never priority.

  • Truong et al., arXiv:2306.08189, §3 / Table 5 (via verifier §3.1): negation NLI benchmarks below random for GPT-J-6B zero-shot (e.g. SNLI-neg 0.316, MNLI-neg 0.275, RTE-neg 0.211, NaN-NLI 0.298), MoNLI at chance (0.500, not below random); InstructGPT improves classification (RTE-neg 0.767, NaN-NLI 0.647) with MoNLI at 0.470; Finding 4's warning that the InstructGPT gain could reflect similar patterns in training data. Fencing: curated datasets, not generated pairs; no template crossing, no selection rule, no flipped control.
  • Ravichander et al. (CondaQA), arXiv:2211.00295, abstract and results section (verifier-corrected pair): UnifiedQA-v2-3B accuracy 73.26% vs human 91.94%; consistency 42.18% vs human 81.58%; 14,182 pairs, 200+ negation cues. Fencing: human-labelled Wikipedia passages with open answers, not generated pairs; consistency across passage edits, not instruction phrasings for one fixed task.
  • Vrabcová et al., arXiv:2503.22395v2, abstract only: paired entailment datasets differing in negation; size may improve negation handling; accuracy and robustness are language-dependent. Fencing: NLI entailment, not a generated binary-choice task; §§2–3 synthesis not used as evidence.
  • Zhou et al., arXiv:2605.03052v1, §3.1 / Table 1 / Table 2 kept separate (verifier §3.1): 162 unique questions × 4 templates = 648 entries; positive accuracy 90.7–95.5% vs negative accuracy 45.4–58.3% across six open-weight models, sensitivity 95.1–98.0% (§4.1, Table 1); late-layer attention ablation raising negative accuracy (e.g. Llama-3.1 50.5% → 67.8%, §4.2, Table 2). Fencing: logit-difference accuracy on single-token answers, not greedy byte-exact generation under a chat template with a boundary; no selection rule; no flipped-criterion control; its mechanistic conclusion is not testable through the lab's Backend interface and must not be claimed by this probe.
  • Literature direction (not digits, except where listed above): negation failure is well-documented across cloze, NLI, and contrastive-consistency paradigms, and no fetched source measures it on this lab's template-family × greedy × boundary instrument — the combination framing, scoped to fetched sources. Anything beyond this paragraph needs fresh primary resolution before it enters a build doc.

docs.title: 10. What a build cycle must NOT do on the basis of this doc
docs.text:
• Do not build the research brief's §1 rule (6/2, "iff"), the loose "negation sensitivity" sketch, or any winner headline.
  • Do not add a decision-input arm (negated-flipped, imperative, double negation, paraphrase) without fresh review.
  • Do not enlarge the echo set, re-derive the (8,5) threshold, or pool discordance across candidates/templates.
  • Do not write a causal "negation changes verdicts" headline, a prose-control framing, or any new verdict word.
  • Do not transfer placement/canonical-form or field-order floors to this panel; its floors are §2.4 and §5 only.
  • Do not ship a run --negation flag until the naming audit against USAGE passes (precedent: the payload round's reserved "payload" sense; a grep of USAGE finds no existing "negation" use, but the audit itself is a build-cycle check, not a conclusion of this doc).
  • Building, if it happens, is a separate cycle, on this doc — and only on this doc's frozen items. A build that deviates from any frozen item needs fresh design review first.

docs.title: Numeric surface-form probe — design (cycle 186, wave-7 rank 7)
docs.text: Status: frozen pre-build design. Sources: wave-7 research §7 as corrected by the cycle-186 researcher refresh (Reddy et al. 2026, arXiv:2601.15251, and Yang et al.'s NUPA, arXiv:2411.03766, were missed by §7 and narrow the claim); red-team A (F1–F17, DO NOT BUILD AS SPECIFIED against the §7 sketch); red-team B's executed cross-check (BUILDABLE AS AMENDED — three of A's remedies disproved or replaced); the verifier's blast-radius brief. Where the briefs disagree, B's executed evidence governs.

docs.title: What it measures, in one sentence
docs.text:
For a user whose prompts carry figures, run --numform shows — per chat-template candidate, per task kind, per numeric surface form — whether the checkpoint copies, compares, and adds generated integers equally well when the same values are written plain, comma-grouped, space-grouped, or in scientific notation, so the user can choose a normalisation for numbers in their own prompts. Monday-morning decision: which written form to normalise figures to before rendering, for this checkpoint, per task kind.

Scoped claim (the combination only): numeric surface form × hand-rendered chat-template family, on a fixed local checkpoint, over generated fixtures with form-matched expected answers, per-candidate paired form contrasts, and the tokenizer's digit grouping measured at run time as a grouping variable only, was not found in the work surveyed in the cycle-186 uniqueness pass (LOGGED in docs/RESEARCH_LOG.md). Format variation over fixed arithmetic is published (Reddy et al. 2026, including a formatted-input → formatted-output condition); representation × task benchmarks including scientific notation are published (NUPA); comma-enforced rechunking is published (Singh & Strouse 2024, arXiv:2402.14903). Per-form selection was part of the §7 sketch and is deliberately NOT in v1 (red-team B, GB5): over 16 values per task an all-pass selection readout carries almost no information per unit of validator surface, and "the winning template changes under comma grouping" is exactly the overclaim the design must not invite. If selection is ever added it takes the leading_analysis form, never the hierarchy form.

docs.title: Domain and forms
docs.text:
Non-negative integers only. Negatives and fractions are excluded and named (with integers only, no decimal marker exists, so a comma can only be a grouping separator — the locale ambiguity Reddy's F2 exposes cannot arise). Digit bands: 1–3, 4–6, 7–9, 10–12 digits. Values per task: 16 (4 drawn per band; a pair's recorded band is its larger operand's band, so compare's recorded per-band counts vary around 4 — read denominators from a payload's own by_band counts, not from this line). Operands never exceed 12 digits; a sum never exceeds 13.

Renderers are total functions of the integer value alone, never of an operand string:

  • plain(v) = str(v)
  • comma(v): 3-3-3 grouping with "," (named 3-3-3 in the docs — Indian 3-2-2 grouping exists and is not this arm)
  • space(v): the same grouping with U+202F (narrow no-break space, the SI grouping separator; ASCII space would collide with operand separation in the prompt text, and the choice is named in the CLI help)
  • sci(v): 0 ↦ "0e0"; otherwise with d = str(v), exp = len(d)−1, mantissa digits = d with trailing zeros stripped, rendered first digit + ("." + rest if any) + "e" + str(exp). Lowercase e, no "+", mantissa in [1, 10) — NUPA's significand precedent.

Totality is proven by an exhaustive round-trip sweep (all values 0–2000 plus edge values, × 4 forms, render → parse → identity, no scientific collisions) and by the regrouping/renormalisation battery (999,999 + 1 → 1,000,000 / 1e6; 9.99e6 + 9.99e6 → 1.998e7; 1.25e6 + 1.25e6 → 2.5e6). Decimal appears nowhere in generation, rendering, or parsing: its default context rounds at 28 significant digits, its parser accepts underscores, whitespace, NaN and non-ASCII digits, and its string forms are not these forms (all executed by red-team B). Arithmetic is Python int; parsing is a frozen ASCII grammar.

docs.title: Tasks and prompts
docs.text:
Three task kinds; each value set is drawn once per task and rendered into all four forms (paired design). All four form arms of one value share one fixture id (nf-{task}-{index}), so core.request_seed_for pairs their request seeds. Frozen prompt templates (verbatim in numform.py, SHA-256 in the protocol) contain no digit and no worked example in any form — a single example is a few-shot arm for one form only, and few-shot recovery is the largest mitigation Reddy et al. measure. The templates instruct the model to answer in the operands' form; pass := correct value ∧ explicitly-requested form ∧ boundary found, which is Reddy's formatted-output condition held constant across arms — part of the task definition, not a confound that varies with the treatment.

  • copy: "Copy this number exactly, character for character:"
  • the operand on its own line. Expected: the operand string.
  • add: "Add these two numbers and reply with only the sum, written in the same format as the numbers:" + one operand per line. Expected: render_form(a + b).
  • compare: "Which of these two numbers is larger? Reply with only the word first or second." + one operand per line. Expected: the label first / second. The same-form rule is amended to exempt compare (the label is form-invariant, which makes compare the one arm where the scorer cannot be a form confound); the exemption is stated in the reporting section. Equal pairs are excluded by construction (a generator invariant, recorded); mixed-form pairs are out of scope (the mixed-notation cell is Yuchi et al. 2026's).

docs.title: Generation
docs.text:
Deterministic, SHA-256-derived (fixturefuzz pattern: parameters from SHA-256 over (seed, task, band, slot, counter); sorted iteration only; no random.Random, no hash(), no set order) — the generated set is byte-identical across runs and PYTHONHASHSEED values, proven by a two-hash-seed regeneration test. Candidate operand pairs are drawn from the hash stream and accepted when an independent digit-wise classifier confirms the target stratum class (bounded retries):

  • copy: one value per slot; slots 0–1 of each band are the round-value stratum (a power of ten; all-nines), labelled by the round stratum. The label is intrinsic — random draws exclude round values — so the validator can recompute it from the value alone. Pairs carry no round label (compare reorders its operands for presentation, so which operand was drawn round is not a record-level fact); round first operands in pair slots 0–1 remain a property of the generated set, bound by generator_sha256.
  • compare: margin classes cycle by slot — different_length, same_length_early (first difference in the leading half), same_length_last_digit; larger-first vs larger-second alternates by slot parity.
  • add: carry classes cycle by slot — none, some, full_chain — computed digit-wise with carry-in propagation.

A pair's band is the band of its larger operand's digit length. Strata ride in every ground record; band/stratum breakdowns are descriptive (below the contrast floor), and bands whose compared forms are byte-identical (plain/comma/space coincide below 1000) report n_form_identical and carry no headline.

docs.title: Stage mechanics
docs.text:
Mirror: hierarchy for synthetic-fixture construction only; leading/distraction for everything else. Per-fixture evaluate() (one call per candidate × task × form, ids shared across forms), cancel and max_context threaded, per-cell fixed-vocabulary details: arm_context_exceeded (rendered + max_new_tokens > max_context), answer_budget_exceeded (expected answer + boundary cannot fit max_new_tokens — insurance at the frozen bands, stated as such), form_not_in_render (an operand string does not appear verbatim in the rendered prompt for that candidate — the check is per candidate × cell, on the real render), and arm_evaluation_failed. Stage-level: the frozen templates are screened with audit_special_token_literals before any generation (fail closed: numform_template_screen_failed); cancellation returns available: False, detail cancelled. The CLI wrapper consults neither the search entries nor the primary decision (there is no native arm and no dependence on the user's fixtures), honours the run's cancel event, and never raises: any failure degrades to numform_unavailable. The section is informational and never touches selection.

Cost: candidates × 3 tasks × 16 values × 4 forms generations — 4,608 at the legal maximum of 24 candidates — stated in the CLI help in those words. Caps frozen in numform.py and carried in the protocol: GENERATION_BUDGET 4608, MAX_GROUND_RECORDS 4608, MAX_RECORDS_BYTES 12 MiB; exceeding the record budget fails the stage closed (numform_record_budget_exceeded).

docs.title: Records and decomposition
docs.text:
Generated values are not user data, so records store the expected side's canonical integer values in the clear (operands, expected value) — and the validator does not merely trust them: it regenerates the whole set from the protocol's seed and compares every record's construction against the regenerated set (cycle 187; before that, the validator hashed whatever records were present, which vouched for a binding it never checked). The answer side, since cycle 190: a record carries the answer text verbatim (answer_text, the raw answer segment, never normalised) beside the value the stage parsed from it, and the cell carries the text's digest. The validator checks sha256(answer_text) == answer_digest (fail-closed on text that cannot be UTF-8 encoded) and re-parses the text under its own mirrored grammars, requiring the result to equal the stored value — the stage's parse is no longer trusted anywhere. Compare answers are words, not numbers: they are bound by the digest alone, and a numeric compare answer ("123") is a legal non-label record. A cell that never completed carries neither text nor value; the validator rejects either one appearing there. Pre-cycle-190 payloads are rejected (the record key set is exact); there is no migration shim, because a shim would re-open the forgery for exactly the payloads it accepted. Records ride in the public results.json (and in sealed bundles) regardless of --include-evidence, like every probe's ground records — an explicit decision, restated in the README: the prompts are synthetic and the stored text is the answer segment only, and stripping it would break diff-reports on the default artifact. The report never renders answer text.

Two consequences of storing text, both accepted and pinned by test. First, byte accounting: the field costs ~26 bytes per record on faithful workloads (428 → 454 B/record; 1.88 → 2.00 MiB at the legal maximum of 4,608 records), and the 12 MiB records cap leaves ~2,277 escaped bytes of headroom per record over that baseline — so a checkpoint that rambles to a large --max-new-tokens can now push a run into numform_records_too_large where the same run stayed available before (at the default 64 tokens the worst case still fits, at 8.75 MiB). The stage fails closed after spending the generation budget; the cap is unchanged. Second, an alternative was considered and rejected: store the text only when it parses (the longest parseable answer is 26 characters, so that field would cost ≤ ~42 B/record) and a sentinel otherwise. The projection is sound — every validator use of the value factors through the parse — but it makes the validator carry a second representation with its own honesty conditions (in the sentinel branch: digest ≠ expected digest, verdict false, value None) in place of one direct equality, to save bytes the cap already accommodates.

Per-cell decomposition (recomputed by the validator from the re-parsed answer value):

  • copy / add: exact_pass (verdict true); else value_pass_form_fail when the parsed answer value equals the expected value (reported split by boundary_found); else value_fail. For copy, value_pass_form_fail is a failure of the task, not a consolation — copying is form fidelity; the class exists there to keep "right digits, wrong costume" distinguishable from "wrong digits", and the section says so.
  • compare: exact_pass; wrong_label (the answer is the other label — groundable from digests alone, since the label set has two known strings); non_label (anything else).

The answer parser is grammar-gated with digit/exponent caps enforced BEFORE any conversion (total digits ≤ 20, exponent ≤ 999 with ≤ 3 exponent digits), applied to model answers as well as expected strings: an answer like 1e999999999 classifies value_fail, never allocates (the live Decimal/DoS surface is answer-side, red-team B GB3). The parser accepts the four form grammars plus plain digit strings (leading zeros parse), and for scientific a capital E or + exponent when parsing only — costume differences belong in value_pass_form_fail, not in value_fail. Wrong-width grouping (1,23,456) does not parse.

Headline contrast: per candidate × task, for each of the six form pairs, paired discordant counts over the common-completer population (values completed in both forms): n_paired, n_pass_a_only, n_pass_b_only, n_both_pass, n_both_fail, McNemar exact p over the discordants (diagnostic only, never thresholded), and a classification from the total function of (n_paired, b, c): paired < MIN_PAIRED_EVALUABLE (6) → insufficient; b = c = 0 → no_difference_observed; b ≥ MIN_DISCORDANT (2) ∧ b > c → {form_a}_advantage; c ≥ 2 ∧ c > b → {form_b}_advantage; b = c ≥ 2 → mixed_discordance; otherwise below_threshold. Marginal per-form rates are reported beside the contrasts with their denominators, never instead of them, and no rate or contrast is ever pooled across tasks (N3, enforced structurally: the payload has no cross-task total for the validator to certify).

docs.title: Tokenizer grouping
docs.text: One run attaches one backend, so grouping takes exactly one value per run: it is a run-level descriptive label and a cross-run diff variable, never a within-run correlation. The classification is measured, never inferred from a family name (§7's "Llama/Gemma-style single-digit" was wrong for Llama 3+, which groups by 3 — TokSuite; Reddy Table 5). A frozen, count-based probe battery over backend.encode: plain renderings of digit strings of every length 1–12 (sequential, all-same-digit, zero-heavy) plus every form of a frozen probe value. Decision rule (frozen): single_digit iff every all-digit probe's token count equals its digit count; chunked_up_to_3 iff every all-digit probe of length ≥ 2 has token count exactly ceil(len/3) and length-1 probes count 1; irregular_or_mixed iff every count lies between those two predictions without matching either rule; otherwise unknown (including any encode failure). Probe evidence (string → token count) is stored in the payload; the diff validator re-runs the decision rule over the stored evidence — a consistency check, labelled as such, since the validator has no tokenizer. unknown never blocks the per-form rates and always blocks grouping language in the section. §7's N2 is demoted from invariant to measured diagnostic: the payload reports the actual per-form operand token counts and deltas from plain; separator merges (a comma fusing with adjacent digits) are data, not classification errors.

docs.title: Protocol and diff
docs.text:
Protocol object: version, tasks, forms, bands, values_per_task, floors (6 / 2), budgets, space codepoint (U+202F), scientific grammar id, prompt templates + templates_sha256, renderer spec id, generator_sha256 over the canonical generated set (operands and expected values per task/value/form), seed, backend fingerprint; fingerprint = SHA-256 over the canonical object. Generator drift ⇒ not comparable.

diff_numform recomputes from the records with independent code (no imports from numform.py): every form rendering and expected string (N1: all forms of a value parse to the same value), every aggregate, the decomposition, the paired contrasts, and the protocol fingerprints; it regenerates the generated set from the protocol's seed with its own mirror of the generator and compares every record's construction against it, checks that candidates agree on the expected answer's token count, and re-runs the grouping decision over stored evidence (consistency) with the stored token means/deltas held to the producer's arithmetic relation (each delta is its form's mean minus the plain mean, up to float summation order). Grouping drift between runs is reported and flags the form-contrast comparison; it does not by itself make sections incomparable. Impossible payloads are rejected: pass > completed, rate ≠ count/denominator, duplicate (task, value, form) record keys, a cell present iff its detail is empty, records over the caps, malformed digests, per-record construction fields (band, strata, operands, expected) inconsistent across candidates, records that are not the protocol seed's generated set, and any pooled cross-task total present at all.

docs.title: Honesty items
docs.text:
• Generated integer tasks, isolated operands, this exact prompt wording, zero-shot, this checkpoint: the section states the scope in the quantity's definition, and per-task readings only — no pooled "best form". A form × template interaction is a per-candidate contrast, never a pooled marginal.
  • A low pass rate in a form means "cannot do the task AND return the answer in this form, under byte-exact scoring" — the decomposition is what licenses any narrower arithmetic reading, and only from the value_fail class.
  • The pre-registered null: all paired deltas at no_difference_observed / below_threshold across forms — a publishable "normalisation does not matter here" result.
  • Compare is a verbalisation-under-form measurement (Yuchi et al.: probed magnitude knowledge exceeds verbalised accuracy); grouping explains nothing by itself within a run, and cross-tokenizer claims require cross-run diffs of different checkpoints, which confound weights with tokenizer.
  • The decomposition's answer side rested on the stage's parse until cycle 190 (see Records and decomposition); the validator now re-parses the digest-bound answer text itself. The parse grammars exist three times (producer, diff validator, cycle-27 test oracle) and are pinned equal — pattern texts by test, behaviour by a differential battery over the grammar alphabet including the five classic divergence classes (non-ASCII digits, trailing newlines, digit-count caps, negative-shift divisibility, uncapped scientific results).
  • Named future work, not in v1: spelled-out number words, locale forms (decimal-comma, 3-2-2 grouping), other space codepoints, mixed-form fixtures, fractional operands, negatives, per-form selection.

docs.title: Round summary (coordinator #35, design round only — nothing built)
docs.text:
• Tree at main 960b70dcde87 (cycle 211 closed green, 8,402 tests, per the round brief). This round was READ-ONLY except for this doc and the briefs; no suite was run, no push was made, no tag was cut or discussed.
  • Specialists (blind to each other): researcher (~/workspace/agents_out/payloadformat/research.md), red-team A (redteam_a.md), red-team B (redteam_b.md), verifier/claims auditor (verifier.md). All four briefs landed; the verifier resolved every externally checkable claim against primary sources and spot-checked the load-bearing tree citations.
  • Convergence: both red teams independently returned NO-BUILD, and the verifier upheld both verdicts. The coordinator re-executed the load-bearing claims itself (see "Adjudication evidence" below) and concurs.
  • Verdict: NO-BUILD — for the candidate as tentatively framed (run --payload-format: JSON vs plain text vs other encodings of "the same content", verdict flips as headline) AND for the researcher's design as written. The reasons are not implementation gaps; they are defects in the defining claim (see §1). §2 specifies what a resubmission would have to satisfy in full. A resubmission satisfying §2 is a DIFFERENT, narrower instrument and must be reviewed as a new design, not built as "this probe with amendments". Accepting the amendments while keeping the original causal claim does not count as accepting them.

docs.title: 1. Why NO-BUILD: the fatal defects (each individually blocking)
F1 — "The task payload" is undefined, and the tree gives it incompatible meanings
docs.text: Placement's payload is a prose fact passage (placement.py:267-283 arm_content); a structured spec's context is prose (structured.py:445-458 render_prompt); a structured spec's answer document is canonical JSON (structured.py:463-480 build_structured_fixtures); shipped user fixtures are instructions, not data (examples/fixtures.json). No module defines a serializable task-data record type. A design that leaves the choice to the builder does not have a population, a scorer, or a headline — underspecification at this level is itself a build-blocker.

docs.title: F2 — "The same content" is false across the named encodings
docs.text: Typing, loss, and parser-dependence change the content before any model runs. Executed in adjudication: json.loads('{"a": 1, "a": 2}') gives {'a': 2} (last-wins); JSON 349 is int while plain-text 349 is str; JSON true/null are boolean/null while plain-text true/null are strings; CSV flattens nesting; XML must choose attributes vs elements. There is no canonical-equivalence theorem for JSON-vs-prose comparable to canonical-form's UAX #15 basis, and prose has no parser to be equivalent under. A content-preserving claim needs, per arm, a frozen byte-exact renderer, a frozen key order, and a lossless value restriction — which the candidate as framed does not supply.

docs.title: F3 — "Serialization" bundles at least six simultaneous treatments
docs.text: Token length, delimiters/punctuation, quoting/escaping, key order, whitespace, and output priming all move together. Key order is already a shipped probe (run --field-order); whitespace is ws_canonical's territory; length/position are needle/distraction/density/placement axes. No paired contrast over such arms attributes a flip to "serialization" rather than to the bundle. The only supportable claim is descriptive pairwise discordance between named frozen renderings, with length and priming stated as bundled, never a causal "serialization changes verdicts" headline.

docs.title: F4 — The byte-exact scorer × output-format priming manufactures and hides flips
docs.text: The verdict is byte-exact with no answer stripping: core.py:797 (exact_match = status == "completed" and answer == case.expected), conjoined with boundary presence in stage cells (experiments.py:9515 pattern). A model answering correctly in the input arm's idiom ({"code": "amber-1234"} on the JSON arm) scores False against a bare expected value; a model failing to parse the JSON arm but guessing the bare code scores True on both. The fixes are closed: parse-then-compare redefines "verdict" relative to every sibling probe and the diff validator's digest identity (the fix canonical-form rejected); outcome-dependent exclusion deflates discordance exactly as field-order's F6 lesson discloses; the scorer-lens ladder has no label-strip operation and cannot rescue JSON-echo answers. The researcher's echo diagnostic beside the headline is necessary but does not cure this: it explains flips, it never rescues them, and the headline still bundles comprehension with priming.

docs.title: F5 — Degenerate populations and arms
docs.text: Single-field cases collapse to punctuation differences (executed: scalar JSON 42 is byte-identical to plain 42; single-field JSON differs from key-value lines only by braces, colon, and quotes). Multi-field populations are already partly owned: field-order owns key order over 15 specs, structured owns output adherence over 9 specs (1–2 fields only — not 1–4, as red-team A misstated; see §4). Whitespace-only JSON variants (compact vs spaced vs pretty) are a whitespace probe under a serialization name. The researcher's multi-record table population is the right shape of answer to F5, but it does not cure F1–F4, and its arm set and headline do not survive (see §2).

docs.title: F6 — The researcher's design as written does not survive its own amendments
docs.text:
Credit where due — the researcher already supplies a frozen multi-record population with unique keys and distinct values, frozen field order, a value alphabet plus a four-way byte-divergence assert, and an echo diagnostic beside the headline. What still kills it as written:

  • The YAML arm must go in v1: zero runtime dependencies (pyproject.toml:28, dependencies = []); no stdlib YAML parser; YAML 6.0.1 importing in this VM is an environment accident, not a declared dependency; a hand-rolled mirror parser is new untrusted code whose quoting choices become hidden treatments. TOML has no stdlib writer (tomllib has no dumps, executed); XML escaping rewrites visible text. V1 arms must be stdlib-serializable frozen renderings only.
  • The falsification headline must be downgraded from causal to descriptive pairwise discordance with ONE pre-registered primary pair; the researcher's prose-vs-rest framing plus all-pairs matrix, with placement's floors borrowed without operating characteristics for a four-arm panel, does not survive the k(k−1)/2 multiplicity problem (10 pairs at 5 arms).
  • The prose "control" framing must go: prose is one encoding among others. The researcher says this, then still computes prose-vs-rest first. The decision rule must pick one framing before building.
  • Missing mandatory machinery: a closed-book screen (placement pattern; canonical-form's lack of one is a gap to avoid copying, not a precedent); a boundary-only vs exact-only discordance decomposition; the full selection-vocabulary transplant; per-arm attrition reporting; a frozen fail-closed vocabulary with renderer failure failing the whole stage closed.

docs.title: 2. Resubmission specification (NOT a build order)
docs.text: A resubmission is reviewable as a NEW design only if it satisfies ALL of the following in full. Partial compliance is still NO-BUILD. The resubmission's working name must reflect the narrowed claim (a descriptive frozen-renderer discordance probe); do NOT ship --payload-format until the naming audit against USAGE §8.46 passes, since placement's "payload" sense is reserved.

docs.title: Monday-morning utility (narrowed instrument)
docs.text: A prompt-assembly owner, deciding whether to pin one frozen rendering (prose or canonical JSON) in their prompt assembly and re-run template selection under that pinned rendering — before a routine upstream format change silently flips eval verdicts. The readout answers "these two frozen renderings discord on N paired cases on this checkpoint", never "serialization is (in)ert in general", and never anything about weights.

docs.title: Arms (frozen, byte-exact, stdlib-only)
docs.text:
• Exactly one pre-registered primary pair, recommended: prose vs canonical JSON as defined by structured._canonical_json (structured.py:336-343: json.dumps(document, sort_keys=True, separators=(", ", ": "), allow_nan=False); default ensure_ascii=True). Executed in adjudication: that rendering is byte-unequal to compact json.dumps ('{"age": 36, "name": "Ada Lovelace"}' vs '{"age":36,"name":"Ada Lovelace"}'), so the canonical form must be pinned by name and by test, never assumed.
  • Every arm is a named total function with a byte-exact specification and a worked example in the resubmission doc, pinned by a test that its output is byte-identical to the doc's example. "Plain text" without such a function is not an arm name; it is a placeholder. Pretty JSON, flow YAML, Markdown lists, and single-record tables are excluded as duplicates, each with the duplicate it duplicates named.
  • CSV stays deferred (loss analysis: CSV flattens nesting and drops types). XML stays deferred (escaping rewrites visible text; no canonical-serialization convention in the tree). YAML stays out of v1 entirely (see F6); it may return only as a separately justified v2 with a declared dependency or a frozen stdlib-only renderer the validator can mirror. No other arms are decision inputs; any further arms are descriptive context only.

docs.title: Population and controls (the attribution contract)
docs.text:
• Generated cases only, stage-local, never entering the user's search/held-out Split (canonical-form invariant 3 pattern; Split compares message inputs by NFC key, core.py:193-214, so variant fixtures would collide — no fixture arm).
  • Fresh multi-record tables (4–6 records × 3–4 fields), one key field (unique per table), one answer field, 1–2 distractor fields whose values are distinct from the answer value in every row. Cases whose answer value appears in more than one row, or whose key field is not unique, are excluded pre-generation with counts, never silently dropped.
  • Value restriction (v1, strictest form): flat, string-only, ASCII, stem-disjoint, reader-entailed tables. Answer field is a plain word-number-style code in every arm. No null, no nesting, no duplicate keys, no floats, no non-string keys, no YAML-reserved words (yes, no, on, off, null, ~), no date-like strings, no leading-digit strings. Non-answer fields are string-shaped too. Integers/booleans are a v2 question with a frozen per-arm type-rendering table, not a v1 entitlement.
  • Held constant across arms (each a generator/validator assert): the same record multiset, field values, key field, and answer field; one frozen field order (alphabetical, the structured.describe_schema convention, structured.py:403-443, which sorts properties) in JSON keys, YAML keys (v2), and table columns alike, and the same sentence field order in prose; a byte-identical question and instruction string in the same position relative to the table (question after the table in all arms); a byte-identical output contract ("Answer with ONLY the value." or equivalent, frozen); greedy decoding, the same --max-new-tokens, the same boundary ids, the same seed, the same template family per candidate. Templates are not touched: serialization lives inside the user message content only.
  • No format label in the instruction unless the label choice itself is frozen identically across arms and its confound is stated.
  • Closed-book screen arm (placement pattern, placement.py:374-380 screened()): a case the candidate passes closed-book is excluded from the live populations, with n_screened and n_closed_book_incomplete reported. Without it the headline is dilutable by cases serialization cannot move.
  • Answer-embedding audit: no field name, key, topic token, or neutral sentence shares a 4-character prefix with, or is a prefix of, any expected value (placement's stem-disjointness pin, extended to keys). Reader-entailment audit per case: a reader given question + table must derive the answer uniquely, or the case is descriptive-only. If a resubmission instead reuses shipped specs, it inherits field-order's paired: False flags verbatim — all five: route-alert, route-order, classify-sentiment, classify-urgency, classify-language (verified by grep: 5 paired: False entries, 10 paired: True, 15 specs total).
  • Byte-divergence assert across arms per case, with excluded counts; boundary-containment screen plus audit_special_token_literals (fixtures.py:471) over every frozen renderer output for every family before generation. Screened cases are excluded pre-generation with counts, never silently dropped.
  • Generation/record/payload caps and the generation count at the legal maximum of 24 candidates are frozen in the module with derivations and stated in CLI help (field-order precedent: 15 specs × 4 arms × 24 candidates = 1,440; canonical-form: 2 × 24 × 24 = 1,152; placement: 4 × 24 × 24 = 2,304).

docs.title: Scorer pins (binding)
docs.text:
• Headline scorer, named before building: byte-exact verdict per core.evaluate (core.py:797). No stripping, no parsing, no normalization is added to the headline path for this probe.
  • Beside the headline, never rescuing flips into passes: a parsed-value / echo-substring diagnostic (per arm, the share of byte-exact failures whose decoded answer contains the expected value as a substring or as a parsed field value — the echo rate); scorer-lens R1 (whitespace trim/collapse, scorerlens.py:146-153) and fence-strip (:176-187) regrade rates as sensitivities; and the exact-only vs boundary-only discordance decomposition (a boundary-only discordance is a boundary effect, never a serialization effect, and cannot falsify any claim).
  • Expected values are pure ASCII (canonical-form SCORER PIN transplant): decomposable characters live in carrier prose only.
  • If byte-exact and parsed-value scorings disagree, the section prints both and says which question each answers; it must not pick the flattering one post hoc.

docs.title: Fail-closed vocabulary (frozen before building)
docs.text:
• Stage details exactly: {cancelled, payload_format_record_budget_exceeded, payload_format_screen_failed}. (The payload_format_ prefix is retained for the stage-detail pattern only; the CLI flag name is still subject to the naming audit above.)
  • Per-cell details exactly: {"", arm_context_exceeded, arm_evaluation_failed}.
  • Model parse outcomes exactly field-order's document_kind set (object / non_object / unparseable / ""), where unparseable means JSON parse failure of the ANSWER only.
  • Model parse failure is scored wrong, never a detail. Any renderer failure, serializer exception, or non-UTF-8 payload degrades the whole stage to {"available": False, "detail": "payload_format_unavailable"} — never to a per-cell verdict.
  • No new verdict words. In particular: no arm_parse_failed, no unparseable as a cell detail for stage-produced inputs, no payload_too_large, no per-arm "not applicable".
  • Per-arm attrition (n_context_exceeded, n_evaluation_failed) printed beside every paired rate; ungated discordance printed as a sensitivity wherever any gating applies.

docs.title: Report shape and decision rule
docs.text:
• Headline population: both arms completed AND full-render id sequences diverged (canonical-form invariants 9–10). Three-way report per pair: ids-identical / divergent-concordant / divergent-discordant, with the per-case id_length_delta list (in case order) and max_abs_id_delta. Same-ids verdict flips are recorded as determinism findings (n_same_ids_verdict_flips), never as serialization fragility. A run landing 100% in the ids-identical bucket reads "instrument inapplicable to this tokenizer", never "the model is robust to serialization".
  • Per-candidate classification over the id-divergent paired population, with the resubmission's OWN operating characteristics printed with the verdict (critical splits, power at a stated gap, expected false falsifications across candidates for its panel size). Borrowed floors are forbidden: placement/canonical-form floors (MIN_PAIRED_EVALUABLE = 6, MIN_DISCORDANT = 2, placement.py:172-173) and field-order floors (6 discordant specs + sign test) may not be transferred to a payload panel without that argument. Below the discordant floor the verdict is insufficient — withheld, never defaulted to acquittal.
  • Selection vocabulary transplanted verbatim from canonical-form (canonicalform.py:566-641): a candidate "passes" an arm iff it passes every completed case on that arm; winner_changed only when both arms select and winners differ; winner_abstention_asymmetric for exactly one side selecting; winner_undefined when neither selects or selection is withheld (completed sets differ across candidates or are empty). Selection-vs-abstention is NEVER a winner change. Per-arm accuracy rates sit beside every selection readout; per-arm completion and withheld rates are printed. The per-case discordance classification is the primary readout; the winner headline is secondary and labelled as such. Discordance is never pooled across candidates/templates: per-candidate contrasts only.
  • Records carry digests only (per-arm content digests, token counts, ids_identical, id_length_delta, cells, details — canonical-form record shape). The diff validator regenerates every arm's rendering from its own literal renderer copies and checks each digest plus pairwise digest inequality across arms, plus ids_identical implies equal arm token counts. Reports render counts/rates only, no payload/question/answer text, every payload-derived string through _escape_text (reporting.py:28), never bare escape().

docs.title: 3. Adjudication evidence (coordinator's own execution)
docs.text:
All snippets read-only; no suite was run.

  • core.py:797: exact_match = status == "completed" and answer == case.expected — verified exact line; no answer stripping in the verdict path (only strip hits are field validation and a prefix-trim repair variant, per the verifier's grep).
  • structured._canonical_json at structured.py:336-343: json.dumps(document, sort_keys=True, separators=(", ", ": "), allow_nan=False) — byte-unequal to compact json.dumps (executed: '{"age": 36, "name": "Ada Lovelace"}' vs '{"age":36,"name":"Ada Lovelace"}').
  • Duplicate-key parse: json.loads('{"a": 1, "a": 2}') → {'a': 2} (last-wins) — executed.
  • tomllib has no dumps (executed: hasattr(tomllib, 'dumps') is False); YAML 6.0.1 imports in this VM while pyproject.toml:28 declares dependencies = [] — executed.
  • Catalog: 29 Format( entries (catalog.py:26) — executed.
  • Placement floors: MIN_PAIRED_EVALUABLE = 6, MIN_DISCORDANT = 2 at placement.py:172-173 — verified.
  • Field-order spec inventory: 15 specs, 10 paired: True, 5 paired: False (route-alert, route-order, classify-sentiment, classify-urgency, classify-language) — verified by grep over fieldorder.py.
  • Placement arm_content at placement.py:267-283 (prose payload, question-position arms) — verified.

docs.title: 4. Removals applied (verifier §6 — none of these enter any build doc)
docs.text:
• Researcher S2 §3.1 grammar sentence (descriptors, separators, casing functions, itemizers; equivalence by shared rule application): REMOVED until re-resolved from the Sclar primary text. The Sclar headline (up to 76 accuracy points on LLaMA-2-13B, weak cross-model correlation) is verified from the abstract and survives; the grammar detail does not.
  • Researcher S2 "(ICLR 2024)" venue tag: REMOVED until re-resolved (the abstract page does not state it).
  • Incorrect line ranges corrected, not carried forward: structured canonical JSON 337–343 → 336–343 with allow_nan=False added; placement 251–279 → 250–283; placement 50–51 → 50–52; cli 177–926 → 174–938; red-team A's experiments.py:9515-1520 range deleted (cell function _canonical_form_cell at 9473–9522, verdict line 9515).
  • POML Mistral second format corrected to "HTML (Ugly) (0.348)", not plain HTML (Table 3 values otherwise verified).
  • Red-team A F3/M1/M6 length figures (66/69/76/86/59/99/93) and the derived "68% longer" / "25% longer" sentences REMOVED as executed evidence: the brief never states the renderers, so the numbers are not reproducible from the brief. The length-confound argument survives on red-team B's reproducible case (canonical JSON 35 chars vs one plain rendering 27 chars, a 29.6% delta) and on canonical-form's per-case id_length_delta discipline.
  • Red-team A F4 "structured spec set … with 1–4 fields" CORRECTED: the shipped structured set is 1–2 fields (9 specs); 3–4-field specs are field-order's six additions.
  • Red-team A M4 prose-selection rendering 'winner': 'A'→ none REMOVED; correct form is {'decision': 'no_candidate', 'winner': None}.
  • Red-team B M4 paired-flag sentence CORRECTED to all five paired: False specs (see §2); B's m1 already handles the single-field three, so the combined text must list five.
  • Design-level removals: the YAML arm in v1; any causal headline of the form "serialization changes verdicts"; prose as "the control" / "baseline truth" / "natural format"; any new verdict word (see §2); the attribution of input_tokens to placement.py (it lives in experiments.py stage cells); any borrowed floors without the resubmission's own operating characteristics.

docs.title: 5. Sources the resubmission may safely cite
docs.text:
• He, Rungta, Koleczek, Sekhon, Wang, Hasan, arXiv:2411.10541v1: Abstract (plain text, Markdown, JSON, YAML templates; GPT-3.5-turbo varies by up to 40% on code translation); §2.2 (five prompt components, content of each placeholder stays the same, only structure/syntax differ); §2.3 (OpenAI GPT-3.5/GPT-4 via Azure only); Table 1 / §3 (MMLU 59.7 JSON vs 50.0 Markdown on GPT-35-turbo-0613); Figure 1 caption ("Accuracy goes up by 42% for JSON compared to Markdown" on MMLU international-law questions). Fencing that must travel with it: He et al. bundle the whole prompt template into one "format" treatment, cross no chat-template family, run no local checkpoint under exact-token discipline, and re-select no winner.
  • Sclar, Choi, Tsvetkov, Suhr, arXiv:2310.11324v2: Abstract only (up to 76 accuracy points on LLaMA-2-13B; format performance only weakly correlates between models; meaning-preserving formatting in few-shot settings on open models). The §3.1 grammar detail and the ICLR venue tag are REMOVED (see §4).
  • Zhang, Chen, Xu, Yang (POML), arXiv:2508.13948v1, §7 Table 3 (100 sampled styles, WikiTQ subset): Claude 3 Haiku CSV (0.449) / Markdown (0.424); DeepSeek V3 HTML (0.801) / JSON (0.800); Gemini 2.0 Flash XML (0.791) / HTML (0.788); Mistral AI 8x7B XML (0.365) / HTML (Ugly) (0.348); §7 text on model-specific optimal table formats. Fencing: POML's 100 styles bundle table syntax with other styling dimensions; no chat-template crossing or winner re-selection.
  • Tam et al., arXiv:2408.02442, §4.1 (via the scoping already in docs/FIELDORDER_DESIGN.md): emitted key order under constrained JSON mode only (100% of GPT-3.5 JSON-mode Last-Letter responses placed the "answer" key first). Fenced off: emitted-order effects are not input-serialization effects.
  • JSONSchemaBench, arXiv:2501.10868v2 (via the citation in structured.py:1-60): output adherence only, fenced off on the same ground.
  • No "first" is claimed anywhere in this doc. The contribution of any future resubmission is the combination stated in §2, never priority. No fabricated citation was found in this round (unlike the wave-9 round); the failures found were one unresolved detail, one dropped qualifier, and sloppy line ranges, all handled above by removal or correction.
  • Two 2026 preprints the researcher saw only as search snippets remain uncited and unrelied on; a resubmission wanting them must verify them from primary text first.

docs.title: 6. What a build cycle must NOT do on the basis of this doc
docs.text:
• Do not build the researcher's four-arm probe, the tentative run --payload-format sketch, or any YAML arm in v1.
  • Do not write a causal "serialization changes verdicts" headline, a prose-control framing, or any new verdict word.
  • Do not transfer placement/canonical-form or field-order floors to a new panel without printing that panel's own operating characteristics.
  • Building, if it ever happens, is a separate cycle, on a fresh design review of a resubmission satisfying §2 in full — and only on a BUILD verdict from that review.

docs.title: Instruction placement design (cycle 193)
docs.text:
Status: v2 — adjudicated, buildable as amended. Swarm record: the researcher verified the uniqueness claim live (HOLDS WITH NARROWING; the narrowed wording is in docs/RESEARCH_LOG.md, cycle 193, with three corrections to the wave-8 brief — the arXiv:2605.28188 instrument is few-shot exemplar segments, not a value anchor; the healthcare role-relocation result is arXiv:2601.18334, recorded in docs/RESEARCH_LOG.md's cycle-185 entry, on closed-weights hosted models (an earlier printing of this summary named the wrong ID and the wrong home; corrected in cycle 197); the framing paper's mitigation is order swaps plus majority vote, never a placement instrument). Red-team A returned DO NOT BUILD AS SPECIFIED (17 findings, 3 fatal). Red-team B cross-checked every finding with its own enumerations and probes: it refuted A's F1/F8 contradiction claim under the design's operative reading, refuted F9's seam evidence and F10's collision mechanism, and confirmed the substantive core — control populations (F2), duplicate candidate names (F7), the missing joint-collapse state (F4/F5), uncalibrated-control disclosure (F6), question duplication accounting (F9 residue), topic-mention screening (F10 residue), closed-book screen accounting (F11), and the missed cycle-44 §6 pin (F16). The nine must-fixes below are B's, adopted wholesale; the body text is amended accordingly.

  1. One falsification formula (R_d), printed verbatim in the Falsification section and in the module docstring; the ambiguous prose sentence is deleted.
  2. Sandwich control blocks are computed on the headline paired population (the control set); the decision list gains a control_set_too_small step.
  3. The stage rejects duplicate format names; _valid_placement states the unique-names clause.
  4. The headline block carries both_fail_dominant; the falsification formula and classification rule 2 account for it.
  5. The control's deliberate conservatism is disclosed with its measured acquittal rates (Falsification section).
  6. Records carry question_tokens, recompute-checked.
  7. The generator's topic and code-word pools are stem-disjoint (pinned), closing topic-mention leakage deterministically.
  8. Aggregates carry closed-book incompleteness accounting (n_screened beside a screening-incomplete count).
  9. The RESEARCH_LOG entry precedes the code (done, cycle 193).

docs.title: Utility
docs.text: A practitioner assembling prompts from a retrieved passage plus a question learns, per template family, whether putting the question before or after the payload changes verdicts on their checkpoint — and picks the layout their winning template actually rewards — instead of copying a layout convention from a blog post measured on a different model.

docs.title: What this probe is not (the boundary, in the design doc's words)
docs.text: Four neighbouring probes vary neighbouring things; none varies this one. Hierarchy varies the position of a folded privilege-marked instruction block against a user instruction. Position permutes the answer options of a multiple-choice question. Distract splices filler into a message at token doses. Needle buries a fact at measured depths inside long filler. This probe varies where the task question sits relative to a short payload inside one user turn — question-first versus payload-first — crossed with the hand-rendered template family. The payload is frozen short by design: this is placement, not dilution (distract owns dose) and not depth (needle owns long contexts). USAGE §8.46 repeats this paragraph's distinctions in the same words.

docs.title: Construction
docs.text:
Cases are generated inside the stage from the run seed by the frozen generator in placement.py (SHA-256-derived draws, the numform/needle discipline: the same seed regenerates the identical set across runs and PYTHONHASHSEED values).

Each case is a short passage plus a question:

  • A frozen topic list, one topic per case (CASE_COUNT = 24). The topic list and the code-word pool are stem-disjoint — no topic word shares a stem with a code word — so a question naming the topic cannot leak the value's word by association (red-team F10 residue; the disjointness is a property of the frozen pools, pinned by test).
  • A fact sentence from a frozen template: The {topic} inspection code is {value}. The value is a code word plus a number (word-1000..word-9999 shape), drawn per case; values are pairwise distinct across cases by the needle redraw rule (a colliding draw redraws both slots at the next counter).
  • A payload of exactly three sentences: a neutral sentence, the fact sentence, a neutral sentence. The fact sits at frozen sentence position 1 (the middle) in every case and every arm — the only thing that moves between arms is the question. The two neutral sentences are drawn per case from a frozen pool of scene sentences written for this probe (no digits, no topic words, no code words, temporally inert), distinct from each other.
  • The question from a frozen template: What is the {topic} inspection code? The expected answer is the value. The question wording is frozen byte-for-byte across arms; any per-arm "naturalness" edit would void the contrast.

docs.title: Arms
docs.text:
Four cells per (candidate, case), all a single user turn, text-level surgery pre-render, joiner "\n\n":

  • question_first: question, payload.
  • payload_first: payload, question.
  • sandwich: question, payload, question repeated verbatim. The sandwich is the control for the headline contrast: it separates "question at the end wins by recency" and "question twice wins by exposure" from a pure order effect. It is reported beside the headline, never pooled into it.
  • closed_book: the question alone, no payload. A screening arm, not a layout (see Screening).

docs.title: Screening
docs.text:
Three screens, in order:

  1. Frozen-text screen (stage-level, fail-closed). Every generated text (templates with slots emptied, topics, code words, neutral pool) is checked with audit_special_token_literals against every candidate, and every candidate's decoded boundary text is checked for containment in the generated texts (the needle pattern). A hit fails the whole stage closed with detail placement_screen_failed before any generation: a special-token literal in frozen text would forge turn structure in every cell of every run.
  2. Pool screen (construction-level). No neutral-pool sentence contains a digit, a code word, a topic string, or the fact template's carrier phrase. This is a property of the frozen pool, pinned by test; it guarantees the payload's only answer-bearing sentence is the fact sentence.
  3. Closed-book screen (per candidate, per case, derived). If a candidate's closed_book cell passes a case, the answer was reachable without the payload for that candidate — the case is excluded from that candidate's placement populations (pair blocks, arm rates, sandwich blocks). The exclusion is derived in aggregation from the closed-book cell's verdict, never a stored flag: the record carries the closed-book cell itself, and the diff validator re-derives the same exclusion when it recomputes. The screened count and the closed-book pass rate are reported per candidate, never silently dropped. A case whose closed-book cell did not complete is not screened (nothing is known), and is handled by the paired-population rules like any other incomplete cell.

docs.title: Records
docs.text:
One record per (candidate, case):

  • fixture (the case id), topic, expected_digest (SHA-256 of the expected value). No payload, question, or value text anywhere in the payload — digests and counts only.
  • arm_tokens: the rendered token length of each arm under this candidate, measured at construction. For a completed cell, the cell's own input_tokens (the evaluation's observation) must equal arm_tokens[arm]; a backend whose encode disagreed with itself surfaces as a validator rejection downstream, never a silently wrong record (the needle discipline). The equality's grounding is the tree's own contract: one id sequence per fixture, as recorded by core.evaluate() — the cell's input_tokens is read from the very encode the stage measures (red-team F3's citation, adopted).
  • question_tokens: the rendered token length of the question alone under this candidate — identical by construction to arm_tokens["closed_book"], and carried as its own field so the sandwich arm's duplicated question is accounted in the recompute-checked fields (the sandwich render contains the question twice at the text level; token counts at the seams are whatever the candidate's tokenizer does, and are recorded, not assumed).
  • cells: per arm, either a cell or None. A cell is {verdict, boundary_found, boundary_text_match, input_tokens, answer_digest} where verdict is derived: the validator recomputes it as (answer_digest == expected_digest) and boundary_found. There is no stored parsed answer to forge (the numform F3 lesson, applied by construction, as in dateline and needle).
  • cell_details: per arm, "" when the cell completed, else one of arm_context_exceeded, arm_evaluation_failed.

docs.title: Readouts
docs.text:
Per candidate, over its own records (the validator recomputes every number):

  • arms: per arm {n_completed, n_pass, rate} over live (non-screened) records; a rate is None only when its denominator is 0.
  • closed_book: {n_completed, n_pass, pass_rate} over all records — the screening yield, reported as itself.
  • n_screened: cases excluded by the closed-book screen, reported beside n_closed_book_incomplete — cases whose closed-book cell never completed, where the screen could not fire and nothing is known. A candidate with incomplete screening is visibly unscreened on those cases, never silently treated as screened (red-team F11).
  • The headline pair block (question_first vs payload_first) over the paired population — live cases where both cells completed: n_paired, n_qf_only, n_pf_only, n_both, n_neither, per-arm pass rates over the paired population, the exact McNemar p (diagnostic only), both_fail_dominant (true iff n_neither >= max(n_qf_only, n_pf_only) and n_neither >= MIN_DISCORDANT: the joint-collapse state, where both layouts fail the same cases and a discordance label alone would hide it), and a classification (below).
  • Two sandwich pair blocks (sandwich vs payload_first, sandwich vs question_first), computed on the control set: the headline paired population further restricted to cases whose sandwich cell also completed. The control is compared against the headline on the same cases or it is not a control (red-team F2, confirmed by B with a worked example where the unrestricted control flipped the falsification verdict). The headline block's rates stay over its own paired population.
  • control_level: the larger discordant total (n_a_only + n_b_only) of the two sandwich blocks, or None when the control set is empty. n_control reports the control set's size.

docs.title: Classification (total function)
docs.text:
Floors frozen at the leading/dateline values: MIN_PAIRED_EVALUABLE = 6, MIN_DISCORDANT = 2. The floors gate this label only, never a reported count or rate. Decision list, first match wins, over the headline block with d = n_qf_only + n_pf_only and J = both_fail_dominant:

  1. n_paired < 6 → insufficient
  2. d == 0 and not J → no_discordance_observed
  3. n_control < 6 → control_set_too_small
  4. control_level is None → control_unavailable
  5. d <= control_level → within_sandwich_control
  6. n_qf_only == n_pf_only and n_qf_only >= 2 → discordant_balanced
  7. max(n_qf_only, n_pf_only) >= 2 → discordant_asymmetric
  8. otherwise → below_threshold

docs.title: Falsification
docs.text:
There is exactly one definition, and this is it (the same formula is printed in the placement.py module docstring; any other sentence in this document is commentary on it, not a second definition):

placement_effect_falsified is true iff n_paired >= 6 and not J and (d == 0 or (n_control >= 6 and control_level is not None and d <= control_level)).

Reading: the falsified condition and the classification are two views of one condition, with joint collapse as the one stated exception. Absent joint collapse, falsified holds exactly when the classification is no_discordance_observed or within_sandwich_control at a sufficient population (the control-set steps in between report why a non-falsified candidate could not be acquitted: no usable control). Under joint collapse the two views part: a candidate whose discordance sits at or below a usable control level is still classified within_sandwich_control while the formula returns false. Zero discordance falsifies with or without a control; joint collapse (J) never falsifies — a candidate failing the same cases under both layouts has a capability story, not an acquittal. The shipped enumeration test pins the equivalence in this joint-collapse-qualified form. Discordance above the control level with a one-sided split is the only outcome that supports a directional placement claim, and even then the claim is a verdict-flip count on generated fixtures, not a recommendation (the utility sentence says the practitioner picks the layout their template rewards — on their own fixtures, with this instrument as the template-axis evidence).

The control is deliberately conservative, and the design says so with numbers (red-team F6, confirmed as a disclosure obligation, not a redesign): the falsification bar sits at control_level + 1 discordant pairs, where control_level is the maximum of two sandwich discordant counts. Under a symmetric-noise null at n = 24 paired cases, a max-based bar acquits 88.2% of the time at a true flip probability of 0.10, 69.2% at 0.15, and 15.6% at 0.25 (red-team A's enumeration, reproduced by B). A supported directional claim must clear a high bar; the price is that weak real effects are acquitted, and the readout reports the counts so a reader can apply a different bar. One mechanism note: the sandwich arm shares the duplicated question with question_first, so its discordance against payload_first partly tracks the headline pair's — another reason the max is a bar, not an estimate.

docs.title: Conditions (per-arm selection)
docs.text: For each layout arm (question_first, payload_first, sandwich — the closed-book arm is a screen, not a layout, and gets no selection readout), the conservative selection rule is re-applied over the arm's completed cases restricted to the shared live population: cases recorded for every candidate and screened for none of them. The readout is withheld with detail selection_withheld_mismatched_sets when the restricted completed sets differ across candidates or are empty (the needle rule). Each arm's flip compares its selection to the payload_first selection recomputed on the same restricted completed set (the conventional layout is the baseline); the baseline arm's own flip is False when not withheld, and a flip is None when either side is withheld.

docs.title: Diff validator
