docs.text: diff_placement in diffreports.py, full-recompute standard (the wave-7 F6 settlement): _placement_recompute carries its own generator mirror (its own derive function, templates, topic list, and neutral pool as literals — no imports from placement.py), regenerates the case set from the protocol's seed, and compares every record's construction against it (fixture id set, topic, expected digest). The protocol is rebuilt from frozen scalars plus the payload's seed and backend fingerprint and its fingerprint recomputed. Every cell's verdict is re-derived from its digest and boundary flag; every completed cell's input_tokens must equal the record's arm_tokens; cells and details must be consistent (a cell is present iff its detail is ""). Every aggregate, pair block, control level, classification, falsification flag, and the conditions are recomputed by mirror code and compared exactly. A one-break-at-a-time battery pins every reject branch.

docs.title: Budget
docs.text: Worst case: 24 candidates (the run cap) × 24 cases × 4 arms = 2,304 generations, stated in the CLI help with the forwards formula before the run (each generation is one greedy decode of at most --max-new-tokens tokens over a short rendered prompt; the payload is three sentences by construction). The stage threads the run's cancel event end-to-end and checks it before and after every evaluation (the multiturn rule: a cancel observed during a generation is never mislabelled an evaluation failure). MAX_GROUND_RECORDS = 576, MAX_RECORDS_BYTES = 12 MiB (the house bound).

docs.title: Pin blast radius
docs.text:
• New pure module placement.py → the test_cycle44 mypy source-file pin moves 55 → 56 in the same push, and test_cycle44's enumeration of the VALIDATION Evidence section's first-paragraph probe list (pinned verbatim) gains the placement entry — VALIDATION's own text moves with it (red-team F16: this pin was missing from the v1 list; the n_positions name nearby in experiments.py is an unrelated local, a red herring). Correction (cycle 203): the original text of this bullet called that list "VALIDATION §6" — no §6 exists in VALIDATION.md; the cycle-203 red-team traced the phantom to this bullet and it is corrected here, at its source.
  • New --placement flag → the cycle-179 parametrized dispatch table (27 stage rows → 28, plus its probe-wrapper audit list, 19 → 20), the cycle-31/64/84 subcommand/flag audits, and the args-Namespace contract gain a case.
  • New diff section placement → test_cycle67's three elements (fuzz oracle + _fuzz_placement_section; the flip-identical gate anchor's original and mutant texts; _identical_expected's key set) plus test_cycle27's oracle stub entry "placement": {"available": ..., "changed": False}.
  • README Capabilities bullet + measured test count; VALIDATION counts and the CI-scope ruff file count; CHANGELOG entry; USAGE §8.46 (the boundary paragraph in the same words as above) and the §6/§12 inventories if they enumerate run stages; RESEARCH_LOG uniqueness entry (after the researcher's live verification lands).
  • The sample report gains nothing: a section renders only when the run recorded its stage, so sample artifacts stay byte-identical (pinned by the existing sample tests).

docs.title: Adjudicated open points (from the v1 draft)
docs.text:
1. New classification labels (within_sandwich_control, control_unavailable, and v2's control_set_too_small): kept. §4's honesty vocabulary governs fail-closed detail words; classification vocabularies are per-probe (dateline's five labels are its own). The three labels name states no existing label names without conflation.
  2. Union screening for conditions: kept, and pinned by a cross-candidate conditions test. The per-candidate blocks use per-candidate screening because they are per-candidate measurements; the conditions readout compares candidates, so its population must be one set — a case any candidate answered closed-book is not a clean shared measurement.
  3. Control populations: resolved by must-fix 2 — the control is computed on the headline paired population.
  4. arm_tokens equality as a false-reject surface: the grounding is the tree's own scoring contract (one id sequence per fixture — the recorded observation in core.evaluate(), with scoring.py's alignment check failing closed on encode inconsistency), the same grounding needle already ships. A backend whose encode is non-deterministic within a run violates that contract everywhere, not just here; the rejection is the instrument working.
  5. Duplicate candidate names (red-team F7, mechanism corrected by B): the stage raises ValueError("formats must have unique names") on duplicate format names — the placement stage's own guard, at its own boundary — and _valid_placement carries the unique-names clause. A two-same-named-formats test pins it. (The shipped needle stage keys candidates by name in a dict; placement states the precondition instead of inheriting the silence.)

docs.title: Load-precision × template (run --precision) — design
docs.text: Cycle 198 (wave-8 rank #7). This document is the shipped contract. It folds the wave-8 research brief (docs/RESEARCH_LOG.md, wave-8 round), the cycle-198 researcher pass, red-team A's nine amendments (A1–A9), red-team B's nine amendments (B1–B9), and a verifier pass that confirmed all ten load-bearing factual claims the two red teams made about this tree. Where the brief and the shipped contract differ, this document wins, and the differences are the amendments.

docs.title: What this is, honestly framed
docs.text:
--precision is a new condition arm of the lab's established second-condition selection-survival pattern (transfer, token-healing, perturbation, placement, …), not a new instrument. What is new is the condition itself — the load dtype of identical weights — which is the first weights-representation condition in the lab (every prior condition varied checkpoint, prompt, fixtures, decoding, or batch composition), and the one-run packaging: paired per-fixture verdict flips, an output-divergence readout, teacher-forced logprob deltas, and selection re-application under the second condition, all fail-closed diff-validated.

Monday-morning utility: a practitioner who will serve the checkpoint in bf16 learns, before deploying, whether the template winner the lab selected under its fp32 measurement is still the winner when the same weights are loaded in bf16 — and gets the per-fixture flip list if it is not.

It measures dtype precision, not quantization. The words "precision" and "quantization" are not interchangeable anywhere in the CLI help, this document, or USAGE: the bf16 arm is a load-time cast of the same unquantized safetensors assets, and the backend's existing quantization_config rejection is untouched, which is what structurally keeps the two apart.

docs.title: Prior art and the scoped uniqueness claim
docs.text:
No surveyed tool or study crosses load precision with a candidate set of hand-rendered template families and asks whether the selection survives. The neighbours, named so a reviewer does not have to discover them:

  • Yuan et al., "Give Me FP32 or Give Me Death?" (arXiv:2506.09501): bf16 numerics demonstrably flip greedy outputs (up to 9% accuracy spread) when GPU count/type/batch size vary under bf16. Runtime configuration is the variable; no rendering, no selection. It is this probe's motivation, not its answer.
  • Du et al., "Greedy Decoding Is Not Precision-Invariant" (arXiv:2609.26621): BF16-vs-FP16 output divergence is large (49–100% of prompts); prompt format appears only as a one-model robustness control for an inference intervention. No candidate set, no selection rule, no winner survival.
  • Szalontai et al., HumanEvalFix reproducibility study (Software 2025, 4, 17): precision moves aggregate scores little (bf16→fp32 mean shift −2.19%/+1.01%; greedy-baseline SD across precision/quantization settings 1.49), and the paper's own conclusion is that precision is a minor factor for aggregate results. Cited with that conclusion attached: an aggregate mean cannot see per-candidate flips that cancel, and the study never crosses precision with template or asks about a selection. That gap is the probe's justification.
  • Zheng et al., Qwen3 PTQ study (arXiv:2505.02214): model quality under post-training quantization. Out of scope by construction; it is what this feature will be mis-cited as replicating, hence the disclaimer discipline above.
  • A practitioner blog's remark that computing log-softmax in bf16 "loses enough precision to flip close choices" is a folk claim about scoring-compute precision, with no experiment behind it; the lab's scoring path already upcasts logits to fp32 and accumulates in float64, so the sentence does not describe this pipeline's mechanism and is not cited as evidence anywhere in the shipped docs. In a bf16 load, the precision loss occurs in the model's forward pass (weights and activations), not in a bf16 softmax.

docs.title: The measurement
docs.text:
Arms. The fp32 arm is the recorded native run — never re-executed. The bf16 arm is one additional search-split evaluation of every candidate under a second LocalHFBackend instance loaded with dtype="bfloat16" from the same checkpoint directory. The primary backend is always fp32: --precision adds an arm; it never replaces the primary, never writes result["decision"] or result["selected_candidate"], and never affects the exit code.

Native gate (A1). The stage runs only when the native search is complete: the choice-audit wrapper gate is adopted verbatim — decision in {failed, cancelled} or len(search) != len(formats) yields {"available": False, "detail": "native_search_incomplete"} with zero forwards. Per candidate, native outcomes come from native_search_outcomes; a candidate whose native report is not aggregate-eligible has passed=None and is excluded from every cell, named in the payload's unavailable list.

Forwarding set (A2). The bf16 instance and stage receive exactly: the same checkpoint path, device=args.device, max_context=args.max_context, max_new_tokens=args.max_new_tokens, seed=args.seed, the same formats tuple, tuple(split.search) as the fixture set, and boundary=args.boundary_ids and boundary_map=boundary_map. The bf16 instance is constructed only in the stage phase, after run_experiment has returned; the top-level backend_fingerprint is never overwritten. Any omission silently compares two different measurements, which is the one failure this lab exists not to produce. EOS needs no forwarding: evaluate never passes an EOS to generate.

Dtype integrity (A3/A4/B4). LocalHFBackend gains a keyword-only dtype parameter restricted to {"float32", "bfloat16"}; anything else (including "float16" and "auto") fails through the existing constructor wrapper as RuntimeError("local_backend_initialization_failed"). Only the dtype= argument value changes in the from_pretrained call; every other kwarg is byte-identical, so the SECURITY.md loading invariants stand (their AST pins scan kwarg structure, not the dtype value — stated here so nobody overclaims what they pin). The identity dict's dtype entry takes its literal from the constructor parameter — exactly "float32" or "bfloat16", never str(torch.dtype) and never the loaded config (executed fact: after a bf16 load the config object still reports float32; deriving the identity from config would collide the two arms' fingerprints). After load, the constructor asserts the model's actual parameter dtype equals the requested dtype and fails closed otherwise; the backend exposes the verified dtype. The bf16 arm is an unconditional load-time cast of the same assets, regardless of storage dtype — there is no config-permission gate. The payload records the checkpoint's declared dtype (both the dtype and torch_dtype config keys, as found) and both arms' verified dtypes, and scopes its wording as load/compute precision: a checkpoint stored in bf16 loads today as fp32 compute over bf16-stored weights, and the report says so when that is the case.

Native-dtype pin (B5). The payload records native_dtype from the primary backend's verified dtype, and the stage is unavailable when it is not "float32" — the reuse argument is an executable check, not a design-doc paragraph. A pin test holds the default path's fingerprint byte-identical: LocalHFBackend(root) == LocalHFBackend(root, dtype="float32") != LocalHFBackend(root, dtype="bfloat16").

Stage shape (A5/B2). The stage is healing-shaped, not a transfer_stage reuse: per candidate it returns {"passed": bool | None, "per_fixture": {fixture_id: bool}, "n_passed", "n_total"} for the bf16 arm, with passed=None and empty per_fixture on any non-aggregate-eligible report. Pairing is by fixture ID against native_search_outcomes, never by list position.

docs.title: The readouts
docs.text:
Flip matrix (A5/A6). Per candidate, over fixtures completed in both arms: the four paired cells (pass/pass, pass/fail, fail/pass, fail/fail) with n_paired beside them, plus n_fp32_only and n_bf16_only, plus a separate unpaired list (candidate, fixture, arm) — a fixture an arm never reached is unpaired, never an arm-failure. The flip list proper contains only true paired flips, sorted by (candidate, fixture), each with its direction. Rates are None at n_paired == 0, never a division (a NaN would crash the report write itself: results serialise with allow_nan=False).

Output divergence (B3). Per paired fixture, the stage also records whether the bf16 generation's token IDs diverge from the native generation's (determinism.compare_token_ids semantics), the first-divergence index, and both generations' output digests. This is the sensitive leading indicator; verdict flips are the lagging one. Per-candidate and overall divergence counts ride beside the flip matrix with their denominators.

Logprob deltas (B3). Per paired fixture, the teacher-forced logprob of the expected answer under each arm (scoring.score_target_logprobs, float64 accumulation, recorded from reported values), and their delta (bf16 − fp32). The fp32 values are computed on the native backend during the same run — one forward per candidate × fixture, the cost class the lab already accepts for the opt-in logprob diagnostic. Per-candidate mean delta and the min/max fixture deltas are derived by the validator from the recorded per-fixture values, never trusted from the producer.

Winner survival (A6). Defined only when the primary decision is winner-bearing (compatible_on_fixture_set / held_out_failed with a selected candidate, the _valid_primary_pair vocabulary). The comparison re-applies the selection rule to both arms over their shared paired population (the placement precedent) and compares (decision, winner) tuples — fp32 selected W vs bf16 ambiguous is a survival failure a winner-only comparison would miss. The bf16 arm's decision uses the existing vocabulary {selected, ambiguous, no_candidate, unavailable}. Survival is withheld — reported as unavailable with its fixed detail — on any per-candidate cross-arm completed-set mismatch, on a non-winner-bearing primary, on bf16 unavailability, and at n_paired == 0.

Falsification, scoped (B3). Zero verdict flips across all candidates falsifies a precision effect on the search split, at the verdict level, in a single bf16 run compared against the recorded fp32 run, for this checkpoint and fixture set — and the readout's sensitivity is conditioned on the pass base rate: on a fixture set where no candidate passes in either arm (the random-weight tiny checkpoint is exactly that), zero flips is guaranteed by the floor effect, not earned by precision robustness, and the divergence/logprob readouts are the informative ones there. The falsification readout is None over zero paired cells. Two things are not claimable and the docs must not claim them: a per-step top1–top2 margin ("short margin to the runner-up token") is not observable post-hoc — core.Observation records no logits or margins and generate() discards each step's logits after argmax — and no causal attribution of any single flip. Held-out behaviour under bf16 is never measured by this probe.

Operator action (B7). The fp32 selection stands as the run's decision. A non-surviving winner means: do not serve this winner in bf16 on this evidence. The bf16 arm's winner is a search-split readout, not a selection; it carries no held-out evidence, and there is no supported primary-bf16 re-run — USAGE says all of this in plain words.

docs.title: Payload and diff validation (A7/B6)
docs.text:
The precision section carries digest-bound ground records for both arms: per candidate × fixture, {verdict, boundary_found, answer_digest} per arm in the placement-cell style, with verdict == (answer_digest == expected_digest) and boundary_found re-derivable by the validator and expected_digest computed from the fixture's expected answer with the tree's surrogatepass-safe digest. Digests only — never answer text: stage payloads pass verbatim into the default results.json. Divergence records carry both output digests, never raw token IDs beyond the first-divergence index. A protocol object binds: version, seed, max_new_tokens, per-candidate boundary token IDs, the fixture-set SHA-256 over the search fixture IDs in split order, candidate names, both backend fingerprints, the declared config dtype, and both verified arm dtypes; the validator requires bf16_fingerprint != fp32_fingerprint and the payload's context fingerprint equal to the fp32 arm's. The diff validator recomputes everything derived — matrix cells and denominators, flip list (exact set and order), divergence counts, logprob deltas and their summaries, per-candidate verdicts, both paired-population selections, the survival flag, the falsification readout — compared type-strictly (_recomputed_equal), under records caps before any recompute loop (legal max 24 candidates × 100 fixtures). Protocol or fingerprint drift surfaces as precision_backend_drift and not comparable, while the section is still listed (the placement drift pattern). Honest ceiling, stated plainly: user-fixture expected answers cannot be regenerated by the validator, so the ground cells are attested at the digest binding — the same residue _valid_primary_pair documents for the primary pair. Where the same results.json carries search observations (evidence mode), the validator additionally cross-checks the fp32 ground cells against them.

Determinism scope (B6). A --precision results.json still verifies under verify --determinism because the primary fingerprint is the fp32 one; the certificate covers the native fp32 search observations only — the bf16 arm's observations are never re-executed — and the precision section and USAGE both say so.

docs.title: Cost (A8/B8)
docs.text: --precision adds: a second full search evaluation, a second full checkpoint load (asset re-hashing included), and both models resident at once (≈1.5× the fp32 weight footprint plus activations). Measured in this lab's sandbox, bf16 generation on CPU ran up to ~6× slower than fp32 on the toy checkpoints — on CPU the stage can dominate run time; on CUDA bf16 is the serving-fast path (untestable here, per VALIDATION). The help text says this, replacing any "reuse halves the cost" framing: reuse is a saving relative to running both arms fresh, not relative to the status quo. The stage threads the run's cancel event into its evaluate calls inside an except Exception → precision_unavailable wrapper; the remaining SIGINT exposure of the whole stage phase (signal handlers are restored before it) is inherited from transfer and is named here rather than inherited silently.

docs.title: Guards and failure vocabulary
docs.text: The stage uses generate/evaluate only — the paths whose non-finite guards are verified: generate checks torch.isfinite(logits) before argmax and returns invalid_next_token_logits, which evaluate collapses to the fixed backend_reported_error; the candidate degrades to None. A forced-non-finite bf16 test pins this (the tiny checkpoints do not exhibit bf16-only non-finites under deliberate attack — LayerNorm/RMSNorm shield the residual stream — so the pin is a mocked-forward requirement, not a tiny-checkpoint claim). Stage-level failure uses the tree's fail-closed shape {"available": False, "detail": "precision_unavailable"} or the specific fixed details above; no new verdict words are invented.

docs.title: Tests
docs.text:
• Backend: fingerprint pins (default == explicit fp32, != bf16); dtype rejection ("float16", "auto", non-string) through the constructor wrapper; post-load param-dtype assertion; declared-dtype recording for both config keys; bf16 load/generate on the tiny GPT-2 and Llama checkpoints; forced-non-finite bf16 → candidate None.
  • Stage/payload: scripted factory fakes (the transfer/healing test pattern) exercise real flips, divergence, survival and non-survival, withheld paths, the native gate, and unpaired denominators. The tiny-checkpoint e2e asserts only availability and the degenerate matrix (no passes in either arm) — no doc cites it as sensitivity evidence.
  • Invariant: a --precision run's top-level fingerprint, decision, selected candidate, and exit code equal the same run without the flag.
  • Validator: the full hostile battery at the tree's standard — one broken identity at a time across every derived field, fingerprint-equality forgery, drift-as-incomparable, caps.
  • Blast-radius pins, updated in the same change: the new pure module moves the test_cycle44 source-file pin (57 → 58); CLI audits (cycle 31/64/84), the args-Namespace contract, the cycle-179 dispatch e2e, README/VALIDATION counts (measured); the fp32-as-absolute statements at backends.py's class docstring, docs/USAGE.md, and README.md are scoped to the primary/default measurement in the same change (cycle-172 lesson). No doctor plumbing: doctor never constructs a backend.

docs.title: Interior content-token loss (--prune-sweep) — design round (ADJUDICATED: NO-BUILD)
Round summary (coordinator #45, design round only — nothing built)
docs.text:
Wave-11 slate rank 4: interior content-token loss (tentatively run --prune-sweep). The candidate sketch (~/workspace/agents_out/wave11/slate_candidates.md Candidate 4): drop a seeded fraction of the content tokens of the last user message (template skeleton untouched) at doses 10% / 25% / 50%, seeded per fixture, and report the first-flip dose per candidate — the dose at which any candidate's pass set changes on the common completed set — as a truncation-budget readout, worst case 3 doses × 100 fixtures × 24 candidates = 7,200 generations.

  • Tree at main a6705d1b9607 (cycle 213 closed green, 8,442 tests, precise coverage 95.3455%). This round was READ-ONLY except for this doc and the briefs; no suite was run, no push was made, no tag was cut.
  • Specialists (blind to each other): researcher (~/workspace/agents_out/prunesweep/research.md), red-team A (redteam_a.md), red-team B (redteam_b.md), verifier (verifier.md). All four briefs landed; the verifier waited for all three briefs to stabilise, mechanically resolved every citation, checked every external source at primary, and re-executed every load-bearing PoC with its own scripts; the coordinator re-executed the load-bearing claims itself (§4). Fabrication sweep: clean — a fifth consecutive round. No invented symbol, paper, or count in any brief; the errors found were four substance-true line drifts in the researcher's citations and one labelling imprecision in red-team A's survival Monte Carlo (its fatal is stronger, not weaker, once corrected), all handled in §5.
  • Convergence: unanimous NO-BUILD for the sketch as specified — researcher, both blind red teams, and the verifier each reached it independently, fatal by fatal, by execution. The two red teams, working blind, converged on the same core defects (evidence destruction, unfrozen policy, grammaticality collapse, the noise-firing falsifier) with independently executed numbers that agree (perfect-reader pass rates 0.86–0.89 / 0.74–0.75 / 0.49–0.50 at 10% / 25% / 50%).
  • The researcher additionally specifies a complete redesigned instrument (generated panel, word-level doses over a protected passage, nested draws, a derived decision rule). The verifier reproduced its decision math exactly and ruled it a resubmission, not an amendment, under this program's own test — the unit, the population, and the readout all change — and the researcher himself classifies it the same way. The coordinator concurs: the verdict is NO-BUILD — for the sketch, and as a build order for the redesigned instrument in this round. §3 records the resubmission candidate in full, including the two points no brief fully closed (the answer-protection utility wound, the absent length-held-constant arm).

docs.title: 1. Why NO-BUILD: the fatal defects of the candidate as specified
docs.text: Each defect below is individually blocking and was established by execution (attribution: R = researcher, A = red-team A, B = red-team B, V = verifier, C = coordinator).

docs.title: F1 — Evidence destruction: the dose-response is answer-survival arithmetic, not robustness
docs.text: The sketch holds expected fixed while pruning deletes the tokens the expected answer is derived from, with no solvability or redundancy screen. A perfect-reader stub through the real core.evaluate passes at exactly the closed-form survival probability of its evidence: 1−k/n for k evidence tokens among n — executed at 0.86/0.75/0.49 (A) and 0.890/0.740/0.485 (B) at 10/25/50% for single-token evidence, rising to 1.000/0.995/0.910 when the same evidence is merely repeated 3×. A prompt-ignoring stub passes all doses. The headline curve therefore measures fixture redundancy, not template robustness: two fixtures with identical templates and different evidence redundancy produce different "first-flip doses" with no template property involved. (A F1, B F1, V upheld, C re-executed: survival = 1−dose to three decimals at n=20 and n=100.)

docs.title: F2 — The pruning policy is an unfrozen second treatment riding on the dose
docs.text: Which tokens are removed is not specified: policy, seed derivation, dose-rounding, and nesting are all unfrozen, and they are not cosmetic. At one fixed dose (drop 5 of 18 words), three honest policies give opposite verdicts — uniform-random broke the "code is" context around a surviving answer while function-word removal passed (A F2, executed). The two red teams themselves, instructed only by the sketch, chose different roundings — the sketch does not determine its own instrument. Rounding is load-bearing at the shipped scale: floor(10%) of every shipped fixture's last user message is 0 tokens (C re-executed on examples/fixtures.json: spans of 7, 8, 5, and 8 words), so the 10% arm is ids-identical filler on the entire shipped population, while ceil-rounding silently turns "10%" into 12.5–14.3%. Non-nested draws additionally make the sketch's own flip-back clause ("a verdict that flips at 25% and flips back at 50% is noise") incoherent: with independent draws per dose there is no fact of the matter about which draw a return belongs to. (A F2, B F2, V upheld.)

docs.title: F3 — Grammaticality and semantics collapse: the construct is not "loss"
docs.text: Pruned text is not shorter text; it is broken text, and the breakage is not dose-monotone in any single construct. Single-token deletions invert ground truth while expected stays frozen — "is not locked" → "is locked", "Ana, not to Ben" → "Ana, to Ben" (A F3, B F5, executed) — at doses as low as one token (~7% of a 14-word span). A numeral drop deletes the answer inside otherwise fluent text; a filler drop is harmless. The sketch pools three different events — evidence loss, meaning inversion, and harmless noise — under one "content loss" headline with no decomposition, so the construct it measures is robustness-to-ungrammaticality-and- inversion, not robustness-to-loss. On the tree's own fixtures the "content span" is an instruction sentence (F7), so the same instrument would measure instruction mutilation there and document loss elsewhere, pooled. (A F3, B F5, V upheld.)

docs.title: F4 — No decision rule: the first-flip falsifier fires on noise with P = 1.000
docs.text: The sketch's falsifier — "the first dose at which any candidate's pass set changes" — is the any-difference rule this program has already killed twice (directive F2, instruction-distance). Over the sketch's own 7,200-cell panel it fires with P=1.000 at per-cell jitter ε ≥ 0.001 (A: 2000/2000 trials at ε ≥ 0.005; B: conditioned selection-flip 0.778–0.998; C re-executed: 300/300 at each of ε = 0.001, 0.005, 0.01, analytic 1−(1−ε)^7200 = 0.9993 at ε=0.001). The selection half is a one-cell tripwire. The falsifier is also shape-blind and self-contradictory: decay, threshold, single-dip, U/recovery, and improvement all return the identical headline "FALSIFIED", while the sketch's own text says a flip-and-return "is noise, counted as such" — a clause the headline cannot express. Borrowed sibling floors fire ≈1.000 at this panel's N=100 (B, executed). The common-completed set the headline conditions on is post-treatment in both directions, with no attrition reporting. (A F4, B F4, V upheld.)

docs.title: F5 — The "sweep" headline is permutation-invariant, and one deletion bundles four channels
docs.text: A first-flip dose is invariant to permuting the dose order: graded decay, a threshold cliff, a single dip, and a U all return the same number, so the word "sweep" promises a shape the readout cannot distinguish (A F5, executed; the instruction-distance F5 settlement). Separately, one interior deletion simultaneously removes information, shortens the prompt, shifts every downstream token's position, and breaks syntax — four channels, one number, no length-matched (pad / sham / placeholder) control to separate them, and no such control exists anywhere in the sketch. The claim names one cause ("loss fraction"); the treatment delivers a bundle. (A F5, B F6 in part, V upheld.)

docs.title: F6 — The dose unit is unexecutable as specified: token fractions are per-checkpoint, and there is no frozen tokenizer
docs.text: Doses are stated as fractions of content tokens, but the tree has no per-candidate frozen tokenizer (the instruction-language fertility settlement: no unexecuted token figures may be printed). The same nominal 25% dose deletes different text under different tokenizers — word-level: clean whole words; character-level: the answer 4821 → 421 (A F6, executed). A "10% dose" is therefore not one treatment across the 24-candidate panel; it is 24 different treatments sharing a label, and any cross-candidate comparison of first-flip doses compares unlike quantities. (A F6, V upheld.)

docs.title: F7 — The population is undefined, and empty on the shipped fixtures under any honest floor
docs.text: The sketch says "100 fixtures" without stating the population or the split scope. On the only population the tree ships, the last user messages are 5–8-word instructions that contain the expected answer itself ("Reply with exactly BLUE…", "Return only the numeral 7.") — not the long documents of the utility paragraph. C re-executed: all four shipped cases (search 2, held-out 2) have last-user spans of 5–8 words; floor(10%) = 0 on all four; any span floor ≥ 9 words — the minimum at which a 10% dose is even one token with margin — makes the evaluable share 0/2 search fixtures. The utility population (long pasted documents, support tickets) is a different population, owned in-tree by the needle/distraction family's generated corpora, and importing it is a new instrument, not a reading of the sketch. The copied token-depth pattern also drags in treated held-out winner evaluation, which the sketch never scopes. (A F8, B F2/F7, V upheld.)

docs.title: F8 — The span machinery does not exist for this use, pruned id sequences are non-canonical, and the build surface is misstated
docs.text: The sketch's span location rests on the behavioural template probe's differencing, but templateprobe.find_span (templateprobe.py:283) resolves a span only between sentinels the probe itself inserted into synthetic probe content; on real fixture renders it returns None for every fixture × family (R S1, B F3, V and C verified: the function counts sentinel occurrences and returns None when either does not occur exactly once). No tree function maps a message's character span to a token-id span in an arbitrary render. The substrate is worse than unlocated: a seam token ('\nR', executed with a merging tokenizer) is simultaneously skeleton and content, so no id interval equals the content span and "skeleton untouched" is unachievable in id space; and pruned id sequences are the tokenisation of no text (decode→re-encode ≠ pruned ids, executed by A, B, and V) — prompts no truncation tool emits, with the sketch's defence being disclosure of the artefact share, not removal of the artefact. The cited wrapper beside backends.py:811 exposes encode(text) only and cannot locate a last-user span from text alone; delivery would need a plan-keyed surface. The sketch's "M–L, a copy of the token-depth pattern" understates the build surface on every axis. (R S1, A F9, B F3, V upheld.)

docs.title: F9 — No frozen fail-closed vocabulary, decomposition, or attrition discipline
docs.text: The sketch freezes no vocabulary for span failure, seam straddling, non-canonical renders, zero-eligible populations, or per-dose attrition; no answer-decomposition (the negation settlement's digest-derived classes); no paired-subset seed discipline; no native-digest binding. Every one of these is a place a build would have to invent verdict words, which the program forbids. Verified by reading the full slate text (B F7, V). (A F10, B F7, V upheld.)

docs.title: Partially upheld — duplication and utility (A F7, B F6)
docs.text: Not a standalone fatal, recorded because it kills the sketch's novelty paragraph: the instrument's shape — a dose ladder over prompt ids with a first-flip headline — is the token-depth sweep's (experiments.py:3621, backends.py:810), and the production operations the utility paragraph names (tail cuts, character caps) are already shipped as prompt_token_depth_sweep / prompt_sensitivity_sweep with the same first-flip headline. Text-level interior deletion also already ships (perturbation punctuation_strip, surface-noise). What is genuinely unshipped is only the residue: dose-graded interior deletion itself. On documents, uniform pruning is furthermore distraction run in reverse — ~90% of drops hit filler (A, executed). A resubmission must argue its utility against the shipped tail-cut sweeps, naming the real operation interior deletion models; the sketch does not.

docs.title: 2. Amendment or resubmission?
docs.text: The settlement from the rank-2/rank-4 rounds applies: an amendment corrects named defects of the same frozen instrument (same population, unit, arms, scorer, and readout shape); a redesign that changes the population, the unit, or the headline readout is a resubmission candidate requiring a fresh blind design review, not a build order. The researcher's redesign changes all three — population (shipped fixtures → generated 24-case panel), unit (token fraction of an id span → word count over a protected passage, delivered by fixture surgery), and readout (first-flip dose → a derived McNemar-gated classification with descriptive shape) — and additionally protects the answer-bearing sentence, which changes the treatment itself. It is therefore recorded in §3 as a resubmission candidate only. No build cycle may act on it without a fresh design round.

docs.title: 3. The resubmission candidate (recorded, NOT a build order)
docs.text:
The researcher's redesigned instrument (research.md §3–§10), verifier-checked (decision math reproduced exactly; PoC2 population invariants and PoC3 scorer path re-run clean):

  • Population. A generated, stage-local panel of 24 cases. Each case is a single user message: a frozen instruction + a 17-sentence passage + a frozen question. Split hygiene and generator mirroring follow the tree's generated-panel precedents.
  • Pruned unit and protection. The eligible set is all 144 words of the 16 context sentences (16×9, construction- asserted). The answer-bearing fact sentence (fixed position 9 of 17), the instruction, and the question are never pruned — this is what makes the instrument sound (F1/F3 cannot fire by construction) and simultaneously its principal wound (below).
  • Dose ladder and operator. Doses 0 / 18 / 36 / 72 words (0 / 12.5 / 25 / 50% of the eligible set), nested via one sha256-ordered permutation per case, so first-flip and returns are well-defined (curing F2's incoherence). The dose unit is words — executable and validator-mirrorable with no frozen tokenizer; rendered-token deltas are reported per candidate via backend.encode (id_length_delta), never asserted and never gated (the F6 settlement). Delivery is fixture surgery (the perturbation.py precedent): no backend wrapper, no span location, no id surgery — F8's machinery is never needed.
  • Controls. tail72, a dose-matched displaced control (descriptive only), and a closed_book screen arm (the placement pattern).
  • Scorer. core.evaluate byte-exact + boundary, unchanged. Decomposition (exact_pass / wrong_value / non_value) derived from answer digests only.
  • Decision rule (derived, never borrowed). Per candidate: C ≥ 12, A ≥ 5, two-sided McNemar (confidentiality.py:293) p < 0.05 → prune_drop_observed, else below_threshold / insufficient in the frozen fail-closed vocabulary. 40,000- trial Monte Carlo: 0 fires on random, competent, and jitter nulls; power 0.40 at a 25% top-dose drop, 0.96 at 50% — printed in the brief as weak-evidence labelling for below_threshold, not hidden.
  • Shape. A descriptive readout, not a gate — with executed proof: a returns-cap collapses graded-drop power 0.960 → 0.031 and intermediate-support collapses threshold-drop power 0.960 → 0.000, so any shape gate makes a real shape invisible (curing F5 by declining to gate what cannot be distinguished honestly).
  • No winner readout (the numform settlement — generated panel). Counts: 2,304 headline generations, 3,456 legal max.
  • Claim, scoped to the treatment actually delivered: robustness to collateral word loss in non-answer-bearing context, per template family — never "truncation budget" in general.

What the fresh review must settle head-on (no brief closed these):

  1. The answer-protection utility wound. Protection empties the scariest cell by construction: the instrument measures robustness to collateral loss only and cannot detect a trim that deletes the answer itself — which is what production trimmers actually risk. The researcher's defence (the unprotected version manufactures unanswerable cases and pools three treatments — F1/F3) is a judgment, not an execution. The fresh review must decide whether the surviving utility (a collateral-loss curve per family) justifies a probe at all.
  2. No length-held-constant arm. The redesign has a dose-matched displaced control but no placeholder / sham arm holding prompt length constant, so the shorter-prompt channel of F5's bundle is disclosed, not separated. Red-team B's resubmission conditions require one.
  3. Red-team B's remaining conditions, in full: per-dose printed grammaticality / negation / numeral shares of the dropped set; per-dose attrition reporting; search-only scope stated; the utility paragraph argued against the shipped tail-cut sweeps (F-partial).

docs.title: 4. Coordinator re-verification (own execution, 2026-10-27)
docs.text:
• Shipped population (F2/F7): read examples/fixtures.json directly — 4 cases; last-user spans 7 (search-copy-blue), 8 (search-latest-green), 5 (held-number), 8 (held-latest-word) words; floor(10%) = 0 on all four.
  • Span machinery (F8): templateprobe.py:283 find_span counts left/right sentinel occurrences in the render and returns None unless each occurs exactly once — sentinel- dependent by construction, as R/B/V state.
  • Falsifier (F4): own Monte Carlo, 300 trials per ε over the sketch's 7,200-comparison panel — fires 300/300 at each of ε = 0.001, 0.005, 0.01 (analytic 0.9993 at ε=0.001).
  • Evidence survival (F1): own Monte Carlo — perfect-reader pass rates 0.902/0.753/0.503 (n=20) and 0.901/0.750/0.492 (n=100) at 10/25/50%, matching 1−dose to simulation noise.
  • Inversion (F3): "The door is not locked" minus not → "The door is locked" — ground truth inverted by one word.

docs.title: 5. Fabrication sweep and minor errors
docs.text: Clean, fifth consecutive round. Every cited tree symbol resolves; all three external citations resolve at primary exactly as cited (LLMLingua, arXiv:2310.05736; LongLLMLingua, arXiv:2310.06839; LLMLingua-2, arXiv:2403.12968, §4.2 for the word-level compression unit). Non-load-bearing errors, corrected here: the researcher's line citations drift by a few lines in four places (perturbation operators at :33, not :20; distraction levels at :74, not :57; needle DOSES at :102, not :57; negation DECISIONS at :95, not :107) — substance intact in each case; red-team A's survival Monte Carlo also requires local context survival, so its pass rates are a lower bound on the pure survival figure — F1 is stronger than A stated, not weaker. The researcher's neighbour-tool re-survey is flagged UNEXECUTED in its own brief; the uniqueness claim stands only in its combination-scoped form and no stronger.

docs.title: 6. Queue state
docs.text: Wave-11 adjudication so far: rank 1 (directive) NO-BUILD, rank 2 (instruction-distance) NO-BUILD, rank 3 (history-frame) NO-BUILD, rank 4 (prune-sweep) NO-BUILD — each with a resubmission candidate recorded, none queued as a build. The resubmission queue now holds seven candidates: payload §2, answer-syntax --document-syntax, instruction-language §3, directive §3, instruction-distance §3, history-frame §3, and this round's §3 — none of them a build order. Next in the wave-11 slate: rank 5 (question bundling, --bundle) design round.

docs.title: Release notes — model-protocol-lab 0.1.0
docs.text: Status: DRAFT notes. Prepared 2026-10-16 by the release-readiness audit worker. These notes are pending the owner's release tag; no tag has been created. Maintainer: review this draft before tagging — the release workflow uses this file for the release notes when its version matches the tag (the versioned RELEASE_NOTES file for that tag), and falls back to a fixed template when no such file exists.

docs.title: What this is
docs.text: Model Protocol Lab measures whether a local language model fails because of its weights or because its conversations are formatted incorrectly. It renders a 29-family catalog of text-only chat-format hypotheses (plus bounded BOS, prefix and thinking-mode mutations) as exact token sequences, sends them to a local checkpoint, and compares task answers and response boundaries token-for-token. A strict search/held-out fixture discipline selects a single winning format or abstains — no leaderboards.

docs.title: What's new in 0.1.0
docs.text:
This is the first runnable release (the 0.1.0a0 label marked a source snapshot that was never executed). Since that snapshot:

  • Catalog 3 → 29 families, each hand-rendered from primary sources (official chat_template.jinja / tokenizer_config.json, preserved byte-identical under docs/evidence/): ChatML; Llama 3/4; Gemma 2/3/4; Qwen3/3.8; DeepSeek V3/R1/V4.1; Mistral v0.3/Large; Phi-4; GLM-4/4.5/5.3; Kimi K2/K3; Kolibri-1; LFM2.5; Nemotron 3.5; Muse Glimmer; Muse Spark; Laguna 2.1; Ling-3.1; K2-Horizon; Hy4; MiniMax-M3; Nanbeige 4.2. Out-of-scope branches (tool calls, reasoning content, auto-injected system blocks) are documented, not modeled.
  • model-protocol-lab debug: an interactive, offline protocol-debugger REPL — render with per-segment char/token maps, stepped boundary detection, fixture auditing; weights never loaded.
  • model-protocol-lab diff-backends: differential testing of emulated backend stop semantics (HF StopStringCriteria, vLLM detokenizer strip/keep, EOS-appended, SGLang) over one recorded token sequence, with a classified divergence taxonomy.
  • model-protocol-lab diff-reports: deterministic comparison of two experiment result directories for the iterate-and-compare operator loop, with a config-drift warning section.
  • doctor --portability-matrix: static template↔tokenizer portability check over 118 mutate candidates, fail-closed (missing_or_unsafe_asset on unreadable assets).
  • Stop-semantics fidelity: line-faithful ports of upstream transformers.StopStringCriteria and vLLM's check_stop_strings, verified against the real implementations over thousands of adversarial differential trials.

See CHANGELOG.md ([0.1.0]) for the full per-cycle record, including every real bug found and fixed during the audit cycles.

docs.title: Post-0.1.0 snapshot additions (2026-10-16 → 2026-10-18, on main)
docs.text:
Development continued after the 0.1.0 snapshot; these additions are on main and covered by CHANGELOG.md's [Unreleased] entries:

  • Deterministic inline-SVG token-budget frontier chart in report.html, with a decision ribbon coloring every budget span by post-hoc outcome (cycles 121–122).
  • Selection-margin trajectory chart under the frontier chart, showing the per-budget leader and lead margin with a safe-budget-floor dashed line (cycle 124).
  • Safe budget floor readout: the first budget from which the native decision never flips again, as a first-class HTML callout and diff-reports comparison (cycle 126).
  • Per-flip-span attribution: the exact (candidate, fixture) pass-status changes driving each decision flip, recorded in the payload and compared by diff-reports (cycles 127–128).
  • Selection-rule consistency audit: proved the frontier's post-hoc decision_at is exactly the selection rule the run would have produced (cycle 129).
  • model-protocol-lab verify: N-version independent results-integrity replay — re-derives decision, winner, frontier, and held-out floor from a stored results.json through independent code paths (cycle 131).
  • Held-out verification-budget floor: the first budget from which the held-out verdict holds unchanged, as an HTML callout and diff-reports comparison (cycle 130).
  • Holdout contamination detector: measures search↔held-out fixture similarity (deterministic difflib + trigram Jaccard tiers) and warns in inspect/fixtures build/doctor --dataset/run (cycle 132).
  • Security red-team hardening of the HTML report renderer against hostile payloads (strict type guards, fail-closed restore, symlinked report-dir rejection) (cycle 132).
  • Prompt-boundary canonicality audit (doctor --boundary-audit): flags prompt templates whose tokenization is fragile at the prompt/response seam, as an HTML section and diff-reports comparison (cycle 134).
  • Chat-marker isolation conformance: verifies that chat markers (e.g. <|im_start|>) survive tokenization as single tokens rather than splitting into pieces (cycle 135).
  • Template conformance firewall: static AST scan of the checkpoint's Jinja chat_template denying RCE primitives (dunder access, |attr sandbox escape, dangerous globals) before any render; the render itself stays inside ImmutableSandboxedEnvironment (cycle 136).
  • Selection robustness under stop semantics: pure post-hoc re-application of the selection rule under each emulated stop semantic (native, HF, vLLM, EOS-appended) — the serving-stack migration signal, as an HTML section and diff-reports comparison (cycle 137).
  • Cross-checkpoint transfer experiment (run --transfer-model): re-evaluates every search candidate against up to 4 local checkpoints with per-checkpoint selection verdicts, as an HTML transfer-matrix section (cycle 138).
  • Transfer comparison in diff-reports (diff_transfer): verdict drift, per-checkpoint and per-cell drift, checkpoints added/removed (cycle 140).
  • Hostile-input crash hardening: three TypeError crashes on non-string dict keys fixed fail-closed (cycle 141).
  • Contamination comparison in diff-reports (diff_contamination): worst-tier drift, pairs added/removed, tier escalations — the fixture-hygiene regression signal (cycle 143).
  • Fixture-perturbation robustness experiment (run --perturb N): re-runs the search evaluation on N deterministically perturbed fixture variants (typo, case flip, whitespace, Unicode variant, punctuation strip) and re-applies the selection rule per variant — answering whether the winner survives phrasing perturbations. New HTML section and diff-reports comparison (diff_perturbation); completes the winner-reliability trilogy with cycles 137 and 138 (cycle 144).

docs.title: Breaking changes
docs.text: None. 0.1.0a0 was a source snapshot that never executed, so there is no prior released behavior to break. This is the first runnable release. The CLI surface (9 subcommands), the fixture schema, and the report formats have been stable across the development cycles; the exit code contract (0/1/2/130) is pinned by tests.

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
Requires Python 3.11+.

From source (verified path):

python -m venv .venv
# Activate with your OS's usual command, e.g. source .venv/bin/activate
python -m pip install -e ".[dev]"
python -m model_protocol_lab catalog

To run a model you also need the optional HF adapter and a trusted, already-downloaded checkpoint (the adapter never downloads models):

python -m pip install -e ".[hf]"
python -m model_protocol_lab doctor --model path/to/checkpoint --dataset examples/fixtures.json

docs.title: Residual risks (accepted, documented in docs/SECURITY.md)
docs.text:
1. torch's +cpu local tag is invisible to pip-audit (manual CVE re-verification on every bump).
  2. No hash-pinned lockfile (CI pip-audit gate mitigates).
  3. ~~_manifest reads weight files twice per run (I/O cost on very large checkpoints).~~ Retired 2026-10-17 (cycle 115): the backend now hashes each weight file once and verifies a cheap stat fingerprint after the load; the double full-hash is gone (documented trade-off in docs/SECURITY.md: a content swap preserving size, nanosecond mtime and inode inside the load window would evade the stat check).

Hostile Jinja templates can still burn CPU inside the render on off-main-thread or non-Unix platforms (same exposure as HF's own apply_chat_template); on Unix, in the main thread, each render runs under a 10 s SIGALRM wall-clock budget (cycle 116) and degrades to "unavailable" on expiry. Template source and rendered output are capped at 1 MB each; memory bombs are capped.

docs.title: Prompt repetition × template — design
docs.text:
model-protocol-lab run --repeat measures whether repeating a request inside the turn changes verdicts when the chat template is the variable. Leviathan, Kalman & Matias (arXiv:2512.14982) show that prompt repetition improves non-reasoning LLMs — measured on API models, each rendered with its provider's own chat template, with a padding ablation showing random-token padding does not reproduce the effect. This probe asks the lab's version of the question: same checkpoint, hand-rendered foreign formats, exact token sequences, a conservative abstention rule — does repetition change who passes, and does the winner survive it?

Monday-morning use: you are about to ship a prompt that asks twice (or are wondering whether to). The probe tells you, per candidate template on your own checkpoint, whether repeating the request changes verdicts once prompt length is held constant — and whether the template you selected still wins under repetition.

docs.title: Arms
docs.text:
Three arms per (candidate, fixture), all over the search split only:

  • x1 — the recorded native search observations, reused. The treated arms are compared against the run that actually happened, not a re-execution; x1 generates zero model calls.
  • x2 — the fixture's last user message with its content repeated verbatim inside the same turn: content + "\n" + content. The surgery happens on the message content before render (the deliforge precedent): a post-render append would land after the assistant prefix, in the assistant's mouth.
  • pad — the same fixture with neutral filler appended after the same joiner, sized so the rendered pad prompt has exactly the x2 prompt's token length for that candidate and fixture.

The headline contrast is x2 − pad (repetition_effect): both arms are longer than x1 by the same number of tokens, so a difference is not explained by length alone. What it does not separate is repetition-specific attention from content position — the design names that limit wherever the number is reported. pad − x1 is the length_effect; x2 − x1 is the raw_gain, labelled joiner-inclusive because the joiner itself (frozen as "\n" across all arms) is part of what x2 adds over x1.

docs.title: Claims
docs.text:
• R1′ (construction). The x2 arm's render is the x1 render with the last user message's content replaced by the doubled content — a string-level claim, verified by rebuilding the render from the arm fixture, never by search-and-replace (identical first/last user contents make replace-based checks certify a wrongly-doubled first turn). Whether the token construction is exact is measured, not assumed: per (candidate, fixture) the payload records id_exact (the x2 content region is exactly region + joiner region + region, by sentinel-free render affixes) or text_level with the seam token ids. A merge-y tokenizer degrades the measurement to text_level; it does not silently inherit an id-level claim.
  • R2′ (attribution). A verdict change between x1 and x2 is a prompt-format effect on this checkpoint, attributable to the treated prompt as rendered — the lab's standing asymmetry applies: it proves the failure was prompt-fixable for fixtures that flip fail→pass, and proves nothing about weights for fixtures that never pass.
  • R3′ (length control). The pad arm is token-length-matched per (candidate, fixture) on the rendered ids, by a bounded search (≤ 512 probes) over whole filler units plus at most one truncated suffix. Pairs that cannot be matched exactly — nonpositive delta with no positive-filler match, overshoot (the empty pad already renders longer than x2), search exhausted — are recorded pad_unmatchable, never shipped mismatched. A match whose filler contributes zero tokens is degenerate and does not count: the search continues.
  • R4′ (provenance). Provenance is claimed for x1 only: the recorded observations, the run's protocol digest, and the per-fixture ground records. The treated arms rest on the frozen protocol (below) plus those records; the payload carries counts, ids, booleans and digests only — no fixture content, no filler text, no answer text.
  • R5′ (selection). Each arm's winner is re-derived under the conservative rule over that arm's completed, non-vacuous fixtures — the same population as the gain denominators. The readout is withheld (decision: "unavailable", flip None) whenever any candidate is arm-unavailable or the completed sets differ across candidates: a flip the denominators cannot explain is a phantom, and the scorer-lens withholding discipline applies. The x1 arm never reports a flip; it is the recorded run by construction. Run decisions are compared after vocabulary mapping (compatible_on_fixture_set and held_out_failed both map to ("selected", winner)).

docs.title: Denominators and abstentions
docs.text:
Every contrast is paired: a fixture enters a contrast's denominator only when both compared arms completed it and it is not vacuous. n_paired travels with every rate; rates are None (never 0.0) when nothing is paired, and evaluable_mismatch flags contrasts whose arms completed different fixture sets. Because pad sizing can fail per pair, the payload discloses n_pad_evaluable and pad_evaluable_share per candidate, plus the delta sign counts — a repetition effect measured on a shrinking pad subset says so on its face. Contrasts are also reported excluding pre-repeated fixtures (below); that readout is a subpopulation estimate and is labelled as such.

Vacuous fixtures (empty or whitespace-only target content) are excluded from every denominator and selection set by content predicate — under the frozen joiner an empty content's x2 render differs from x1 by the joiner alone, so a render comparison would certify a treatment that did not happen. They are counted (n_vacuous), never generated.

Degradation is per fixture, never per cell: a treated arm whose rendered length plus the generation cap exceeds the run's context budget (max_context, the same value the CLI passes to the backend constructor; equality is measured, one token over degrades) records arm_context_exceeded for that fixture alone. A backend generation failure records arm_evaluation_failed. A fixture whose expected answer occurs inside the filler unit (or whose candidate boundary text occurs in it) is pad_screened: its pad arm would hand the model its answer or its terminator, so the fixture leaves the pad denominators visibly rather than poisoning them. If the filler unit itself ever collided with a candidate's special-token inventory, the whole stage would fail closed (filler_screen_failed); the shipped unit is clean against the shipped catalog.

docs.title: Protocol (frozen, v1)
docs.text:
Joiner "\n"; filler unit one frozen declarative sentence (no digits, no instruction text), screened per run as above; pre-repetition detector v1; sizing rule whole-units-plus-one-truncated-suffix-v1; at most 2400 ground records (candidate × fixture, arms folded into one record) — the stage returns repetition_cell_budget_exceeded before any generation past the cap. The payload's protocol block carries a SHA-256 fingerprint over the canonical protocol table including the fixture-set hash and the backend fingerprint; any component change is a protocol version bump, and diff-reports reports protocol / fixture-set / backend drift with comparable: false.

The detector is exact and mechanical. Let c be the target content after whitespace collapse (case-sensitive). Flag iff (i) c = t + sep + t for some nonempty t and sep ∈ {"", " "}, or (ii) c contains two immediately adjacent copies of a substring of length ≥ 8. Consequences worth stating plainly: "ha ha ha ha" is flagged (t = "ha ha"); a repeated sentence whose second copy is identical including its trailing period is flagged (t = "the cat sat.", sep = " "); a near-repeat that differs anywhere inside a copy is not flagged, and neither is a repeat whose only decomposition needs a longer separator. Excluding-flagged contrasts are reported, but the pooled readout remains the headline: the detector screens for fixtures the treatment cannot change, it does not certify the rest as repetition-free.

An echo flag marks fixtures whose expected answer occurs in the target content: under x2 the model is handed a second copy of the answer span, so echo-completion stays separable from re-reading in the records even though v1 reports the flag as a count only.

docs.title: Cost
docs.text: Treated arms cost 2 generations per (candidate, fixture) with x1 reused: at the run caps (24 candidates × 100 fixtures) that is 4,800 generations, on top of the native search. This lab's decoder recomputes the full prefix with no KV cache, so a generation on an L-token prompt costs M·L + M(M−1)/2 token forwards for M generated tokens; the stage therefore costs roughly 2.4–4× one native search pass over the same fixtures, depending on the content share of the prompts. The paper's "no latency increase" claim does not transfer and is not made.

docs.title: Cancellation and gating
docs.text: The run's cancel event is threaded dispatch → wrapper → stage → evaluate; a cancelled stage returns {"available": false, "detail": "cancelled"} with no partial aggregates. If the run's decision is failed or cancelled, or its search entries do not cover every candidate, the wrapper gates the probe to zero generations (native_search_incomplete): treated arms with no sound native baseline are not measured. The probe is search-split only by construction — held-out fixtures exist as recorded x1 for the selected candidate alone, and a treated held-out arm would pair it against candidates that were never selected; no held-out fixture id appears in any ground record.

docs.title: Validation
docs.text: The payload's ground records are the contract: diff-reports recomputes every aggregate from them with independent code — contrasts, mismatch flags, boundary rates, pad shares, delta signs, the per-arm selection readout with its withholding rule, flips against the mapped primary, think-group means in both per-candidate and render-deduplicated form, and the protocol fingerprint from its own components and the record fixture ids. A payload whose numbers its records do not support does not validate. Recompute is internal consistency: it detects aggregates inconsistent with their records, not fabricated records — the standing limitation of every ground layer in this lab.

docs.title: Research → Plan → Develop Cycle Log
docs.text:
How this product is built: repeating cycles of (1) online research from reputable primary sources, (2) planning based on findings, (3) development — then back to (1) with new questions raised by what was built. There is no iteration cap: thoroughness over speed. Cycling continues until consecutive cycles yield nothing significant — a single quiet round does not end the process. Sources are official docs, specs, and top-tier open-source projects; never marketing copy or unverified blogs. Each round below records what was researched, the sources used, what changed in the plan, and what was built.

Every cycle additionally ends with a differentiation review: for each major competitor, write down exactly what they do, then state the concretely different answer this lab gives — verifiable in code, never marketing fluff — and ask: is this substantially different from everything else out there, and would it make someone star the repo? Creative additions must be genuinely novel and working: new experiment modes, novel report visualizations, developer-experience tooling (the doctor concept extended), fixture generation, analysis views nobody else offers. Every addition is real, tested, documented, and secure — no gimmicks.

docs.title: Prior rounds (2026-10-12 → 2026-10-13, summarized)
docs.text:
• Hardening rounds 1–2. Full audit, test suite grown to 224 tests (97% coverage), ruff/mypy/bandit/pip-audit clean, two adversarial red-team rounds with all findings fixed and regression-tested. Evidence in VALIDATION.md; methodology in docs/SECURITY.md.
  • Round A — competitive research (2026-10-13). Primary-source study of lm-evaluation-harness (huggingface.py, utils_hf.py), vLLM v1 detokenizer.py, llama.cpp server, HF transformers docs (chat_templating, stopping_criteria.py), lighteval, HELM, Unitxt, Guidance/Outlines/llguidance. Findings: every competitor renders the model's own chat template; all detect stops at string level with mitigations that hide tokenization mismatch; lm-eval auto-appends EOS to stop lists; none has a selection/abstention discipline; none verifies boundary portability across tokenizers. 10 ideas killed (already covered by competitors). Proposed P1–P5 (below), ranked by value/effort.
  • Round B — hostile audit (2026-10-13). 5 bugs found and fixed (doctor report shape, codec/parser text leaks, fingerprint-less backend AttributeError, NFC evasion gap in evaluate, chmod through symlinks), each with regression tests. 231 tests green, 97% coverage held.
  • Round C — differentiation features (2026-10-13). Implemented all five proposals: P1 template-conformance diff (core.template_diff, doctor.template_conformance), P2 stop-behavior isolation matrix (HF overhang / vLLM holdback / EOS-appended emulations, verified against real transformers.StopStringCriteria as an oracle — 0 mismatches on 9 docstring cases), P3 prompt-boundary sensitivity sweep (core.truncate_text_tail, opt-in --sensitivity-sweep), P4 cross-tokenizer boundary portability (core.check_boundary_portability, doctor --reference-model), P5 failure-mode taxonomy (experiments.classify_observation, cited in the decision banner). 352 tests, 98% coverage, full battery green.
  • Round D — red-team round 3 (2026-10-13, in progress). Adversarial review of the new P1–P5 surface plus full verification battery.

docs.title: Cycle 1 — research (2026-10-13)
docs.text:
Emulation fidelity re-check. - HF transformers: PR #46530 (fix for issue #46519, merged ~123 days ago, present in the installed transformers 5.19.0) changed StopStringCriteria table construction to byte space for byte-level and byte-fallback decoders (_get_stop_string_matching_mode, _token_to_bytes, _get_stop_strings_for_matching; __call__ runtime path unchanged). Source: installed transformers/generation/stopping_criteria.py (5.19.0, read locally) and https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/pull/46530 (byte-space fix) / https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/issues/46519 (the CJK byte-fragment repro). The lab's _hf_overhang_match ports the matching rule correctly but feeds it per-token decode strings, so on UTF-8 fragment tokens real HF now fires where the emulation does not -- the residual documented in docs/USAGE.md §8.2 is now a known upstream-fixed divergence, not just an approximation. (The round-3 1500/1500 differential trials still pass because they were ASCII-only: byte-space and string-space agree when no fragment token appears.) - vLLM: check_stop_strings earliest-completing selection (PR #49391, ~82 days ago) is already what the lab emulates; stop_buffer_length = max(len(s)) - 1 confirmed unchanged in docs.vllm.ai v0.16.0 (vllm/v1/engine/detokenizer.py). Source: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/49391, https://docs.vllm.ai/en/v0.16.0/api/vllm/v1/engine/detokenizer/. No material change since the 2026-10-13 verification.

Prior art check. No tool found doing any of: token-ID-level diffing of hand-rendered format hypotheses against a checkpoint's own chat template (Ferric gates its own renderer's fidelity vs HF apply_chat_template -- a serving-correctness check, different question: https://github.com/dcharlot-physicalai-bmi/ferric/commit/b0b4448917712125a5780e839460c77482ec23d1); cross-tokenizer boundary portability checks; mid-token prompt-boundary sensitivity measurement; stop-semantics isolation matrices. Academic prompt sensitivity work (arXiv 2509.01790 "Flaw or Artifact?", ProSA findings-emnlp 2024, arXiv 2509.13680) measures semantic template variants, never sub-character token-boundary perturbations. The niche is still empty.

Creative territories. (a) The agent-eval-autopsy master plan states the methodological principle this cycle adopts: report the sensitivity curve before the effect size -- "step budget: too high, and no ablation can change the outcome" (https://github.com/kush1311/agent-eval-autopsy/blob/HEAD/agent-autopsy-master-plan.md). No eval harness found that derives pass-rate-vs-token-budget from already recorded outputs. (b) Doctor-style DX: the recurring best-practice pattern is GUIDE -- actionable next steps after a clean scan (specific commands, re-scan to verify). (c) Packaging, grounded in specific repos: ruff's README "Show Your Support" badge block and docs/ hub layout (https://github.com/astral-sh/ruff); sortitionfoundation's docs/{index,quickstart,concepts,adapters,advanced}.md structure. Honest gaps here: no FAQ/troubleshooting doc, no guided next step after doctor.

Plan (selected). 1. HF byte-space stop matching -- close the upstream-fixed divergence: generalize _hf_overhang_match to str|bytes, add an optional per-token byte mapper on the backend (port of upstream's decoder-mode detection + _token_to_bytes), thread it through emulate_hf_stop_string / stop_matrix / CLI. Differentially verified against the real StopStringCriteria, including the issue-#46519 fragment shape. 2. Token-budget robustness frontier -- new experiments.budget_frontier: from the recorded search observations, the exact pass/budget curve per candidate (pass(b) ⟺ native pass ∧ b ≥ cut+len(boundary)), the budgets where the selection decision/winner would flip, surfaced in results.json and the HTML report. Post-hoc, no extra model calls; directly answers "was N=64 load-bearing for this verdict?". 3. doctor next-command suggestion -- on a clean doctor with --dataset and --boundary-ids, emit the exact run invocation with --max-context filled from the checkpoint's declared window (the value users get wrong, per the round-2 GPT-2 finding). Machine-readable in the doctor JSON. 4. docs/FAQ.md -- troubleshooting grounded in documented behaviors (boundary IDs, context window, tokenization-mismatch diagnostic, empty expected, interrupted runs, report privacy); linked from README/USAGE.

Rejected. llama.cpp stop-semantics cell (needs primary-source verification of its current matching semantics -- next-cycle candidate); init-fixtures scaffold (marginal over examples/fixtures.json); per-fixture boundary-position histogram (subsumed by the frontier's min-budget data); confidence intervals (violates the not_estimated discipline); inline-SVG charts (XSS review cost; text bars suffice); non-greedy backends (out of scope; post-hoc exactness rests on greedy).

docs.title: Cycle 1 — built (2026-10-13)
docs.text:
1. HF byte-space stop matching. backends._hf_overhang_match generalized to str|bytes (TypeVar; the overlap algorithm is encoding-agnostic). New backends._hf_byte_token_mapper(tokenizer): ports upstream's _get_stop_string_matching_mode + _token_to_bytes (byte_level via bytes_to_unicode, byte_fallback via <0xNN>), returning a per-token-id byte mapping or None (classic string path). LocalHFBackend exposes it as hf_stop_token_bytes (construction failure degrades to None, never fails init); TruncatedPromptBackend forwards it; emulate_hf_stop_string / stop_matrix / CLI thread an optional token_bytes through, with per-token fallback to isolated-decode→UTF-8 and OOB→b"" (mirrors HF's clamp-to-dummy). Differentially verified against the real StopStringCriteria: the issue-#46519 fragment shape (old path silent, oracle fires, new path fires) and 200 randomized ASCII trials where classic path, byte path and incremental oracle all agree.
  2. Token-budget robustness frontier. experiments.budget_frontier derives the exact per-candidate pass/budget curve from recorded search observations (pass(b) ⟺ native pass ∧ b ≥ cut+len(boundary); proven via a 300-case brute-force truncation-lemma test), plus per-budget selection decisions, flip_ranges, and budget_robust. Always-on run diagnostic (degrades to "unavailable", never fails the run); new report.html section with winner pass curve and flip notices; stored in results.json.
  3. doctor next-command suggestion. examine_model reports model.context_window (declared n_positions/max_position_embeddings); clean doctor with --dataset + --boundary-ids emits a suggestion with the exact run command (--max-context from the declared window, shell-quoted paths, FAMILY placeholder + catalog families in the note).
  4. docs/FAQ.md. 12 troubleshooting/interpretation Q&As grounded in documented behavior; linked from README and USAGE.

Tests: 47 new in tests/test_cycle1.py (361 → 408 total). Docs: USAGE §2 (suggestion), §8.2 (byte-space HF bullet, residual note rewritten), new §8.6 (frontier); CHANGELOG [Unreleased]; README feature list (+1 line).

docs.title: Cycle 1 — differentiation review (2026-10-13)
docs.text:
For each major competitor: what they do → this lab's concretely different answer (verifiable in code) → would it make someone star the repo?

  • lm-eval (lm-evaluation-harness). Renders the checkpoint's own chat template via tokenizer.apply_chat_template; string-level stops with a "tokenizers suck" lookback (MultiTokenEOSCriteria); appends EOS to stop sequences; ranks candidates with no abstention discipline. This lab: hand-renders format hypotheses and encodes with add_special_tokens=False (core.Format.render), then diffs each hypothesis as an exact token-ID sequence against the checkpoint's own template rendering (core.template_diff, doctor.template_conformance) -- measuring the model on sequences its own template would never produce; token-ID boundary match with a text cross-check (core._boundary_text_match); unique-all-search-pass selection or abstention (experiments.run_experiment). Star-worthy for the narrow audience asking "weights or formatting?": no other tool asks that question at the token-ID level.
  • vLLM. Inference server: renders the model's Jinja template, detects stops in the detokenizer (check_stop_strings, earliest-completing wins), stops on EOS by default. This lab: not a server -- it emulates vLLM's stop semantics post-hoc as one cell of an isolation matrix (backends.emulate_vllm_holdback, experiments.stop_matrix) to ask whether the verdict survives under competitor semantics, a question vLLM cannot ask about itself. Nobody else ships a stop-semantics isolation matrix.
  • llama.cpp. Server with its own template rendering and string-level stops; EOS stopping by default. Same structural differentiation as vLLM. Honest gap: no llama.cpp stop cell yet -- its current matching semantics need primary-source verification first (deferred to a later cycle, not claimed).
  • lighteval / HELM. Benchmark suites measuring task accuracy (HELM adds fairness/calibration/efficiency) with standardized prompts. This lab is not a benchmark: it contributes measurement-integrity instruments none of them has -- the token-budget frontier (experiments.budget_frontier: the exact pass/budget curve and decision-flip ranges from recorded outputs, no extra model calls), the stop matrix, the failure taxonomy, the mid-token sensitivity sweep. The frontier in particular answers the "report the sensitivity curve before the effect size" principle no harness implements for token budgets.
  • Unitxt. Dataset/task preparation recipes. No overlap with the novel features; the lab's fixture schema is a strict local contract (datasets.parse_dataset), not a preparation framework.

Cycle-1 additions against this landscape: (1) byte-space HF stop matching tracks a merged upstream transformers change (issue #46519 / PR #46530) that string-level tools never needed to care about -- the emulation now fires where real HF fires on byte-fragment tokens, differentially verified against the real StopStringCriteria; (2) the budget frontier is a new analysis view (no prior art found); (3) the doctor next-command suggestion closes the most common operator error (wrong --max-context) at the moment it matters. Star-worthy? For the niche -- local checkpoint debuggers -- the honest answer is "these are real, verifiable differences, not marketing"; the FAQ and doctor DX lower the floor for everyone else.

docs.title: Cycle 1 — verification (2026-10-13, Python 3.12, Linux x86-64)

[dev]-only path (transformers/tokenizers/torch blocked): OK (skipped=76) — the byte-space mapper no longer needs the HF stack (the bytes_to_unicode table is ported, cross-checked against transformers when present), so only the true oracle tests skip.

  • Types: mypy model_protocol_lab clean (10 source files) in both venvs.
  • Coverage: 98% total line coverage (1753 statements) in both venvs, above the 97% bar; every new-code branch is covered (remaining misses are the pre-existing defensive lines).
  • Security: bandit -r model_protocol_lab — 0 issues; pip-audit — no known vulnerabilities (torch 2.14.1+cpu local tag invisible to the OSV DB, the accepted residual).
  • Differential evidence: byte-space emulation vs real StopStringCriteria — the issue-#46519 fragment shape: old path silent, oracle fires, new path fires (exact agreement); 200 randomized ASCII trials: classic path, byte path and incremental oracle agree on all 200. (One test-authoring trap found and fixed along the way: the oracle must be consulted per prefix, as generate() does — a final-state-only oracle disagrees with the real criterion on mid-sequence completions.)
  • CLI smoke (tiny locally-generated GPT-2 checkpoint, no downloads, in the fresh venv): catalog, inspect, doctor (suggestion present with --max-context 64, the checkpoint's declared window), run --mutate --sensitivity-sweep --max-drop-bytes 2 (exit 2 no_candidate as expected with random weights; budget_frontier and sensitivity_sweep sections present in results.json; frontier section in report.html). Byte-level backend smoke: LocalHFBackend.hf_stop_token_bytes maps correctly on a real byte-level checkpoint and generation still works.
