(2) The frontier's exactness rests on greedy decoding, like the stop matrix. (3) No llama.cpp stop cell yet. (4) The doctor suggestion's --family is a placeholder the operator must fill — deliberate, not inferred.

docs.title: Cycle 2 — research (2026-10-13)
docs.text:
llama.cpp stop cell — primary-source verification, then killed. Read the current llama.cpp sources directly (master, 2026-10-13): tools/server/server-context.cpp server_slot::find_stopping_strings (L820-848) and server_slot::process_token (L2591-2765), common/common.h string_find_partial_stop, common/sampling.cpp, the server README's sampling-params table, and PR #13785 (partial-stop streaming fix). Findings:

  • Full stop: for each antiprompt word, text.find(word, max(0, size - word.size() - last_token_size)) on the unsent text tail; the earliest-starting word wins; on fire the generated text is truncated at the stop start -- exclude semantics, the stop word never appears in the final text.
  • Partial stops only withhold streamed deltas; per PR #13785 "partial stop words aren't erased by server_context::process_token, but full stop words are" -- they have no final-text effect and there is nothing to emulate post-hoc.
  • EOS: llama_vocab_is_eog(vocab, result.tok) stops generation (STOP_TYPE_EOS) with no text truncation; --ignore-eos is documented as "ignore end of stream token and continue generating (implies --logit-bias EOS-inf)" -- i.e. exactly the lab's native generate-through-EOS behavior.
  • Verdict for the matrix (single stop string = decoded boundary text, recorded greedy outputs, post-hoc truncation): llama.cpp's rule is the same "truncate before the completed stop word" as the vLLM cell. The deltas do not survive emulation -- multi-word earliest-start vs earliest-completion selection is inapplicable (one stop string), the 1-char search-window offset sits below the emulation's incremental-decode approximation floor, partial stops are streaming-only, and EOS is covered (EOS-appended cell for stop-on-EOS; native behavior for --ignore-eos). A cell would duplicate the vLLM cell on every realistic input while doubling the decode-approximation stack. Killed with reasons; the analysis is recorded in docs/USAGE.md §8.2 so the decision is checkable.

Per-candidate boundary support — scientifically justified, built. USAGE §4 documented the limitation ("the current CLI therefore cannot fairly compare candidates requiring different boundary sequences") and promised per-candidate support. The justification is not convenience: each candidate is a format hypothesis, and real formats terminate the assistant turn with different markers (ChatML <|im_end|>, Llama 3 <|eot_id|>, Gemma <end_of_turn>), so one boundary for all candidates is the unscientific choice. Design: --boundary-ids stays the default, repeatable --boundary-map NAME=ID,ID overrides per candidate name (validated against the actual candidate set -- unknown/duplicate names fail fast before any compute); run_experiment(..., boundary_map=...) resolves per candidate; every search entry records its boundary_token_ids; held-out, stop matrix (via the winner's boundary), budget frontier (per-entry boundaries) and sensitivity sweep all follow. The selection rule is untouched: exactly one candidate passing every search fixture under its own boundary; ties and failures abstain. doctor --boundary-map checks each mapping against the checkpoint vocabulary.

Fixture-generation UX — surveyed, built. lighteval: Python prompt_fn converting a dataset line to a Doc, plus declarative LightevalTaskConfig (docs: adding-a-custom-task). promptfoo: YAML tests: with vars/assert, CSV column-as-vars expansion with the __expected assertion column, file:// globs, promptfoo init scaffolding (promptfoo.dev docs). Unitxt: Python Task/templates over data, create_dataset, unitxt-explore UI (IBM/unitxt README). The pattern across all three: a more compact authoring surface than the runtime schema. None of them enforces a search/held-out separation discipline at authoring time -- promptfoo has no held-out concept; lighteval has splits but no group-overlap or identical-message leakage checks. The lab's answer: fixtures build compiles a one-row-per-fixture CSV (id,group,partition,expected,user_1,assistant_1,...) to the strict JSON, with the partition explicit per row; group overlap, duplicate IDs and identical message sequences across partitions raise with row numbers before any file is written, and the emitted JSON is round-tripped through the strict loader before it is returned -- discipline by construction, not by post-hoc inspection. CSV chosen over YAML (stdlib only, promptfoo-consistent columns-as-vars DX); empty-string message content stays JSON-only (documented).

Richer report views — built, scriptless. Surveyed best-in-class static reports (pytest-html's filterable tables need JS -- rejected under the lab's scriptless CSP; criterion.rs's self-contained inline SVG; coverage.py's annotated views). Cycle 1's inline-SVG rejection stands (text achieves the value with no new review surface). Built, all post-hoc from recorded observations, all values escaped, zero new assets: (1) per-fixture x candidate outcome grid (✓/✗/–, ★ on the selected candidate) -- the debugging view the report lacked; (2) decisive fixtures (fixtures passed by exactly one candidate while all others failed -- the evidence the verdict actually rests on; empty with an honest message when no fixture separates the field); (3) per-candidate token-budget pass-curve sparklines (block elements, aria-labeled, ≤48 sampled budgets) next to the winner's exact table; (4) a boundary-IDs column in the candidate table and per-candidate boundary lines in the run configuration.

Re-verification against latest upstream — no drift. transformers main stopping_criteria.py: _get_stop_string_matching_mode, _token_to_bytes, _get_stop_strings_for_matching, _stop_string_get_matching_positions and __call__ are identical to the ported 5.19.0 logic (byte-space table build for byte-level/byte-fallback decoders intact). vLLM main vllm/v1/engine/detokenizer.py: check_stop_strings earliest-completing selection with tie-break by stop-list order, stop_buffer_length = max(len(s)) - 1, include_stop_str_in_output=False default, min_tokens gating -- all unchanged since the Cycle-1 verification; the lab's documented min_tokens=0 assumption still holds.

Plan (selected). 1. Per-candidate boundaries (--boundary-map, experiments/CLI/doctor/ reporting threading, USAGE §4 + FAQ updates). 2. fixtures build CSV authoring (model_protocol_lab/fixtures.py, examples/fixtures.csv, USAGE §9). 3. Report views: outcome grid, decisive fixtures, frontier sparklines, boundary column (reporting.py, sample report regenerated). 4. llama.cpp kill documentation (USAGE §8.2).

Rejected. llama.cpp stop-semantics cell (verified duplication of the vLLM cell -- see above); inline-SVG charts (Cycle-1 rejection stands); a YAML authoring format (CSV needs no new dependency); confidence intervals (still violates not_estimated); non-greedy backends (still out of scope).

docs.title: Cycle 2 — built (2026-10-13)
docs.text:
1. Per-candidate boundaries. experiments._resolve_boundaries (default + map resolution, validated: unknown names, non-dict maps and bad ID tuples rejected); run_experiment(..., boundary_map=None) -- each search entry records boundary_token_ids, held-out uses the winner's boundary (selected_boundary_token_ids); budget_frontier reads per-entry boundaries with fallback to the single-boundary argument (backward compatible); prompt_sensitivity_sweep threads the map through. CLI: repeatable --boundary-map NAME=ID,ID on run (parsed by parse_boundary_map, validated against the real candidate set via _resolve_boundary_map -- duplicates/unknown names exit 2 before any compute) and on doctor (duplicates only; per-name vocab checks in examine_model); the stop matrix uses the winner's boundary; the doctor suggestion note mentions --boundary-map. Reporting: search table gains a boundary-IDs column; the run configuration lists per-candidate boundaries when they differ (single line when uniform). Docs: USAGE §4 rewritten (+ ### Per-candidate boundaries), FAQ updated, CHANGELOG, README (+1 line).
  2. fixtures build. New model_protocol_lab/fixtures.py: read_authoring_file (O_NONBLOCK + fstat regular-file gate, 2 MB cap, UTF-8), parse_fixture_csv (strict header id,group,partition,expected
  3. user_1,assistant_1,... pairs, row-numbered errors, verbatim cells, quoted newlines, blank-line tolerance, short-row padding; the Split constructor enforces the separation discipline before any write), split_to_json_text (round-trips through parse_dataset -- by construction), write_fixture_file (O_EXCL, 0o600, parent must exist, partial-write cleanup). CLI fixtures build SOURCE --output OUT prints a JSON summary, warns on empty expected like inspect, and exits 1 with the reason on authoring errors. examples/fixtures.csv builds to the exact equivalent of examples/fixtures.json (verified). Docs: USAGE §9 + §1 cross-reference, CHANGELOG, README (+1 line).
  4. Report views. reporting._search_outcomes (tolerant post-hoc reader), _outcome_grid_section, _decisive_section, _sparkline + _frontier_spark_table (exact counts from recorded minimal budgets, ≤48 sampled budgets), boundary column + per-candidate config lines. New CSS classes only (glyph colors, spark); CSP unchanged, no scripts. Committed sample report regenerated (byte-identical re-runs verified).
  5. llama.cpp kill note in USAGE §8.2 with the primary-source analysis.

Tests: tests/test_cycle2.py, 81 tests -- boundary resolution and selection semantics under the map (FakeBackend scripted generations prove each candidate is measured with its own boundary, and that the map flips ambiguous/selected outcomes exactly as designed), frontier per-entry boundaries, sweep passthrough, CLI flag parsing/validation (exit-2 paths), a full run --boundary-map on the tiny GPT-2 checkpoint (per-candidate boundaries recorded in results.json and rendered in report.html), doctor per-name checks (including the no-transformers degradation path), fixtures build unit + CLI tests (row-numbered errors, discipline refusals, 0o600/O_EXCL behavior, control-char stripping), and report-view tests (glyphs, escaping of hostile fixture IDs, decisive logic, sparkline scaling). Suite: 410 -> 491 tests.

docs.title: Cycle 2 — differentiation review (2026-10-13)
docs.text:
• lm-eval. Renders the checkpoint's own template and measures with one stop configuration for every task. This lab now additionally measures each format hypothesis with its own protocol terminator (--boundary-map) -- the "weights or formatting?" question asked with per-format end-of-turn markers, which a single-boundary harness cannot express without run multiplication. Verifiable: per-entry boundary_token_ids in results.json.
  • vLLM / llama.cpp. Servers with one stop-word list per request. The lab's answer to "which stop semantics would flip my verdict" remains the isolation matrix; Cycle 2 verified from primary sources that a llama.cpp cell would add nothing (documented in USAGE §8.2) -- an honest non-duplication competitors cannot claim, since they never ask the question.
  • lighteval / HELM. No per-format boundary discipline, no decisive-fixture analysis, no token-budget frontier. The new decisive fixtures view ("the evidence the verdict rests on") and the frontier sparklines are measurement-integrity instruments neither suite has.
  • Unitxt. Dataset preparation recipes with no search/held-out leakage discipline. fixtures build is the only authoring tool found that makes split leakage structurally unbuildable (explicit partition column + build-time refusal + loader round-trip by construction).
  • promptfoo. The closest DX analogue (CSV test cases, __expected column). promptfoo has no held-out concept and no leakage checks; the lab's CSV keeps the strict schema and the separation discipline, and its report stays a single zero-asset file while promptfoo needs its viewer.

Star-worthy? The per-candidate boundary support turns the lab's central question ("weights or formatting?") from a single-terminator approximation into a per-format measurement -- the feature the docs had been promising. fixtures build removes the most tedious step between the user and a disciplined experiment. The report views answer "what decided this?" at a glance. All three are real, tested, and unlike anything in the surveyed tools. The honest limit stands: the niche is local-checkpoint debugging, not general benchmarking.

docs.title: Cycle 2 — verification (2026-10-13, Python 3.12, Linux x86-64)
docs.text:
Fresh venv (pip install -e ".[dev,hf]", CPU torch index): - python -m unittest discover -s tests -t .: 491 tests OK, three consecutive greens (10.9s / 10.1s / 10.1s). - Dev-only venv (pip install -e ".[dev]", no hf): 491 tests OK, 78 skipped (HF-dependent tests skip cleanly, including the new Cycle 2 ones via the established HAS_HF guard). - ruff check + ruff format --check: clean (24 files). - mypy model_protocol_lab: no issues, 11 files. - coverage: 98% total (fixtures.py 100%, experiments.py 100%, reporting.py 98%; remaining misses are pre-existing defensive branches) -- bar is 97%. - Main venv: bandit -r model_protocol_lab: 0 issues; pip-audit: no known vulnerabilities (torch's 2.14.1+cpu local tag is invisible to the OSV database -- accepted residual, same as Cycle 1; everything auditable is clean). - CLI smoke: catalog, inspect, fixtures build examples/fixtures.csv (-> byte-equivalent of fixtures.json, inspect says valid), run --help shows the new --boundary-map flag, fixtures --help lists build. - Sample-report golden test: green in every run (regenerates byte-identically); committed report contains the new outcome grid, decisive-fixtures section and boundary column, no http/https strings, no <script>. - Config YAML validation: ci.yml, pre-commit-config.yaml, dependabot.yml, CITATION.cff all parse.

Known/accepted: (1) torch CPU wheel's local version tag is not auditable by pip-audit. (2) Exactness still rests on greedy decoding, as documented. (3) The doctor suggestion's --family remains a deliberate placeholder. (4) No llama.cpp stop cell (verified duplication -- see research section). (5) The sample report shows the single uniform "Boundary token IDs" line rather than per-candidate lines because its boundaries are uniform -- the intended display behavior, covered by test.

docs.title: Cycle 3 — research (2026-10-13)
docs.text:
Fresh upstream sweep — no material drift. - transformers main src/transformers/generation/stopping_criteria.py re-fetched 2026-10-13 and compared against installed 5.19.0 and the lab's port: _token_to_bytes, _get_stop_string_matching_mode, _get_stop_strings_for_matching, _stop_string_get_matching_positions and __call__ are identical on every line the emulation ports. New in main since 5.19.0: STOP_STRING_EMBEDDING_CACHE + clean_and_embed_tokens_with_cache (a table-construction perf refactor -- same matching semantics) and a new_token_length parameter on EosTokenCriteria (not emulated, not relevant). The lab's _hf_byte_token_mapper matches both byte-for-byte on the ported logic. - vLLM main v1/engine/detokenizer.py: check_stop_strings earliest-completion selection with stop-list-order tie-break, stop_buffer_length = max(len(s)) - 1, include_stop_str_in_output default False, min_tokens gating -- all unchanged since the Cycle-2 verification. New: _protected_step overflow/invalid-prefix recovery in the fast detokenizer (error handling, not matching semantics). No drift affecting the emulation. - transformers #47975 (deferred/async stopping check) and #48814 (attention-mask elision) touch generate-loop timing/perf, not the criterion matching rule the lab ports; the lab's backend is its own greedy loop, so there is nothing to track. llama.cpp stays killed with the Cycle-2 primary-source documentation; lm-eval is comparison-only (not emulated), so no re-check was needed.

Recent literature — nothing adoptable, one related-work grounding. Searched 2025–2026 work on prompt/chat-format sensitivity and tokenizer-boundary effects: arXiv 2604.18389 ("Understanding the Prompt Sensitivity", 7 modification types incl. token misalignment and orthographic errors), arXiv 2608.18539 (interaction-based prompt sensitivity), arXiv 2411.10541 (prompt-formatting impact, NAACL 2025), arXiv 2609.35869 ("The Price of Token Boundaries", compression cost of pre-tokenization, Sept 2026), and the token-healing literature (guidance-ai 2023; measured effects in arXiv 2402.01035 §Table 8). Every paper measures semantic or surface prompt variants; none does sub-character token-boundary perturbation of format hypotheses against a checkpoint's own template -- the lab's niche is still empty. Token healing is the serving-side mitigation for exactly the bias the lab's sensitivity sweep measures (a prompt ending mid-token skews the next-token distribution); it is now cited as related work in USAGE §8.5. No paper suggests a method the lab should adopt.

Mutation testing — feasible with cosmic-ray, infeasible with mutmut; found one real gap. - mutmut 3.8.0 is unusable for this repo: its config loader crashes on the documented tests_dir string shape (TypeError in its own code), its mutants/ working-dir model drops examples/ so the baseline suite fails (tests resolve fixtures via __file__), and its pytest-only runner does not match the project's unittest invocation. - cosmic-ray 8.7.0 works: it runs the project's own test command in-tree. Scoped trial on model_protocol_lab/fixtures.py (261 lines, 100% line coverage): 416 mutants, ~15 s/mutant sequentially. Interim result 27/32 killed (84%); the 5 survivors split into 3 real gaps and 2 equivalent mutants. The real gaps, all fixed with regression tests in this cycle: (1) len(content) > MAX_BYTES vs >= survived -- no test pinned that a file of exactly MAX_BYTES bytes is accepted; (2) len(cases) > MAX_CASES_PER_SPLIT vs >= survived -- same boundary pattern for the per-split fixture cap; (3) not record or all(...) vs and survived -- a row of only empty cells (,,,) was silently tolerated by luck of no test, and the mutant turned it into a downstream validation error instead of a skipped blank line. The 2 equivalent mutants are unkillable by construction (os.O_RDONLY | os.O_NONBLOCK with O_RDONLY=0, so >> is identical; type(x) is not str vs !=, identical for type objects); one further survivor was cosmetic (json.dumps indent 2 -> 3, no behavioral difference -- not pinned, documented here). - CI practicality: ~1.7 h for one small module at sequential speed; ~11 modules extrapolate to ~10–15 h for the whole codebase. Not practical as a per-commit CI gate; conceivable as a weekly scheduled job with parallel workers. The honest-limits item ("no mutation-testing run") is now a documented trial with numbers instead of a blank.

First-run UX walk — two genuine rough edges, both fixed. Walked install → catalog → inspect → fixtures build → doctor → run → report against a tiny locally-generated GPT-2 checkpoint (n_positions=64): 1. The doctor's suggested run command used a fixed --max-new-tokens 64; with an 18-token prompt in a 64-token window the suggested command itself failed with context_limit_exceeded. The suggestion now sizes --max-new-tokens so the longest fixture prompt (rendered with every catalog candidate, encoded with the checkpoint tokenizer) fits the declared window, and warns when even the longest prompt fills it. 2. A failed run's report banner said only "backend-error ×1"; the sanitized cause was recorded on the observation but stripped from the default evidence-excluded report. evaluate now passes the built-in backend's fixed-vocabulary codes through an allowlist (arbitrary backend text still collapses to backend_reported_error), summaries carry failure_code, and the banner prints a "Failure diagnosis" line with operator guidance. - FAQ gaps closed: no entry existed for runtime context_limit_exceeded (only the init-time local_context_limit_exceeds_declared_window), and the "doctor says ok but run fails" entry did not mention the diagnosis banner. Both fixed.

Deferred list revisited — nothing newly feasible. Cycle 1/2 rejections all stand: the llama.cpp cell (killed with primary-source documentation in Cycle 2), the init-fixtures scaffold (superseded by fixtures build), the boundary-position histogram (subsumed by the frontier), confidence intervals (violates not_estimated), inline-SVG charts (XSS review cost), non-greedy backends (out of scope). No deferred item became feasible or more valuable.

Plan (selected). 1. Doctor suggestion window-fit (doctor._longest_prompt_tokens, _suggestion_tokenizer, _build_primary_tokenizer extraction). 2. Failed-run diagnosis (failure_code in experiments._summary, _FAILURE_GUIDANCE + _failure_diagnosis in reporting, allowlisted backend-code pass-through in core.evaluate). 3. Regression tests for the three mutation-found gaps (authoring size-limit boundary, per-split case-count boundary, all-blank-cell row tolerance). 4. Docs: FAQ entries, USAGE §2 (suggestion sizing) and §8.5 (token-healing related work), CHANGELOG, README test-count correction (361 → 491).

Rejected. Upstream emulation changes (no material drift found); literature-driven new methods (none adoptable); mutmut in CI (infeasible for this repo -- documented above); a full mutation-testing CI gate (impractical per-commit at ~15 s/mutant -- documented above).

docs.title: Cycle 3 — built (2026-10-13)
docs.text:
1. Doctor suggestion window-fit. doctor._build_primary_tokenizer extracts the tokenizer construction (same 128 MB cap, same fail-closed/skipped semantics in examine_model). New doctor._longest_prompt_tokens renders every fixture with every candidate of every family (both mutate states) and encodes with the checkpoint tokenizer -- mirroring the backend's encode (add_special_tokens=False) -- so the budget fits whichever family the operator picks; any measurement failure degrades to the default 64, never fails doctor. _next_command emits --max-new-tokens = max(1, min(64, window - longest)) and the note states the sizing; when the longest prompt already fills the window it keeps 1 and warns to shorten fixtures or use a larger-window checkpoint. Verified on the tiny GPT-2 checkpoint: suggestion now says --max-new-tokens 10 (64 - 54) and the suggested command completes (no_candidate on random weights) instead of failing.
  2. Failed-run diagnosis. core.evaluate passes through only allowlisted fixed-vocabulary backend codes (_BACKEND_ERROR_CODES); everything else -- None, empty, arbitrary text -- still collapses to backend_reported_error, so the sanitization boundary holds (existing PRIVATE-marker tests unchanged). experiments._summary records failure_code (None when nothing failed); reporting._failure_diagnosis renders a "Failure diagnosis" banner line mapping known codes to operator guidance (_FAILURE_GUIDANCE), generic guidance for unknown codes, all HTML-escaped. The code survives the evidence-excluded public view, so the default results.json names the cause.
  3. Mutation-found boundary test. read_authoring_file accepts exactly MAX_BYTES (the > vs >= survivor) -- pinned by test_exactly_at_size_limit_is_accepted.
  4. Docs. FAQ: new context_limit_exceeded entry + diagnosis-banner pointer; USAGE §2 documents the sizing, §8.5 cites token healing as related work; CHANGELOG [Unreleased]; README status count corrected.

Tests: tests/test_cycle3.py, 14 tests -- suggestion sizing on a 64- and a 2048-window checkpoint, the fill-warning, tokenizer-less degradation, measurement-failure degradation, allowlist pass-through vs collapse, failure_code in summary and banner, diagnosis emptiness rules, and the three mutation-found boundary/tolerance cases. docs.text:

The lab's documented min_tokens=0 assumption still holds.

Mutation trial, part 2 — scoped to the evaluation heart. cosmic-ray 8.7.0 (same version as Cycle 3) on model_protocol_lab/core.py (662 lines, 1316 mutants total). Scoped to the evaluation-critical definitions — evaluate + its inner helpers record/terminate/abort, first_boundary, _valid_generation, _valid_token_ids, _boundary_text_match — 510 mutants, full 505-test suite per mutant, the lab's own unittest invocation, in-tree like the Cycle-3 trial. The pending_work_items queue is served in random order, so a time-boxed run is an unbiased random sample; the full 510 would take ~15 h sequentially on this 2-CPU machine, so the trial was time-boxed (~90 min, N mutants — final count below) and then stopped.

Methodology note (learned the hard way): cosmic-ray baseline CONFIG --session-file resets the session file — the first attempt wiped the scoped work queue and the exec then "completed" after a single item. The scoped session was rebuilt from the init database and the baseline was verified by running the suite directly instead.

First-run UX walk — two genuine rough edges, both fixed. Walked install → catalog → inspect → fixtures build → doctor → run → report with fresh eyes against a tiny locally-generated GPT-2 checkpoint: 1. README's Status section still said "491 tests" — Cycle 3 corrected 361→491, then added 14 more tests without re-updating the number. Fixed to the true count, and added a regression test (test_readme_test_count_matches_discovered_suite) that discovers the suite and asserts the README's claim matches, so the drift cannot recur. 2. run's stdout printed only {"decision": ..., "selected_candidate": ...} — a new user following the README ("then open examples/sample-report/report.html") was left guessing where their report went. fixtures build already reports its output path; run was inconsistent. The final JSON line now also carries "results" and "report" with the written file paths (captured from save_report's return value).

Everything else on the path was clean: the doctor suggestion (sized --max-new-tokens, window-fit note, boundary-map pointer) produced a command that completed; doctor without --dataset correctly emits a null suggestion; the report renders all sections (outcome grid, decisive fixtures, frontier, template conformance) with no scripts.

All Cycle 1–3 rejections stand (llama.cpp cell killed with primary-source documentation; init-fixtures superseded; histogram subsumed; confidence intervals violate not_estimated; inline-SVG rejected; non-greedy out of scope; per-commit mutation gate infeasible — this cycle's ~2 min/mutant sequential cost on 2 CPUs confirms it).

Plan (selected). 1. run stdout report paths (cli.py, CHANGELOG). 2. README test-count fix + discovery-count regression test (tests/test_cycle4.py). 3. Analyze the mutation-trial sample: fix every real survivor, document equivalents honestly.

Rejected. Any upstream emulation change (no drift); new measurement features (none justified); a larger mutation scope this cycle (the evaluation heart is the named scope; the time-box binds it).

docs.text:

Machine-readable, consistent with fixtures build's output-path reporting. CHANGELOG [Unreleased].

  3. Mutation-trial analysis (56 mutants, evaluation heart). Scoped cosmic-ray trial on core.py (evaluate + record/terminate/abort, first_boundary, _valid_generation, _valid_token_ids, _boundary_text_match; 510 mutants in scope, time-boxed to a random 56-mutant sample — the pending queue is served in random order, so the sample is unbiased): 42 killed, 14 survived. Of the survivors, 12 are equivalent mutants — 11 annotation-position X | None → X <op> None (never evaluated under from __future__ import annotations; verified no get_type_hints/__annotations__ use anywhere in source or tests) and 1 == "cancelled" → <= "cancelled" (behaviorally identical on the reachable inputs: _valid_generation restricts reason to the three literals and the "error" branch returns first, so <= agrees with == on both remaining values). 2 real survivors, both fixed with regression tests (kill verified by applying each mutant manually): (a) result.reason == "error" → is "error" survived because every scripted backend used the interned literal — test_error_reason_detected_by_equality_not_identity feeds a dynamically-built equal string; (b) the seed: int = 0 default → seed: int = 1 survived because every test passed seed explicitly — test_evaluate_default_seed_is_zero pins the default by comparing derived request seeds. Net: 100% of non-equivalent mutants in the sample are killed (42/42 by the pre-existing suite, 2/2 by the new regression tests). Trial hygiene notes: cosmic-ray baseline --session-file resets the session (rebuilt the scoped queue after the first attempt wiped it); always clear __pycache__ after restoring sources mid-trial — a size-preserving mutant (==→is) left a stale pyc that validated against the restored file (pyc headers store second-granularity mtimes) and briefly made a passing test fail.

docs.title: Round 4 — Cycle 1 research (2026-10-14, restarted by owner mandate)
docs.text: All sources observed 2026-10-14. Three parallel research passes fed this cycle.

docs.title: R1 — Exact chat-template structures for 2025–2026 model families
docs.text:
Primary sources: huggingface.co model cards / tokenizer_config.json / chat_template.jinja raw files, HF transformers repo, meta-llama/llama-models prompt_format.md. Plain-text, no-tools renders (hand-renderable core); · = literal.

  • Qwen3 (Qwen/Qwen3-8B, tokenizer_config.json): <|im_start|>{role} {content}<|im_end|> per message; no BOS; open suffix <|im_start|>assistant . Qwen2.5 differs only in always injecting a default system prompt (dropped in Qwen3). Source: https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3-8B
  • DeepSeek V3/R1 (deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V3, DeepSeek-R1): BOS <｜begin▁of▁sentence｜> (full-width bars, U+2581), user = <｜User｜>{content} (no closing token), assistant = <｜Assistant｜>{content}<｜end▁of▁sentence｜>; system concatenated raw with no framing. Open suffix: V3 <｜Assistant｜>, R1 <｜Assistant｜><think> . Source: https://huggingface.co/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V3
  • Mistral v0.3 release (2024-05-22 revision): <s>[INST] {u} [/INST]{a}</s>[INST] {u2} [/INST] — note space before [/INST], no leading space on assistant. The Hub file was rewritten post-release (2024-07-17/2024-08-02: system merging, leading-space assistant, tool blocks) — version-dependent, pin to the release revision. Source: https://huggingface.co/mistralai/Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.3
  • Phi-4 (microsoft/phi-4): <|im_start|>{role}<|im_sep|>{content}<|im_end|> — <|im_sep|>, no trailing newlines. No BOS in template. Open suffix <|im_start|>assistant<|im_sep|>. Phi-5 not released as of 2026-10-14. Source: https://huggingface.co/microsoft/phi-4
  • Gemma 3 (HF transformers tests/models/gemma3/test_processing_gemma3.py @ main — authoritative; repo gated): <bos> <start_of_turn>{role} {content}<end_of_turn> , assistant→model. Vs Gemma 2: system folds into first user turn, 262K tokenizer. Sources: https://github.com/huggingface/transformers, https://ai.google.dev/gemma/docs/formatting
  • Llama 4 (meta-llama/llama-models models/llama4/prompt_format.md): <|header_start|>/ <|header_end|> replace <|start_header_id|>/<|end_header_id|>; <|eot|> replaces <|eot_id|>; new token. BOS `<|begin_of_text|>`. Open suffix `<|header_start|>assistant<|header_end|> `. Stop-token selection (`<|eot|>` vs) not fully verifiable (HF template gated). Source: https://github.com/meta-llama/llama-models/blob/main/models/llama4/prompt_format.md
  • GLM-4-9B (THUDM/glm-4-9b-chat): prefix [gMASK]<sop>, frames <|{role}|> {content} concatenated with no separators. Open suffix <|assistant|>. GLM-4.5/4.6 (zai-org): [gMASK]<sop> , per-message trailing , mandatory empty <think></think> blocks; GLM-5.3-Flash (Aug 2026, MIT): auto-injected <|system|>Reasoning Effort: Max, open suffix <|assistant|><think>. Sources: https://huggingface.co/THUDM/glm-4-9b-chat, https://huggingface.co/zai-org/GLM-4.6
  • Kimi K2 (moonshotai/Kimi-K2-Instruct, chat_template.jinja): <|im_{role}|>{role_name}<|im_middle|>{content}<|im_end|> (role name twice); default Kimi system injected if missing; no BOS emitted. Kimi K3 (Jul 2026): abandoned K2 format for Python-built XTML (<|open|>message role="user"<|sep|>…<|end_of_msg|>). Sources: https://huggingface.co/moonshotai/Kimi-K2-Instruct, https://huggingface.co/moonshotai/Kimi-K3
  • DeepSeek V4.1-Flash (Oct 2026, MIT): same BOS/EOS as V3; <｜System｜> framing, ｜DSML｜ tool markup, auto "Reasoning Effort: 75" preamble, <｜Assistant｜> as a post-user transition token. Source: https://huggingface.co/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash

All are hand-renderable without Jinja for short plain-text conversations (deterministic once branches are fixed: no tools, no images, thinking on/off, system or not). Version-dependent flags: Mistral v0.3 rewrite, Gemma 3 <bos> newline (HF test says yes, third-party docs simplify away), Kimi K2 [BOS] declared-but-unused, Llama 4 stop-token selection, Phi-4 deployment-dependent BOS.

docs.title: R2 — HF transformers vs vLLM stop/boundary semantics (primary: transformers main stopping_criteria.py, vLLM main v1/engine/detokenizer.py, both docs)
docs.text:
• HF StopStringCriteria (wired via generate(..., stop_strings=[...], tokenizer=...)): matching over token IDs with the match table built in string or byte space. Byte-mode selection (_get_stop_string_matching_mode): ByteLevel decoder → byte-level, ByteFallback in decoder config → byte-fallback, else plain string. Table precomputes end-overlaps + valid positions per token including overhangs off either end (["st","opera"], ["las","topper"], ["s","to","pped"] all fire on stop "stop"); runtime fires only on a suffix match. 2026 change: PR #46530 (fixing #46519) added the byte-space path — before it, isolated per-token decodes yielded U+FFFD and silently missed stop strings split across byte-fragment tokens. Stop token is always kept in returned ids; there is no include/exclude option. Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/huggingface/transformers/main/src/transformers/generation/stopping_criteria.py
  • vLLM (V1 detokenizer check_stop_strings): stop strings matched purely in text space on incrementally detokenized output; window start len(output_text) - new_char_count - len(stop) + 1. Stop strings are stripped by default (include_stop_str_in_output=False) — hard divergence from HF, which always keeps them. Overshoot: completing token is kept in token_ids while text truncates to stop start (token_ids/text can disagree). Earliest-completing stop wins (PR #49391; ties → list order); min_tokens gates all stops (PR #22014); reasoning-parser stop scoping (#45846, 2026). Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vllm-project/vllm/main/vllm/v1/engine/detokenizer.py
  • Determinism: HF greedy deterministic under controlled config; vLLM greedy has a documented practical nondeterminism source — continuous batching (batch-sensitive kernels; Thinking Machines Lab, "Defeating Nondeterminism in LLM Inference", Nov 2025). Implication: emulate the stop algorithm, never the token sequence.
  • Flag: both backends stop on EOS by default (HF EosTokenCriteria auto-added; vLLM ignore_eos=False); the lab's "exactly N tokens, no implicit EOS stop" discipline matches neither out of the box and must be configured explicitly on both sides (HF: eos_token_id=None; vLLM: ignore_eos=True, stop=[], stop_token_ids=[], min_tokens=0).

docs.title: R3 — Property-based fuzz testing + single-file HTML reports
docs.text:
• Hypothesis best practices (official docs, v6.168.x): st.text() defaults exclude surrogates; use bare characters() to hunt encode/decode asymmetries; composite strategies for (text, byte-split-index) pairs; RuleBasedStateMachine for streaming decoders; assume() over filtering; derandomize=True for deterministic CI. Source: https://hypothesis.readthedocs.io/en/latest/reference/strategies.html
  • Real tokenizer edge cases: mid-token UTF-8 splits break incremental decode (COLM 2025, "UTF-8 Plumbing: Byte-level Tokenizers Unavoidably Enable LLMs to Generate Ill-formed UTF-8", https://arxiv.org/pdf/2511.05578.pdf); BPE merge fragments spanning stops (HF StopStringCriteria docs overhang cases); SentencePiece byte-fallback (google/sentencepiece api.md); special-token/regular-token ID collisions (tokenizers CHANGELOG v0.10.0, issue #1544); NFC/NFKC normalization shifting byte offsets (tokenizers components docs).
  • Advisory: GHSA-g5f9-3xfg-p9mf (Decepticon v1.1.17, CVE pending, CVSS 9.8) — role-boundary forgery via chat-template special-token literals in untrusted input composed into LLM context (small-vendor source; concept itself well-established in prompt-injection literature). Actionable as a fixture-hygiene audit: flag special-token literals in fixture inputs that collide with candidate formats' special tokens. llama.cpp GHSA (tokenize heap overflow, memory-safety) noted.
  • Report techniques (zero external assets): the lab's report is currently zero-JS; adding small inline JS is an extension, not continuation. Adoptable: CSS-only tabs/<details name> exclusive accordions, sticky anchor TOC, inline SVG heatmaps/sparklines (print-safe), ~15-line sortable tables on data-sort keys (ptyunit pattern), pytest-html-style self-contained guarantee as a tested property (assert no remote URLs in output). Models: pytest-html/pytest-reporter-html1, enes-ak/covsnap single-file report (inline CSS/JS, SVG charts).

docs.title: Cycle 1 build decisions
docs.text:
1. Expand catalog to 11 families (qwen3, deepseek, mistral-v0.3-release, phi4, gemma3, llama4, glm4, kimi2) with exact hand-renders and per-family tests.
  2. Hypothesis property-based fuzz tests for boundary detection (overhang property, UTF-8 byte-split property, NFC property), derandomize=True.
  3. Stop-matrix hardening: vLLM strip-vs-HF-keep text semantics (include_stop_str_in_output), min_tokens gating emulation, documented no-EOS-discipline divergence; regression tests.

docs.title: R2a — Differential testing of inference-backend stop/boundary behavior
docs.text:
Finding: no published methodology specifically differential-tests stop/boundary semantics across backends (firing step, kept-vs-stripped text, stop-reason precedence). Closest tools diff whole outputs, not stop events: infer-check (2026-03-09, https://github.com/nullpointerdepressivedisorder/infer-check, diff command, identical/minor/moderate/severe buckets) and inferlint (engine-specific T1-T14 behavioral tests, no stop focus). The gap is real; the vendors' own bug trackers are the primary-source evidence:

  • vLLM #49391 (2026-07): earliest-completing vs list-order stop selection under speculative decoding (streaming vs non-streaming diverged).
  • vLLM #46113 (2026-06): Rust frontend rposition() vs Python find() -- rightmost vs leftmost match on repeated stop strings leaked the stop.
  • vLLM #47137 (2026-06): streaming vs non-streaming tool-parser/stop divergence (kept-vs-dropped content).
  • SGLang #28802 (2026-06): stop-string vs EOS precedence in one step (speculative decoding); ports vLLM #23938 -- both engines shipped the same bug independently.
  • vLLM #3672 (2024): multi-token stop string not excluded in streaming.
  • lm-eval #3587 (2026-02): wrong until reuse across requests -> near-zero task accuracy (stop-handling bug destroying a benchmark verdict).
  • tnguyen9210/llm-reasoning-methods 8752906 (2026-07): kept "\n\n" stop string produced a bogus empty PRM step, replacing the true last-step score (0.30 vs 0.51).
  • TorchTrade #233 (2026-07): stripped </answer> stop string broke an action parser (live agent defaulted to action 0; mocks passed).
  • vLLM-Omni #4260 (2026-06): stripped </recaption> broke downstream truncation, losing ~30% of CoT.
  • lm-eval belt-and-suspenders: vllm_causallms passes stop=until AND re-strips client-side via postprocess_generated_text; swiss-ai docs note HF-vs-vLLM stop-string visibility differences silently corrupting per-turn responses, plus ~0.5-1pp kernel drift at T=0 bf16.
  • Spec anchors: vLLM/SGLang default strip (include_stop_str_in_output=False); HF keeps the completing token; OpenVINO Model Server documents a streaming-dependent default (excluded when stream=false, included when stream=true).

Recommended divergence classes for mpl diff-backends: firing order, match position (leftmost/rightmost), kept-vs-stripped, stop-vs-EOS precedence, streaming vs non-streaming, min_tokens gating, harness-side normalization reliance.

docs.text:

No existing tool combines format-hypothesis switching + exact per-segment token IDs + stepped boundary detection + special-token audit in an offline terminal REPL: - mohitpandeycs/token-visualizer (browser, js-tiktoken): token IDs + chat-template preview for 90+ models, but no segment-level IDs, hypothesis switching, boundary stepping, or audit; needs a browser. - vLLM Render APIs (/v1/chat/completions/render): closest "render over messages" surface, but needs a running GPU server; no segment IDs, stepping, or audit. - llama.cpp tokenize CLI / /tokenize endpoints: one-shot, needs GGUF. - Ollama / LM Studio: aggregate counts only, no inspector.

Build guidance: stdlib cmd.Cmd (dot-command dispatch, help, completion, cmdqueue scripting) over code.InteractiveConsole; steal sqlite3 CLI conventions verbatim: dot-command meta namespace, abbreviations, multiline with continuation prompt, .help PATTERN, # comments, .read FILE for scripted sessions, startup banner with context prompt. Sources: https://github.com/mohitpandeycs/token-visualizer, https://docs.python.org/3/library/cmd.html, https://sqlite.org/cli.html.

docs.title: Cycle 1 -> 2 transition fix (coordinator, 2026-10-14)
docs.text: test_cycle3.DoctorSuggestionSizingTests.test_suggestion_sizes_new_tokens_to_fit_declared_window started failing after the catalog grew to 14 families: the longest render (kimi3 XTML, verbose) now tokenizes to 106 tokens on the tiny test model's GPT-2 BPE, exceeding its 64-token window, so doctor correctly takes the documented warning path (--max-new-tokens 1 + WARNING) instead of the fit path the test asserted. This is NOT transformers drift and NOT environmental (two builder agents misdiagnosed it; it fails deterministically in isolation): it is catalog growth meeting a fixed-size synthetic window, and the product behavior is correct per the documented design (_longest_prompt_tokens deliberately measures over every catalog candidate). Fix was test-only: the fit-path test now uses a 512-window variant and pins the exact sizing formula new_tokens = max(1, min(64, window - longest)); the warning path remains covered by test_suggestion_warns_when_prompt_fills_window.

docs.text: All sources observed 2026-10-14 via fresh clones of the official repos (full source reads).

docs.title: SGLang (sgl-project/sglang @ 12dc623)
docs.text:
• Stop strings STRIPPED by default (like vLLM, unlike HF): DetokenizerManager.trim_matched_stop (python/sglang/srt/managers/detokenizer_manager.py:190-221) cuts at the leftmost occurrence; no_stop_trim=True keeps (SamplingParams.no_stop_trim, default False; sampling_params.py:153).
  • Multi-stop: FIRST-LISTED wins, NOT earliest-completing — Req._check_str_based_finish (schedule_batch.py:1836-1847) iterates stop_strs in list order; the code even carries # TODO(lmzheng): handle the case where multiple stop strs are hit. Hard divergence from vLLM (PR #49391 earliest-completion). Caveat: with 1 token/step the earlier-completing stop still fires at its own step; list order decides only when ≥2 stops match within one check.
  • No min_tokens equivalent: min_new_tokens exists but only clips the length budget (scheduler.py:2631-2634); the finish path never consults it. vLLM gates all stops behind min_tokens; SGLang gates nothing.
  • Precedence: stop string BEATS EOS in the same step (update_finish_state, schedule_batch.py:1913-1950; shipped fix for SGLang #28802). A stop past max_new_tokens is demoted to a length finish.
  • SGLang-only extras: stop_regex (MAX_STOP_REGEX_COUNT=32, MAX_STOP_REGEX_LEN=256) — neither vLLM nor HF has it; MAX_STOP_COUNT=32.
  • Sources: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang, https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/28802

docs.title: HuggingFace TGI (huggingface/text-generation-inference @ b4adbf2 — upstream HEAD is 2026-03-21, genuinely stale)
docs.text:
• Stop sequences KEPT (like HF, unlike vLLM/SGLang): verified constructively — no stripping code at any layer (StoppingCriteria only detects, tokens.py; full decode incl. stop tokens in models/flash_causal_lm.py, models/causal_lm.py:789-791; Rust v3 forwards, backends/v3/src/backend.rs:513-521; router verbatim, router/src/server.rs:426). Corroborated: langchain_community strips client-side ("remove stop sequences from the end"), which only makes sense if the server keeps them.
  • Multi-stop: FIRST-LISTED wins — StopSequenceCriteria compiles re.escape(s) + "$" suffix matches (tokens.py:131-139); __call__ returns on first matching criterion.
  • No min_tokens equivalent. Precedence: length > EOS > stop-sequence (reverse of SGLang).
  • Genuine quirk: match buffer truncated to last 200 chars (tokens.py:184-187) — a stop sequence longer than 200 chars can never fire. Too narrow for a cell; documented only.
  • Sources: https://github.com/huggingface/text-generation-inference

docs.title: Continuous dev — Cycle 10: Kolibri-1 + LFM2.5-24B-A2B catalog entries + deepseek41 re-verification (2026-10-15, VERIFIED)
docs.text:
Catalog 17 -> 19 families: kolibri (Aleph-Alpha Kolibri-1, released 2026-10-03, Apache 2.0) and lfm25 (LiquidAI LFM2.5-24B-A2B, released 2026-10-13). 787 -> 883 tests, 2819 -> 2843 subtests, all green; ruff check + format clean; mypy clean on catalog.py, cli.py and the new test file.
