Kolibri-1 research (https://huggingface.co/Aleph-Alpha/Kolibri-1): - Evidence tier 1: the official tokenizer_config.json chat_template, byte-verified by an independent fork. - User/assistant turns are standard ChatML (<|im_start|>user {content}<|im_end|> , no BOS) -- so the text-only no-system core renders byte-identical to chatml (pinned in tests/test_cycle10_families.py, including the mutate-set equality modulo the thinking-off branch). - The real template ALWAYS emits a system block, even with no system message: <|im_start|>system # Reasoning effort <SENTENCE>[+ user system content]<|im_end|> . SENTENCE is effort-dependent; the lab has no effort knob, so the catalog documents the DEFAULT-effort (unset -> "high") behavior and pins ONLY the byte-verified sentence prefix ("Reasoning effort is set to high. Think carefully through...") -- the wording beyond it is deliberately not asserted. The system role is not modeled in Format (same convention as mistral_large's [SYSTEM_PROMPT] frame and gemma4's system turn). - Thinking ON (default): the generation prompt ends at <|im_start|>assistant (the model opens <think> itself). Thinking OFF: the generation prompt prefills an empty think block (<|im_start|>assistant <think> </think> ). Design decision: the thinking-off branch rides the mutate path as "kolibri/thinking-off" (candidates()), not a second catalog entry -- it is a generation-prompt branch of the same template, and the mutate path is the lab's existing mechanism for generation-prompt variants (BOS/prefix local repairs). No other family gains a branch (pinned by a subTest loop). EOS is <|im_end|> (a generation stop, not a Format field).

LFM2.5-24B-A2B research (https://huggingface.co/LiquidAI/LFM2.5-24B-A2B): - Evidence tier 2: the official model card plus the HF blog rendered example. - Rendered: <|startoftext|><|im_start|>system {system}<|im_end|> <|im_start|>user {content}<|im_end|> <|im_start|>assistant <think> -- <|startoftext|> BOS, ChatML-like frames, and -- unlike LFM2 -- the 24B variant always thinks (generation prompt appends <think> ). - Documented caveats (pinned as test constants, never asserted in code): whether <|startoftext|> comes from the bos_token field or a template literal is UNVERIFIED (byte-identical either way); whether the system block is auto-injected or merely illustrative in the card example is UNVERIFIED (and the system role is unmodelable regardless).

DeepSeek V4.1 system-framing re-verification (CONFIRMED -- catalog claim stands, no code change): - The catalog claimed V4.1 frames system messages as <｜System｜>{content} (fullwidth), unlike V3's raw concatenation; third-party docs of the sibling V4 official encoder suggested system text may render raw. - Primary-source re-check 2026-10-15: the official model card (deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, "Prompt Encoding") states the release ships no Jinja chat template and points to the encoding/encoding.py reference implementation; a direct quote of that official encoding shows the system block opened with the fullwidth System frame ("<｜System｜>Reasoning Effort: 75 (range 1-100, ...)"); the official deepseek-ai/deepseek-recipe repo defines a dedicated V4.1 System role token (id 128799) -- no such frame exists for V4. Sources: https://huggingface.co/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-recipe, https://github.com/corvous/hi-blue/blob/HEAD/docs/prompting/deepseek-v4-1-flash-guide.md - Contrast (sibling V4, NOT V4.1): the official V4 encoder (encoding_dsv4.py) renders system RAW -- <｜begin▁of▁sentence｜>{system}<｜User｜>{question}<｜Assistant｜>... ("System content is bare text with no wrapper"). Source: https://github.com/waybarrios/vllm-mlx/pull/676 - Conclusion: the V3/V4-vs-V4.1 difference the catalog documents is real -- V4.1 added the frame, V4 never had it. Regression test added (tests/test_cycle10_families.py, Deepseek41SystemFramingTests): pins the documented frame constant against the catalog's escape-composed frame, pins the render carries no system frame and no effort preamble (the latter deliberately omitted per the catalog comment), and pins the V4.1-vs-V3 modeled delta is exactly the chat-mode <｜Assistant｜><think> open suffix.

Deferred (out of window, TIER-3 only): nemotron35, muse_glimmer, laguna -- no primary-source template evidence (official tokenizer_config.json chat_template or model-card render) was available; only third-party/secondary claims. Per the lab's evidence discipline (primary sources only; tier-3 claims never become catalog entries), they are documented here and deferred, not added.

docs.title: Continuous dev — logprob-diagnostic wiring (2026-10-15)
docs.text:
Built the Cycle 1 STAR PICK's "report wiring planned next": run --logprob-diagnostic wires the existing model_protocol_lab/scoring.py engine into the run flow and the HTML report (DEVELOPMENT_PLAN.md §9.3–§9.5). Tests-first: tests/test_cycle10_logprob.py (23 tests) written before the implementation, red→green.

What changed: 1. model_protocol_lab/experiments.py: logprob_diagnostic(backend, result, fixtures) — for every search candidate × fixture, teacher-forces the fixture's expected answer (score_target_logprobs over prompt_ids + encode(expected)) after the recorded prompt. Returns per-fixture scores (status/reason/total/mean/token counts/byte length), per-candidate aggregates (§9.4: total, token-weighted mean, scored token count, target byte length), and a plain-language interpretation separating "greedy derailed" (mean ≥ −2.0 nats/token on failed fixtures) from "weights don't know" (mean < −5.0); between the bands it withholds judgment. Bands are declared heuristics in the payload's thresholds. Alignment refusals surface as unavailable with the engine's fixed reason codes -- never raised, never guessed. The input result dict is never mutated; the selection rule is untouched (diagnostic only). NaN/inf degrades aggregates to None (defense in depth; results.json is written with allow_nan=False). Deterministic: no timestamps, fixed ordering. 2. model_protocol_lab/cli.py: opt-in --logprob-diagnostic flag on run (verified in live --help); runs after search inside the diagnostics-must-not-fail-the-run guard, storing result["logprob_diagnostic"]. 3. model_protocol_lab/reporting.py: "Log-likelihood diagnostic" HTML section (self-contained, no new CSS/JS): per-candidate total/mean logprob table, one plain-language reading per candidate, per-fixture scores in <details>; degrades to an explicit unavailable note; renders nothing when the key is absent, so the byte-identical sample-report golden test still holds. Every model/fixture-derived string escaped (hostile fixture IDs / candidate names pinned by test). 4. Docs: docs/USAGE.md §8.9 + §6 section list; CHANGELOG.md [Unreleased]; every run flag re-verified against live --help (pre-existing gap found: --seed is not documented in USAGE.md).

Verification: 23 new tests green; test_cycle9_scoring.py, test_sample_report.py (byte-identical golden) green; ruff check + format clean on all touched files; mypy clean on model_protocol_lab. Full-suite note: concurrent sibling agents are editing catalog.py and adding their own test_cycle10_* files in the same tree -- one transient test_e2e subprocess failure during the full run traced to a sibling's mid-edit catalog state (passes in isolation; not this change), and the README test-count pin (test_readme_test_count_matches_discovered_suite) now fails because the discovered count moved (+23 here, plus sibling additions while their suite is not green). Left for the coordinator per the Cycle 1 precedent (coordinator-owned pin).

Sources: DEVELOPMENT_PLAN.md §9.3–§9.5 (the design being implemented); https://github.com/EleutherAI/lm-evaluation-harness/blob/main/docs/task_guide.md (loglikelihood request type — scores a fixed target string by teacher forcing, corroborating the probe design); https://www.shedge.com/metrics/llm-benchmarks/helm-benchmark/ (HELM adapter token-probability measurements). No new external sources needed: the engine and backend primitives already existed.

docs.title: 2026-10-15 -- Red-team fix round: H1/M1/L1 (diffbackends bounds + loader sanitization)
docs.text:
What changed and why:

  1. H1 (quadratic CPU hang): _checked_ids in model_protocol_lab/ diffbackends.py previously capped every token-id sequence at 131072, but emulate_vllm_holdback/emulate_sglang_stop do one backend.decode(prefix) per output step -- O(n^2) total. Measured on the repo's own linear stub (TableBackend-style O(k) decode): 0.22 s / 0.49 s / 2.31 s at n = 1000/2000/4000 for one stop, i.e. tens of minutes at the old cap -- reachable via the CLI and via divergence_section_data over hostile recorded observations. Fix: split the bound into two named constants. MAX_OUTPUT_IDS = 4096 guards the quadratic term: at the cap a single stop completes in ~2-3 s on the reference stub, and 4096 is exactly mpl run --max-new-tokens' own cap, so the lab can never record a longer generated output (legitimate inputs are never rejected). Prompts keep MAX_PROMPT_IDS = 131072 (4x the 32768 max context window): prompt tokens are decoded once each (linear cost) and recorded observations legitimately carry long prompts. _observation_ids applies the output cap to output_ids and the prompt cap to input_ids, so over-cap hostile observations are skipped (section omitted), not hung.
  2. M1 (unbounded stop texts): _checked_stop_texts had no length/count bound -- a 10 MB stop text would balloon json.dumps(result) (verbatim in records + {stop_text!r} details) and the list-based dedup was O(m^2). Fix: MAX_STOP_TEXT_LEN = 1024 chars per stop (stop_text_too_long), MAX_STOP_TEXTS = 16 deduped stops per call (too_many_stop_texts). Rationale: a stop string is a needle, not a document (sibling prompt/output text caps are 1 MB); each stop adds five emulated cells, two of them quadratic, so 16 keeps the absolute worst case (~40 s at both caps on the reference stub) advertised and bounded. Dedup is now set-based (linear, order-preserving) and runs before the count check. The diff-backends CLI path flows through the same validation (pinned: exit 1 with the fixed code, hostile text not echoed), and the run diagnosis second hop (backend.decode(winner_boundary) -> divergence_section_data) hits the identical check -- a hostile tokenizer's huge decode degrades to "section omitted", pinned by test.
  3. L1 (hostile-checkpoint exception text on the terminal): debug.py's run_debug interpolated the loader exception into stderr and only caught (ValueError, OSError) (uncaught traceback otherwise); diff-backends' ValueError branch claimed a fixed vocabulary but PreTrainedTokenizerFast parse failures can echo checkpoint bytes. Fix: doctor._loader_failure_code -- an exact-match allowlist over the one genuinely fixed code (oversized_tokenizer_file); everything else collapses to tokenizer_load_failed. Both CLI paths use it inside a blanket except Exception sanitization boundary (cli.py:713-730 pattern). The debug REPL's onecmd error path now strips terminal-control characters from exception text via the existing _sanitize_display.

Verification: 26 new tests in tests/test_cycle10_security.py (stub backends only, deterministic); existing cap-pinning test in tests/test_cycle7_properties.py updated to the new constant; ruff check + format clean; mypy clean on model_protocol_lab. Docs: docs/USAGE.md §11 gained an "Input bounds" paragraph documenting every bound, its rationale, and its fixed code; CHANGELOG.md [Unreleased] records all three fixes.

docs.title: Continuous dev — Cycle 2: SGLang column for mpl diff-backends (2026-10-15, VERIFIED)
docs.text:
Implements the Cycle 1 recommendation ("Recommendation (for Cycle 2)"): mpl diff-backends gains an SGLang column (sglang_stop) and three new divergence classes, each grounded in the cited source lines:

  • backends.emulate_sglang_stop: ports Req._check_str_based_finish (schedule_batch.py:1836-1847) -- the first output step whose decoded text contains the stop string fires -- and DetokenizerManager.trim_matched_stop (detokenizer_manager.py:190-221), which cuts the returned text at the leftmost stop occurrence by default (no_stop_trim=False, sampling_params.py:153): stripped like vLLM, unlike HF. Takes deliberately NO min_tokens parameter: upstream min_new_tokens only clips the length budget (scheduler.py:2631-2634); the finish path never consults it.
  • MULTI_STOP_SELECTION (high): SGLang's check iterates stop_strs in list order (first-listed wins; the code carries # TODO(lmzheng): handle the case where multiple stop strs are hit) vs vLLM's earliest-completion rule -- min(stop_index + len(stop_str)), ties broken by list order (vLLM PR #49391, pinned by tests/detokenizer/test_check_stop_strings.py; Rust parity in PR #50200). Port: the SGLang winner is the fired stop with the smallest firing step, ties by list order (the Cycle 1 caveat: with 1 token/step the earlier-completing stop still fires at its own step); the vLLM winner ports the PR #49391 formula off the strip/keep cells' firing steps and trimmed texts. Re-verified 2026-10-15 from the PR descriptions: #49391 selects "the one whose match completes earliest in the text (min(stop_index + len(stop_str))), breaking ties by stop-list order"; #50200 confirms "Python selects the one that completes earliest in the text, ties broken by list order".
  • NO_MIN_TOKENS_GATE (medium): the SGLang column on the existing MIN_TOKENS_GATED class -- a stop vLLM's min_tokens gate blocks still fires under sglang_stop.
  • STR_OVER_EOS_PRECEDENCE (high): stop string and EOS fire in the same step, so precedence decides the outcome and the engines disagree -- SGLang's shipped fix for #28802 gives the stop string the win (update_finish_state runs the str-based check before the token-based one, schedule_batch.py:1913-1950; corroborated 2026-10-15 by the fix PR "reorders the finish condition checks in update_finish_state to ensure that stop strings take precedence over stop/EOS tokens in the same step"), while TGI's documented precedence is length > EOS > stop-sequence (EOS beats the stop string -- the reverse of SGLang).

Deliberate exclusions, as recommended: NO TGI cell -- every TGI stop rule is covered by composition of the existing cells (kept sequences = the hf_stop_string cell; first-listed multi-stop = the sglang_stop selection rule; no min_tokens = the ungated sglang_stop path; EOS-beats-stop = the documented contrast in STR_OVER_EOS_PRECEDENCE); SGLang stop_regex gets a USAGE.md note only (outside stop-string scope).

Verification: 27 new tests in tests/test_cycle10_sglang.py (each SGLang rule vs vLLM/HF behavior, all three new classes, the no-TGI-cell rationale, hostile-string escaping in the report, determinism); existing severity/count pins in tests/test_cycle7_divergence.py and tests/test_cycle7_properties.py updated from 5 to 8 classes; the pairs_verdict one-liner now reads "HF vs vLLM vs SGLang stop semantics: …". ruff check + format clean; mypy clean. Docs: USAGE.md §11 (new column, new classes, flags re-verified against live --help, no-TGI-cell rationale, stop_regex note), CHANGELOG.md [Unreleased].

docs.title: 2026-10-15 -- Residual fix: observation-count bound on divergence_section_data
docs.text:
What changed and why:

The H1/M1/L1 red-team fix cycle bounded each observation's ids (MAX_OUTPUT_IDS/MAX_PROMPT_IDS) and the stop texts (MAX_STOP_TEXT_LEN/MAX_STOP_TEXTS), but left one residual: the count of observations divergence_section_data processes was unbounded. The run diagnosis path hands it the winner's recorded observations, and each observation costs one full diff_backends emulation (~2-3 s worst case per stop text at the output cap on the reference stub) -- so a hostile results.json with millions of recorded observations would burn open-ended hours, even though every individual observation was "valid".

Fix: named constant MAX_DIVERGENCE_OBSERVATIONS = 512. Rationale, all from the lab's own caps: the section consumes only the winner's recorded observations (search + held-out fixture outputs), and experiments.py rejects fixture splits above 100 search / 100 held-out fixtures, so a legitimate run hands over at most 200 observations. 512 is comfortably above that maximum (2.56x headroom) but far below DoS territory. No legitimate run is affected; the bound can only engage on inputs no real experiment can produce.

Contract (deliberate): degrade by omission, never fail the run. Over-count input processes the first 512 observations in input order and records the fixed-vocabulary observations_truncated: true plus observations_total (the offered count) and observations_processed (the bound) in the section dict; the HTML report renders an explicit "Observation bound reached" note naming both numbers. No exception is raised (a raise would be swallowed by cli.py's diagnosis try/except and silently drop the whole section; omission keeps the first-512 verdicts). Per-observation skip semantics (non-dicts, invalid ids) are unchanged, including inside the first-512 window. Deterministic: the same first-N prefix truncates every run. Boundary N is accepted fully; N+1 truncates.

Verification: 8 new tests in tests/test_cycle11_bounds.py (stub backend only, deterministic): named-constant pin, full processing at N, truncation flag/counts at N+1 with first-N order, hostile-scale input finishes fast without raising, per-observation skip contract preserved under truncation, same-input determinism, all-unusable first-N still degrades to an omitted section, tuple input handled. ruff check + format clean; mypy clean. Docs: docs/USAGE.md §11 "Input bounds" paragraph, CHANGELOG.md [Unreleased] (new ### Fixed block), this entry.

docs.title: Drift check 2026-10-15 (all backends NO CHANGE)
docs.text: Re-verified vLLM, HF transformers, SGLang, TGI stop/decoding semantics against 2026-10-01..2026-10-15 upstream. All pinned behaviors stand (vLLM #49391 earliest-completion, HF stop-kept, SGLang first-listed + stop-beats-EOS #28802, TGI stale @b4adbf2). No divergence class or emulation cell invalidated. WATCH: sgl-project/sglang#42466 (open, unmerged, CI failing) proposes earliest-start multi-stop selection — would change MULTI_STOP_SELECTION if merged; differs from both current SGLang (first-listed) and vLLM (earliest-completion). Re-check on next drift sweep.

docs.title: Continuous dev — Cycle 11: Nemotron 3.5 Lightning + Muse Glimmer 30B + Poolside Laguna 2.1 catalog entries (2026-10-15, VERIFIED)
docs.text:
Catalog 19 -> 22 families: nemotron35 (NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning, released 2026-08-11), muse_glimmer (Meta Muse Glimmer 30B, released 2026-08-10, Apache 2.0), laguna (Poolside Laguna 2.1, Jul 2026, OpenMDW-1.1). 891 -> 915 tests (24 new in tests/test_cycle11_families.py); ruff check + format clean; mypy clean on catalog.py and the new test file. Three pre-existing catalog-listing tests (cycle5/6/7) updated to 22 families; the e2e module-catalog set gained all three families; the cycle-10 thinking-off cross-catalog invariant gained the nemotron35 exception; the <|im_start|> audit collision counts went 5 -> 6 (+nemotron35); README "19-family" claims updated to 22 and the test-count claim to 915 (new regression test pins the naming); CHANGELOG [Unreleased] extended. Full suite green except pre-existing environmental failures in this sandbox (torch/hypothesis/transformers not installed: 5 loader errors, the diff-backends tiny-tokenizer test, and the README-count test whose discovery is shrunken by those same missing modules) -- all unrelated to this change.

Tier promotion (revises the Cycle 10 deferral). Cycle 10 deferred these three as TIER-3 (only secondary claims, no primary-source template evidence). This cycle re-examined them against newly verified evidence and promotes all three to TIER-2 (official sources + independent byte-level corroboration): - laguna: the renderers library's LagunaXS21Renderer/LagunaS21Renderer are token-exact parity-verified against apply_chat_template on the official chat_template.jinja (upstream rev 575f0f28); the PR texts (#99, #111) were re-read directly this cycle and corroborate every modeled string (hugging tags, thinking gates, </assistant> terminator, gen prompts, empty-system opt-out). - nemotron35: the official HF model card + NeMo SFT docs + the community osaurus byte-level renderer (PR #2360) agree on the frames and thinking tails; the BOS question stays explicitly UNVERIFIED/conflicting at official level and is pinned as such (no BOS token asserted). - muse_glimmer: the official meta-oss-cookbook quickstart + HF transformers model docs + HF blog walkthrough agree on the frame protocol; the gen prompt is community-refined (the simpler <|start|>assistant alternative was superseded) and is marked tier-2/community-corroborated.

Nemotron 3.5 Lightning research (https://huggingface.co/nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Lightning-30B-A3B-BF16): - Per-turn frames are ChatML (<|im_start|>{role} {content}<|im_end|> ) -- so the text-only core renders byte-identical to chatml except the generation tail (pinned in tests/test_cycle11_families.py, including the mutate-set equality modulo the thinking-off branch). - Thinking ON (default -- enable_thinking defaults true): the generation prompt ends at <|im_start|>assistant <think> (the base entry's open_suffix). Thinking OFF: the generation prompt prefills an EMPTY think block, <|im_start|>assistant <think></think> -- with NO trailing newlines, unlike kolibri/thinking-off's " " tail (the byte difference is pinned). - Design decision: the base entry is the thinking-on DEFAULT branch; the thinking-off branch rides the mutate path as "nemotron35/thinking-off" (candidates()), a generation-prompt branch of the same template, not a second catalog entry (kolibri/thinking-off convention). - CRITICAL: BOS behavior is UNVERIFIED/conflicting at official level. The catalog models bos="" as an ABSENCE-OF-EVIDENCE placeholder and does NOT assert any BOS token -- a test pins both the modeled value and the source-level UNVERIFIED marker in the catalog comment, and asserts no BOS-like token appears in the render. - Sources: the HF model card above, https://github.com/nvidia-nemo/nemotron/blob/HEAD/docs/nemotron/lightning35/sft.md, https://github.com/osaurus-ai/osaurus/pull/2360

Muse Glimmer 30B research (https://github.com/meta-models/meta-oss-cookbook/blob/HEAD/quickstart/README.md): - Frame: <|begin_of_text|><|start|>{role}<|message|>{content}<|eot|> -- no newline anywhere. Assistant turns use recipient channels: the reasoning trace is <|start|>assistant to=self<|message|>... and the user-facing reply <|start|>assistant to=user<|message|>...<|eot|> -- the lab's plain-text no-reasoning hypothesis models the assistant turn as to=user and does NOT render the to=self trace (same class of omission as kimi3's empty think block and glm45/glm53's empty : the reasoned-content branch is not a hypothesis). - Generation prompt: <|start|>assistant to=user<|message|> -- COMMUNITY-REFINED (tier 2/community-corroborated); the simpler <|start|>assistant alternative was superseded (pinned: the open_suffix equals the refined form and not the simple form). - Documented, NOT modeled: system messages render the caller text with " Reasoning strength: high. # Valid recipients: "self", "user"." APPENDED after the caller content (single newlines -- not a standalone preamble block); the system role is not modeled in Format (same convention as mistral_large/gemma4/kolibri). EOS is <|end_of_text|> (id 200001); is the end-of-MESSAGE marker, NOT a stop token. All three are pinned as documented test constants only. - Closest-family diff (pinned): llama3 shares the <|begin_of_text|> BOS, but every frame differs. - Sources: the quickstart README above, http://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/main/model_doc/muse_glimmer, https://github.com/huggingface/blog/blob/main/muse-glimmer.md

Poolside Laguna 2.1 research (https://huggingface.co/poolside/Laguna-XS-2.1): - Frames ("hugging tags", no inner newlines): <user>{content}</user>, <tool_response>{content}</tool_response>, <system>{content}</system>. - Reasoning gated on enable_thinking -- on: every assistant turn renders <think>{reasoning}</think> VERBATIM (empty included); off: turns open with a bare </think> and reasoning is dropped. Gen prompt: <assistant> + (<think> | </think>), no trailing newline. Completed assistant turns terminate with </assistant> (tier-2 via the renderers PR text: "the two opener tokens are unsampled scaffold; everything through the sampled is the model's emission"). - Design decision: the base entry is XS-2.1 DEFAULTS (enable_thinking FALSE -- documented choice): gen prompt <assistant></think>, history assistant turns <assistant></think>{content}</assistant>. S-2.1 (enable_thinking defaults TRUE) is the "laguna/thinking-on" mutate-path variant -- the kolibri/thinking-off convention: a generation-prompt branch of the same template, not a second catalog entry. Its history assistant turns render an EMPTY think block verbatim (<assistant><think></think>{content}</assistant>) -- the lab's deterministic no-reasoning hypothesis (the reasoned-content branch is not a hypothesis here, kimi3 convention). - EOS is 〈|EOS|〉 -- DECODE-ONLY, never rendered in the prompt (documented, not modeled; pinned as a constant that must not leak into any render). BOS: no BOS token appears in any tier-2 render; modeled as empty with the absence-of-evidence caveat (contrast nemotron35, whose BOS is explicitly conflicting). - System role: not modeled (lab convention). The upstream template ships a default Poolside system prompt, but an empty caller system message suppresses the <system> block entirely -- and the lab never sends system messages, so the no-system render modeled here is byte-identical either way; the default-prompt wording is deliberately NOT asserted. - Sources: the HF model card above, https://github.com/PrimeIntellect-ai/renderers/pull/99, https://github.com/PrimeIntellect-ai/renderers/pull/111

Watched, NOT shipped: Mistral Large 4 and Reflection Beam are not released -- deliberately not catalog entries. Tracked as watched; a future cycle may add them once primary-source template evidence exists (the tier-3 bar from Cycle 10 still applies: tier-3 claims never become catalog entries).

Strings deliberately not pinned: nemotron35's BOS token (UNVERIFIED / conflicting at official level -- see the catalog comment); the wording of Laguna's default Poolside system prompt (suppressed in the lab's no-system render either way); the muse_glimmer to=self reasoning-trace content and the system-appendage beyond the documented suffix (unmodelable roles / generation stops, documented only); the laguna reasoned-content branch (non-deterministic, kimi3 convention).

docs.title: Continuous dev — Cycle 12: static template↔tokenizer portability matrix (2026-10-15, VERIFIED)
docs.text:
Builds the research recommendation from docs/RESEARCH_PORTABILITY_2026-10-15.md (kept as-is): doctor --portability-matrix SECOND_CHECKPOINT checks every catalog candidate's special-token inventory (fixtures._extract_special_tokens) against the second checkpoint's tokenizer -- registered in added/special tokens, encodes as exactly one token id, encoded id == registered id -- via the new core.template_tokenizer_compatibility, a deliberate generalization of core.check_boundary_portability (same probe-must-not-fail-caller, fixed-vocabulary, exact-token-ID discipline). Tokenizer only, never weights: one tokenizer load + O(candidates × tokens) encodes, reusing doctor's _build_primary_tokenizer path, the 128 MB tokenizer.json cap, and the _loader_failure_code sanitization boundary (hostile checkpoint bytes never reach the terminal).

The asymmetry is the design and is stated loudly everywhere (report section, CLI table, docs/USAGE.md §2): incompatible ⇒ the format cannot be that checkpoint's native format ⇒ re-running the experiment there is scientifically pointless, answered at ~zero compute. compatible ⇒ the markers are merely encodable ⇒ NO prediction about experimental success (weights decide). No portability score is emitted anywhere; a recursive key-scan test pins that no score/prediction/transfer key can appear in the section. BOS-less formats (8 catalog families, bos="") skip the BOS requirement by design (bos_skipped per row -- the inventory simply holds no BOS literal); empty inventories and encode failures report unknown, never compatible. The matrix is triage, never a gate: it cannot fail the doctor verdict, and an unusable second checkpoint yields unavailable with a fixed-vocabulary detail.

Verification: 38 new tests in tests/test_cycle12_portability.py -- incompatible pinned for all three failure modes (unregistered / fragments / id_mismatch), unknown for empty inventory and degraded encodes, first- failure-in-inventory-order, degrade-beats-incompatible, BOS-less skip both ways, hostile dirs (missing / oversized-sparse / malformed-JSON with hostile marker bytes / non-dict doc / unloadable tokenizer) all collapse to fixed codes, determinism (two runs byte-identical), CLI flag wiring (stdout stays parseable JSON, table + ASYMMETRY WARNING on stderr), and a no-transfer-claim scan over the whole section. 915 -> 953 tests (README count updated; the pinning test passes); ruff check + format clean; mypy clean on all 14 source files.

Deliberate exclusions: no primary-checkpoint matrix row (the research's "natural second row" -- deferred; the experiment's own checkpoint is covered by template_conformance, and the flag's question is strictly "can I rule out checkpoint B without running it?"); no behavioral template-inference feature (rejected by the research as speculative science); no AutoTokenizer-vs-minimal-loader validation on real checkpoints yet -- the encode path is the same Rust tokenizer the file defines, and behavior is pinned against tokenizers-built synthetic checkpoints; operators should still verify encode behavior against the checkpoint's intended tokenizer before trusting results (USAGE.md §3 already carries that caution for the primary path).

docs.title: Continuous dev — Cycle 13: Ling-3.1-flash catalog entry (2026-10-15, VERIFIED)
docs.text:
Catalog 22 -> 23 families: ling (inclusionAI/Ling-3.1-flash, released 2026-10-15, MIT; https://huggingface.co/inclusionAI/Ling-3.1-flash). Evidence TIER-1: the official chat_template.jinja ("Bailing V3"), read and derived line-by-line by hand (preserved at docs/evidence/ling31-chat-template.jinja); the tokenizer_config.json bos_token field was verified live against the HF repo (read 2026-10-15): <|startoftext|>.

What the template says (plain-text, no-tools core): an always-emitted system block (with system message X: <role>SYSTEM</role>X detailed thinking on<|role_end|>; without: <role>SYSTEM</role>detailed thinking on<|role_end|>); user <role>HUMAN</role>{content}<|role_end|>; assistant history <role>ASSISTANT</role> <think></think>{content} <|role_end|>; generation prompt <role>ASSISTANT</role> <think> (thinking defaults ON, jinja line 12). The catalog models the default thinking-on render; thinking-off prefills an empty think block and rides the --mutate path as ling/thinking-off (kolibri/thinking-off convention). The system block is documented, not modeled (lab convention); tool-call branches, reasoning-content branches, and the multi-step tool scan are out of scope for the plain-text core.

EOS correction (verified, not assumed): the official eos_token field is <|role_end|> -- NOT <|endoftext|>, which is the pad_token and a special added token. Documented in the catalog comment; Format asserts no EOS string.

BOS caveat (documented): the jinja template itself emits no BOS literal and add_bos_token is false; the entry takes the config's bos_token (lfm25 convention), so a raw apply_chat_template call would not emit it -- noted in the catalog comment.

954 -> 964 tests (10 new in tests/test_cycle13_families.py: byte-exact render pins, thinking-off mutation pin, dedup-key no-collision pin, diff-vs-all-other-22-families pin, README naming/count pin); the cycle-10/cycle-11 thinking-branch invariants and the cycle-11 README count pin updated for the new family; README "22-family" claims updated to 23 and the test-count claim to 964; CHANGELOG [Unreleased] extended.

docs.title: Continuous dev — Cycle 13: mpl diff-reports iterate-and-compare tool (2026-10-15)
docs.text:
Research recommendation, no external research needed (pure local tooling): the core operator workflow is iterate-and-compare -- tweak a template or fixture, re-run, see what changed -- and eyeballing two HTML reports is imprecise. mpl diff-reports OLD_RESULTS NEW_RESULTS (new module model_protocol_lab/diffreports.py, wired into the CLI at the two ANCHOR sites) compares two results.json files deterministically: same inputs → byte-identical output, no model, no network, exact comparisons only (no fuzzy matching).

Compared axes: decision flip (old → new), winner change, per-candidate pass/fail verdict flips on search and held-out (held-out verdicts exist only for each run's winner; others report absent), per-fixture outcome diffs per candidate (pass requires exact answer + boundary token match, the run criterion; changed-only by default, --all lists everything), and a config-drift warning section -- the classic operator mistake of comparing runs that were never comparable. Drift flags different candidate families (base names; results.json does not store the --family flag, so this is the exact family signal available), candidate sets, per-candidate boundary token IDs, --max-new-tokens, backend fingerprints (model identity), and fixture sets (when evidence exists). Per-fixture comparison needs --include-evidence on both runs and degrades loudly otherwise; exit 0 on success even when differences are found (differences are the output, not a failure).

Security posture mirrors the repo's bounded-reader discipline: 32 MB cap (results_too_large), regular-file-only reads via the os.open(O_NONBLOCK) + fstat pattern from datasets.load_dataset, duplicate-field and non-finite rejection with fixed codes, shape validation of only the compared axes (everything else degrades to unknown rather than failing), and control-character stripping of operator-visible identifiers before they reach stderr. All failures map to fixed ValueError codes -- no tracebacks, no file content in error text.

Verification: 30 new tests in tests/test_cycle13_diffreports.py -- decision/winner flips, verdict flips (search, held-out, absent, malformed summary → unknown), per-fixture diffs (changed-only default, --all, deterministic (stage, candidate, fixture) ordering), config drift for all six fields with fixed field order, identical-run → "no differences", missing-evidence degradation, hostile inputs (malformed JSON, duplicate keys, NaN, non-UTF-8, oversized, FIFO, missing paths, deep nesting, directory resolution) all collapsing to fixed codes with no tracebacks, stderr sanitization of hostile identifiers, byte-identical determinism, and CLI wiring (JSON on stdout, summary on stderr, exit 0 with differences). ruff check + format clean; mypy clean on all 15 source files.

Deliberate exclusions: no fuzzy fixture matching (exact fixture-ID comparison only -- cross-fixture alignment is a research question, not a diff feature); no HTML report comparison (results.json is the source of truth); no verdict inference from missing summaries (degrades to unknown, shown as such); the --family flag is not recovered (not stored in results.json -- candidate base names are the exact available signal, documented as such).

docs.title: 2026-10-15 -- Red-team fix round: diffreports H1/M1-M3/L1 + finding 6 documentation
docs.text:
What changed and why:

A red-team pass over the cycle-13 mpl diff-reports code found six findings; findings 1-5 were fixed (each pinned by a regression test in tests/test_cycle13_diffreports.py), finding 6 documented in a code comment with no behavior change.

  • H1 (CI-blocking): the README test-count pin test shells out to python -m pytest --collect-only, but pytest was not in the pyproject.toml dev extras or installed by .github/workflows/ci.yml -- the pin test would fail deterministically in CI. Fix: added pytest>=8.0 to the dev extras (pytest is the suite's actual runner; it belongs there). Verified from the workflow file that both jobs installing the suite (static installs .[dev], test installs .[dev,hf]) pull the dev extra, so pytest is present wherever the suite runs. No skip guard added -- the conditional did not trigger. Pin test verified passing in the repo venv (README count updated 994 -> 1000 for the 6 new tests).

  • M1: render_summary interpolated decision["old"]/["new"] (hostile results.json strings) and the source path labels raw into stderr -- ANSI escape / OSC sequence injection. Fix: both now pass through the existing _display_id sanitizer, like every other operator-visible identifier.

  • M2: _config_snapshot's name not in names list-scan dedup was O(n^2) and hung ~1.5h on 800k candidate names. Fix: set-based dedup preserving first-occurrence order. Regression test holds 50k distinct names to <10s (measured well under 1s).

  • M3: _search_verdicts dropped per-candidate planned counts, so planned 2 vs 50 (no evidence) reported identical: True -- a "pass" verdict means "all planned fixtures passed", making the comparison a lie of omission. Fix: _search_verdicts now also returns the per-candidate planned counts (first-entry wins, None for malformed/missing summaries), and the diff emits planned:<candidate> config-drift entries (fixed order, after the five _drift fields) which render in the stderr drift section.

  • L1: identical: True plus "identical on every compared axis" was reported when evidence existed on only one side -- a whole axis was never compared. Fix: evidence-presence asymmetry now sinks identical (with a new machine-readable summary["evidence_asymmetric"] flag), and the identical-run stderr line names the axes actually compared (decision, winner, candidate verdicts, configuration, plus per-fixture evidence only when both sides carry it).

  • Finding 6 (theoretical): duplicate fixture IDs inside one candidate's observations are last-wins, while duplicate candidate names in "search" are first-wins. Documented in a comment at _fixture_outcomes; behavior deliberately unchanged -- mpl run never emits either duplicate, so reconciling the conventions would change only hostile-input behavior.

Verification: 6 new tests in tests/test_cycle13_diffreports.py (hostile decision/label sanitization with ANSI + OSC payloads, config-snapshot scaling, planned-count drift, evidence-asymmetry sinks identical, identical summary names compared axes) plus one assertion added to the existing missing-evidence test. Full suite: 964 unittest-discovered tests OK (README pin: 1000 pytest-collected). ruff check + format clean; mypy clean on all 15 source files. Docs: CHANGELOG.md [Unreleased] ### Fixed, this entry.

docs.title: 2026-10-15 -- Red-team fix round (follow-up): diffreports drift-field sanitization + README pin test debuggability
docs.text:
A follow-up red-team pass over the cycle-13 mpl diff-reports code produced two small genuine low-severity findings. Both are fixed and regression-pinned.

  • Finding 1 (Low): render_summary interpolated the config-drift field string raw into stderr. The field is built as f"planned:{name}" with the raw candidate name (diff_reports, ~line 434), and was rendered via f" - {entry['field']}: ..." (~line 504), so a hostile candidate name carrying ANSI/OSC escapes reached stderr raw (confirmed live). Fix: the field now passes through the existing _display_id sanitizer at the render loop. Sanitizing at render -- rather than at construction -- was chosen deliberately because it covers every drift field type: planned:<name> (hostile), the fixed config fields (families, candidates, max_new_tokens, boundaries, backend_fingerprint), and fixtures:search/held_out (fixed stage suffixes). The _compact JSON rendering of drift values was already ASCII-safe (ensure_ascii=True), and the JSON stdout payload keeps the raw field for machine consumers -- sanitization applies only to the human-readable stderr summary. Pinned by a new test in tests/test_cycle13_diffreports.py: hostile candidate name in a planned-drift entry reaches the payload (planned:<evil> present) but the rendered summary contains no raw \x1b/\x07 bytes, while the readable text ("PWNED") and the planned: prefix survive.

  • Finding 5 (Low): the README test-count pin test in tests/test_cycle4.py never inspected proc.returncode/proc.stderr, so a pytest collection error surfaced as the misleading "could not parse pytest collection count", hiding the real failure. Fix: the test now asserts proc.returncode == 0 first, and both failure messages include the last ~2000 characters of stderr/stdout, so CI collection failures are debuggable from the test output alone.

Verification: new regression test passes; tests/test_cycle13_diffreports.py 37 passed; the hardened pin test correctly surfaced a real collection error (missing torch in a throwaway venv) instead of the misleading parse message, then passed in the real environment after the README count was bumped 1000 -> 1001 for the new test. Full suite: 1001 passed + 3142 subtests, ruff check + format clean, mypy clean on all source files. Docs: CHANGELOG.md [Unreleased] ### Fixed, this entry.

docs.title: 2026-10-15 (cycle 13 upstream drift)
docs.text:
Five-item upstream-drift sweep, all primary sources re-read this round. No code changed; recommendations only.

1. SGLang PR #42466 (multi-stop selection) — STILL OPEN, NOT MERGED. Re-read https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/42466 (page text, 2026-10-15): title "[Fix] Stop at the earliest matching stop_str when several match" by untrall; CI still failing on all three listed runs (Latest PR Test Base / Extra / AMD ROCm 10 all red). Independently confirmed absent from main via GitHub code search of sgl-project/sglang: the # TODO(lmzheng): handle the case where multiple stop strs are hit comment is still present in python/sglang/srt/managers/detokenizer_manager.py, and the PR's new test file test/srt/test_multi_stop_str.py does not exist in the repo. Proposed behavior (unchanged from the earlier drift note, quoted from the PR): "Collect every matched stop string in _check_str_based_finish (schedule_batch.py) and record the one with the earliest occurrence in the decoded text (ties keep list order; single-match behavior unchanged)" — i.e. within one decode step, the leftmost occurrence wins instead of list order. WATCH: if it merges, the repo's SGLang multi-stop tie-break (currently smallest firing step, ties broken by list order — see emulate_sglang_stop docstring in model_protocol_lab/backends.py) must become: same firing step -> earliest occurrence position in decoded text, ties keep list order. No repo change until merged.

2. Mistral Large 4 / Reflection Beam weights — NOT SHIPPED. - Mistral Large 4: API preview live since 2026-10-06; the HuggingFace pages https://huggingface.co/mistralai/Mistral-Large-4-1T-A52B and https://huggingface.co/mistralai/Mistral-Large-4.0-1T05-A52B both show "Upcoming release" / "Expected release: October 31, 2026. Current ETA". No downloadable weights. - Reflection Beam: announced 2026-10-05 (501B/23B-active MoE, 1M context); weights promised "later in October 2026" under Apache 2.0 after final red-teaming, early access via waitlist only (https://www.cryptopolitan.com/reflection-ai-beam-early-access-open-weights/, https://aistockwire.com/blog/reflection-ai-beam-open-weight-model-nvidia-nvda-kimi-glm-benchmarks-october-2026). No downloadable weights. Catalog impact: NONE. The mistral (Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.3) and mistral_large (Mistral-Large-Instruct-2411) entries remain accurate for all released Mistral models. Recommendation for the next cycle: when the weights land, add NEW family entries (do not edit the existing ones) — Large 4 is natively multimodal with a new template/tokenizer, Beam is a new 501B lab/family.

3. New open-weight releases since 2026-10-01. - DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash: weights went live 2026-10-06 on Alibaba's ModelScope hub and the Qwen platform (552B, MIT) (https://abhs.in/blog/deepseek-v4-1-flash-552b-moe-1m-context-mit-pricing-benchmarks-2026). ALREADY IN CATALOG as deepseek41 (sourced from https://huggingface.co/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash). No gap. - Decision 3.0 (vllm-sr/d3, d3-flash, d3-mini, d3-nano, d3-lite, d3-edge): uploaded 2026-10-10, Apache-2.0, safetensors on HuggingFace (verified via the HF model cards, e.g. https://huggingface.co/vllm-sr/d3). BUT they are non-generative decision models — "returns a probability for every answer, without generating text" — so they have no chat template; out of scope for the chat-template catalog. Watchlist only. - AutoTrust AI JEV-27B-VL / GEV-26B-Decide (announced 2026-10-08, open-weight decision/vision models): same verdict — notable, non-chat, no catalog entry. (https://www.morningstar.com/news/pr-newswire/20261008cn66859/...) - EmbeddingGemma 2 (2026-10-06, Apache 2.0): embedding model, no chat template, out of scope. - Out-of-window backlog for a future research cycle (all before 2026-10-01, all missing from the catalog): IFM/MBZUAI K2-Horizon fleet (6 models 0.9B–375B, Apache 2.0, released ~2026-09-03, on HF with day-zero vLLM/SGLang support — genuine missing chat families); Tencent Hy4 preview (2026-08-28, Apache 2.0, 770B/49B); MiniMax-M3 (2026-06, MiniMax Community License); Nanbeige4.2-3B (release date uncertain, likely ~Sept 2026).

4. vLLM stop-string/min_tokens semantics (releases since 2026-09-01: v0.28.0, v0.29.0, v0.30.0) — NO CHANGE to modeled semantics. Read the official release notes at https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/releases/tag/v0.28.0, /v0.29.0, and /v0.30.0. Stop-adjacent items found: - v0.28.0 #49227/#50595: request stop tokens masked in xgrammar until the grammar terminates (structured-output path only, not the core stop-string holdback the lab models); #51447: new VLLM_MAX_STOP_STRINGS cap (default 4) on stop strings per request — a request-level limit, not a selection-semantics change; #51997/#51556: Anthropic/Cohere frontend stop-sequence bounding/reporting. - v0.29.0 #54218 (read the full PR): "terminal grammars stop under min_tokens" — fixes the min_tokens+structured-output terminal-state hang, does NOT change stop-string/EOS min_tokens holdback; #53750: applies the stop-string count limit to Cohere requests (frontend validation). - v0.30.0 #55325: Anthropic stop_sequence reported in message_delta (streaming frontend); #51450: invalid structured-output requests no longer stop the engine. None alters vLLM's core semantics pinned by the repo (all stops gated behind min_tokens; multi-stop earliest-completion selection per vLLM #49391). emulate_vllm_stop and the diffbackends cells stand.

5. transformers stop_string semantics since 5.19.0 — NO CHANGE. The releases page https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/releases tops out at v5.19.0 (no v5.19.1, no v5.20): the repo's pinned knowledge is the current upstream. No generate() stop_string handling change to report. (v5.19.0 notes read this round: MoE router-logits breaking change, CB cache/attention work, no generation stopping-criteria items.)

Net: no repo change warranted on any item this round. Keep the SGLang

docs.title: 2026-10-15 (cycle 14 K2-Horizon family research)
docs.text:
Catalog 23 -> 24 families: k2horizon (IFM K2-Horizon fleet, Institute of Foundation Models launched by MBZUAI, released 2026-09-03, Apache 2.0). Evidence TIER-1: the official chat_template.jinja, read and derived by hand (preserved at docs/evidence/k2horizon-chat-template.jinja); the tokenizer_config.json bos_token/eos_token fields verified live against the HF repos (read 2026-10-15).

Org + fleet verification (primary: HF API + model cards). The HF org is IFM (not "IFM/MBZUAI" as the backlog note guessed). All six fleet repos verified present, ungated, with download counts, via the HF API author listing: IFM/K2-Horizon-375B-A23B, IFM/K2-Horizon-MoVA-36B-A4B (note: "MoVA" is in the repo name), IFM/K2-Horizon-32B, IFM/K2-Horizon-7B, IFM/K2-Horizon-3.7B, IFM/K2-Horizon-0.9B. Safetensors weights publicly downloadable: the 375B-A23B repo file listing shows all 61 model-*-of-00061.safetensors shards. License Apache 2.0 and 2026-09-03 release confirmed on the official model card (https://huggingface.co/IFM/K2-Horizon-375B-A23B).

Primary sources read this round (URL + what was read): - https://huggingface.co/IFM/K2-Horizon-375B-A23B -- model card: fleet composition, Apache-2.0 license, vLLM/SGLang day-zero recipes, reasoning_effort high/medium/low via chat_template_kwargs, k2_horizon reasoning/tool-call parsers. - https://huggingface.co/IFM/K2-Horizon-375B-A23B/raw/main/tokenizer_config.json -- bos_token <|ifm|begin_of_text|>, eos_token <|ifm|endoftext|>, PreTrainedTokenizerFast. - https://huggingface.co/IFM/K2-Horizon-MoVA-36B-A4B/raw/main/tokenizer_config.json -- byte-identical bos/eos fields (fleet shares the tokenizer config). - https://huggingface.co/IFM/K2-Horizon-375B-A23B/raw/main/chat_template.jinja -- the full official template (1014 lines), downloaded and preserved at docs/evidence/k2horizon-chat-template.jinja. md5-verified byte-identical across the 375B-A23B, 7B and MoVA-36B-A4B repos (150b0fd46f7babfc6bfd8b769ad0475c) -- one template for the fleet. - https://huggingface.co/IFM/K2-Horizon-375B-A23B/raw/main/generation_config.json -- eos_token_id [1, 250019] (250019 = <|ifm|im_end|> per the 7B added_tokens_decoder). - https://huggingface.co/IFM/K2-Horizon-375B-A23B/raw/main/modeling_k2_horizon.py -- confirms no chat-template handling in modeling code (the template is the whole story).

Template decisions (plain-text, no-tools core; line numbers in the preserved 1014-line file): BOS {{- bos_token }} (line 1) = <|ifm|begin_of_text|>; user <|ifm|im_start|>user {content}<|ifm|im_end|> (line 959, no trailing newline); assistant history <|ifm|im_start|>assistant <ifm|think> </ifm|think>{content}<|ifm|im_end|> (lines 983-997) -- the template REQUIRES a thinking field on assistant messages (think/think_fast/think_faster/reasoning_content/reasoning as a string, lines 962-976; a content-only assistant message raises), so the lab's deterministic no-reasoning hypothesis is an EMPTY think field (line 989), kimi3/laguna/ling convention; generation prompt <|ifm|im_start|>assistant <ifm|think> for the default reasoning_effort='high' (lines 1005-1006), <ifm|think_fast> for medium (line 1008), <ifm|think_faster> for low (line 1010) -- the medium/low branches ride the --mutate path as k2horizon/effort-medium / k2horizon/effort-low (kolibri/thinking-off convention); system block <|ifm|im_start|>system {content}<|ifm|im_end|> (line 948) documented, not modeled. The catalog entry's render was verified byte-identical against the official template rendered with a no-op Jinja extension for the custom tag (1-turn, 2-turn, effort variants, system block).

{% generation %} caveat (verified, not assumed). The official template wraps the assistant's inner content in {% generation %} / {% endgeneration %} block tags (lines 984, 998), which are NOT valid stock Jinja2 -- verified TemplateSyntaxError ("unknown tag 'generation'") with jinja2 3.1.6 AND the exact ImmutableSandboxedEnvironment(trim_blocks/lstrip_blocks) transformers 5.19.0 uses for apply_chat_template. They emit no bytes; serving stacks must supply the extension. The after "assistant" in the history frame is the source line break inside the {% generation %} block under standard Jinja block-extension semantics -- the only render consistent with the template's own explicit generation prompt (<|ifm|im_start|>assistant <ifm|think> , line 1006). Community renderers that strip the tags textually emit the frame WITHOUT that -- a known, documented ecosystem divergence. The template was last touched 2026-10-14 ("Support OpenAI-style text content lists (#8)"), so the md5 above is the revision pin.

Fetch warning for future cycles. browser.open's text extraction MANGLES this template (it dropped </...> closing-tag fragments and whole think-tag literals, showing 1830 phantom lines vs the real 1014): for chat_template.jinja files, always curl the raw bytes and derive from the file, never from the browser text view.

Triage of the other backlog models (all pinnable from primary sources today; deferred to a later cycle -- this cycle's test file is k2horizon-scoped): - Tencent Hy4 preview (2026-08-28, Apache 2.0): HF org tencent, repo tencent/Hy4-preview; chat_template.jinja publicly readable (309 lines, compiles under stock Jinja). Plain core: frames <｜hy_start:opensource｜>{role}<｜hy_middle:opensource｜>{content}<｜hy_end:opensource｜> (｜ = U+FF5C fullwidth bar, DeepSeek-style); history assistant <｜hy_start:opensource｜>assistant<｜hy_middle:opensource｜><think:opensource></think:opensource>{content}<｜hy_end:opensource｜> (empty think for plain messages); generation prompt ...<think:opensource> for the default reasoning_effort='high', ...<think:opensource></think:opensource> for no_think; a system block is ALWAYS synthesized when no leading system message (<｜hy_start:opensource｜>system<｜hy_middle:opensource｜><｜reasoning_mode:opensource｜>reasoning_effort:{effort}<｜hy_end:opensource｜>) -- documented-not-modeled, kolibri convention. Config bos_token <｜hy_start:opensource｜>, eos <｜hy_end:opensource｜>; the template emits no BOS literal. Template + tokenizer_config.json both read 2026-10-15. READY TO ADD. - MiniMax-M3 (2026-06, MiniMax Community License): HF org MiniMaxAI, repo MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3; chat_template.jinja publicly readable (247 lines). Plain core: template-local tokens bod ]~!b[, bos-var ]~b], eos-var [e~[; ALWAYS-emitted system super-prompt (]~!b[]~b]system + default identity + <thinking_instructions> block) and developer super-prompt (]~b]developer You are a helpful assistant.) -- both documented-not-modeled; user ]~b]user {content} [e~[ ; history assistant ]~b]ai </mm:think>{content}[e~[ (think_end prefix when no reasoning); generation prompt ]~b]ai (thinking_mode undefined/adaptive), ]~b]ai </mm:think> (disabled), ]~b]ai <mm:think> (enabled). Template read 2026-10-15. READY TO ADD. - Nanbeige4.2-3B (Nanbeige LLM Lab / Boss Zhipin; paper 2026-07-27): HF org Nanbeige, repo Nanbeige/Nanbeige4.2-3B; no standalone chat_template.jinja (404) but tokenizer_config.json embeds a full chat_template (primary source, read 2026-10-15). Plain core: ChatML-like with mandatory think blocks -- ALWAYS-emitted default system prompt <|im_start|>system + Chinese Nanbeige identity line + <|im_end|> (documented-not-modeled); user <|im_start|>user {content}<|im_end|> ; history assistant <|im_start|>assistant <think> </think> {content}<|im_end|> ; generation prompt <|im_start|>assistant <think> (default), <|im_start|>assistant <think> </think> with enable_thinking=false (mutate-path branch). Config bos <|im_start|>, eos <|im_end|>; template emits no BOS literal. READY TO ADD.

Built this cycle. k2horizon catalog entry + k2horizon/effort-medium + k2horizon/effort-low mutate variants in model_protocol_lab/catalog.py; tests/test_cycle14_k2horizon_families.py (12 tests: byte-exact 1-turn and 2-turn renders, character-exact marker pins, system-block/EOS documentation pins, effort-branch mutation + dedup pins, diff-vs-all-23-others pin, README naming pin); docs/evidence/ k2horizon-chat-template.jinja preserved. ruff check + format clean, mypy clean. Full suite: 1109 passed, 10 failed, 1 skipped, 5994 subtests passed. The 10 failures are all count/README pins for the coordinator: test_cycle10/11 README count pins (23 vs 24), test_cycle13 ling diff pin (22 vs 23 others) + README count pin (23 vs 24), test_cycle4 README test-count pin (1108 vs 1120 discovered), test_cycle5/6/7 twenty-two pins (pre-existing -- catalog was already at 23 before this cycle), test_e2e catalog-set pin (missing "k2horizon"), and the new ReadmeK2HorizonTests pin (README lacks "K2-Horizon"). No README/ CHANGELOG/VALIDATION edits made (coordinator handles).

docs.title: 2026-10-15 (cycle 15 Hy4/MiniMax-M3/Nanbeige family research)
docs.text:
Catalog 24 -> 27 families: hy4 (Tencent Hy4 preview), minimax3 (MiniMax-M3), nanbeige42 (Nanbeige 4.2-3B). All three were triaged as pinnable in the cycle-14 research; this round re-verified every template fact against the primary source (raw HF URLs, fetched with curl per the cycle-14 fetch warning -- browser.open mangles chat_template.jinja text; small text files only, no weights downloaded). All three repos are ungated (HTTP 200 on the raw files). All three templates VERIFIED pinnable -- none skipped.

Primary sources read this round (URL + what was read): - https://huggingface.co/tencent/Hy4-preview/raw/main/chat_template.jinja -- the official template, 309 lines, md5 a0b7e28386487d804009340155e7be2b (preserved byte-identical at docs/evidence/hy4-chat-template.jinja). Compiles under stock Jinja2: raise_exception (lines 36/38) is render-time only. Fullwidth bar ｜ = U+FF5C verified at the byte level (0x3c 0xff5c 0x68 ...). - https://huggingface.co/tencent/Hy4-preview/raw/main/tokenizer_config.json -- bos_token <｜hy_start:opensource｜>, eos_token <｜hy_end:opensource｜>, pad_token <｜hy_pad:opensource｜>. - https://huggingface.co/MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3/raw/main/chat_template.jinja -- the official template, 247 lines, md5 455403f9cba16ea73388aeb8898da752 (preserved byte-identical at docs/evidence/minimax-chat-template.jinja). raise_exception (line 203) is render-time only. - https://huggingface.co/MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3/raw/main/tokenizer_config.json -- bos_token ]~b], eos_token [e~[, pad_token ]!p~[, unk_token [e~[, PreTrainedTokenizerFast. - https://huggingface.co/Nanbeige/Nanbeige4.2-3B/raw/main/tokenizer_config.json -- 103 lines; no standalone chat_template.jinja (verified 404). The embedded chat_template (7961 chars) is the primary source, preserved at docs/evidence/nanbeige-chat-template.jinja (195 lines, exact extraction of the JSON string). Template decisions (plain-text, no-tools core; line numbers in the preserved files):

docs.title: 2026-10-15 (cycle 50: adversarial HF stop-emulation differential)
docs.text: Adversarial differential of emulate_hf_stop_string vs the real transformers 5.19.0 StopStringCriteria (tests/test_cycle50_stop_emulation_adversarial.py, 58 tests + 493 subtests): real tokenizers-built PreTrainedTokenizerFast on all three upstream matching modes (ByteLevel, ByteFallback, classic/Metaspace), 427 seeded adversarial cases + ~50 directed edge cases. 4 REAL divergences found, all documented with reproducers; coordinator decision: DOCUMENT, do not change behavior -- (1) empty stop: lab invalid_emulation_input (unreachable by design: diff_backends raises invalid_stop_texts; stop_matrix degrades an undecodable boundary to an unavailable cell; upstream's fire-at-step-1 is pathological); (2) multi-stop window: lab composes per-stop len(stop) windows (deliberate, mirrors the single-stop tensor walk); upstream's joint global-window bound is an artifact reachable only with exotic empty-string vocab entries; (3a) classic path WordPiece: stop "ab" over ["a","b"] false-positives here vs true "a b" (disclosed approximation; no catalog family uses non-concatenative decoders); (3b) upstream fires a step early on its own cleaning artifact (lab fires at the true position -- lab is more correct); (4) non-contiguous vocab ids: degenerate (real checkpoints are 0..N-1). Disclosure added to emulate_hf_stop_string's docstring ("Known divergences") + one sentence in diff_backends on deliberate per-stop composition. Tie-break verified: transformers has literally no selection code (torch.any); earliest-completing wins by construction, same-step ties outcome-identical. Mutation gate 6/6 caught on /tmp copies. docs.title: Research: template portability analysis without doubling compute (2026-10-15)
docs.text: Research subagent report. Question: is there a principled, constraint-compatible design for template portability analysis that does NOT re-run the experiment on a second checkpoint (which doubles compute) and does NOT weaken the per-checkpoint philosophy?

docs.title: Short answer
docs.text: Yes — but only as a static exclusion screen, not as a portability measurement. There is no established methodology anywhere (lm-eval, HELM, 2025–2026 literature) for "template X works on models A, B, C" that the lab could adopt, and the honest limits of a static check must be stated up front: it can rule out formats on a second checkpoint, it can never predict that the winning format would win there. That asymmetry is the whole design.

docs.title: 1. What the ecosystem does (and does not do)
docs.text:
lm-eval (lm-evaluation-harness). Renders each checkpoint's own chat template via tokenizer.apply_chat_template; task prompts are fixed Jinja templates in YAML configs. There is no template-portability concept: one template per task, one rendering per model, and per-model scores are compared. Recent movement toward multi-prompt evaluation: PR #2520 added a --examples argument as "the first step towards efficient multi-prompt evaluation with PromptEval" (source: EleutherAI/lm-evaluation-harness v0.4.9 release notes, https://github.com/EleutherAI/lm-evaluation-harness/releases/tag/v0.4.9).

PromptEval (Polo et al., NeurIPS 2024, arXiv 2405.17202). Estimates the performance distribution across many prompt variants, borrowing strength across prompts and examples; can estimate quantiles over 100 prompt templates on MMLU with a budget equivalent to ~2 single-prompt evaluations (source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.17202). Also used for best-prompt identification via best-arm identification (Shi et al., 2024). This is the closest thing to "which prompt works" methodology — but it (a) measures the distribution per model, never portability of one template across models, and (b) is statistical estimation, fundamentally incompatible with this lab's exact-token-sequence / no-estimation discipline (not_estimated). Not adoptable.

Prompt-sensitivity literature. Sclar et al. 2024 ("Does Prompt Formatting Have Any Impact on LLM Performance?", arXiv 2411.10541): matched-pairs t-tests between best/worst formats per model and a CMD dispersion metric — per-model format sensitivity, never cross-checkpoint portability of a specific template. The 2025 follow-up "Flaw or Artifact? Rethinking Prompt Sensitivity in Evaluating LLMs" (arXiv 2509.01790) shows heuristic evaluation exaggerates sensitivity (Gemma-2.0 ARC-Challenge 0.25–0.90 under heuristics vs. far tighter under LLM-as-judge; model rank correlation 0.31 → 0.92) — a cautionary note: any "portability" claim built on accuracy deltas is partly measuring the evaluator, not the template. The lab's RESEARCH_LOG (Cycle 3) already surveyed arXiv 2604.18389, 2608.18539, 2509.13680 and found every paper measures semantic or surface prompt variants; none does token-level template×checkpoint compatibility. The niche is still empty.

HELM / lighteval / Unitxt. Standardized prompts, task accuracy; no template-portability axis at all.

Conclusion for Q1: no established "template X works on models A, B, C" methodology exists. Every existing approach either (a) renders each model's own template (sidestepping the question), (b) estimates per-model prompt distributions (PromptEval — estimation, not exactness), or (c) measures format sensitivity per model (not portability). The lab would be defining the methodology, not adopting one.

docs.title: 2. The cheap static signal (the actual proposal)
docs.text:
Idea: template↔tokenizer compatibility matrix, computed from the tokenizer alone — no model forward passes.

For each candidate Format, the lab already extracts a special-token inventory (fixtures._extract_special_tokens: token-shaped substrings of bos, user_prefix, assistant_prefix, turn_end, per-role terminators, open suffix — e.g. <|im_start|>, <|eot_id|>, <end_of_turn>, [INST]). Against a second checkpoint's tokenizer (loaded exactly the way doctor already loads tokenizers — PreTrainedTokenizerFast from the local tokenizer.json, never weights), check per inventory token:

  1. Registered — the literal is in the tokenizer's added/special token map (added_tokens, bos_token/eos_token/etc.). The doctor already collects these dicts (special_tokens, added_tokens in examine_model).
  2. Single-token encodable — encode(literal, add_special_tokens=False) returns exactly one token id. If <|im_end|> fragments into subword pieces under checkpoint B's tokenizer, the model cannot be seeing the atomic control token the format assumes.
  3. ID-consistent — when registered and single-token, the encoded id equals the registered special-token id (catches vocab collisions where the string happens to be one ordinary token).

Verdict per (candidate, checkpoint): compatible / incompatible:<reason> / unknown (degraded, never fails the caller — the lab's established fail-closed convention).

Why this is principled, not a heuristic. There is direct 2026 literature grounding for the registered-vs-fragmented distinction: "Same Bytes, Different Authority: Reserved-Token Representations in Chat-Template Prompt Injection" (arXiv 2609.35932) establishes that "in every tokenizer we use, each marker string is either an added token or several ordinary tokens" and shows reserved/added marker vectors carry different representational authority than subword-mean surrogates (source: https://arxiv.org/html/2609.35932). A format whose markers are not atomic special tokens in checkpoint B's vocabulary is, with high confidence, not a format B was trained with. Conversely the practitioner literature is unanimous that a wrong template produces garbage/hallucinated turns (e.g. the "When Chat Templates Go Wrong" analysis of Jinja-engine mismatch and hardcoded-template substitution, https://medium.com/@pielouNobodyWho/when-chat-templates-go-wrong-8a437c62490e).

Logical status (must be documented honestly). The check is a necessary-condition gate: - incompatible ⇒ the format cannot be B's native format ⇒ re-running the experiment on B is scientifically pointless ⇒ portability answer obtained at ~zero compute (tokenizer load + a few encodes). - compatible ⇒ the markers could be B's control tokens ⇒ no prediction about whether the experiment would select it on B. That depends on weights; claiming otherwise would violate the lab's exactness discipline.

So the feature answers "can I rule out checkpoint B without running it?" — the exact question the deferred "cross-checkpoint portability re-measurement" item was gesturing at — at a cost comparable to doctor (a tokenizer load), i.e. ~0% of a re-run.

Fit with the exact-token-sequence discipline. Perfect fit: the matrix makes statements about token sequences (how the rendered prompt encodes under tokenizer B), never about estimated scores. No stochasticity, no greedy-decoding assumption, no sampling. It is also the natural generalization of the existing core.check_boundary_portability (cross-tokenizer re-encoding of the boundary string, P4) from boundary text to full format framing — same cost class, same fail-closed conventions.

Suggested shape (for the coordinator): doctor --portability-matrix <second-checkpoint-path> (or a core.template_tokenizer_compatibility function + doctor wiring), emitting per-candidate rows: {candidate, token, registered, single_token, id_match, verdict}. A natural second row of the same matrix: run it against the primary checkpoint too — a compatible row there plus incompatible on the second checkpoint is itself evidence about why the winner won (it was the only natively-encodable format), which is exactly the lab's "weights or formatting?" question.

What could go wrong (must be in the docs): 1. False-compatible via token pollution. A checkpoint can register ChatML-style added tokens without being trained with them (merges, sloppy conversions). compatible is explicitly not a prediction — the docs must say so, loudly, or users will misread the matrix. 2. Added-token encode behavior. tokenizers only splits on added tokens when they are registered as such in the loaded tokenizer; a hand-rolled PreTrainedTokenizerFast(tokenizer_file=...) may not carry the added_tokens metadata the same way the full from_pretrained path does. The lab's doctor already builds tokenizers this minimal way (doctor._build_primary_tokenizer) — the matrix must be validated against AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained behavior on real checkpoints before shipping, or it inherits a silent-encode trap. 3. BOS-less formats. chatml/qwen3-style formats have empty bos; the matrix must skip the BOS requirement for them (a naive "bos missing ⇒ incompatible" would be wrong). 4. Shape-based inventory limits. _extract_special_tokens is regex-shape-based; a format whose control tokens don't match the shapes (unlikely for the catalog, possible for user formats) yields an empty inventory ⇒ unknown, not compatible. 5. It does not replace the re-run. If both checkpoints report compatible for the winner, the only honest statement is "not ruled out" — the deferred re-measurement item stays deferred for that case. The matrix shrinks the set of checkpoints worth re-running; it does not eliminate re-running.

Cost. One tokenizer load per extra checkpoint + O(candidates × tokens) encodes. No weights, no forward passes, no GPU. Effectively free next to a run.

docs.title: 3. Template fingerprinting / inference from behavior
docs.text: Not worth building. The literature on fingerprinting is about model identity/lineage (under-trained-token fingerprints, arXiv 2410.12318; TokenPrint token-space provenance, arXiv 2608.08139; API token-count fingerprinting, arXiv 2608.29930) — not about inferring which chat template a checkpoint expects. No established method exists for "which template is this checkpoint trained for" beyond the white-box answer: read tokenizer_config.json's chat_template (which doctor.template_conformance already does). Black-box behavioral probing (feed candidate markers, watch for format adherence) would require model inference — the expensive thing the static matrix avoids — and would be speculative science, not a measurement instrument. The static compatibility matrix in §2 already answers the actionable version of the question ("is format F encodable as control tokens by checkpoint B?") cheaper and exactly.

docs.title: Recommendation
docs.text: Build the static template↔tokenizer compatibility matrix as a doctor extension (tokenizer-only, fail-closed, exact token-ID statements). Frame it in docs/USAGE as a necessary-condition exclusion screen: it can rule out checkpoints without running them; it can never transfer a selection verdict. Explicitly reject: a "portability score", any claim that compatible predicts experimental success on the second checkpoint, and any behavioral template-inference feature. This keeps the per-checkpoint philosophy intact (the experiment still runs on exactly one checkpoint; the matrix is pre-flight triage, like doctor itself), costs ~nothing, and fills a methodology gap no competitor or paper addresses.

docs.title: Context rotation design (cycle 203)
docs.text: Status: v2 — amended after the full adversarial round (red-team A: agents_out/cycle203/redteam_a.md, verdict DO NOT BUILD AS SPECIFIED, 2 FATAL / 8 MAJOR / 5 MINOR; red-team B: redteam_b.md, mandated to disprove A, confirmed A's core by independent execution and added two findings; verifier: verifier.md, design claims re-executed; coordinator adjudication: coordinator_adjudication.md). v1's classification compared two different statistics (A F1, fatal) and its construction classification had no primitive beneath it (A F4); v2 rebuilds both. The uniqueness pass is the wave-9 research brief (§3.1), verified live by the researcher against primary sources and recorded in docs/RESEARCH_LOG.md (cycle 203 entry); the adjudicated amendments from the wave-9 coordinator adjudication are binding on this design: (a) the pass-by-absolute-slot headline is presented as a cross-check against needle's depth curve, not a novelty claim; (b) arXiv:2511.20836 is cited as v3 (retitled "Structured Prompts Improve Evaluation of Language Models") or not at all — and its ranking-shift figure, if ever used, is 5/7 per the v3 abstract; (c) Lialin (arXiv:2404.02054) and Richardson (arXiv:2310.20081) are struck as rotation sources — the citation autopsy in the wave-9 research brief §1 shows neither supports a rotation, block-ordering, or position-sensitivity claim, and no sentence in this design rests on either name. The Chroma Context Rot report is cited corporately (its page carries no byline).

docs.title: Utility
docs.text: A practitioner whose RAG stack assembles a prompt from five retrieved chunks learns, per template family on their own checkpoint, whether cyclically rotating the same chunks — same content, same total text length, same relative order — changes the verdict, and whether the template they were about to ship keeps the same winner under rotation, before a retriever re-ranking silently reorders chunks in production and flips their eval.

docs.title: What this probe is not (the boundary, in the design doc's words)
docs.text: Four neighbouring probes vary neighbouring things; none varies this one. Needle moves one fact through a fixed filler stream at five depths and two doses; the filler is topically dissimilar prose, everything else stays put, and the readout is a recall-vs-depth curve for that fact. Position permutes the answer options inside one multiple-choice question; there is no multi-block context span. Placement moves the question around a frozen three-sentence payload; the payload itself never reorders. Distract splices filler at token doses. This probe pins the question after the span and rotates the span's five fact-bearing blocks themselves, holding the content multiset, the total text length, and the cyclic relative order constant across arms — the controlled sub-case of reordering that separates an absolute-position effect from an order effect. USAGE §8.50 repeats this paragraph's distinctions in the same words.

docs.title: Construction
docs.text:
Cases are generated inside the stage from the run seed by the frozen generator in rotation.py (SHA-256-derived draws, the needle/placement discipline: the same seed regenerates the identical set across runs and PYTHONHASHSEED values). CASE_COUNT = 20 is a construction constant; fixture ids are rotation-{index:02d} in canonical index order.

Each case is a span of five blocks plus a question. Blocks are indexed [0 = asked, 1..4 = distractors, 5 = replacement]; every arm order below is a list of block indices in span order.

  • Blocks. One asked block and four distractor blocks. Every block is one fact sentence from a frozen template: The {topic} access code is {value}. A distractor block is fact-shaped — same carrier, different topic, different code — not prose filler, so the span reads as five retrieved chunks competing for the same question shape. A sixth block (the replacement) is generated per case for the absent arm.
  • Topics. Six topics per case (asked, four distractors, one replacement), drawn from a frozen pool of thirty. The pool's pinned properties: topic phrases are pairwise distinct and no topic is a substring of another; every topic token has at least four characters; no topic token shares a four-character prefix with a code word, and no topic token is a substring of a code word or vice versa. A case's six topics are pairwise distinct, so the asked topic's full phrase occurs in exactly one block of the case and the question cannot leak a value by association.
  • Values. Each block binds a code (word-1000.. word-9999 shape) drawn per block. All six values in a case are pairwise distinct, and asked values are distinct across cases (the draw rules below).
  • Question. From a frozen template: What is the {topic} access code? — naming the asked topic, byte-identical in every arm, pinned after the block span. The expected answer is the asked block's value.
  • Span assembly. Block texts joined by a single space; the question follows the span after a "\n\n" joiner. The span text of an arm is exactly the five block texts in the arm's order — text-level surgery before render, per candidate (the placement pattern).

docs.title: Draw rules (frozen; the diff validator's mirror reproduces them exactly)
docs.text:
One derivation primitive, the house form: _derive(seed, index, slot, counter) is the big-endian first eight bytes of SHA-256 over the ASCII material "{seed}|rotation|{index}|{slot}|{counter}". Slot meanings are frozen: for block b in 0..5, the code word is slot 2b and the number is slot 2b + 1; the asked topic is slot 20; the distractor topics for blocks 1..4 are slots 21..24; the replacement topic is slot 25. Each slot has its own counter, starting at 0 for each case. Topic counters and value counters are independent streams: a value redraw never perturbs a topic draw and vice versa.

  • Asked topic. Draw pool[_derive(seed, index, 20, c) % 30] at counter c = 0, 1, ..., taking the first index not used as an earlier case's asked topic (without replacement across cases; 20 cases from a pool of 30 always terminate).
  • Distractor and replacement topics. For slot s in 21..25, draw at that slot's own counter from 0, taking the first topic that is neither the case's asked topic nor already chosen for this case.
  • Values. For block b, at its current counters: word = WORDS[_derive(seed, index, 2b, c_b) % len(WORDS)], number = 1000 + _derive(seed, index, 2b + 1, c_b) % 9000, value = "{word}-{number}". All six blocks draw at counters starting at 0. If any two of the case's six values collide, or the asked value repeats an earlier case's asked value, all six blocks' counters increment by one and all six values redraw (the needle whole-set redraw rule, widened to the case's set and frozen here).

Per-case construction checks (generator-enforced, pinned by test over the generator and seed sweeps): the six topics are pairwise distinct; the six values are pairwise distinct; each block's value occurs in exactly one block text of the case (its own), and the asked topic's phrase occurs in exactly one block text — the containment screen restated as a construction property of the frozen pools, proven over the pools, not inferred from the value format (A F15).

docs.title: Arms
docs.text:
Eleven cells per (candidate, case), all a single user turn:

  • rot_0..rot_4: cyclic rotations of the block sequence. Rotation r moves block r to the front: order = [r, r+1, ..., 4, 0, ..., r-1]. Content multiset, total text length, and cyclic relative order are identical in all five; among internal block–block pairs exactly one adjacency is lost and one gained per rotation (the wrap pair) — two blocks additionally change predecessor context at the render's head and tail seams (A F14; the construction discipline below covers the whole render, not only internal pairs). The asked block sits at absolute slot (5 - r) % 5 under rotation r, so across the five rotations the asked block occupies every slot exactly once.
  • mir_1..mir_4: the mirror arms — cyclic rotations of the reversed block order [4, 3, 2, 1, 0], named by the slot the asked block occupies: mir_4 = [4, 3, 2, 1, 0] (the reversal arm), mir_3 = [3, 2, 1, 0, 4], mir_2 = [2, 1, 0, 4, 3], mir_1 = [1, 0, 4, 3, 2]. Together with rot_0 they form the classification's control set (see Classification): the same five asked slots {0,1,2,3,4}, reached by non-cyclic reorderings. Reported beside the rotation readouts, never pooled into them.
