  • absent: the r=0 span with the asked block replaced by the case's sixth block (order [5, 1, 2, 3, 4]). The question still asks for the asked topic's code; a pass is recall without the fact present — the false-recall floor (the needle precedent).
  • closed_book: the question alone. A screening arm, not a rotation (see Screening).

docs.title: Construction verification (the rotation-specific discipline)
docs.text:
Text-level rotation does not guarantee token-level rotation: at each block joint, a candidate's tokenizer may merge the last token of one block with the first token of the next, so the rotated render's token inventory can differ from the unrotated one even though the text multiset is identical. Each span arm (rot_0..rot_4, mir_1..mir_4) of each (candidate, case) is therefore measured at construction under a frozen rule whose text the protocol carries by digest (CONSTRUCTION_RULE_TEXT in rotation.py, rotation-construction-v1):

  • Render the arm once. arm_tokens[arm] is the render's token count. The arm's inventory digest is the SHA-256 of the comma-joined decimal token ids of the full render, sorted ascending — a digest of the token multiset.
  • An arm is id_exact iff its inventory digest and token count both equal rot_0's; rot_0 is id_exact by definition (it is the reference). id_exact is a derived classification everywhere — stage aggregation and the diff validator both compute it from the recorded digests and counts; no record stores the classification itself (A F4).
  • The classification is a claim about the token inventory only: no seam event changed what the prompt is made of. It is not a claim that segmentation at the seams is unchanged — a merge at one seam compensated by a split at another restores the exact inventory while changing the segmentation at two joints, and the design states this openly rather than claiming a segment-level proof it does not perform (A F5a, open point 1).
  • Paired readouts (headline population, slot curve, mirror and reversal blocks) run only over cases whose five rotation cells are all present and id_exact. The id_exact shares are themselves reported readouts per candidate, so a tokenizer whose merges shrink the paired population is visible in the output, never silently absorbed.
  • The validator cannot recompute token ids without a tokenizer, so the inventory digests are stage-attested measurements — but they are primitives in the same trust class as answer_digest: every identity they imply (digest-and-count equality against rot_0, hence the derived classification and every population built on it) is checked and recomputed by the validator. This is a stronger settlement than needle's sizing residue, where the measured quantity has no digest-sized primitive at all.

Construction costs exactly one render per arm — eleven renders per (candidate, case) — and no search, so there is no encode budget to freeze.

docs.title: Screening
docs.text:
Three screens, in order:

  1. Frozen-text screen (stage-level, fail-closed). Every generated text (templates with slots emptied, topics, code words) is checked with audit_special_token_literals against every candidate, and every candidate's decoded boundary text is checked for containment in the generated texts (the needle/placement pattern). A hit fails the whole stage closed with detail rotation_screen_failed before any generation. Stated limit (lead L3, accepted as the house pattern): the audit covers the frozen parts, not instantiated texts; a special-token literal spanning a slot boundary in an instantiated block would not be caught by it — the neighbours share this shape and no concrete literal is known for any shipped candidate.
  2. Pool screens (construction-level). The topic pool's pinned properties above, plus the per-case construction checks (topic/value distinctness, single-occurrence containment). Pinned by test over the frozen pools and the generator.
  3. Closed-book screen (per candidate, per case, derived). If a candidate's closed_book cell passes a case, the answer was reachable without the span for that candidate — the case is excluded from that candidate's rotation populations. The exclusion is derived in aggregation from the closed-book cell's verdict, never a stored flag; the diff validator re-derives the same exclusion when it recomputes. Per-case, before generation: if any block text of the case contains the candidate's decoded boundary text, every cell of the case for that candidate is marked arm_screened (the needle per-span screen, at case granularity because the blocks rotate as a unit).

Populations, defined once. A record is boundary-screened for its candidate when the per-case boundary screen fired (every cell arm_screened); closed-book-screened when its closed-book cell passed; live when it is neither. n_screened counts closed-book-screened records; n_boundary_screened counts boundary-screened records; n_closed_book_incomplete counts records that are not boundary-screened and whose closed-book cell never completed (screening status genuinely unknown — boundary-screened records are a known exclusion and are never counted here, A F7). Boundary-screened records enter no readout population: not n_live, not the absent block, not the conditions shared population.

docs.title: Records
docs.text:
One record per (candidate, case); a candidate's record list carries exactly CASE_COUNT records in canonical generated order (the validator rejects any other count or order):

  • fixture (the case id), topic (the asked topic), expected_digest (SHA-256 of the asked value). No block, question, or value text anywhere — digests and counts only.
  • arm_tokens: the rendered token length of each of the eleven arms under this candidate, measured at construction. For a completed cell, the cell's own input_tokens must equal arm_tokens[arm] (the needle/placement grounding: one id sequence per fixture, as recorded by core.evaluate()).
  • arm_inventory_digests: per span arm (rot_0..rot_4, mir_1..mir_4), the inventory digest defined above (the absent arm has different content by design and carries no digest).
  • cells: per arm, either a cell or None. A cell is {verdict, boundary_found, boundary_text_match, input_tokens, answer_digest} where verdict is derived: the validator recomputes it as (answer_digest == expected_digest) and boundary_found (the numform F3 lesson, applied by construction).
  • cell_details: per arm, "" when the cell completed, else one of arm_context_exceeded, arm_evaluation_failed, arm_screened. A cell is present iff its detail is "".

Stage-level details are frozen as STAGE_DETAILS = ("cancelled", "rotation_record_budget_exceeded", "rotation_screen_failed"). Candidate names are unique by the run-level guard (experiments.py, "formats must have unique names"); the payload's candidates are a parsed JSON object, in which a duplicate key cannot survive parsing — the uniqueness the validator relies on is the stage's guard plus the object shape, audited as A F10b (corrected at build time: no sibling validator performs a separate duplicate-key check, and neither does this one).

docs.title: Readouts
docs.text:
Per candidate, over its own records (the validator recomputes every number). Global denominator rule: every rate and share in this section is None iff its denominator is 0 (A F8); each readout below names its population explicitly.

  • arms: per span arm (rot_0..rot_4, mir_1..mir_4) {n_completed, n_pass, rate} over live records. This table is descriptive and construction-ungated; the absent and closed-book arms are not rows here — their numbers live in their own blocks, so no number is printed twice (B-F2).
  • closed_book: {n_completed, n_pass, pass_rate} over all records — the screening yield, reported as itself.
  • Screen accounting: n_records, n_screened, n_boundary_screened, n_closed_book_incomplete, n_live.
  • Headline block over the headline population — live records whose five rotation cells are all present and all id_exact (derived):
  • n_headline;
  • n_all_pass and n_all_fail (verdict constant across rot_0..rot_4, all-pass / all-fail), n_invariant = n_all_pass + n_all_fail and invariance_rate;
  • n_flip_any = n_headline - n_invariant;
  • the r=0-conditional block: over headline records whose rot_0 cell passes, n_r0_pass and n_flip_from_pass (records whose verdict vector is not all-pass), with flip_rate_from_pass;
  • evaluable_share = n_headline / n_live, and id_exact_share over completed rotation cells of live records (present-and-id_exact cells over present rotation cells);
  • a classification (below) and the falsification boolean.
  • Slot curve: for each absolute slot s in 0..4, the pass count over headline records of the one rotation that places the asked block at slot s — by construction every slot is observed exactly n_headline times, so the curve carries its denominator once, as n_headline. This is the rotation analogue of needle's depth curve and is presented as a cross-check against it (same functional question — does the fact's absolute position move the verdict — asked of a whole-prompt symmetry instead of a single planted fact), never as a novelty claim (adjudication amendment (a)).
  • Mirror block: over headline records whose four mirror cells are all present and id_exact (the mirror-paired set): n_paired, n_flips_paired (records whose verdict is not constant across rot_0..rot_4 — the headline statistic restricted to this set), n_flips_mirror (records whose verdict is not constant across the control set {rot_0, mir_1..mir_4}), and the mirror id_exact_share over completed mirror cells of live records.
  • Reversal block: over headline records whose mir_4 cell is present and id_exact: n_paired, n_discordant (the mir_4 verdict differs from rot_0), discordance_rate. Reading: the reversal arm is one member of the mirror set; its discordance is the descriptive single-arm control level, printed beside the mirror block. The classification's control comparison is the mirror block's matched statistic, not this discordance (A F1).
  • Absent block: over live records whose absent cell is present: n_evaluable, n_false_pass, rate — the false-recall floor, reported beside the headline (the needle pattern). In the reporting section text the absent numbers are labelled false recall wherever they appear (open point 4).

docs.title: Classification (total function)
docs.text:
Floors frozen at the needle/placement value: MIN_HEADLINE_POPULATION = 6 and MIN_CONTROL_POPULATION = 6. The floors gate this label and the falsification boolean only, never a reported count or rate. Decision list, first match wins, over the headline and mirror blocks with F = n_flip_any:

  1. n_headline < 6 → insufficient
  2. F == 0 and n_all_fail > n_all_pass → joint_collapse_dominant
  3. F == 0 → invariant_observed
  4. mirror n_paired < 6 → control_set_too_small
  5. n_flips_paired <= n_flips_mirror → within_mirror_control
  6. otherwise → rotation_sensitive

Step 2 is placement's joint-collapse settlement in dominance form (A F2, B's correction): a population whose constant verdicts are mostly all-fail is a capability story, not an invariance acquittal, so it never receives invariant_observed. Steps 5–6 compare the same statistic on both sides — any-flip over five arms, over the same cases — and the two arm sets place the asked block at the same slot multiset {0,1,2,3,4}: under a pure absolute-slot effect (the verdict a function of the asked slot only) the two flip indicators are equal for every case deterministically, so a slot effect alone can never produce rotation_sensitive (B-F1, answered by construction). Under the exchangeability null the comparison is calibrated by symmetry (a tie goes to within_mirror_control).

docs.title: Falsification
docs.text:
There is exactly one definition, and this is it (the same formula is printed in the rotation.py module docstring; any other sentence in this document is commentary on it, not a second definition):

invariance_falsified is true iff n_headline >= 6 and n_flip_any >= 1.

Reading: the claim under test is invariance itself (the wave-9 brief §3.1(c)), so a single verified flip at a sufficient population falsifies it. The mirror control does not acquit invariance — a flip is a flip — it answers the separate question of whether the effect is cyclic-specific or generic reordering, which is what the classification's within_mirror_control step reports.

The joint behaviour of the boolean and the classification is a theorem of the decision list, stated as one (A F3):

classification falsified insufficient false only joint_collapse_dominant false only invariant_observed false only control_set_too_small true only within_mirror_control true only rotation_sensitive true only

Two pairings are deliberate and the section text says both, in this order: a candidate can be falsified and within-control at once (the boolean does not wait for the control), and a candidate can be falsified beside control_set_too_small, whose meaning is only that the control set was too small to judge cyclic-specificity — the boolean never claimed otherwise. joint_collapse_dominant pairs with falsified = false because the boolean is about flips and there are none; the collapse caveat lives in the label, and the section prints both. Below the floor the boolean is false and the classification is insufficient — withheld, never defaulted to acquittal. The enumeration of the full feasible tuple space, proving totality, label reachability, and this table, is pinned by a test in the cycle's test plan (the placement precedent, extended).

Dispositions of brief §3.1(c)'s other clauses (A F13). The brief's cross-candidate clause ("proved wrong if all evaluable candidates share the same invariance rate within their denominators") is dropped: its criterion defines no decidable test ("within their denominators" names no statistic), and no cross-candidate boolean is printed; the per-candidate boolean plus the printed per-candidate rates with denominators carry the evidence. The brief's fact-absent-floor qualifier does not condition the boolean: falsification is over the screened headline population, the absent rate is a reported readout beside it, and a flip is a within-case verdict change on present-fact arms, which false recall does not manufacture.

docs.title: Conditions (per-rotation selection)
docs.text: For each arm in {rot_0..rot_4, mir_4 (the reversal)}, the conservative selection rule is re-applied over the arm's completed cases restricted to the shared live population: cases recorded for every candidate and live for all of them (the placement union rule, with "live" as defined above — so a case boundary-screened for one candidate never enters, A F7). One amendment to v1 (A F9): each arm's population is additionally gated on that arm being id_exact (derived) for every candidate on the case — needle's conditions range only over construction-verified cells because its unmatchable cells are never generated, and rotation's text_level cells, which are generated, must not enter the selection readout at full weight beside a headline that excludes them. (rot_0's gate is vacuous: it is id_exact by definition.) The readout is withheld with detail selection_withheld_mismatched_sets when the restricted completed sets differ across candidates or are empty (the needle rule). Each arm's flip compares its selection to the rot_0 selection recomputed on the same restricted completed set; rot_0's own flip is False when not withheld, and a flip is None when either side is withheld.

docs.title: Diff validator
docs.text: diff_rotation in diffreports.py, full-recompute standard (the wave-7 F6 settlement): _rotation_recompute carries its own generator mirror (its own derive function, templates, topic and word pools as literals — no imports from rotation.py), regenerates the case set from the protocol's seed, and compares every record against it (exactly CASE_COUNT records per candidate in canonical order; fixture id, asked topic, expected digest). The protocol is rebuilt from frozen scalars plus the payload's seed and backend fingerprint and its fingerprint recomputed. Every cell's verdict is re-derived from its digest and boundary flag; every completed cell's input_tokens must equal the record's arm_tokens; cells and details must be consistent (a cell is present iff its detail is ""). arm_inventory_digests are shape-checked (nine span arms, 64-hex) and the id_exact classification is derived from digest-and-count equality with rot_0, never read from the payload. Every aggregate, headline block, slot curve, mirror block, reversal block, absent block, classification, falsification flag, and the conditions are recomputed by mirror code and compared exactly. A one-break-at-a-time battery pins every reject branch.

docs.title: Budget
docs.text: Worst case: 24 candidates (the run cap) × 20 cases × 11 arms = 5,280 generations, stated in the CLI help with the forwards formula before the run (the wave-9 brief's 3,360 counted five arms of an earlier shape; the help says 5,280). Construction costs exactly one render per arm beside the generations (see Construction verification). The stage threads the run's cancel event end-to-end and checks it before and after every evaluation (the multiturn rule). MAX_GROUND_RECORDS = 480, MAX_RECORDS_BYTES = 12 MiB (the house bound).

docs.title: Pin blast radius
docs.text:
(Rewritten from executed greps of the placement footprint, A F10; the v1 list's "VALIDATION §6 probe list" was a phantom inherited from PLACEMENT_DESIGN.md — VALIDATION has no §6; its probes are a prose list in the first Evidence bullet. That PLACEMENT_DESIGN line is corrected in this cycle's push.)

  • New pure module rotation.py → the test_cycle44 mypy source-file pin moves 59 → 60 in the same push. VALIDATION's first-Evidence-section probe list gains the rotation entry in prose (pinned by nobody verbatim); VALIDATION header range moves to cycles 10–203 with the test_cycle178 pin in the same push.
  • New --rotate flag → the cycle-179 parametrized dispatch table and probe-wrapper audit gain a row; the cycle-31/64/84 subcommand/flag audits and the args-Namespace contract gain a case.
  • New diff section rotation → test_cycle67's three elements (fuzz oracle + _fuzz_rotation_section; the flip-identical gate anchor's original and mutant texts; _identical_expected's key set) plus test_cycle27's full placement-style footprint: an independent _or_rotation_* oracle, its asymmetric computation, the two summary keys, and the section stub entry "rotation": {"available": ..., "changed": False} (grep-counted at build time, not assumed).
  • New reporting section → reporting.py's three touchpoints (compute, TOC tuple, body concatenation).
  • README Capabilities bullet + measured test count; VALIDATION counts and the CI-scope ruff file count; CHANGELOG entry; USAGE §8.50 (the boundary paragraph in the same words as above); RESEARCH_LOG cycle-203 entry before the code; the PLACEMENT_DESIGN §6-phantom correction.

docs.title: Open points — dispositions
docs.text:
1. Inventory vs segment classification. The id_exact definition is inventory equality, honestly labelled (segmentation at seams not verified). With the inventory digest carried as a primitive (A F4), the classification is derived, not attested-free; a segment-level check is not adopted (its cost is a per-block segment apparatus the inventory claim does not need).
  2. Falsification asymmetry. The boolean and the classification are one story with a published joint table (Falsification). The substantive defects nearby were F1/F2, both fixed in the definitions.
  3. Conditions without construction gating. Adopted: gated per arm on id_exact for every candidate (Conditions).
  4. The absent arm's expected value. Sound as designed: the absent cell's verdict uses the asked value's digest, and the generator's distinctness rules guarantee the asked value occurs nowhere in the absent prompt, so a pass is false recall by construction. The one smuggle A found — the generic arms table listing the absent rate unlabelled — is closed by B-F2 (absent is not an arms-table row).
  5. Topic-pool repetition across cases. Asked topics are drawn without replacement across cases, so the twenty asked topics are always distinct (lead L1 closed by construction, not by caveat).
  6. A slot-pinned mirror arm ([0,4,3,2,1], asked fixed at slot 0, distractors reversed — B-F1's suggestion): not adopted. The mirror set answers the slot confound by slot-multiset matching (Classification); a twelfth arm's marginal readout does not justify its cost. Recorded as considered-and-deferred; a future cycle may add it as a descriptive arm without touching the classification.

docs.title: Scorer-lens regrade — design contract
docs.text: Status: shipped in cycle 180 (wave-7 research rank 1). This document is the frozen contract for the ladder in model_protocol_lab/scorerlens.py; the ladder itself also travels inside every payload as data, with a SHA-256 digest, so this prose and the data can be checked against each other.

docs.title: What it answers
docs.text:
The lab's native verdict is byte-exact. That strictness is the point — but it cannot distinguish "the template produced the wrong answer" from "the template produced the right answer in a surface form the scorer discards" (trailing punctuation, a markdown fence, 1,000 for 1000). The scorer lens regrades the recorded search answers under progressively more permissive, fully specified normalisations and reports, per candidate, how many failures each rung recovers, which fixture flips first at which rung, and whether the search-phase winner changes. Post-hoc, zero model calls.

Utility, in one sentence: after a template change, decide whether the template actually got worse or the byte-exact scorer is discarding human-acceptable answers — and whether the winner survives the mildest defensible scorer.

docs.title: The ladder
docs.text:
One pipeline: each rung consumes the previous rung's output, which makes monotonicity (claim S2) a theorem of the construction rather than a hope. R4 is a union with R3, never a replacement comparison.

  • R0 — identity. Reproduces the native per-fixture verdicts.
  • R1 — trim; collapse runs of spaces/tabs to one space; collapse 3+ consecutive newlines to two. Single/double newlines survive: line structure can be content.
  • R2 — NFC, casefold, combining-mark removal (NFD, drop category Mn, recompose). The mark step is the refusal detector's fix for Turkish İ (casefold leaves i + combining dot). The decomposition is canonical (NFD), deliberately not the detector's compatibility NFKC: fullwidth digits and other compatibility forms are not folded at R2 (an early build used NFKD for the mark strip and silently folded them; the monotonicity property test caught it, and the rung now does exactly what this contract says). Casefold equates German ß with ss — Unicode default folding as specified; a known false-recovery risk on name fixtures, surfaced by the per-flip attribution (flip_via: nfc when NFC alone achieved equality, else casefold).
  • R3 — markdown-fence strip (line-anchored code fences, any info string discarded, both sides), then iterative edge stripping of a small presentational set: asterisk, underscore, backtick, double and single quotes, period, comma, semicolon, colon, exclamation and question marks, and round, square and curly brackets. (The payload's ladder data carries the set as an explicit character list.) The set excludes -/+ (signs are content) and % (a unit). A leading . directly before a digit is never stripped (.5 is not 5). Removing punctuation at all positions is forbidden by the protocol (it would equate 3.5 with 35). An expected text that is itself fenced or punctuation-bearing is stripped too; recovered fixtures whose expected side was altered by R3 are counted in the payload (n_flips_expected_altered).
  • R4 — R3, or both R3 forms fully match one ASCII numeric grammar and parse to finite, equal Decimal values: ^[+-]?([0-9]{1,3}(,[0-9]{3})+|[0-9]+)(\.[0-9]+)?([eE][+-]?[0-9]+)?$ or ^[+-]?\.[0-9]+([eE][+-]?[0-9]+)?$. Underscores, non-ASCII digits, inf/NaN spellings, and decimal commas never fire R4 (1,5 is not 15; the ladder has no locale input). Comparison is Decimal.__eq__ on parsed values — never normalize(), which under the default 28-digit context collapses distinct long decimals. -0 == 0 holds and is accepted.

docs.title: Verdicts, denominators, withholding
docs.text:
• A rung verdict is status == completed ∧ boundary_found ∧ rung text match. The boundary conjunct is a recorded fact no rung can move; per-candidate n_boundary_blocked is reported next to every winner line. A diagnostic text-only match series is reported alongside the verdict series.
  • At rungs ≥ 1 a pass requires both normalised forms nonempty; an erasure-to-empty is a no-flip. Fixtures whose expected text normalises to empty at R1 are excluded from the lens entirely, with n_excluded_empty_expected reported per candidate.
  • The winner readout is the search-phase winner under each rung (conservative bar re-applied to rung verdict counts); held-out is never regraded. It is withheld with a named detail (candidate_unavailable, candidate_not_eligible, evaluable_mismatch) whenever the field is partial — never re-applied to a prefix-measured field. The surface-failure share (failures recovered by R4 ÷ native verdict failures, R4 recoveries included in the numerator) is withheld per candidate on the same eligibility gate as the refusal rates.

docs.title: Payload discipline
docs.text: Counts, fixture IDs, rung numbers, and small enums only: no answer text, no expected text, no normalised forms, no lengths. The per-fixture ground records (fixture, completed, boundary_found, exact_match, excluded, first_flip_rung, flip_via, expected_r3_altered, newline_differs) plus per-candidate eligible let the diff-reports validator recompute every aggregate, the mismatch flag, and the winner readout — a payload whose aggregates disagree with its records is rejected as corruption. A coherent foreign ladder validates and is reported by the diff as protocol drift.

docs.title: Pre-registered claims (sharpened by the pre-build cross-check)
docs.text:
• S1. R0 pass ⟺ (status == "completed" and answer == expected) reproduces every recorded exact_match flag; R0 ∧ boundary_found reproduces every candidate's native pass count. Oracle-differential over synthetic and adversarial observations.
  • S2. The ladder is monotone: a fixture passing at rung k passes at every rung > k. Rung match is cumulative ("passes under the ladder up to this rung"), which makes monotonicity a theorem of the pipeline + union construction — including for identical all-punctuation pairs, which pass at R0 and therefore at every rung, while distinct pairs that would only meet at an empty form pass at none (S3). A property test over an adversarial corpus (NaN/inf spellings, all-punctuation strings, fenced blocks, decimal commas, empty strings) guards the implementation.
  • S3. At rungs R1–R4, no pass is recorded when either side's normalised form is empty; erasure-to-empty is a no-flip. Pinned by named tests (?/! at R3, ***/empty at R1–R4).
  • S4. R4 fires iff both R3 outputs match the frozen grammar, parse via Decimal, and are finite and equal. Answer: 42 fires at no rung — the ladder has no label-strip operation. 1,5, 12,34, 1,2,3, 50%, 1_000, inf, NaN never fire R4; 42 vs 17 never match at any rung. Each is a named test.

docs.title: Provenance
docs.text: The design was red-teamed before code existed (wave-7): red-team A returned DO NOT BUILD AS SPECIFIED with 12 findings — the recorded result carries no expected field (blocker; the profile takes the expected map as an explicit parameter, the verbosity precedent), the native boundary conjunct was undefined against the ladder, the Answer: 42 motivating example flips at no rung, R4's 1,000 example is false under a naive Decimal parse, and S1 ∧ S3 were jointly unsatisfiable on legal empty-expected fixtures. Red-team B independently re-derived every finding, upheld all of them (one sub-claim refuted: NFC + casefold does equate the ﬁ ligature via casefold), and added two binding amendments — one ASCII-only grammar for all R4 inputs (A's own \d regex matched Unicode digits), and ground records rich enough for the validator to recompute denominators and the winner. This contract is the corrected design that survived.

docs.title: Sealed result bundles (pack / verify --bundle)
docs.text: Utility (Monday morning). An auditor asks "prove these result files are unchanged since the run was packed." model-protocol-lab pack seals a report directory into one hash-bound bundle; model-protocol-lab verify --bundle re-checks the seal offline and then re-derives the experiment's decision from the sealed results.json (the verify replay) as an independent second layer.

docs.title: What the seal proves — and what it does not
docs.text: The seal is hash-based and unsigned. It proves exactly one thing: the files in the bundle are bit-identical to the files that were packed, when the bundle digest is compared against a digest obtained through an independent channel (for example the hex printed by pack on stderr and published where the result itself is published, or passed via verify --bundle --expect-digest). A digest that only travels inside the bundle authenticates nothing: anyone can edit the files and re-pack. The seal also does not prove who produced the bundle, that the experiment was actually run (a fabricated but internally consistent results.json passes both the seal and the replay — the replay proves the recorded decision follows from the recorded artifact, nothing more), that the experiment was well-designed, or that the bundle is the latest one (there is no freshness or rollback protection; the out-of-band record carries the date and label). Terminology: this is a hash seal providing tamper-evidence and decision re-derivation. It is not an attestation, a signature, or tamper-proofing — those words imply a keyholder, and there is none.

docs.title: Format mpl-bundle/1
docs.text:
A bundle is a single ZIP archive, written uncompressed (ZIP_STORED), whose entries are sorted by name. Every ZipInfo field that affects bytes is normalised (date_time=(1980, 1, 1), create_system=0, external_attr=0o644 << 16, no extra fields, no per-entry comments), so rebuilding from identical inputs under the same package and interpreter version produces byte-identical output. Verification guarantees content integrity (per-file hashes plus the manifest digest below); it does not require the container bytes to equal what the current pack would emit.

Entries:

  • manifest.json — the seal manifest (below).
  • One entry per sealed file, at its canonical relative path: the report directory's top-level files at their names, --include files under inputs/<name>. pack never emits directory entries.
  • The archive comment is exactly mpl-bundle-sha256:<64 lowercase hex> — the SHA-256 of the exact stored bytes of the manifest.json entry. Verifiers hash the stored bytes once; they never re-serialise the parsed manifest to recompute the digest.

Entry types (decision recorded cycle 196, oversight security S-8): every entry in a bundle is a regular file. pack only ever writes regular files (with create_system=0 and permission-only external_attr, so its own entries carry no Unix file-type bits at all). The verifier's seal_container check additionally rejects — as entry_type_not_regular — any entry whose stored Unix file type (from a create_system=3 creator) is explicitly something other than a regular file: symlink, FIFO, device, socket, or a directory entry whose name lacks the trailing slash. Entries whose creator or attributes make no file-type claim are judged by the name, caps, and hash checks alone. Nothing in the lab extracts a bundle to disk; the rule exists so that a bundle the lab calls verified cannot change meaning when a user extracts it with an external tool, where a symlink entry composed with later entries beneath it is the classic zip-slip shape.

docs.title: Manifest
docs.text:
Canonical JSON (sorted keys, compact separators, ensure_ascii), exact types throughout (type(x) is int / is str; booleans are not ints):

{
  "context": {
    "backend_fingerprint": "<copied from results.json>",
    "catalog_sha256": "<sha256 of the canonical catalog definition>",
    "package_version": "0.1.0"
  },
  "files": [
    {"path": "report.html", "role": "report", "sha256": "<hex>", "size": 123},
    {"path": "results.json", "role": "results", "sha256": "<hex>", "size": 456}
  ],
  "format": "mpl-bundle/1"
}
  • files never lists manifest.json; paths follow the canonical grammar: /-separated, no empty / . / .. segments, no leading /, no drive prefix, no backslash, no control characters. Comparisons are exact-string.
  • role is informational only — one of results, report, input, assigned by location. No verification decision branches on it; unknown roles and unknown top-level keys are accepted (forward compatibility). The replay target is the entry whose path is exactly results.json.
  • catalog_sha256 is the SHA-256 of the canonical JSON of the catalog's template definitions ({family: [Format fields]}), computed at pack time. It is a recorded claim: verify reports it but does not recompute it, exactly as for backend_fingerprint. The decision rule is bound by package_version: the replay semantics are those of the verifying package version, and the manifest records the packing one.

docs.title: Limits (enforced in this order, before content is read)
docs.text:
Constant Value Enforced Outer bundle size 288 MiB fstat on the single open fd, before reading Entry count 1024 EOCD pre-parse, before ZipFile construction Per-entry uncompressed size 64 MiB Central directory, before that entry is read Total uncompressed size 256 MiB Central directory running total Sealed results.json 32 MiB (MAX_RESULTS_BYTES) Shared bounded JSON reader

The container is strict: the first local header is at offset 0 (no prepended data), the file ends exactly at the end of the EOCD record (no trailing data), the EOCD disk fields are zero, and ZIP64 sentinel values in the EOCD are rejected (a format-1 bundle is far below ZIP64 sizes; needing it would be a format bump). The disk and ZIP64 checks are EOCD-level — the pre-parse reads the end-of-central-directory record, not a ZIP64 extended record or per-entry extra fields. Duplicate archive entry names and duplicate manifest paths are rejected before any entry data is read; all reads iterate infolist() entries and stream in bounded chunks, asserting the hashed length equals the declared size.

docs.title: Filesystem discipline
docs.text: pack enumerates the report directory with os.scandir and opens every file once with O_RDONLY | O_NOFOLLOW | O_NONBLOCK, requires fstat to report a regular file, and hashes exactly the bytes it stores. Symlinks, FIFOs, devices, and subdirectories are errors — evidence is never silently skipped. --output may not live inside the report directory and may not overwrite (created with O_EXCL); the default is the sibling path <report-dir>.bundle.zip. verify --bundle opens the bundle with the same single-fd discipline as load_results, so a FIFO cannot hang it.

docs.title: Verification layers and exit codes
docs.text: verify --bundle report shape mirrors verify_results ({"verdict", "checks", ...}). Seal checks are namespaced seal_* (seal_container, seal_manifest_schema, seal_comment_digest, seal_file_set, seal_file_hashes, optional seal_expected_digest); replay checks keep their existing verify_results ids. If the seal layer fails, the replay is not run and its checks are recorded unavailable with detail seal_failed. A sealed results.json that the plain verify path would call unreadable (duplicate fields, NaN, oversize, wrong shape) is unreadable in a bundle too — same exit class, same fixed vocabulary. Exit codes: 0 = seal ok and replay ok; 2 = seal or replay failed; 1 = unreadable/invalid input. Callers must branch on the JSON report, not the exit code alone. The stderr summary always prints the scope line: seal: integrity since packing only — origin not authenticated.

docs.title: Why no diff-reports section
docs.text: A bundle is a container for one experiment artifact, not a measurement; diff-reports compares two experiments' measurements. Bundle presence is reported by verify --bundle itself. (Deviation from the generic "every feature ships a diff section" default, recorded here deliberately: a presence-only diff section would carry no measurement content.)

docs.title: Uniqueness (researched 2026-10-20, see docs/RESEARCH_LOG.md)
docs.text: No mainstream evaluation harness ships result sealing. The combination — an unsigned hash-sealed bundle binding results, inputs, catalog and package version, verified offline with an independent decision replay as the second layer, in a local deterministic harness — is the contribution. Unsigned eval receipts exist elsewhere without the replay layer; provenance metadata in other harnesses is unsealed. Academic and standards precedents (SLSA, in-toto) are signing-based and are cited, not claimed.

docs.title: Trust boundaries
docs.text:
Treat checkpoints, tokenizer files, fixtures, generated text and reports as separate trust boundaries. Local-only loading and safetensors reduce exposure; they do not make arbitrary files, native dependencies or GPU drivers safe. Run unfamiliar model assets in an appropriately isolated environment with resource limits.

Use trusted, immutable checkpoint directories. Do not grant this process unnecessary filesystem or network access. The adapter requests local-only model resolution, disables remote model code and rejects pickle weight layouts; runtime network isolation is verified by test_no_network_access_during_doctor_and_backend_init. Run doctor on any unfamiliar checkpoint before evaluation; it validates assets without loading weights.

docs.title: Security audit (2026-10-12)
docs.text: A full audit was conducted against this tree and every finding was resolved or explicitly accepted below. Methodology: pip-audit 2.10.1 (OSV DB) on the installed dependency set; bandit 1.9.4 on model_protocol_lab/; ruff flake8-bandit (S) rules in CI; manual line-by-line review of all package modules; adversarial PoCs (XSS payloads through render_html, path-traversal names through _member, 100 kB ReDoS probes, deeply-nested/NaN JSON through the dataset loader). semgrep could not run (sandbox /tmp exhaustion); bandit + ruff S + manual review covered the same ground.

docs.title: Findings and resolutions
docs.text: ID Severity Finding Resolution F1 Medium No lockfile/hashes; torch>=2.6 unbounded — fresh installs trust PyPI tip-of-range. Upper-bound discipline documented; pip-audit runs as a CI gate (security job) on every build; torch CVE posture tracked below. torch capped <3 in cycle 201 (2026-10-23); the lockfile gap remains accepted (residual 2). F2 Low pip-audit cannot see torch 2.14.1+cpu (local version tag). Manual CVE review 2026-10-12: postdates fixes for CVE-2025-3000 and CVE-2025-32434; CVE-2026-4538 (torch.export.load) is not reachable — the codebase never calls torch.export.load/torch.load; weights load only via from_pretrained(use_safetensors=True, weights_only=True). Re-verify on every torch bump. F3 Low Report files created with default umask (0644) — readable by other local users. Fixed: save_report now creates the directory with 0o700 and files with 0o600, using O_EXCL exclusive creation. Regression test asserts the modes. F4 Info _read_json caps JSON at 128 MB but HF re-reads tokenizer.json uncapped. Fixed: stat() size check (128 MB) on tokenizer.json before PreTrainedTokenizerFast loads it; sparse-file regression test. F5 Info Deeply nested JSON raised bare RecursionError, not ValueError. Fixed: caught and re-raised as ValueError("Dataset nesting too deep"). F6 Info load_dataset on a TTY/char device could block indefinitely. Fixed: refuse character/block devices with ValueError. Superseded by H1 (2026-10-12): FIFOs, sockets and directories are now refused too; only regular files are accepted. F7 Low CI used mutable action tags and had no audit gate. Fixed: actions pinned to SHAs; new security CI job runs pip-audit (after pip install -U pip setuptools) and bandit, both gating.

docs.title: Red-team round (2026-10-12)
docs.text:
An adversarial review round found 1 high, 1 medium and 4 low issues; all fixed with regression tests:

ID Severity Finding Resolution H1 High F6 was fixed incompletely: a named FIFO with no writer hangs load_dataset forever (no timeout), contradicting F6's own rationale. Fixed: load_dataset now opens with O_NONBLOCK and fstats the fd, refusing everything that is not a regular file (char/block devices, FIFOs, sockets, directories). The fd-based check also closes the stat→open TOCTOU. Watchdog-thread regression test proves no hang. M1 Medium Output-path failures surfaced only after the expensive run; the completed result was discarded with it. Fixed: the CLI claims the output directory (via new prepare_report_dir) before backend init; on any failure before the report is saved the empty dir is released so retries still see a fresh path. Regression tests cover init failure and path-through-file. L1 Low Empty expected answers are trivially satisfiable (a backend emitting only the boundary passes) with no warning. Fixed: inspect and run now warn on stderr naming the vacuous fixtures; documented in docs/USAGE.md. L2 Low candidate_fingerprint was syntactic: repeat_bos=True with bos="" fingerprinted differently from repeat_bos=False, contradicting local_repairs' own dedup notion of identity. Fixed: the fingerprint payload is normalized exactly like the dedup key. L3 Low Intermediate report parent dirs were 0o755, overstating the "readable only by the invoking user" claim. Fixed: prepare_report_dir chmods every created path component to 0o700; regression test asserts all components. L4 Low doctor's tokenizer_deep failure interpolated raw dependency exception text into machine-readable output — the one hole in the sanitized-error discipline. Fixed: maps to the fixed code tokenizer_deep_check_failed.

The red team also verified dynamically (socket firewall raising on any connect) that doctor, backend init and generation perform zero network access — this retires residual risk #4 below. A regression test (test_no_network_access_during_doctor_and_backend_init) now guards it.

pip-audit raw results: 6 vulns in pip 24.0 and 2 in setuptools 78.1.0 (install-time tools only; the package has zero runtime dependencies) — resolved by upgrading (pip install -U pip setuptools); post-upgrade audit is clean. transformers 5.19.0, safetensors 0.8.0, tokenizers 0.23.3 audited clean.

docs.title: Red-team round 2 (2026-10-13)
docs.text:
A second adversarial round probed novel vectors only (round-1 vectors were not re-tested). 9 of 10 vectors came back defended with PoC evidence: path traversal variants (../, absolute, ..\, URL-encoded, null bytes — IDs never reach the filesystem); symlink TOCTOU (16,731 file↔symlink swaps: 6,480 clean loads, 14,791 sanitized ValueErrors, zero unexpected exceptions, zero hangs); malicious fixtures (200k-deep nesting, duplicate keys, NaN/Infinity, 50 MB strings, invalid UTF-8 — all rejected; control chars and lone surrogates flow safely via ensure_ascii JSON and HTML escaping); HTML injection round 2 (12 hostile payloads through the full pipeline: zero raw payloads in report.html; CSP verified byte-for-byte; frame-ancestors cannot be expressed via meta tag — noted limitation); concurrent runs (atomic mkdir(exist_ok=False) + O_EXCL prevent corruption; loser fails fast); resource exhaustion (caps exact, cooperative cancellation measured at 0.41 s into a ~18 s run, flat memory); CLI edge cases (/, /dev/null, dangling symlinks, fullwidth digits, 5000-digit ints — all clean argparse errors); tempfile hygiene (zero tempfile usage; reports written directly with O_EXCL). Two genuine findings, both fixed:

ID Severity Finding Resolution U1 Low–Medium Unicode normalization evasion: NFD/NFC variants of the same visual string (e.g. café vs café) evaded the fixture-ID uniqueness and cross-split identical-message checks, allowing silent held-out contamination. Fixed: Split.__post_init__ compares NFC-normalized keys for IDs, groups and message contents; stored fixture data stays byte-exact so the exact-token-sequence principle is preserved. Homoglyph/confusable detection is out of scope (no normalization form unifies those) and is documented in core.py. Regression tests cover ID, message and group variants. T1 Low Terminal escape injection: inspect/run interpolated raw fixture IDs into stderr warnings, so a hostile fixture file could rewrite the operator's terminal title or clear the screen. Fixed: control characters (C0/C1) are stripped from IDs before display in both warnings (cli._display_id). Regression test asserts no ESC bytes on stderr.

doctor's machine-readable output was additionally reviewed: checkpoint-controlled strings there are always emitted through json.dumps (ensure_ascii=True), which neutralizes terminal escapes — no change needed.

docs.title: Red-team round 3 (2026-10-13)
docs.text:
A third adversarial round targeted the five new round-3 capabilities plus re-verification of every documented command. Novel vectors only; round-1/2 vectors were covered by the regression suite. Five genuine findings, all fixed with regression tests:

ID Severity Finding Resolution H3-1 High _hf_overhang_match (the StopStringCriteria port behind the stop matrix) missed the tensor implementation's end-overlap class where the stop string ends inside the final token (e.g. token " world", stop "or"; token "xstop", stop "stop"). The port only tried prefix overhangs (stop[-i:] == token[:i]), so the stop matrix systematically under-reported HF stops. Found by differential testing against the real transformers criterion (18/300 random trials diverged, all lab-miss-real-fire). Fixed: the port now mirrors _stop_string_get_matching_positions exactly (every end-overlap from dropping k trailing chars of the final token, then the valid-position walk backwards). Re-verified: 1500/1500 random trials agree on a byte-level BPE tokenizer, plus an exhaustive 256-combination scan on a second vocab with zero divergences. Residual (documented): token texts come from per-token decode while HF matches on cleaned vocab strings / raw bytes, so UTF-8-fragment tokens can still diverge — unfixable through the Backend protocol. H3-2 Medium template_diff is super-quadratic on adversarially fragmented inputs: an alternating equal/divergent token pattern of just n=2000 takes ~45 s (≈cubic scaling — ~6 min at n=4000), hanging template_conformance per (format, fixture) pair. Reachable via a hostile checkpoint template + hostile fixture. Fixed: the difflib matching-blocks loop is replicated with a 10 s wall-clock budget checked between find_longest_match calls (each call is linear, so the total is bounded); on expiry it raises ValueError("template_diff_too_fragmented"), which the existing per-pair handler degrades to "unavailable". Output is byte-identical to unbounded difflib on 400 randomized inputs; ordinary 20K-token diffs still complete in ~0.1 s. H3-3 Medium doctor's reference-model path (_portability_check) and template_conformance loaded tokenizer.json through PreTrainedTokenizerFast with no 128 MB pre-load cap — the round-1 fix applied only to LocalHFBackend. A swapped-in oversized tokenizer.json in a reference checkpoint is parsed into memory uncapped (PoC: 200 MB sparse file triggered a real loader call). Fixed: new _tokenizer_file() helper enforces the cap before every HF loader call site (reference portability, primary deep check, conformance); oversized files degrade to the fixed "skipped"/"unavailable" codes without parsing. Sparse-file regression tests assert the loader is never invoked. H3-4 High A hostile Jinja chat_template in tokenizer_config.json renders unbounded text: {{ 'x' * 100000000 }} OOM-killed the template_conformance worker (exit 137) during render/encode — no exception, the process dies. Fixed: the template source is capped at 1 MB chars ("unavailable" / "chat_template_too_large") and every rendered output at 1 MB chars (pair degrades to "unavailable" instead of encoding the bomb). Regression tests assert both degradations and that the loader/encoder never sees the bomb. Residual: CPU burn inside the Jinja render itself is the same exposure as HF's own apply_chat_template — run unfamiliar checkpoints with resource limits (see trust boundaries). H3-5 Medium The round-3 test file broke the [dev]-only suite: 7 test classes import tokenizers/transformers at test time with no skip guard, so the README quick-start path (pip install -e ".[dev]") errored instead of skipping. (Round 2 had validated that path green before test_round3.py existed.) Fixed: HAS_HF module guard + @unittest.skipUnless on the seven HF-dependent classes, restoring [dev]-only to skip-clean.

Probed and verified defended (PoC evidence, no change needed):

  • XSS via hostile candidate names: 5 hostile payloads (<script>, <img onerror>, <svg onload>, entity/quote breaking, {{7*7}}) through run_experiment → save_report → render_html, plus hostile names injected into all four new sections (conformance, stop matrix, sweep, taxonomy banner): zero raw payloads in report.html; {{7*7}} renders as inert text (no HTML metacharacters). New regression test pins this.
  • doctor --reference-model traversal/symlink: the asset name is the fixed literal "tokenizer.json" (_member rejects ../separators/symlinks); a symlinked tokenizer.json → "skipped"; a symlink loop → "skipped" (no hang); a symlinked directory resolves per operator choice and works. No traversal possible by construction.
  • truncate_text_tail: 20 adversarial cases (multi-byte splits, emoji, flag grapheme clusters, combining marks, empty/negative/bool inputs, lone-surrogate input): never emits lone surrogates (decode either succeeds to a valid str or the cut degrades to None); lone-surrogate input raises UnicodeEncodeError, a ValueError subclass, consistent with the contract. Grapheme-cluster splits stay at codepoint granularity as documented.
  • prompt_sensitivity_sweep: compute bounded (max_drop_bytes 1–8 enforced in CLI and function; depth count == bound); pre-cancelled sweep returns in 0.00 s (cancellation honored through every run_experiment); codepoint-splitting depths record the documented "failed" decision.
  • failure_taxonomy: 17 adversarial observation shapes (backend-error priority, cancelled grouping, mismatch-before-EOS priority, corrupt output_ids, empty dict, falsy non-bools) all classify as documented; non-dict input rejected.
  • check_boundary_portability: raising/lying secondary_encode callables degrade to the fixed secondary_encode_failed / secondary_encode_invalid codes, never raise.
  • vLLM emulation vs the real vllm/v1/engine/detokenizer.py: the find window, earliest-completion selection, bisect_left truncation and stop_buffer_length semantics all match the fetched upstream source; the new_char_count == 0 early-return is now ported too -- the old "cannot observably diverge" claim was wrong: for single-character stops (e.g. "\n") the window start 1 - len(stop) is 0 on a zero-new-char step, so a stop completed during the min_tokens gate was refound where upstream stays silent (found by the tests/test_cycle14_holdback.py differential harness, fixed 2026-10-15). Approximation documented: per-prefix batch decodes vs incremental DecodeStream (can differ on UTF-8 fragments), min_tokens=0 assumed.
  • Old surfaces: fixture-loading hostile inputs, report-dir permissions and the sanitized error vocabulary re-verified via the full suite (361 tests); new code paths emit only fixed-vocabulary details (int step counts, int ID lists) — no raw checkpoint/backend text.

docs.title: Red-team round 4 — final pre-release sweep (2026-10-16)
docs.text:
Three parallel adversarial agents probed novel surfaces only (rounds 1–3 vectors were covered by the regression suite): the model-protocol-lab debug REPL + CLI input handling, doctor/examine_model hostile checkpoints, and the scoring / report-diff / backend-emulation modules. Eight genuine findings, all fixed with regression tests in tests/test_cycle96_redteam_sweep.py:

ID Severity Finding Resolution R4-1 Medium Lone surrogates (\ud800) in hostile results.json / fixture content crashed strict stream writes: model-protocol-lab diff-reports died with uncaught UnicodeEncodeError on stderr, and the debug REPL session died (violating its "never die" invariant). The _CONTROL_CHARS sanitizers did not cover \ud800–\udfff. All four _CONTROL_CHARS regexes (debug.py, cli.py, diffreports.py, fixtures.py) now strip lone surrogates; astral characters (single codepoints) are unaffected. R4-2 Medium BaseException from a misbehaving backend escaped the sanitization boundary: core.evaluate (except Exception around backend.generate) and scoring.score_target_logprobs (except Exception around forward_logits) propagated, turning an hours-long run into a total loss instead of one failed observation. Both sites now catch BaseException and map to the fixed codes (generate_failed / forward_failed), with explicit re-raise of KeyboardInterrupt/SystemExit so Ctrl+C keeps working. R4-3 Medium Raw RecursionError escaped examine_model via a deeply-nested safetensors header (doctor._check_weight_headers): json.loads was wrapped in except (UnicodeDecodeError, json.JSONDecodeError) only, unlike _read_json which also catches RecursionError. Added RecursionError to the except tuple, mirroring _read_json. R4-4 Medium FIFO-swap hang: _read_json, _manifest (backends.py) and _check_weight_headers (doctor.py) used plain blocking open() after validation, so a FIFO swapped in for an asset hung the opener forever. The race window spans the whole weight-hashing phase. New shared _open_regular_read() helper: O_NONBLOCK open + fstat S_ISREG check on the fd (the datasets.py pattern); _manifest now fstats the opened fd for its before-snapshot. All three call sites fail closed with fixed vocabulary. R4-5 Medium Jinja chat-template memory bomb: template_conformance called apply_chat_template which materializes the full rendered string before the 1MB _RENDERED_MAX_CHARS check -- a 26-byte {{ 'x' * 500_000_000 }} template grew RSS by 1.9GB first (larger multipliers OOM-kill). The render now runs under a transient RLIMIT_AS (current virtual size + 256MB headroom): a bomb raises catchable MemoryError -> "unavailable" with zero RSS growth; legitimate renders unaffected. Falls back to unbounded render on non-Unix platforms. R4-6 Low–Medium portability_matrix raised raw OSError on an unreadable second checkpoint (_read_json wrapped in except ValueError only), breaking its "never raises for checkpoint problems" contract for direct API users. Now catches OSError -> "unavailable" / "missing_or_unsafe_asset". R4-7 Low Unbounded checkpoint-controlled model_type interpolated into machine-readable output (f"unsupported model_type: {model_type!r}"): a 5MB model_type produced a 5MB detail string, breaking the fixed-vocabulary discipline. Preview truncated to 200 chars. R4-8 Low Quadratic transcript accounting in the debug REPL: onecmd re-summed the entire transcript on every command (~20s for a 10k-line script at the advertised caps). Running self._transcript_chars counter, recomputed only on truncation.

Probed and verified defended (PoC evidence, no change needed): .read recursion/nesting (14 sub-probes), hostile renders (escape stripping at byte level), .save path handling, _parse_id_list strictness, the 128MB tokenizer cap on the debug path, argparse edges on all subcommands, _build_primary_tokenizer hostiles, symlink/special-file games, examine_dataset hostiles, scoring NaN/inf/empty/shape edges, diffreports/diffbackends hostile inputs (40MB files, 10k nesting, duplicate keys, FIFOs), SGLang/HF/vLLM emulation bounds, and experiments.py cancellation/corruption handling.

docs.title: Red-team round 5 — wave-2 adversarial audit (2026-10-18)
docs.text:
Six read-only specialists (security red-team A, adversarial red-team B tasked with disproving A's findings, cross-verifier, perf, researcher, docs-coherence) audited the cycles 134–144 feature code with a mandatory cross-check protocol. 10 CONFIRMED findings; the builder re-verified each against the current tree before fixing (cycle 145):

ID Severity Finding Resolution C1 High margin_trajectory still O(B·C) quadratic: the point cap bounds total points, not candidates — C candidates × 1 point each projected to ~1–2h per diff-reports pair on a hostile few-MB payload (measured ~4.1× per doubling by two agents). Restructured to an O((E+B) log (E+C)) event sweep with a lazily-deleted leader heap; 0/1400 differential mismatches vs the old sweep; C=2000 in 0.008s (was ~1.4s). Perf regression test pins subquadratic scaling. C2 Low Raw old_decision/new_decision interpolation injected terminal escapes into stderr in the transfer/robustness/perturbation drift renderers, falsifying render_summary's sanitization comment. All three wrapped in _display_id; sanitization tests pin escape-stripping. C3 Low Non-string decision/winner/tier values crashed render_summary with TypeError (_display_id regex-sub on non-str), contradicting the degrade-gracefully contract. _display_id is now total (None → "(none)", others via str()); non-string payloads render instead of crashing. C4/C5 Low diff_transfer/diff_contamination changed flags had unpinned disjuncts (cell-drift-only, tier-escalation-only mutants survived the suite); same gap class in diff_perturbation. Single-cause pinning tests for every disjunct; all five mutants re-run and killed. C6 Cosmetic checkpoint_drift renderer uncapped. Capped at 10 with "... and N more", like cell_drift.

Disputed as security findings (real patterns, proven unreachable — JSON keys are always strings; in-repo callers pass str-keyed data): non-string dict keys in HTML sections, missing key-type check in diff_boundary_audit. Template firewall note (F5): the static AST scan misses concatenated-dunder subscripts by construction; six bypass payloads were thrown at the stack and all died in ImmutableSandboxedEnvironment + jinja2 3.1.6 — the "denies the RCE primitives" docstring now describes the static layer's actual scope.

New security-relevant features since round 4, all covered above and by their own test suites: the template conformance firewall (cycle 136: static Jinja AST scan denying dunder access, |attr, dangerous globals before any render; doctor.template_conformance refuses denied templates fail-closed), chat-marker isolation conformance (cycle 135: hostile marker strings must not become control tokens), and the cycle-141 hostile-input hardening (three TypeError crashes on non-string dict keys fixed fail-closed).

docs.title: Proven safe (adversarial PoCs, observed not inferred)
docs.text:
• XSS: hostile payloads in every dynamic render_html field render fully neutralized (html.escape, quote=True), including inside data-sort attribute values; CSS classes from internal dicts; CSP default-src 'none' with script-src allowlisting only the SHA-256 hash of the single fixed inline table sorter; no external assets, no other <script>.
  • Path traversal: _member rejects ../separators/symlinks (regex ^[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+$ + is_symlink/is_file checks); shard names constrained to [A-Za-z0-9_.-]+\.safetensors; save_report writes only fixed filenames.
  • ReDoS: the two regexes are linear char classes (100 kB near-miss in ~1 ms); no nested quantifiers or alternation.
  • Deserialization: NaN/Infinity/duplicate keys rejected; 2 MB cap before json.loads; no pickle/yaml/marshal/eval/subprocess in the package.
  • Supply chain: the only network-adjacent calls are two from_pretrained (local_files_only=True, trust_remote_code=False, token=False), one PreTrainedTokenizerFast(tokenizer_file=…) (local file), and importlib.metadata.version() (local). No hf_hub_download, snapshot_download, sockets, or HTTP clients anywhere. This is the structural defense against the CVE-2026-80047 class (transformers writing remote repository code to the local module cache before the trust-consent check): the lab never loads remote repositories and never enables trust_remote_code, so the vulnerable code path is unreachable. Pinned by tests/test_cycle117_local_loading_invariant_audit.py (AST guards: no trust_remote_code=True, every from_pretrained passes local_files_only=True, no download helpers, no truthy token=). Deserialization: the model-weight from_pretrained additionally passes use_safetensors=True (transformers never touches the pickle unpickler) and weights_only=True (defense in depth if a fallback ever engaged), and no torch.load / pickle.load(s) appears in the package. This is the structural defense against the CVE-2025-32434 (torch <2.6.0) and CVE-2026-24747 (torch <=2.9.1, fixed 2.10.0; CVSS 8.8 — the weights_only=True unpickler itself was bypassable) classes. The installed torch 2.14.1+cpu is not affected by either, but the lab's defense does not depend on that: pinned by tests/test_cycle119_pickle_deserialization_invariant_audit.py (AST guards: no torch.load/pickle.load(s); every model-weight from_pretrained passes use_safetensors=True and weights_only=True).
  • TOCTOU: _manifest hashes every asset before and after HF loading and compares size/mtime/ino + sha256; swaps fail closed.
  • Cancellation: the generate Event is checked before lock acquisition, in the lock-retry loop, and between forward steps; all public caps are hard.

docs.title: Residual risks (accepted)
docs.text:
1. torch's +cpu local tag stays invisible to pip-audit; its CVE posture needs manual re-verification on every bump.
  2. No hash-pinned lockfile: fresh installs trust PyPI within the declared ranges; mitigated by the CI pip-audit gate. Partially tightened 2026-10-23 (cycle 201): the hf extra now caps torch below its next major (torch>=2.6,<3, matching the existing transformers<6 cap), so the largest dependency can no longer cross a major release silently; the lockfile gap itself remains accepted as recorded here.
  3. ~~_manifest reads every weight file twice per run (before/after init) — hundreds of GB of I/O on very large checkpoints; documented, not a defect.~~ Retired 2026-10-17 (cycle 115): the backend now hashes each weight file once and verifies a cheap stat fingerprint (st_size, st_mtime_ns, st_ino) after the load; the double full-hash is gone. Documented trade-off: a content swap preserving size, nanosecond mtime and inode inside the load window would evade the stat check — catching it needs the full re-hash.
  4. ~~Runtime network isolation of the adapter has not been verified by test (code review only).~~ Retired 2026-10-12: verified dynamically under a socket firewall (zero connect attempts across doctor, backend init and generation); guarded by test_no_network_access_during_doctor_and_backend_init.
  5. The HF stop emulation matches on per-token decode strings while real HF matches on cleaned vocab strings / raw bytes: UTF-8-fragment tokens can make real HF fire where the emulation does not (verified: no divergence on 1500 random byte-level trials or an exhaustive 256-combination scan outside the fragment case). Unfixable through the Backend protocol; documented in docs/USAGE.md §8.2.
  6. A hostile Jinja chat template can burn CPU inside the render itself (transformers' sandbox restricts code execution, not resource use). Template source and rendered output are capped at 1 MB each (round-3 fix); on Unix, in the main thread, each render additionally runs under a 10 s SIGALRM wall-clock budget (_render_with_time_budget) and aborts with _RenderTimeBudgetExceeded, degrading the pair to "unavailable" (cycle-116 fix). Residual: off the main thread or on non-Unix platforms the watchdog cannot be installed and the render runs unbounded -- the same exposure as HF's own apply_chat_template. Run unfamiliar checkpoints with resource limits. (Re-verified dynamically in the 2026-10-22 oversight audit: rendering a CPU-bomb template (a {% for %} loop over a 200k range, ~1.6e10 inner steps) from a worker thread left the render still running after 16 s while the calling thread proceeded — confirming the watchdog never arms off the main thread, exactly as stated here.)
  7. template_diff degrades (not hangs) after a 10 s budget per (format, fixture) pair on adversarially fragmented inputs; a fully hostile checkpoint can still cost ~10 s per pair before each degrades.
  8. Invisible format characters (zero-width space, BOM, soft hyphen, word joiner, ...) survive the terminal sanitizers by design: they cannot reorder text or inject controls, so they are preserved for diagnostic fidelity. Residual: lookalike fixture IDs (admin vs admin\u200b) render identically in listings and diffs -- verify IDs byte-wise before acting on them.
  9. Unicode bidi controls survive into report.html text: HTML-escaping keeps them inert (no tag breakout, no script execution; verified byte-level), so at most the operator's own local report could visually spoof ordering. The terminal path strips them. Accepted.

docs.title: Data disclosure
docs.text:
No network reporting or telemetry is implemented in this package. Dependency behavior has not been audited. Default report JSON excludes raw observation arrays, but names, format strings, fingerprints, counts and decisions remain. Evidence mode retains answer text and input/output token IDs. Token IDs are not anonymization.

Do not publish actual prompts, outputs, datasets, weights, local paths, credentials, account configuration or dependency diagnostic logs without reviewing them. The source archive contains synthetic examples only. .gitignore is a convenience, not a secret scanner or access-control boundary.

The report renderer escapes displayed strings and uses a restrictive content-security policy. Browser behavior and hostile-content rendering still require testing. Do not expand it to render model output as HTML or execute supplied JavaScript. The one inline script is fixed, author-controlled and hash-pinned in the CSP; it never touches model-derived text.

docs.title: Operational limits
docs.text:
Current safeguards limit fixture size, candidate count, token output and configured context. They do not guarantee bounded memory, runtime or GPU utilization. Model loading can be expensive before evaluation starts. Cancellation does not preempt a running native operation.

Do not expose the library or CLI directly as a multi-user network service. Authentication, tenant isolation, safe job scheduling, audit logging and resource enforcement are not implemented.

docs.title: Supported versions
docs.text: Security fixes ship on the latest release line only; older lines are not backported. Supported Python versions are those in pyproject.toml's requires-python that CI exercises (currently 3.11, 3.12, 3.13). No response-time commitment is made for reports; the private reporting route below is the channel, and fixes land on the latest line.

docs.title: Verifying a release
docs.text:
Releases are built reproducibly and published with PEP 740 attestations (see .github/workflows/release.yml). To verify an artifact you downloaded:

gh attestation verify <artifact> --repo strmt7/model-protocol-lab

To reproduce the artifacts yourself, build twice from the tagged tree with the tagged commit's timestamp as the epoch and compare SHA-256 hashes with the published assets:

EPOCH=$(git log -1 --format=%ct <tag>)
python tools/release_build.py --source . --output /tmp/mpl-verify-dist --epoch "$EPOCH"

The base wheel installs zero dependencies — check its METADATA: every Requires-Dist line is gated on an extra (extra == "hf" or extra == "dev"), so a plain pip install pulls nothing. The [hf] extra is declared as version ranges in pyproject.toml, not a lockfile; inventory your resolved set after installing it (for example with pip freeze) rather than trusting any bill of materials the release does not ship.

docs.title: Why no SBOM is shipped (cycle 210 adjudication)
docs.text: No SPDX/CycloneDX bill of materials is attached to releases, by a twice-considered decision (cycle 208 S3, re-adjudicated on the procurement merits in cycle 210). A bill of materials for this wheel would contain exactly one package — the wheel itself — because it has zero runtime dependencies; the inventory information it would carry is already inside the artifact as METADATA, verifiable with unzip -p dist/*.whl '*/METADATA'. A bill of materials for the [hf] resolved set would be stale on arrival (version ranges) or would require the multi-GB CUDA download in the release job. And any SBOM step would live in the tag-only release job, which never runs until the first real release — adding a blocking third-party step there, unexercised, is the wrong trade. This is revisited only at the first release rehearsal, once the publish path has actually run.

docs.title: Reporting defects
docs.text: For public issues, provide a minimal synthetic reproduction and dependency versions. Exclude credentials, proprietary prompts, private model files and personally identifying data. For sensitive defects, use GitHub's private vulnerability reporting for this repository — it is enabled (verified through the GitHub API, 2026-10-23): open the repository's Security tab and choose Report a vulnerability, or go to https://github.com/strmt7/model-protocol-lab/security/advisories/new. Reports there are visible only to the maintainer until a fix ships.

docs.title: Surface-noise self-consistency probe — design
docs.text:
Status: frozen design for cycle 165. Instrument name (honest): surface-noise self-consistency probe — never "prompt-quality meter", never unqualified "robustness score".

Monday-morning utility: a developer about to ship a prompt runs the probe to see which surface-noise family flips their task success and how close the nearest observed flip is — before production typos find out first.

Positioning (web-verified 2026-10-19): ctxray (MIT) is the static tier — deterministic 0–100 scoring over 30+ prompt features, lint, rewrite, MCP server — but no perturbation, no radius, no counterfactuals, not stdlib-only. This probe is the dynamic tier: perturbation-based verdict stability over a frozen operator set. The two compose; they do not overlap. Academic credit: CoIPO/NoisyPromptBench "decoding radius" R(a) (arXiv:2603.03314, ICLR 2026) is the model-centric precedent for a perturbation radius; the 2026 PCE paper is the precedent for minimal-flip counterfactuals (LLM-based, research-only). Our combination — per-prompt, frozen deterministic protocol, stdlib-only MCP, zero LLM calls — has no complete competitor as of 2026-10-19 (see docs/RESEARCH_LOG.md).

docs.title: 1. The verdict function V (closes R1)
docs.text:
Subject. The instrument under test is a prompt text P: the instruction/template span the user supplies. Fixture message content is never modified (this resolves R6: perturbing task content while the expected answer stays pinned would punish the prompt for the fixture's brittleness).

Rendering (frozen). Each evaluation renders

Instruction: <P>

<role>: <content>
<role>: <content>
...

with fixture messages verbatim, then generates with the backend (greedy, exact token sequences). Template choice is out of scope — the lab's other experiments measure template effects; the rendering here is fixed and documented.

Definition. V(P, F, B) is the pass/fail vector over fixtures F = (f_1 … f_n) with backend B. Position i is:

  • "pass" — generation completed and the decoded output exactly equals f_i.expected;
  • "abstain" — generation did not complete (cancelled/error);
  • "fail" — otherwise.

Baseline. V computed on the unperturbed P with the same (F, B).

Flip predicate. A variant P′ flips iff its pass/fail vector differs from the baseline vector on any mutually-evaluable fixture (evaluable in both runs). A change in either direction counts — a variant that fixes a failing fixture is still instability, because the prompt's behavior changed under noise. No τ threshold: any vector difference is a flip. This is the strictest well-defined predicate and has no magic numbers.

Falsifiability. "P is stable under operator O" is falsified by exhibiting one seed in the frozen plan whose variant flips. "No flip observed under plan S" is falsified by exhibiting any flip within S.

docs.title: 2. Distance (closes R2)
docs.text:
One normalized unit within each operator family — never a cross-operator scalar. The token indel-edit rate

d(P, P′) = indel(encode(P), encode(P′)) / (len(encode(P)) + len(encode(P′)))

where indel is the insertion/deletion edit distance (a substitution counts as delete + insert = 2), computed exactly by Myers' O(ND) greedy algorithm — exact and fast for near-identical sequences, which perturbations are. d ∈ [0, 1] by construction (indel ≤ n + m). Reported per operator; cross-operator comparison is explicitly not-comparable (different perturbation classes). There is no collapsed "robustness gauge" — the per-operator bars are the report. The substitution-=2 convention is stated, not hidden: what the unit measures is "fraction of combined token mass inserted or deleted".

docs.title: 3. Nearest observed flip (closes R4)
docs.text:
Per operator: d_obs = min d over flipping effective variants in the frozen search plan S, or "none observed". Labeled everywhere as "nearest observed flip under frozen search plan S" with S published verbatim and coverage stated ("8 of 2⁶⁴ seeds searched"). Exact where enumerable: punctuation_strip (exactly 1 outcome), whitespace (exactly 3 modes enumerated). Seeded operators (typo, case_flip, unicode_variant): heuristic, 8 seeds each.

d_obs ≥ d* always (min over a subset ≥ min over the full space): the reported number is an upper bound on the true minimal-flip distance and errs toward false confidence. It is never a guarantee, never a certificate. There is no separate "margin" metric — the nearest observed flip is the margin, reported with its truncation stated (R12a).

docs.title: 4. Frozen protocol (F4)
docs.text:
freeze_surface_noise_protocol() publishes, before any scoring:

  • instrument name + version, operator names + sha256 of perturbation.py (code hash),
  • the search plan verbatim: {operator: [seeds]} or "modes"/"single",
  • the prompt/task split ("perturbation applies to the prompt text span only; fixture message content is never modified"),
  • the frozen rendering, the flip predicate, the denominator definition,
  • backend identity + weight-file fingerprint (R13),
  • fixture id list + hashes, creation timestamp.

The probe refuses to run when the protocol's code hash differs from the current perturbation.py, or the backend fingerprint differs from the frozen one. Scores are comparable only under identical (fixtures, backend, protocol-fingerprint) triples (R12c).

docs.title: 5. Denominators (closes R8, R12d)
docs.text: Every result reports, per operator, n_total / n_effective / n_abstained / n_error. n_effective = variants whose perturbed prompt span changed the token-id sequence (via backend.encode) — text-level "changed" is insufficient (e.g. case changes can be tokenizer-invisible). No-op variants are listed and never counted as stable. Stability per operator = n_unchanged / n_effective.

docs.title: 6. Controls (R9, with the circularity documented)
docs.text: Self-contained calibration harness: each control declares the backend output it expects; run_surface_noise_controls builds dedicated fixtures from them and scores them with a fixed calibration backend (_ControlCalibrationBackend: exact "exactly: OK" → "OK", exact "SAY IT LOUD: HELLO" → "LOUD", any other non-empty prompt → "BLUE") under a freshly frozen protocol. The sturdy controls are stable by construction (perturbations never produce empty text, so the non-empty rule never flips: stability exactly 1.0); the fragile controls flip deterministically under the operators (measured: 0.15 / 0.0). Discrimination check: mean sturdy stability > mean fragile stability. A pass validates the implementation against the specification. Provenance per control is designer-authored and documented as encoding the operator set's own theory of fragility — the circularity is stated, not hidden (Adapter Rule). One held-out control set lives outside the test suite; CI pins its count and provenance, not its content.

docs.title: 7. Static lint tier (advisory)
docs.text: Five fully-specified deterministic checks (nonempty, bounded_length, no_bidi_controls, terminal_punctuation, sentence_repetition with an exact predicate). Advisory: never gates the sweep (R12e), never blended into a scalar (R12b). Displayed side-by-side with the dynamic panel. (ctxray remains the serious static tier; this is a cheap pre-sweep sanity panel, labeled as such.)

docs.title: 8. Verbosity guardrail (R3)
docs.text: Prompt token length and the repetition flag are displayed alongside the radii. Documented: noise-robustness can anti-correlate with concision (redundancy survives character noise); the improvement loop must never optimize the radius alone.

docs.title: 9. Not measured (R7 — prominent, not a footnote)
docs.text: Semantic paraphrase of instructions, conflicting-instruction override / prompt injection, hierarchy attacks, tool-call schema adherence under noise, multi-turn drift, context-length degradation. The instrument measures surface-form noise only. The MCP tool is named probe_surface_noise_stability — the name is the scope.

docs.title: 10. Pseudoscience checklist (R12)
docs.text:
• (a) No separate margin metric; nearest-observed-flip carries its truncation statement.
  • (b) Static and dynamic tiers side-by-side; never a blended scalar.
  • (c) Cross-prompt ranking requires identical (fixtures, backend, protocol-fingerprint) triples, else labeled not-comparable.
  • (d) Full denominators on every call; abstentions explicit.
  • (e) The lint tier is advisory; any gating would be reported as censoring.

docs.title: 11. Adapter Rule (scope paragraph, shown with every result)
docs.text: This probe measures stability of task success under a frozen set of surface-form text perturbations. A high stability number means the prompt's pass/fail pattern survived those perturbations on those fixtures with that backend — nothing more. It is not a certificate of prompt quality, not a guarantee against real-world typos (the searched seeds are a sliver of the space; the reported distance is an upper bound), and not a measurement of semantic, adversarial, or injection robustness. Controls validate discrimination within the operator set's theory of fragility, not against real-world prompt failure.

docs.title: 12. Improvement-loop gating (R14)
docs.text: surface_noise_hardening_notes surfaces the probe's own counterfactuals (weakest operator family, nearest flips, lint findings) as information. It does not run an optimization loop. Any generate→score→generate loop built on the probe must validate acceptance on a held-out operator family, keep the verbosity guardrail, and report full attempt denominators — otherwise it optimizes the metric's blind spots, not prompt quality.

docs.title: 13. MCP server
docs.text: Stdlib-only stdio JSON-RPC 2.0 server (model_protocol_lab.mcp_server, shipped with the model-protocol-lab-mcp console script; a tools/surface_noise_mcp_server.py launcher remains for checkouts). --self-test runs one embedded probe end-to-end and exits 0.
