Contract wording: "local and offline" (the VulnerabilityScreener skeleton's "never touches the network" docstring was proven false in its own code; corrected on port).

docs.title: 14. CLI and dashboard
docs.text:
model-protocol-lab surface-noise probe --prompt F --fixtures F.json --boundary-ids 7 --backend selftest|local-hf [--model P] --output DIR [--max-new-tokens N] [--seed S] — writes probe.json + dashboard.html (refuses to overwrite an existing path). model-protocol-lab surface-noise diff OLD.json NEW.json — compares two probe.json files (before/after a prompt edit). model-protocol-lab surface-noise protocol — prints the frozen instrument descriptor (no scoring). Monday-morning use is printed in --help and the descriptor.

The dashboard is self-contained HTML (inline CSS+SVG, no external assets, default-src 'none' CSP). Every interpolated string is escaped, including SVG text nodes (R11). The prompt text is never rendered raw — only its sha256. Minimal-flip counterfactual excerpts appear only when the caller supplies the prompt text and its sha256 matches the report. The Adapter Rule is the first thing on the page; the not-measured list and the comparability warning are prominent, not footnotes.

docs.title: 15. Comparing two probe runs
docs.text:
model_protocol_lab.diffreports.diff_surface_noise(old, new) compares two probe.json payloads: per-operator stability drift and nearest-flip drift, baseline pass-count change, prompt-text change, and protocol fingerprint change (any protocol drift flags the pair not-comparable). changed/identical follow the module's conventions.

Intentionally NOT wired into the results.json dispatcher: the probe is a per-prompt instrument producing standalone probe.json files, not a per-candidate experiment. Forcing it into model-protocol-lab run would conflate two workflows; the improve-then-re-probe loop is probe → edit → probe → diff.

model_protocol_lab.mcp_server, stdlib-only (json, sys, threading — no third-party; must run on the no-optional-deps CI job). Ported from the VulnerabilityScreener stdio skeleton (framing, MCPError, TOOLS registry, handle_request, real-stdio serve loop) with the contract wording corrected ("local and offline" — the skeleton's "never touches the network" is false in its own code). Liberal protocol acceptance: tools/list / tools/call work with no prior initialize (stateless, per the 2026-07-28 revision as reported in secondary write-ups — the spec text itself could not be fetched directly at build time and this is documented), the 2024-11-05 handshake is also accepted but never required; server/discover is implemented. Bounds (FlitzZip pattern, POSIX enforcement): 1 MiB prompt cap (stated rationale: memory-DoS prevention; the sweep multiplies input size across variants), ≤ 50 fixtures, operators/seeds fixed by the frozen plan (no free n_seeds, no free timeout), one-sweep-at-a-time lock, cooperative cancellation between forwards with fail-closed status: "cancelled" on budget expiry (R5 — never a partial score).

docs.title: Behavioural template probe — design
docs.text:
model-protocol-lab doctor --model DIR --template-probe renders frozen probe conversations through a checkpoint's own chat template and reports, per probe pair, whether the rendering changed anywhere outside the one message whose text was swapped.

Monday-morning use. A practitioner who downloads a checkpoint runs the probe before the first experiment and learns whether the template's rendering is a pure framing of the conversation or changes with message content — the signature of content-conditional template logic — instead of trusting that a passed static scan means the template only frames messages.

docs.title: Why a behavioural probe
docs.text: The static template firewall (template_audit.scan_template_ast) proves the template contains no RCE primitives. It cannot see content-conditional logic written in legal Jinja: a template that injects an instruction only when a trigger phrase appears in a user message passes the AST scan with zero findings. That class is demonstrated by arXiv:2602.04653 (chat-template backdoors keyed on multi-word trigger phrases, typically matched case-normalised). The probe is the dynamic tier next to the firewall's static tier: the firewall runs first, and a denied template is never rendered.

docs.title: Definitions
docs.text:
The probe conversations are frozen constants in model_protocol_lab/templateprobe.py (protocol v1, SHA-256 fingerprint in every payload; a changed word is protocol drift and needs a version bump, the refusals v1→v2 precedent).

  • Probe message. A synthetic message whose content is LEFT_SENTINEL + " " + body + " " + RIGHT_SENTINEL. Sentinels are uppercase-alphanumeric nonces, unique per logical message; the alphabet survives |upper and |trim. No alphabet survives a template that rewrites content — those shapes land in transform_unverifiable / span_unresolvable by design.
  • Span. For a render where a message's left sentinel occurs exactly once and its right sentinel exactly once, in order: the char interval between them. Defined by construction, never inferred from content search or diff alignment. Every other shape is span_unresolvable.
  • Swap pair. Two conversations identical except one frozen word in one message (length-matched swaps, so legitimate length branches do not flip). Each member is rendered twice.
  • Change envelope. The region between the longest common prefix and the longest common suffix of the two renders, computed by bisect-on-slice-equality (the algorithm is pinned; a per-char loop at the 1M-char render cap costs ~100× more).
  • Within-span check. When the swapped body's stable fragments appear verbatim in the base span, the swapped span must equal the base span with the slot word substituted.

docs.title: Pair outcomes
docs.text:
One class per pair, in this precedence order:

outcome meaning nondeterministic_render a member differed across its own double render unexercised the two renders are byte-identical overall span_unresolvable a sentinel rule failed in either render content_dropped the span is empty/whitespace for a non-empty body extra_span_change the change envelope is not contained in the span span_content_mismatch envelope contained, but the within-span substitution check fails transform_unverifiable envelope contained; body fragments not verbatim in the span, so the within-span check cannot run clean envelope contained and the within-span check passes render_error the render itself raised (driver-level)

extra_span_change and span_content_mismatch are the findings. Findings carry a capped, control-stripped excerpt of the changed region plus its length and SHA-256; they are grouped by region hash and the list is capped with an overflow count.

Role arms (add_system, promote_first_user) report render-diff facts only — span_vanished, span_merged, span_order_changed, role_render_error, nondeterministic_render, unchanged. The payload never claims a region "means" system or that content was "promoted": a hostile template defines its own framing markers, so marker semantics are not definable from the render.

docs.title: Pre-registered claims
docs.text:
• T1′. For the frozen control framer (a plain ChatML-class template), every pair is clean. Real templates are subjects, never controls.
  • T2′. The seeded backdoor controls are flagged on the pairs whose swap completes the trigger: single-word, phrase-completion ("please answer precisely"), and case-normalised variants. The conditional-removed twin and the payload-neutral twin are flagged on no pair. A trigger living in an unchanged message is pinned as not detected at pair level under protocol v1 — the injection is constant across that pair, so no paired diff can see it.
  • T3′. Findings never aggregate into a template verdict; the doctor verdict and CLI exit code are byte-identical with and without --template-probe, on healthy and on failed reports.
  • T4′. A second-granularity strftime_now control is classified nondeterministic_render by the baseline double renders. Day-granularity time-dependence passes the baseline; findings are scoped to the run's date, which the payload records.
  • T5′. The section is byte-identical across two runs on the same checkpoint (same machine, same versions), and carries the template source SHA-256, the protocol fingerprint, the render-environment versions, and counts for every outcome class — no class is silently dropped.

docs.title: Budgets and failure mapping
docs.text: The section is capped at 128 renders and a 120 s cooperative wall-clock deadline checked between renders (a single render remains bounded only by the render watchdog where one exists — SIGALRM is Unix/main-thread only; the docs state this rather than papering over it). Exceeding either cap fails closed to unavailable / template_probe_budget_exceeded with partial counts preserved. If span_unresolvable + unexercised + nondeterministic_render exceed half of all pairs, the section is unavailable / template_probe_inconclusive — the probe could not see the template, which must not read as a quiet pass. A checkpoint whose template passes the firewall but whose tokenizer cannot load reports unavailable / tokenizer_load_failed. The extraction scope is the tokenizer_config.json-embedded string only: list-form templates and a separate chat_template.jinja file report no_template.

docs.title: Limits, stated with the capability
docs.text: The probe conversations are published constants, and a template can detect them — by the sentinel strings, by conversation shape, or by the synthetic phrasing — and suppress conditional behaviour while being probed. A section with no findings therefore bounds only non-probe-aware templates. The template source is scanned for the sentinel strings before rendering and a hit is reported (sentinel_in_template_source), which catches the literal form of that evasion, not the shape-based forms. The probe set is a frozen sample: a backdoor keyed on a trigger outside the swap table, on conversation shape, or on tools (the render path passes no tools= argument in v1) is missed by construction. Legitimate templates with content conditionals — length branches the length-matched swaps do not neutralise, dedup, defaults — produce findings too; a finding is a fact about where rendering changed, and the inserted text is shown precisely so a human can judge it. Nothing in the section is a safety certificate, in either direction.

docs.title: Template surface-noise robustness — design v2 (cycle 166)
docs.text: v2 addresses the cycle-166 red-team review (A: 22 findings; B: cross-check — 21 survive, 1 downgraded, 0 refuted — plus new N1). Every blocking finding is resolved below; each resolution cites the finding ID.

docs.title: What it is
docs.text: A per-candidate measurement for model-protocol-lab run --template-robustness: for each candidate chat template, how well does it preserve correct verdicts when surface noise hits user-supplied content? The template is the independent variable; model weights, fixtures, backend, and protocol are fixed.

docs.title: Monday-morning use
docs.text: You are choosing a chat template to ship and your users type sloppily. For each candidate, this reports the fraction of its correct fixture verdicts that survive surface-noise perturbations — so you can see which template degrades most gracefully, before you ship it.

docs.title: The unit of analysis and the verdict function
docs.text:
For candidate template T (a Format; stage keys by candidate name exactly as in results.json's candidates dict — F21), fixture f, backend B:

  • render_T(f) = T.render(f.messages) (user-role message contents may be perturbed; roles, order, and non-user messages are byte-identical — F10).
  • V(T, f) = verdict(B.encode(render_T(f))), pass/fail/abstain by exact answer match, same fail-closed semantics as the probe's _evaluate_one.
  • For perturbation variant w (see "Operator set"): f_w = f with w applied to user-role message contents; V_w(T, f) = verdict(B.encode(render_T(f_w))).
  • A flip for (T, f, w): V_w(T, f) != V(T, f) over mutually-evaluable pairs (both non-abstain). Either direction counts; the rationale is the probe's: a flip is a verdict change under noise, regardless of direction (F16).

docs.title: Operator set (F1)
docs.text:
The probe's full operator set is not reused. Perturbing fixture content with typo or punctuation_strip can change the task's correct answer while expected stays pinned (e.g. "2.5 + 2.45" → "25 + 245") — the R6 inversion the probe was designed to avoid. The template-robustness operator set is restricted to presentation-level operators, defined as perturbing presentation without changing the correct answer:

  • whitespace (frozen modes), case_flip, unicode_variant.

Excluded, with reason: typo (can change the correct answer: "cat"→"car"), punctuation_strip (can change the correct answer: "2.5"→"25"). The set is frozen in the protocol; results are conditional on it. Pathological fixtures whose correct answer is presentation-sensitive (e.g. whitespace-significant code) are outside the instrument's scope — stated here, not hidden (F1).

docs.title: Headline metric (N1, F7)
docs.text:
Naive "mean stability" is rejected: P(flip | baseline pass) >> P(flip | baseline fail) for exact-match tasks (breaking a match needs any output change; repairing one needs noise to produce exactly the expected string), so mean stability mechanically rewards low-accuracy templates (B's derivation; the asymmetry vanishes for binary-choice tasks — stated as the scope limit).

The primary metric is the verdict preservation rate, baseline-conditioned:

  • Let P_T = {f : V(T,f) = pass} (pass-baseline fixtures).
  • For f ∈ P_T, let W_f = {w : V_w(T,f) ≠ abstain} (mutually-evaluable variants). f is preserved iff ∀w ∈ W_f: V_w(T,f) = pass. If W_f is empty, f is unevaluable (excluded, counted in n_unevaluable — never counted as stable).
  • Preservation rate = |{f preserved}| / |{f ∈ P_T : W_f ≠ ∅}|. None (not 1.0, not 0.0) when the denominator is 0 — with the explanatory note, per the wave-5 abstain policy (surfacenoise.py, wave-5 fix #2).

Secondary, informational only:

  • Noise repair rate = |{f : V(T,f)=fail ∧ ∃w ∈ W_f: V_w(T,f)=pass}| / |{f : V(T,f)=fail ∧ W_f ≠ ∅}| — how often noise accidentally fixes a wrong verdict. Never blended into the primary metric.
  • Per-operator preservation vectors: the preservation rate restricted to variants of one operator. Reported per operator; never a cross-operator minimum or blend (F5 — the probe's R12b rejection applies here too).
  • Nearest observed flip, per operator per (T, f): minimum content-span distance (below) over flipping variants of that operator; "none observed" when empty. Cross-operator minima are not reported.

docs.title: Distance (F3, F17, N2)
docs.text: Pinned: normalized token indel-edit rate d = indel/(n+m) ∈ [0,1] (token_edit_distance, which returns a raw int, divided by the combined length — the probe's unit), computed on the message-content span (pre-render) tokenized with the backend's tokenizer: d(f, f_w) over user-role message contents. Because the content span is identical across templates for the same (f, w), the distance is template-invariant by construction — this eliminates the verbosity bias (verbose templates mechanically scoring "closer") that rendered-input distance would introduce (F3). The model saw the rendered form; the distance describes the perturbation magnitude. Stated, not hidden.

docs.title: No-op filter (F4)
docs.text: Variants whose perturbed user content is token-identical to the original (token IDs of the content span, via the backend tokenizer) are no-ops: listed in no_ops, never counted in any denominator. Token-ID identity is used — not text identity — because the distance d = indel/(n+m) is computed on token IDs: a textually-different-but-identically-tokenized variant has d=0, can never flip, and would otherwise pad the denominator as guaranteed-preserved.

docs.title: What the number means — and doesn't (F2, F12, F15, N1)
docs.text:
• With weights, fixtures, backend, protocol, and operator set fixed, cross-template differences in the preservation rate reflect the template's causal contribution to this measured quantity — which includes genuine robustness differences and template-induced measurement differences (tokenization, abstention propensity). Denominators (n_evaluable, n_unevaluable, n_base_abstain) are reported per template so the latter are visible; we do not claim to separate them (F2).
  • The number is a template×backend-tokenizer interaction, not a backend-independent template property. Cross-backend comparison requires identical (fixtures, backend, protocol-fingerprint) triples (F15).
  • The per-template readout is a comparative ranking across the run's candidates — valid only within identical triples, never an absolute quality score, never blended into winner selection (which stays purely accuracy-driven and conservative) (F12).
  • A template can be perfectly robust and perfectly wrong; the preservation rate is reported next to accuracy, and the accuracy-driven decision does not see it (F12, N1).

docs.title: Falsifiability (F6)
docs.text: This measurement would be proven uninformative if: (1) the controls harness (below) fails to discriminate a known-robust from a known-fragile template implementation; (2) the preservation rate is identical across all templates on every fixture set tried (no signal); (3) the preservation rate does not reproduce when the run is repeated byte-identically (nondeterminism — the instrument's core promise). Note the number is a template×backend-tokenizer interaction (see below): changing the tokenizer is expected to change it, which is a scope boundary, not a retirement criterion.

docs.title: Frozen protocol (F9, N3)
docs.text: freeze_template_robustness_protocol(backend_fingerprint, fixtures) / verify_template_robustness_protocol(protocol, backend_fingerprint, fixtures): instrument name + version, perturbation_code_sha256 (perturbation.py), scorer code hash (hash of the template-robustness implementation, not just perturbation.py — F9a), the frozen search plan (3 operators, seeds/modes fully specified — F9d), fixture ids + hashes (bound at verify time — the wave-5 finding-1 fix), backend fingerprint. The renderer is per-candidate context: protocol records template name + sha256 of the Format's defining fields and of the rendered base and perturbed inputs (N3). The subject_span text states the fixture-scope condition explicitly (v1.0.1, wave-6 red-team A finding 3: results are conditional on fixtures whose correct answer is invariant under the operators; presentation-sensitive fixtures are out of scope). Comparability rule (F9c): rankings are only valid across runs with identical (fixtures, backend, protocol-fingerprint) triples.

docs.title: Degradation granularity (F8, N5)
docs.text: Per-variant backend exceptions → abstain (fail-closed, inherited from _evaluate_one); they enter denominators, never the numerator. unavailable is reserved for stage-level failure (backend down, protocol mismatch, frozen-plan drift) and is prominent in the report (N5a) — a silently missing measurement is worse than a noisy one for the ship decision. The stage runs post-winner-selection over the run's candidate set (N5b), never raises, never fails the run (the --verbosity precedent).

docs.title: Controls (F14)
docs.text:
The probe's controls don't transfer (different unit of analysis). The stage ships two implementation controls, with the probe's honest caveat (they validate the machinery, not the concept):

  1. Determinism: the same template probed twice yields byte-identical preservation vectors.
  2. Scripted-response discrimination: against a backend scripted to flip on any content change, preservation rate = 0.0; against one that never flips, 1.0. (Validates the flip-counting machinery end-to-end.)

docs.title: Scope decisions
docs.text:
• Split: search split — the fixtures the winner was selected on; the decision-relevant question is whether the selection is noise-fragile (F22).
  • Multi-turn: user-role messages in any fixture are perturbed; assistant (few-shot demonstration) messages are never perturbed — they are not user content, and perturbing them would be the R6 inversion again (F10).
  • Zero denominators: no user-role messages → fixture excluded with reason; all variants no-op → n_unevaluable; baseline abstain → excluded from the preservation denominator, counted in n_base_abstain (F11).
  • Candidate key: the Format candidates exactly as passed to run_experiment, keyed by candidate name as in results.json (F21).

docs.title: Cost (F18)
docs.text: Per candidate: F fixtures × (1 baseline + V variants) generations, plus F×(1+V) encodes for verdicts and F×(1+V) encodes for the content-span no-op filter/distance (2× encode factor). V = 8 seeds × 2 seeded operators (case_flip, unicode_variant; whitespace modes are data-dependent, counted exactly). Total per run ≈ C × F × (17 + n_whitespace_modes) generations. Opt-in (model-protocol-lab run --template-robustness); the cost formula is in --help.

docs.title: Differentiation (F13)
docs.text: Web-research pass logged in docs/RESEARCH_LOG.md (cycle 166): PromptBench / NoisyPromptBench measure model robustness (PDR); arXiv:2604.18389 studies prompt-wording sensitivity as a paper, not a tool; no shipped tool measures per-chat-template surface-noise robustness deterministically. Framed as "the combination", never "first". Academic work cited, not claimed over.

docs.title: Artifacts (F20)
docs.text:
• results.json: template_robustness key (per-candidate vectors + denominators + protocol fingerprint).
  • HTML report: per-candidate preservation bars with denominators, per-operator vectors, nearest-flip display, the "nearest observed flip is an upper bound over the searched subset (d_obs ≥ d*), never a guarantee" warning, and "Scope — read first."
  • diffreports.diff_template_robustness: per-candidate drift with the comparability gate (protocol-drift → not comparable).
  • model-protocol-lab surface-noise (per-prompt probe) is unchanged.

docs.title: Token-depth sensitivity sweep — cycle 206 design (ADJUDICATED: buildable on the amendments below; red-team A, red-team B, and verifier converged, coordinator adjudication in ~/workspace/agents_out/cycle206/coordinator_adjudication.md)
Background: the gap this closes
docs.text: The lab ships a prompt-boundary sensitivity sweep (run --sensitivity-sweep, USAGE §8.5): the search re-runs with the prompt truncated mid-token at each depth 1..--max-drop-bytes (bytes, tail-only, cap 8), reporting the depths where the selected winner or decision changes. Wave-9 red-team B proved the shipped coverage is byte-granularity, tail-only, depth ≤ 8 bytes, and recorded the qualification: for templates whose turn-closing suffix spans more than 8 bytes (multi-token assistant headers do), a token-granularity ladder at depths beyond that suffix is measured by no shipped readout — not by the sweep, not by budget_frontier (output side), not by stop-cause. The boundary-truncation ladder candidate was dropped on that evidence; the token-depth extension of the existing sweep is the recorded backlog item. This design extends the existing sweep. It is not a new probe.

docs.title: Pre-registered claim (falsifiable)
docs.text: For a given run, the selected winner and decision are invariant to dropping up to K trailing prompt tokens. The claim is falsified by a flip (winner or decision change) at any depth ≤ K; the readout is the first flip depth in tokens, or "no flip up to K". Scope: a per-run readout. A flip exhibits prompt sensitivity at token depth; it proves nothing about weights, and a no-flip result acquits the run only up to K, never in general.

docs.title: Monday-morning utility
docs.text: A prompt-format researcher deciding whether a comparison's winner survives losing its trailing prompt tokens — for example the multi-token assistant turn-closing header — checks the token-depth flip readout before trusting the verdict.

docs.title: Invariants (binding on the build)
docs.text:
1. The token mode shares the sweep's search and selection machinery (same native baseline, same decision rule via run_experiment). It is a parallel implementation — a new truncation wrapper, a parameterised/second sweep, CLI validation, and reporting — not a unit swap of the byte sweep, which hardcodes TruncatedPromptBackend (experiments.py:3497).
  2. The depth unit is the backend's own tokenization: dropping K trailing token ids from the encoded prompt. No text decode round-trip sits in the measurement path — detokenization would confound token identity with decode fidelity.
  3. Fail-closed with an explicit status: every token depth carries a per-depth status field. winner_changed is gated on status == "applied"; flips_at derives from the gated flag; and inapplicable depths are listed separately in inapplicable_at. Inapplicability is decided by a pre-run token-length check (K at or beyond the prompt's token count), never inferred post-hoc from a failed decision — otherwise a genuine run failure is relabelled inapplicable and vice versa. Status is per-depth, because one un-truncatable prompt aborts the whole depth (the run_experiment early-return path, experiments.py:3742–3744). An inapplicable depth keeps decision: "failed" for that depth, and the spec states that status governs all flip consumption. This corrects the byte sweep's known flaw, where a failed depth is counted as a flip (experiments.py:3509, :3523) — byte mode itself stays untouched, as test_cycle17 pins its behaviour.
  4. The payload labels its granularity: byte and token readouts must be distinguishable in the recorded result, so no consumer can mistake a token depth for a byte depth. The token payload is a separate key, sensitivity_sweep_tokens, carrying granularity, max_drop_tokens, and per-depth drop_tokens / status; the sweep payload carries no fingerprint, so granularity must live in these fields. The token wrapper's fingerprint suffix is +prompt-trunc-{K}t, distinct from the byte wrapper's b suffix (backends.py:788).
  5. Compute multiplies by depth count, exactly as the byte sweep's does. Ladder bounds must be justified against that cost.
  6. Eligibility: a backend is eligible when its generate consumes ids as given. The rule covers id-rewriting wrappers, not only char-wise backends: TokenHealingBackend.generate forwards healed ids, so a token wrapper stacked over it would measure healed ids, not prompt ids. The token wrapper is defined on the base prompt encoding: it must never naively slice a prefill-wrapped encoding, because PrefillBackend.encode appends prefill ids that a naive [:-K] would drop first, leaving the prompt intact. Scripted backends are plumbing-only: they may prove the machinery runs, but never P4 evidence (a flip on a scripted backend says nothing about real weights).

docs.title: Frozen acceptance probes (what the build must demonstrate)
docs.text:
• P1 (shape): token mode on a known fixture produces the sweep's readout shape with granularity labeled and a native baseline present.
  • P2 (fail-closed): a depth beyond the prompt's token count records a failed decision for that depth with status: "inapplicable", is excluded from flips_at, and appears in inapplicable_at — not a skip, and not a flip.
  • P3 (no regression): byte mode behaves exactly as before; its existing tests pass with no behavior change, and byte report HTML is byte-identical.
  • P4-reach (discrimination, proven existentially before build): every shipped suffix is longer than 8 bytes and begins with a special token (chatml 22 B, llama3 47 B, gemma 21 B, measured from Format.render and the catalog), so dropping all suffix tokens yields the pre-suffix prompt, which no byte drop ≤ 8 can yield. P4-reach existence is therefore proven for all three families, tokenizer-free. What the build must still measure, per checkpoint tokenizer (amendment A4), is which K that whole-suffix depth is per candidate.
  • P4-flip (reported measurement, never a build gate): on a named checkpoint, a token-depth flip is reported either way. A no-flip result is a measurement, not a build failure, and a flip on a scripted backend is plumbing-only, never P4 evidence.

docs.title: Resolved design questions (adjudicated)
docs.text:
• Q1 Ladder: contiguous 1..max. Default 4, cap 8 are working hypotheses, frozen only after A4 (per-candidate suffix token counts measured on the real checkpoint tokenizer); A4 may raise the cap with justification, never silently. Contiguous beats sparse: a sparse ladder can skip the whole-suffix depth. Cost: native + one run_experiment per depth, so 5 runs at default 4 and 9 at cap 8 per mode.
  • Q2 CLI surface: separate combinable flags --token-depth-sweep + --max-drop-tokens alongside --sensitivity-sweep / --max-drop-bytes, sharing one native run. Sharing saves exactly one run_experiment versus two sweep calls (not two: the CLI main run is already a separate native). Token flag validation mirrors the byte flag's 1..8 range (cli.py:2967–2968) unless A4 justifies a wider cap. Token mode inherits the diagnostics_unavailable fallback (cli.py:4095–4096); this is documented, not hidden.
  • Q3 Reporting: separate key sensitivity_sweep_tokens and a separate report section, via reporting.py's three touchpoints (compute, TOC tuple, body concatenation). Generalising _sweep_section is allowed only if byte HTML stays byte-identical (test_cycle33 pins it).
  • Q4 Motivation: the assistant-header case is named as the motivating probe; the ladder itself stays generic.

docs.title: Uniqueness (combination, not "first")
docs.text: Exact token-sequence selection machinery + a token-depth truncation ladder + a flip-depth readout on a local checkpoint. Neighbors checked in the research pass (RESEARCH_LOG cycle-206 entry): prompt-sensitivity work studies paraphrase and template sensitivity of scores (Hua et al., arXiv:2509.01790), not truncation ladders; lm-eval-harness truncation is a length cap on few-shot examples when prompts are too long, not a sensitivity probe; no token-depth prompt-truncation ladder over a fixed selection rule was found in HELM or LightEval. The surviving claim is this combination.

docs.title: As built (cycle 206)
docs.text:
• Pre-run length check scope: the minimum prompt token length is taken over search AND held-out prompts for every candidate (a conservative superset, stated in the sweep docstring: a depth whose truncated winner's held-out prompt alone was too short is labelled inapplicable rather than claimed as a flip, because a flip claim must never rest on a prompt that never ran).
  • B1 is enforced, not just documented: TokenTruncatedPromptBackend refuses a prefill-wrapped inner at construction. B2 is documented with fingerprint transparency: a sweep over an id-rewriting backend measures healed ids, and the fingerprint chain shows the healing step; such runs are plumbing-only, never evidence.
  • Shared native: when both sweeps are requested the CLI computes one native and passes it to both (saving exactly one run_experiment versus two sweep calls); each sweep alone recomputes its native, as before. Byte sweep behaviour, payload, and HTML are byte-identical; its failed-depth-counts-as-flip semantics are pinned and unchanged.
  • Default 4 / cap 8 remain provisional: A4 (per-candidate suffix token counts on a real checkpoint tokenizer) was NOT measured in this cycle — no checkpoint is available in the gate environment — and no real-checkpoint count is claimed anywhere. The payload's suffix_token_counts (standalone-suffix encoding, documented as an annotation, not in-prompt tokenization) is the mechanism by which a future run performs A4 and may raise the cap with justification, never silently.

docs.title: What would prove this design wrong
docs.text:
• Token-depth flips turn out to be fully explained by byte-depth flips at corresponding boundaries on every fixture tried.
  • The token unit cannot be defined without a decode round-trip on the lab's backends (invariant 2 fails).
  • (Retired by adjudication: "P4 cannot be constructed" — the existential whole-suffix argument proves P4-reach for chatml, llama3, and gemma before any build.)

docs.title: Usage
docs.text: For troubleshooting and interpretation questions, see docs/FAQ.md.

docs.title: 1. Inspect the fixture schema
docs.text:
Each dataset has exactly two arrays: search and held_out. Every fixture has id, group, messages and expected. Messages have exactly role and content; roles alternate user/assistant, beginning and ending with user. System messages, tools and assistant prefills are not supported.

IDs are globally unique. Groups must not overlap across partitions. Identical message sequences cannot appear in both partitions. These checks do not detect paraphrases or other semantic leakage. Deliberately separate task families and freeze the held-out set before search. ID-uniqueness, group-overlap and identical-message comparisons use NFC-normalized text, so NFD/NFC variants of the same visual string cannot evade them; the stored fixture data itself is left byte-exact.

Limits include a 2 MB UTF-8 file, 100 fixtures per partition, 21 messages per fixture and 16,384 characters per text field. The dataset path must be a regular file — character/block devices, named FIFOs, sockets and directories are refused (a FIFO with no writer would block forever). Inspect the loader for the authoritative contract. To author fixtures without hand-writing this JSON, see fixtures build in §9.

Empty expected answers are allowed but pass vacuously: any output that emits only the boundary token satisfies them. inspect and run warn on stderr naming such fixtures so the measurement gap is visible.

inspect also runs a search/held-out contamination check: every held-out fixture is compared against every search fixture over NFKC-normalized, format-char-stripped, lowercased, whitespace-collapsed user text plus the expected answer, using character-level SequenceMatcher ratio and token-3-gram Jaccard. Pairs at duplicate (ratio ≥ 0.98), near_duplicate (≥ 0.90) or paraphrase_suspect (≥ 0.80 or Jaccard ≥ 0.85) print a stderr warning and appear in the JSON contamination block. The check is advisory -- thresholds are heuristic and heavy paraphrases still evade -- and never fails the command. doctor --dataset reports the same block, and run records it in results.json with a "Fixture hygiene" line in the report's run-configuration section.

python -m model_protocol_lab inspect examples/fixtures.json
python -m model_protocol_lab catalog

docs.title: 2. Pre-flight check with doctor
docs.text:
Before any model run, validate the checkpoint directory and fixture file without loading weights:

python -m model_protocol_lab doctor --model path/to/checkpoint --dataset YOUR_FIXTURES.json

doctor checks the asset manifest (required files, no symlinks, size caps), the model config (supported GPT-2/Llama causal-LM settings only), the tokenizer document structure, and the fixture schema. With --boundary-ids it additionally verifies each ID against the tokenizer vocabulary (loading the tokenizer only, never the weights). Exit 0 means the run inputs look sane; exit 1 lists the failing checks. It reports the tokenizer's declared added_tokens with their IDs to help choose --boundary-ids.

When every check passes and both --dataset and --boundary-ids were supplied, the doctor report carries a suggestion with the exact run invocation implied by the pre-flight result: --max-context is filled from the checkpoint's declared window, --max-new-tokens is sized so the longest fixture prompt (rendered with every catalog candidate and encoded with the checkpoint tokenizer) still fits that window, paths are shell-quoted, and the format family stays an explicit FAMILY placeholder for you to choose (see catalog). If even the longest fixture prompt fills the window, the suggestion keeps --max-new-tokens 1 and warns you to shorten the fixtures or use a larger-window checkpoint. The suggestion is omitted whenever it could mislead (failed verdict, no dataset, no boundary IDs, or no declared window).

docs.title: Template↔tokenizer portability matrix (doctor --portability-matrix)
docs.text:
python -m model_protocol_lab doctor --model PRIMARY --portability-matrix SECOND_CHECKPOINT

For every catalog candidate (each base format plus its bounded local repairs -- the same hypothesis space run --mutate measures), doctor checks the candidate's special-token inventory against the second checkpoint's tokenizer: each token must be registered in the checkpoint's added/special tokens, encode as exactly one token id, and encode to its registered id. Tokenizer only -- weights are never loaded -- so this costs about as much as the other doctor checks (one tokenizer load plus a few encodes per candidate).

Asymmetry warning: incompatible means the format cannot be the second checkpoint's native format -- re-running the experiment there is scientifically pointless, and you learned that for one tokenizer load. compatible means the format's control tokens are merely encodable as atomic special tokens by that tokenizer; it predicts NOTHING about experimental success, which depends on the checkpoint's weights. The matrix never transfers a selection verdict across checkpoints and never emits a portability score: it is a static exclusion screen, not a portability measurement (research basis: docs/RESEARCH_PORTABILITY_2026-10-15.md).

Details: formats with an empty bos (chatml/qwen3-style) skip the BOS requirement -- a missing BOS token is not an incompatibility for them, and each report row carries bos_skipped to document the skip. A format whose special-token inventory is empty reports unknown, never compatible; an encode failure degrades to unknown the same way. The matrix never fails the doctor verdict: an unusable second checkpoint yields an unavailable section with a fixed-vocabulary detail. The JSON report carries the full matrix under portability_matrix (per-candidate rows with per-token checks); the CLI also prints a readable table to stderr so stdout stays parseable JSON.

docs.title: Behavioural template probe (doctor --template-probe)
docs.text:
The static template firewall (section 8.12) proves a checkpoint's chat template contains no RCE primitives. It cannot see content-conditional logic written in legal Jinja — a template that injects an instruction only when a trigger phrase appears in a user message passes the AST scan untouched. model-protocol-lab doctor --model DIR --template-probe is the dynamic tier: it renders frozen probe conversations — synthetic messages bracketed by sentinel strings — through the checkpoint's own tokenizer, in pairs that differ by one frozen word swap, and reports per pair whether the rendering changed anywhere outside the swapped message's own span. Run it on a downloaded checkpoint before trusting its template; that is the decision it informs.

The JSON report carries the section under template_probe: counts for every pair outcome (clean, extra_span_change, span_content_mismatch, transform_unverifiable, content_dropped, span_unresolvable, unexercised, nondeterministic_render, render_error), a findings list (capped, grouped by the changed region's SHA-256, each with a capped control-stripped excerpt), role-arm render-diff facts (a message's span vanished, merged into another span, or changed order when a system message is added or a user message is relabelled), the template source SHA-256, and the probe protocol fingerprint. Findings never change the doctor verdict or the exit code, in either direction: the probe reports facts, not a certificate. The full design — definitions, pre-registered claims, budgets — is in docs/TEMPLATE_PROBE_DESIGN.md.

Limits, in the same breath as the capability: the probe conversations are published constants, and a template can detect them (sentinel, shape, or phrasing) and suppress conditional behaviour while being probed, so a section with no findings bounds only non-probe-aware templates; the probe set is a frozen sample, so a backdoor keyed on anything outside its swaps is missed; the probe reads only the tokenizer_config.json-embedded template string, so list-form templates and a separate chat_template.jinja file report no_template. Legitimate content conditionals produce findings too — judge the inserted text, which is why it is shown.

docs.title: 3. Prepare a local model
docs.text:
Use trusted local GPT-2 or Llama causal-LM assets supported by the adapter. Required files include config.json, a self-contained tokenizer.json, and either model.safetensors or model.safetensors.index.json with its flat-named shards. Optional generation_config.json is fingerprinted but does not control generation.

The adapter rejects remote-code mappings, quantization configurations, adapter-only directories, encoder-decoder configurations, cross-attention configurations, conflicting weight layouts, asset symlinks and incomplete weight loading. No automatic downloads, pickle weights, custom model code, model-specific tokenizer Python code, quantized loading or LoRA merging are provided.

The tokenizer is loaded directly from tokenizer.json. Encoding disables automatic special-token insertion. Verify its behavior against the checkpoint's intended tokenizer before trusting results. Literal special-token markers may not behave as expected for every checkpoint.

The device is cpu or cuda (CUDA device 0). Weights and computation are requested in float32 for the primary measurement (the run --precision probe loads a second, bfloat16 copy purely as a comparison arm), with eager attention and no cache. Context limits are checked against model configuration; practical RAM/VRAM limits remain your responsibility. Stock GPT-2 checkpoints declare n_positions=1024, below the CLI default --max-context 2048: pass --max-context 1024 (or less) for them, or backend initialization fails fast with the distinct code local_context_limit_exceeds_declared_window instead of the generic init failure.

docs.title: 4. Establish the response boundary
docs.text:
--boundary-ids is a comma-separated token-ID sequence expected to end an assistant answer. It is not automatically inferred and is not assumed to equal the checkpoint's EOS token. Determine it from the actual tokenizer and intended protocol. Do not copy token IDs from another model.

The boundary match is an exact token-ID subsequence match by design. It can miss when the model emits the boundary text with a different tokenization than the configured IDs (one string can be many token sequences, e.g. [" ", " "] vs [" "]; see HF transformers' StopStringCriteria). Each completed observation therefore also records boundary_text_match: whether the decoded output ends with the decoded boundary text. A boundary_found=false with boundary_text_match=true flags that false-negative mode for investigation; it never changes the pass criterion. Prefer boundary sequences whose tokenization is stable in the checkpoint's tokenizer (verify with doctor --boundary-ids).

docs.title: Per-candidate boundaries (run --boundary-map)
docs.text:
--boundary-ids is the default boundary for every candidate, and the repeatable --boundary-map NAME=ID,ID flag overrides it for individual candidates:

python -m model_protocol_lab run ... --family chatml --mutate \
    --boundary-ids 128001 \
    --boundary-map chatml/prefix-newline=128001 \
    --boundary-map chatml/prefix-trim=128002

This is the scientifically honest choice, not just convenience: each candidate is a format hypothesis, and real formats terminate the assistant turn with different markers (ChatML <|im_end|>, Llama 3 <|eot_id|>, Gemma <end_of_turn>). Judging every hypothesis by a single sequence would mis-measure the formats whose own terminator differs. Each candidate is therefore measured with its own boundary -- the one its format's protocol actually uses -- and the report records every candidate's boundary (boundary_token_ids per search entry, per-candidate lines in the run configuration, a boundary column in the candidate table).

The selection rule is unchanged: exactly one candidate must pass every search fixture, each under its own boundary; ties and failures still abstain, and the held-out set still only sees the frozen winner (measured with the winner's boundary). The stop matrix and the budget frontier use each candidate's own boundary as well. A mistyped candidate name fails fast (the valid names are listed); --mutate variants are named <family>/toggle-bos, <family>/no-bos, <family>/prefix-newline, <family>/prefix-trim (some collapse when the family has no BOS marker -- see catalog), plus kolibri/thinking-off (the Kolibri-1 thinking-disabled generation-prompt branch), nemotron35/thinking-off (the Nemotron 3.5 Lightning thinking-disabled generation-prompt branch), ling/thinking-off (the Ling-3.1-flash thinking-disabled branch), laguna/thinking-on (the Laguna S-2.1 thinking-enabled generation-prompt branch), qwen38/thinking-off, nanbeige42/thinking-off, k2horizon/effort-medium and k2horizon/effort-low (the K2 Horizon reasoning-effort branches), hy4/no-think, and minimax3/thinking-disabled / minimax3/thinking-enabled.

Discipline: use each format's genuine end-of-turn marker, verified against the checkpoint tokenizer with doctor --boundary-ids (or doctor --boundary-map NAME=ID,ID, which checks each mapping). A boundary chosen to make a candidate pass is not a measurement -- it is gaming the operator's own experiment.

docs.title: 5. Run a bounded experiment
docs.text:
Replace every uppercase placeholder below. This is an invocation template, not a validated command for a specific checkpoint.

python -m model_protocol_lab run --model LOCAL_MODEL_DIRECTORY --dataset YOUR_FIXTURES.json --family chatml --mutate --boundary-ids TOKEN_ID --max-new-tokens 64 --max-context 2048 --device cpu --output NEW_REPORT_DIRECTORY

The local adapter emits the full requested number of tokens unless cancelled or failed. It does not stop automatically on EOS or the supplied boundary. The evaluator finds the first boundary sequence, decodes preceding tokens, and checks the exact expected answer. This separates boundary observation from backend stop behavior.

--seed accepts an unsigned 64-bit integer (default 0). It is validated up front and recorded in results.json for provenance, but it does not change greedy selection: the local adapter decodes greedily, so the seed has no effect on outputs. It exists so future sampling backends can share the flag.

With --mutate, the bounded candidate set adds BOS and assistant-prefix variants. The prefix mutations explore the same space as assistant-prefill controls in chat APIs (HF's add_generation_prompt / continue_final_message, vLLM's guided prefill): prefix-newline and prefix-trim vary how the assistant turn is opened, toggle-bos and no-bos vary BOS placement; several families additionally yield generation-prompt variants for thinking-mode control (the empty-<think>-block prefill convention, and reasoning-effort branches): kolibri/thinking-off, nemotron35/thinking-off, ling/thinking-off, qwen38/thinking-off (enable_thinking=false), nanbeige42/thinking-off, laguna/thinking-on (S-2.1 thinking-enabled generation prompt), k2horizon/effort-medium / k2horizon/effort-low (reasoning_effort branches), hy4/no-think (reasoning_effort='no_think'), minimax3/thinking-disabled / minimax3/thinking-enabled (thinking_mode branches). Search does not modify weights. A unique candidate passing all search cases is frozen before held-out evaluation. Ties cause abstention; the held-out set is not used to break them.

Ctrl+C requests cooperative cancellation after model loading. Interrupted evaluation can retain a partial report. Model loading and individual backend operations are not guaranteed to be promptly interruptible.

docs.title: 6. Read the outputs
docs.text:
• results.json: structured decision, summaries, candidate formats and fingerprint. Each observation carries boundary_text_match (see §4).
  • report.html: offline static comparison -- decision banner (with selection margin, see §8.7), section table of contents, run configuration, candidate table with per-candidate boundary IDs, per-fixture outcome grid, decisive fixtures, token overhead, template conformance, backend divergence, stop matrix, token-budget frontier with per-candidate pass curves, a deterministic inline-SVG frontier chart with a decision ribbon coloring every budget span by post-hoc outcome, a selection-margin trajectory chart with the safe-budget-floor dashed line, a per-candidate sparkline table, per-flip-span attribution lines, a prompt-boundary canonicality section, a chat-marker isolation matrix (see §8.11), a template-firewall verdict block (see §8.12), a selection-robustness matrix under stop semantics (see §8.13), a cross-checkpoint transfer matrix (see §8.14), a fixture-perturbation robustness section (see §8.15), a token-healing sensitivity section (see §8.16), an instruction-hierarchy adherence section (see §8.17), an assistant-prefill sensitivity section (see §8.18), a protocol-portfolio section (see §8.19), a synthetic-history selection stability section (see §8.20), a batch-invariance audit section (see §8.21), a position-sensitivity section (see §8.22), a stop-cause termination audit section (see §8.23), a whitespace-canonicalization section (see §8.24), a structured-output adherence section (see §8.25), a delimiter-authority section (see §8.26), a few-shot x template section (see §8.27), a fake-turn history-tampering section (see §8.28), a prompt-only tool-call adherence section (see §8.29), a response-verbosity profile (see §8.30), a template surface-noise robustness section (see §8.31), a template field-ablation section (see §8.32), a prefix-cache sharability profile (see §8.33), a labeled-block confidentiality section (see §8.34), an answer-collision audit section (see §8.35), a suspected-refusal profile (see §8.36), a scorer-lens regrade (see §8.37), a candidate aliasing audit section (see §8.38), a prompt-repetition section (see §8.39), a distractor-dilution section (see §8.40), sensitivity sweep, log-likelihood diagnostic (see §8.9) and held-out cards (including the held-out verification-floor callout). A section renders only when the run recorded its stage; a run without that stage omits the section rather than rendering an empty one. Tables sort on header click via one small inline script (hash-allowlisted in the report's Content-Security-Policy); no fonts or remote assets. The report reads identically with scripting disabled.

A byte-deterministic example is committed at examples/sample-report/report.html (produced from examples/fixtures.json by examples/make_sample_report.py, which regenerates the directory rather than appending to it) -- open it to see most of the sections above with no model required. The sample's scripted run does not record every stage, so the template-conformance, backend-divergence, stop-matrix, sensitivity-sweep, log-likelihood, token-healing, template-robustness, field-ablation, scorer-lens, candidate-aliasing, prompt-repetition, distractor-dilution, leading-claim, numeric-surface-form and date-line sections are absent from the sample even though real runs render them.

Open the HTML file in a browser. It loads no fonts or other remote assets. The only script is a small inline table sorter; the content is unchanged with scripting disabled. Raw evidence is never embedded in this HTML view. Add --include-evidence only when you deliberately want raw observations in JSON and understand that token IDs can reveal private prompts.

Output requires a new directory and will not overwrite an existing one. Inspect a partial directory after any write failure. Do not assume that a file's existence proves a complete run.

Exit status: 0 for compatibility on the supplied fixture set; 2 for completed negative or ambiguous decisions; 130 for cancellation; 1 for recorded evaluator failure or caught initialization, loading or filesystem errors. Argument-parser errors also return 2. Inspect the decision field rather than interpreting exit 2 alone.

Exit codes for every subcommand (the table is the contract; a failure path always exits non-zero with a fixed-vocabulary message on stderr, never a traceback):

Subcommand 0 Non-zero catalog listed the catalog — (no failure code; misuse is an argparse error, 2) inspect fixture file valid 1 invalid fixture file doctor verdict ok 1 any other verdict run decision compatible_on_fixture_set 2 negative or ambiguous decision; 130 cancellation; 1 recorded evaluator failure or caught initialization, loading, or filesystem error fixtures build fixture file written 1 invalid authoring source or output collision fixtures fuzz report ok 1 otherwise diff-reports comparison written, even when it finds differences 1 input load failure diff-backends comparison written 1 tokenizer, encode, or validation failure debug session or script completed 1 invalid dataset, tokenizer, or script surface-noise probe probe completed 2 cancelled; 3 unavailable; 1 invalid input surface-noise diff, surface-noise protocol completed 1 invalid input verify verdict ok 2 any other verdict; 1 when the determinism-audit backend cannot initialize, or on a bundle ValueError pack bundle written 1 fixed-vocabulary failure (unreadable entry, unwritable output, or similar)

The run code 2 is deliberately shared: a negative or ambiguous decision and an argparse usage error both return 2, which is why the decision field — not the exit code alone — is the verdict for run.

Output contract: machine-parseable JSON goes to stdout for catalog, inspect, doctor, fixtures, run, verify, pack, diff-reports, diff-backends, and surface-noise; human-readable summaries, warnings, and progress notes go to stderr, so stdout stays parseable when stderr is discarded. A long run prints nothing until it finishes — there is no progress heartbeat and no --verbose flag; that silence is the documented behavior, not a missing feature. Scripts should read the JSON on stdout and the exit code, not scrape stderr.

results.json carries "schema_version": 1. Validators reject any other value as unsupported_schema_version. Additive fields may appear within a version; a breaking change to the result shape bumps the version. Consumers should check the field before parsing the rest of the payload, and treat an unknown version as unreadable rather than guessing at its layout.

docs.title: 7. Validate the source
docs.text:
From the repository root, in a disposable environment:

python -m pip install -e ".[dev]"
python -m unittest discover -s tests -t .
ruff check model_protocol_lab tests examples
ruff format --check model_protocol_lab tests examples
mypy model_protocol_lab

The core tests use fake backends and do not require model weights. They do not establish Hugging Face adapter compatibility, CPU/GPU parity or real-model effectiveness. Follow the staged plan for those checks and preserve exact dependency versions, model hashes and logs.

docs.title: 8. Experiment diagnostics
docs.text: Every run attaches diagnostic sections to results.json and report.html. None of them changes the selection rule or the pass criterion; the decision banner cites the failure-mode taxonomy whenever the run did not select cleanly.

docs.title: 8.1 Template conformance
docs.text: run diffs each candidate's hand-rendered prompt (encoded with add_special_tokens=False) against the checkpoint tokenizer's own apply_chat_template output for the same messages, as exact token-ID sequences. Each divergent segment lists the token-ID subsequences that differ and their positions; a byte-identical rendering reports an empty diff. If tokenizer_config.json declares no chat template, the section reports "no template declared" and the run continues. This makes "sequences its own template would never produce" mechanically checkable instead of a slogan.

docs.title: 8.2 Stop-behavior isolation matrix
docs.text:
For the frozen winner, run re-measures every fixture under emulated competitor stop semantics and reports which semantics flip the verdict:

  • HF StopStringCriteria: emulates the overhang matching from transformers' stopping_criteria.py on the decoded boundary text -- generation stops after the token that completes the stop string, even when the stop string never appears as a literal suffix of the decoded text (token-boundary overhangs). For byte-level and byte-fallback decoders the match runs in byte space, mirroring current transformers (which builds the match table from raw token bytes and UTF-8-encodes the stop string); tokens the byte table cannot represent fall back to the isolated decode encoded as UTF-8.
  • vLLM detokenizer: emulates vllm/v1/engine/detokenizer.py check_stop_strings -- the earliest-completing stop string in the decoded text truncates the output before it (exclude semantics, the vLLM default). The stop_buffer_length holdback only withholds streamed deltas and does not change the final truncation.
  • EOS-appended: truncates before the first EOS token, emulating competitors that stop on EOS (lm-eval appends EOS to its stops; vLLM and llama.cpp stop on EOS by default). The lab itself generates through EOS.

Each cell recomputes the lab's pass rule (exact answer and token-ID boundary) on the truncated output. Emulations are post-hoc truncations of the recorded greedy N-token outputs -- exactly what early stopping would have produced under greedy decoding; an approximation for non-greedy backends. A cell is marked unavailable (never a failure) when the emulation cannot run, e.g. the boundary text cannot be decoded.

The HF emulation ports the tensor implementation's matching rule, including stop strings that end inside the final token (verified differentially against transformers' own StopStringCriteria). Known approximations remaining: on the classic string path, token texts come from per-token decode, while real HF matches on cleaned vocab strings, so exotic spacing edge cases can diverge; on the byte path, tokens the byte table cannot represent (e.g. special tokens) fall back to the isolated decode encoded as UTF-8, approximating HF's cleaned-vocab-string fallback for them. The vLLM emulation likewise approximates incremental DecodeStream detokenization with per-prefix batch decodes, and assumes min_tokens=0 (the lab never sets it).

Why no llama.cpp cell. Verified against llama.cpp's current sources (tools/server/server-context.cpp, common/common.h), a llama.cpp stop-semantics cell would duplicate the vLLM cell on every realistic input: its full-stop rule is the same exclude-semantics "truncate before the completed stop word" (find_stopping_strings: windowed text.find of each antiprompt word on the unsent text tail, earliest start wins, the stop word excluded from the final text). The differences do not survive post-hoc emulation: partial stops only withhold streamed deltas and are never erased from the final text; the multi-word earliest-start vs earliest-completion selection is inapplicable to the matrix's single stop string; the 1-character search-window offset sits below the emulation's incremental-decode approximation floor; and EOS handling is already covered -- llama.cpp stops on any end-of-generation token by default (the EOS-appended cell), while --ignore-eos means "ignore end of stream token and continue generating (implies --logit-bias EOS-inf)", i.e. the lab's own native generate-through-EOS behavior. Adding the cell would double the decode-approximation stack for zero new information, so it stays out by design.

docs.title: 8.3 Failure-mode taxonomy
docs.text:
Every non-passing observation is classified into a closed, deterministic taxonomy, with per-candidate counts in results.json:

  • no-boundary-in-N: no boundary-delimited expected answer within the token cap (covers an absent boundary and a wrong answer with a found boundary; the per-observation records keep the finer distinction).
  • boundary-text-mismatch: no token-ID boundary, but the decoded output ends with the decoded boundary text (the tokenization-mismatch false-negative mode).
  • eos-without-boundary: the model emitted EOS without the boundary (only classified when an EOS id is known, e.g. from the checkpoint tokenizer).
  • held-out-divergence: the search winner failed held-out evaluation.
  • backend-error: the backend failed, reported an error, or the observation was cancelled.

docs.title: 8.4 Boundary portability (doctor --reference-model)
docs.text:
python -m model_protocol_lab doctor --model PRIMARY --reference-model REFERENCE \
    --boundary-ids 1,2,3

doctor decodes --boundary-ids with the primary checkpoint's tokenizer and re-encodes the marker text with the reference checkpoint's tokenizer (tokenizer only, never weights), reporting portable/non-portable with both ID lists. A divergent encoding means the boundary IDs are tokenizer-specific and will not transfer. Non-portability is reported as mismatch -- informational, not a verdict failure, because boundary IDs are per-checkpoint by design. Without --reference-model (or without --boundary-ids) the check is skipped.

docs.title: 8.5 Prompt-boundary sensitivity sweep (run --sensitivity-sweep)
docs.text:
python -m model_protocol_lab run ... --sensitivity-sweep --max-drop-bytes 3

For each depth in 1..--max-drop-bytes, every prompt is truncated by that many trailing bytes and re-encoded -- truncating the prompt in the middle of its final token -- and the full search re-runs. The report lists the depths where the selected winner or decision changed, measuring boundary sensitivity as a variable. This multiplies search compute by the number of depths, so it is opt-in. Depths that would split a UTF-8 codepoint record a failed decision for that depth instead of silently skipping.

Related work: this measures the prompt-boundary tokenization bias that token healing (guidance-ai, 2023) exists to mitigate -- when a prompt ends mid-token, the next-token distribution is skewed because the final token could have been encoded differently. Serving stacks that heal the boundary (back up and constrain the first token) hide this effect; the sweep quantifies it instead, telling you how much your verdict depends on the exact byte where the prompt ends.

docs.title: 8.6 Token-budget robustness frontier
docs.text:
Every run recomputes the search-stage decision at every smaller token budget from the recorded outputs and reports it as budget_frontier in results.json and the HTML report -- answering "was the token cap load-bearing for this verdict?" with no extra model calls.

The derivation is exact, not sampled: for an observation that passed natively with the boundary first occurring at token offset cut, it passes at every budget b >= cut + len(boundary) (the boundary occurrence and the answer region are unchanged) and at no smaller budget (cut is the first occurrence, so no complete boundary fits in a shorter prefix). An observation that did not pass natively cannot pass at any smaller budget. Each candidate is summarized by its per-fixture minimal passing budgets, the pass-count step curve, and the budget ranges where the decision or winner would have differed from native (flip_ranges); budget_robust is true when the decision is identical at every budget from 1 to --max-new-tokens. safe_budget_floor is the first budget from which the native decision never flips again (1 when nothing flips; null when a flip reaches the sweep maximum) -- the HTML report calls it out and marks it on the frontier and margin charts, and model-protocol-lab diff-reports compares it between runs. flip_attribution lists, for each flip span, the (candidate, fixture) observations whose minimal passing budget falls inside the span -- exactly the pass-status changes the span brackets, i.e. the observations to inspect when asking why the decision flips there (a span with none records an empty list: the decision already differed at its start). Structural fact: the per-budget full-passer set only grows with the budget, so flip_ranges is always empty or a single prefix span [1, K]; the floor is then simply K + 1. Like the stop matrix, this is a post-hoc diagnostic: it never changes the selection rule, and it degrades to an "unavailable" marker (never a run failure) when the search did not complete.

The held-out stage gets the same treatment on a smaller scale: held_out_budget_floor in results.json records the per-fixture minimal passing budgets for the winner's held-out observations and safe_budget_floor -- the first token budget from which the verification verdict holds unchanged (the maximum of those budgets; null when the held-out failed natively, since no budget achieves a passing verification). The held-out verdict is monotone in the budget, so this single number is the whole story. The HTML held-out section calls it out ("verification floor ≥ K tokens", or a robustness/failure notice), and model-protocol-lab diff-reports compares it between runs.

docs.title: 8.7 Selection margin (decision fragility)
docs.text:
Every completed run reports selection_margin in results.json and one line in the decision banner -- answering "is any fixture load-bearing for this verdict?" with no extra model calls. The margin is a closed-form integer over the recorded search outcomes: for a unique winner, the minimum over runners-up of their failing-fixture counts (flips to a tie); for no_candidate, the minimum over candidates (flips to a winner); for ambiguous, the tied-candidate count minus one (flips to uniqueness). failed/cancelled runs report no margin. The banner names the closest runner-up and the decisive fixtures. The margin is descriptive; it never changes the decision. A margin of 1 on a unique winner means the verdict hinges on a single borderline fixture -- treat it as barely more informative than a tie and consider authoring more discriminating fixtures (see §9).

The HTML report's margin-trajectory chart (under the frontier chart) shows the per-budget leader and its lead margin across the whole budget sweep, answering "how decisive was the race at each budget?" -- the visual complement of the scalar selection_margin above (gray spans mark tied leads; the dashed line marks the safe budget floor from §8.6).

docs.title: 8.8 Protocol token-overhead accounting
docs.text: Every run with an attached checkpoint tokenizer reports token_overhead in results.json and a "Token overhead" card in the HTML report: per candidate, mean/max prompt tokens (exact tokenizer.encode counts of the rendered prompts, add_special_tokens=False) and mean output tokens, the cheapest candidate, and the winner's token tax versus the cheapest passing candidate as a percentage. Token counts in reports are retained-input/output counts, not equal-compute accounting. Decision utility: context-window budgeting and serving cost when two candidates both pass, or when the winner is token-hungry -- formats differ substantially in control-token overhead.

docs.title: 8.9 Teacher-forced log-likelihood diagnostic (run --logprob-diagnostic)
docs.text:
python -m model_protocol_lab run ... --logprob-diagnostic

Opt-in because it costs one extra forward pass per candidate x fixture. After search completes, each candidate's expected answer is teacher-forced through the checkpoint after the recorded prompt (model_protocol_lab/scoring.py: one forward pass over prompt_ids + encode(expected); prompt positions masked, answer tokens gathered with the causal shift). results.json carries logprob_diagnostic and the HTML report renders a "Log-likelihood diagnostic" section with per-candidate total/mean logprob (nats, per scored token) plus a plain-language reading that separates the two failure attributions:

  • Greedy derailed: the weights assign the expected answer high teacher-forced likelihood, yet greedy generation did not reproduce it -- a decoding/search problem, not missing knowledge.
  • Weights don't know: even teacher-forced, the weights assign the expected answer low likelihood under this candidate's framing.

The reading bands are declared heuristics recorded in the payload (thresholds): mean >= -2.0 nats/token reads as derailment, mean < -5.0 as missing knowledge; between the bands the diagnostic withholds judgment. When the alignment check refuses a fixture (e.g. a token straddling the prompt/answer boundary) the score is unavailable with a fixed reason -- reported, never guessed. Diagnostic only: it never changes the selection rule or the pass criterion.

Related work: this is the lab's own DEVELOPMENT_PLAN.md §9.3-§9.5 design, corroborated by lm-eval's loglikelihood request type and the HELM adapter's token-probability measurements, which likewise score a fixed target string by teacher forcing rather than by sampling.

docs.title: 8.10 Prompt-boundary canonicality (boundary_audit)
docs.text:
Every run re-encodes each stored rendered prompt x greedy completion and requires the joint encoding to equal the recorded prompt_ids + completion_ids. A mismatch is the Prompt Boundary Problem: the tokenizer re-segments the text at the prompt/completion seam, so the ids the model saw are not what the stored text would reproduce. The check is post-hoc and exact (one extra encode per observation, no model calls); encode/decode failures degrade an observation to "unusable", never a run failure.

results.json carries boundary_audit with the overall rate, per-candidate rates, and per-family rates (chatml/x and chatml/y roll up into chatml). The HTML report renders a "Prompt-boundary canonicality" section with the family table; a zero rate is presented as a certificate of boundary-canonicality for the run's templates. model-protocol-lab diff-reports compares the overall and per-family rates between runs (boundary_audit_changed / boundary_audit_asymmetric summary flags feed the identical verdict). The metric is descriptive: it measures text->ids reproducibility of the stored artifacts, not model quality, and a nonzero rate names the families whose prompts the tokenizer re-segments rather than condemning them.

docs.title: 8.11 Chat-marker isolation (marker_isolation)
docs.text:
Every run also probes structural template injection at the tokenizer level: each of 16 hostile marker strings (<|im_start|>, <s>, [INST], <|begin_of_text|>, a forged <|im_start|>assistant<|im_end|> turn, and others) is injected into user text, and the checkpoint tokenizer's control-token ids are counted before and after — the number should not change. The probe uses add_special_tokens=False, the same call the backend's encode makes, so any control token in the output came from the text itself; the special set is the tokenizer's all_special_ids union special-flagged added tokens. A nonzero delta means the hostile text's literal markers became real control tokens (the ChatInject/Phantom injection class, via HF's split_special_tokens=False default).

results.json carries marker_isolation with per-(format, fixture, marker) probes, per-family isolation scores, and the overall isolation rate. The HTML report renders a "Chat-marker isolation" section with the families x markers conformance matrix (isolated vs smuggled cells). The check is pure tokenizer work (no model calls, no weights loaded) and never fails the run: a tokenizer declaring no special ids reports no_special_ids (unmeasurable, not a failure), and one bad triple degrades to unavailable. The core lives in model_protocol_lab/control_tokens.py with render/encode injected, so the whole probe is testable without a model; doctor.marker_isolation is the checkpoint-backed driver.

docs.title: 8.12 Template firewall (template_firewall)
docs.text:
A checkpoint's chat_template is attacker-controlled Jinja, and the conformance check renders it locally. Before any render, every run statically scans the template source for RCE primitives (model_protocol_lab/template_audit.py): dunder attribute/subscript access, the |attr filter (CVE-2025-27516 sandbox escape), dangerous Jinja globals (lipsum, cycler, joiner, self), super() calls, and non-literal or huge range() bounds. A denied template is never rendered — template_conformance fails closed with status denied — and the findings surface as a "Template firewall" section in the report.

results.json carries template_firewall with the verdict (allowed / denied / no_template / unavailable) and fixed-vocabulary findings. An allowed verdict is not a safety proof: it means none of the known primitives were found, and the render still runs inside transformers' ImmutableSandboxedEnvironment (the lab pins jinja2>=3.1.6 for the sandbox-escape fix) under the existing CPU watchdog and memory cap. The stack is: static firewall -> sandboxed render -> watchdog + memory cap.

docs.title: 8.13 Selection robustness under stop semantics (selection_robustness)
docs.text:
The stop matrix (§8.2) re-measures only the winner under emulated stop semantics; the selection rule itself is only ever applied to native generations. A user deploying on vLLM has no answer to "would a different protocol have won under my serving stack's stop semantics?" Every run now answers it post-hoc (experiments.selection_robustness, pure: tokenizer-only, no model calls): for every search candidate it builds the stop matrix, re-derives per-candidate pass/fail under each semantic (exact answer + boundary on the truncated output), and re-applies the conservative selection rule per semantic.

results.json carries selection_robustness with the per-semantic verdicts (native, hf_stop_string, vllm_holdback, eos_appended), the per-candidate pass matrix, and flips -- the semantics whose (decision, winner) differs from native's, e.g. vllm_holdback: ambiguous -> selected(chatml). A semantic whose emulation cannot run for every candidate (e.g. an unknown EOS id) is reported as unavailable, never as a phantom no_candidate: "unknown" must not masquerade as a verdict. The report renders a "Selection robustness under stop semantics" section with the verdicts, the candidate x semantic matrix, and flip callouts. diff-reports compares the per-semantic verdicts and the flip pattern between runs (selection_robustness_changed and selection_robustness_asymmetric, both feeding identical) -- the serving-stack migration signal: the same stack selecting a different winner than before.

docs.title: 8.14 Cross-checkpoint transfer (transfer)
docs.text:
run --transfer-model (repeatable, max 4) answers "does the winner also win on my other checkpoints?" After the primary run, every search candidate is re-evaluated against each transfer checkpoint on the search split only (same boundary, same --max-new-tokens; greedy, exact), and the conservative selection rule is re-applied per checkpoint (experiments.transfer_stage + pure experiments.transfer_portability).

results.json carries transfer with the checkpoint ids, paths and fingerprints, the per-checkpoint decision/winner, the candidate x checkpoint verdict matrix, and the transfer verdict (full / partial / none / unavailable). Per-cell verdicts: transfers (the primary winner is the unique winner there), wins_there (another candidate wins there), ties_there, fails_there, checkpoint_incompatible (the candidate could not be evaluated there -- e.g. boundary IDs outside the checkpoint's vocabulary -- fail-closed, never silently skipped). The report renders a "Cross-checkpoint transfer" section; the decision banner notes the verdict. Compute multiplies by (1 + #checkpoints); the transfer stage never fails the run. diff-reports compares the transfer experiment between runs (diff_transfer: transfer-verdict drift, per-checkpoint (decision, winner) drift, per-cell candidate x checkpoint verdict drift, checkpoints added/removed — transfer_changed / transfer_asymmetric feeding identical): the fleet-portability regression signal after a checkpoint or fixture update.

docs.title: 8.15 Fixture-perturbation robustness (perturbation)
docs.text:
run --perturb N (1-8) answers "does the winner survive fixture phrasing perturbations, or did it win on phrasing luck?" After the primary run, every search candidate is re-evaluated against the primary checkpoint on N deterministically perturbed fixture variants (search split only; same boundary, same --max-new-tokens; greedy, exact), and the conservative selection rule is re-applied per variant (experiments.perturbation_stage + pure experiments.perturbation_robustness).

The perturbation operators (model_protocol_lab.perturbation, pure and seeded -- no model needed for the transforms themselves) rewrite fixture message content only: typo (seeded character substitutions), case_flip, whitespace (collapse / double / newline-split), unicode_variant (ASCII alphanumerics to their NFKC-foldable fullwidth forms -- nearly identical to a human reader, different tokens to most tokenizers), and punctuation_strip. Fixture ids, groups, and expected answers are never touched, so per-variant verdicts stay comparable to the primary run; operators are assigned round-robin from the run seed, so the whole experiment reproduces exactly.

results.json carries perturbation with the per-variant (decision, winner), the flips (variants whose verdict differs from the primary run), the stability summary (how many evaluable variants retain the primary winner/decision), and a per-operator breakdown with the mean fixture-change rate -- so you can see which phrasing noise the winner is fragile to. A variant where no candidate could be evaluated is reported as unavailable, never as a phantom verdict. The report renders a "Fixture-perturbation robustness" section with the stability line, the per-operator table, and the per-variant verdict table. diff-reports compares the stability triplet, the per-variant verdicts, and the variant set between runs (diff_perturbation; perturbation_changed / perturbation_asymmetric feed identical) -- the phrasing-fragility regression signal after a fixture or checkpoint update. Compute multiplies by (1 + N); the stage never fails the run. Together with stop-semantics robustness (§8.13) and cross-checkpoint transfer (§8.14) this completes the winner-reliability trilogy: serving stack, checkpoint fleet, and fixture phrasing.

docs.title: 8.16 Token-healing selection sensitivity (token_healing)
docs.text:
Tokenizers like SentencePiece split trailing whitespace into the next token, so a prompt ending in "hello" encodes differently from the same prompt decoded and re-encoded -- the greedy-tokenization bias at the prompt boundary. Hugging Face's token_healing countermeasure replaces the prompt's tail token with the highest-scoring vocabulary extension at inference time. model-protocol-lab run --token-healing replays the whole experiment once more, with every prompt healed before generation, and re-applies the conservative selection rule to the healed outcomes.

The implementation does not call generate() -- this backend decodes greedily by hand -- but ports transformers.GenerationMixin.heal_tokens faithfully into the lab's manual decoder (model_protocol_lab/healing.py, a pure function with injected decode/re-encode/vocab/argmax callables): decode the prompt, re-encode it (canonical re-tokenization), extend the tail token with every vocabulary token that starts with it (sorted for determinism), trim the tail, then take a single biased argmax that adds +10.0 to every extension and +1.0 to the original tail token. Two deliberate adaptations: decoding keeps special tokens (the lab's prompts are exact id sequences), and an empty trimmed prompt fails closed to the native ids instead of HF's BOS substitution (this pipeline never injects implicit specials).
